etymology_story.zh: 这个20世纪的物理学名称由 beta 和仪器名成分 -tron 构成。beta 在这里联系到作为负β粒子的电子，名称因而指向一种加速电子的装置。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century physics term combines beta with the device-naming element -tron. Beta refers here to electrons as negative beta particles, so the name identifies a machine for accelerating electrons.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：beta（此处联系负β粒子，即电子）＋ -tron（仪器、装置名成分）。可数名词，复数 betatrons；没有常用的普通英语派生词。相关术语 betatron oscillation（电子感应加速器振荡、横向振荡）属于复合术语。考试标签中的 CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: beta (here associated with negative beta particles, or electrons) + -tron (a device-naming element). It is a countable noun with plural betatrons and has no common general-English derivatives. The related expression betatron oscillation is a compound technical term. The CEFR-C2 tag is an estimated learning level, not an official word-specific classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: induction electron accelerator（感应式电子加速器）是描述其原理的对应说法；electron accelerator（电子加速器）范围更广；particle accelerator（粒子加速器）范围更广，还包括加速其他粒子的装置。cyclotron（回旋加速器）工作原理不同，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Induction electron accelerator is a descriptive equivalent that identifies its operating principle; electron accelerator is broader; particle accelerator is broader still and includes machines that accelerate other particles. Cyclotron describes a different accelerator design and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: beta 联想到电子，-tron 联想到机器：让电子绕圈加速的感应装置。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link beta with electrons and -tron with a machine: a betatron accelerates electrons around a ring by induction.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 blintz 借自意第绪语 blintse，而该词来自斯拉夫语的薄饼名称，与俄语 blin 属于相关词。这个词随东欧犹太饮食文化进入英语，通常指包馅后折叠的薄煎饼。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed blintz from Yiddish blintse, a word of Slavic origin related to Russian blin, meaning a pancake. It entered English through Eastern European Jewish food traditions and usually denotes a thin pancake folded around a filling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再分析的单纯借词 blintz，不能把结尾拆作英语后缀。可数名词，复数 blintzes；常见复合表达有 cheese blintz（奶酪馅薄饼）和 fruit blintz（水果馅薄饼），没有常用的派生词族。考试标签中的 CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非官方逐词定级。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, blintz is a morphologically simple loanword; its ending is not an English suffix. It is countable, with plural blintzes; common compounds include cheese blintz and fruit blintz, but it has no established family of common derivatives. The CEFR-C2 tag is an estimated learning level, not an official word-specific classification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: filled pancake（馅煎饼）是较宽泛的描述性对应说法；crêpe（法式薄饼）也很薄，但不一定包馅；pancake（煎饼）是上位词，厚薄和做法均可不同。blintz 特指东欧犹太饮食传统中的包馅薄饼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Filled pancake is a broader descriptive equivalent; a crêpe is also thin but need not contain a filling; pancake is the broader category and includes different thicknesses and preparations. Blintz specifically identifies the filled pancake associated with Eastern European Jewish cooking.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with the related word blini: picture a thin pancake, then fold cheese or fruit inside.

etymology_story.zh: 这一植物名称很可能源于 blue（蓝色），与其常见的淡蓝色花朵有关；英语中的相关用例可追溯至约1821年。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bluet)
etymology_story.en: The plant name probably comes from blue, referring to its often pale-blue flowers; this English use is recorded from around 1821. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bluet)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整植物名学习；blue（蓝色）+ -et（小称后缀）可辅助理解，但不宜将这一拆分视为完全确定的历史构词过程。复数为 bluets；没有常用的直接派生词。相关基础词族有 blue（蓝色；蓝色的）、bluish（略带蓝色的）、blueness（蓝色状态），它们并非由 bluet 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, learn bluet primarily as a complete plant name. Blue + the diminutive suffix -et is a useful analysis, although that precise historical formation is not certain. The plural is bluets, and there are no common direct derivatives. Related forms of the underlying base include blue, bluish, and blueness; these are not derivatives of bluet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: azure bluet（天蓝蓝花草）和 Quaker ladies（贵格会女士花，俗名）均可指 Houstonia caerulea；bluet 的范围较宽，也可指蓝花草属的其他植物，因此这些名称只在特定物种意义上互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Azure bluet and Quaker ladies are alternative common names for Houstonia caerulea. Bluet can also refer more broadly to other Houstonia species, so these names are interchangeable only when that particular species is intended.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: blue（蓝色）→ 一朵小蓝花 → bluet（蓝花草）；记住它也可能开白花。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Blue → a tiny blue flower → bluet; remember that its flowers can also be white.

etymology_story.zh: Boatel 由 boat（船）和 hotel（旅馆）缩合而成，英语中至少自1949年已有记录。它既用于接待乘船旅客的水滨旅馆，也用于以船只作为住宿场所的旅馆。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/boatel)
etymology_story.en: Boatel blends boat and hotel and is recorded in English from at least 1949. It names both a waterside hotel serving boat travelers and a boat used as hotel accommodation. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/boatel)

morphology_enriched.zh: boat（船）+ hotel（旅馆，保留末尾 -el）→ boatel，属于缩合构词，而不是词根加后缀。复数为 boatels；没有常用的直接动词、形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Boat + hotel, retaining the ending -el, produces boatel through blending rather than ordinary suffixation. The plural is boatels. There are no common directly derived verb, adjective, or adverb forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: floating hotel（水上旅馆）最接近船上住宿义，但也可指其他漂浮式住宿设施；botel（船上旅馆）是相近的缩合词；waterside hotel（水滨旅馆）只说明临水位置，并不保证设有码头。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Floating hotel closely matches the accommodation-on-water sense but can include other floating structures. Botel is a similar blended term. Waterside hotel describes location alone and does not necessarily imply docking facilities.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: boat + hotel：船与旅馆合在一起，既可住船上，也可靠船住岸边。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Boat + hotel: sleep aboard a boat, or dock your boat beside a hotel.

etymology_story.zh: Bohrium 以丹麦物理学家 Niels Bohr（尼尔斯·玻尔）的姓氏命名，采用元素名称常见的新拉丁语式词尾 -ium。它是纪念科学家的专名，并非由某种物质性质发展而来。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bohrium)
etymology_story.en: Bohrium was named after the Danish physicist Niels Bohr, using the New Latin element-name ending -ium. Its name commemorates a scientist rather than describing a physical property. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bohrium)

morphology_enriched.zh: Bohr（玻尔）+ -ium（元素名后缀）→ bohrium（𬭛）。Bh 是化学符号，不是派生词；bohrium 通常为不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词。bohrium atoms（𬭛原子）中的 bohrium 是名词作定语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Bohr + the element-name suffix -ium → bohrium. Bh is its chemical symbol, not a derivative. Bohrium is normally uncountable and has no common direct derivatives. In bohrium atoms, the word functions as a noun modifier rather than an independently established adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Bh（化学符号）和 element 107（107号元素）是同一元素的替代指称，而非普通词汇近义词：Bh 适合化学符号表达，element 107 强调原子序数；bohrium 没有常用的普通近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bh and element 107 are alternative designations for the same element rather than ordinary lexical synonyms. Bh serves as the chemical symbol, while element 107 emphasizes atomic number. Bohrium has no common everyday synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Bohr（玻尔）+ -ium（元素）→ 纪念玻尔的107号元素𬭛。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bohr + -ium → the element honoring Bohr: bohrium, number 107.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语 boscage 借入此词；其基础是表示树林或木材的 bois、bos 或 bosc，加上 -age。原来表示林木或林地的名称，在英语中用于树丛、灌木丛等成片生长的植被。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/boscage)
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed boscage from Anglo-French, where it was formed from bois, bos, or bosc, meaning wood or woodland, plus -age. The woodland term came to describe a growth of trees or shrubs in English. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/boscage)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常视为完整借词；历史上可分析为 bosc-（林木）+ -age（集合性后缀）。boskage 是异体拼写；该词通常用作不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词。相关词有 bosk（小树丛）和 bosky（林木茂密的），但不应把它们写成由 boscage 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats boscage as a complete loanword; historically, it contains bosc- meaning wood and the collective suffix -age. Boskage is a spelling variant. The noun is usually uncountable and has no common direct derivatives. Bosk and bosky are related words, not direct derivatives of boscage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thicket（密灌木丛）强调枝叶密集、难以穿行；copse（小树林）强调面积较小的一片树木；brushwood（灌木丛；灌木枝条）侧重低矮灌木，也可指砍下的枝条。boscage 更具文学色彩，可统指树木与灌木形成的植被。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thicket emphasizes dense, often difficult-to-cross growth. Copse means a small group of trees. Brushwood emphasizes low woody vegetation and can also mean cut branches. Boscage is more literary and can encompass both trees and shrubs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bosc-（林木）+ 集合意象 → 树木聚成一片浓密树丛。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Wood + a collective idea → trees and shrubs gathered into a dense mass.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从挪威语 brisling 借入此词，后者源于低地德语 bretling，其中 bret 意为“宽”，与英语 broad 同源。它作为鱼名进入英语，后来也常见于小型罐装鱼的商品名称中。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/brisling)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed brisling from Norwegian, which took it from Low German bretling; its base bret means broad and is related to English broad. It entered English as a fish name and is also familiar from labels on canned small fish. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/brisling)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的鱼名，不宜机械拆成 bris + -ling。历史上的低地德语形式可分析为 bret（宽）+ -ling（名词后缀）；英语复数可用 brisling 或 brislings，没有常用的直接派生词。brisling sardines 中 brisling 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, brisling is a borrowed fish name rather than a productive combination of bris and -ling. Its historical Low German source contains bret, meaning broad, plus the noun suffix -ling. English plurals include brisling and brislings, and there are no common direct derivatives. In brisling sardines, brisling is a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sprat（黍鲱）是最接近的对应词；European sprat（欧洲黍鲱）明确指 Sprattus sprattus；sardine（沙丁鱼）是范围较宽的食用鱼或商品名称，可包括不同种类的小型鲱科鱼，因此并非总与 brisling 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sprat is the closest equivalent, while European sprat specifically identifies Sprattus sprattus. Sardine is a broader food and commercial term covering several kinds of small herring-family fish, so it is not always interchangeable with brisling.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the historical idea of broad to the fish's flattened side profile, then picture a tin of little sprats.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语晚期已有记录，更早的来源尚不确定，可能与欧洲大陆表示靴子的词有关。由于这种靴子与古代悲剧演员联系紧密，buskin 后来又成为悲剧艺术的代称。
etymology_story.en: The word is recorded in late Middle English; its earlier origin is uncertain, though it may be related to continental European words for boots. Its association with ancient tragic actors later made it a literary symbol of tragedy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 buskin 视为不可进一步分析的基本词，不宜把词尾误拆为独立后缀。复数为 buskins；buskin + -ed → buskined，意为“穿高靴的”，也可在文学中表示“悲剧的、悲剧风格的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, buskin is an unanalyzed base rather than a transparent combination of smaller elements. Its plural is buskins; buskin + -ed forms buskined, meaning 'wearing buskins' and, in literary use, 'tragic or characteristic of tragedy.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boot 是靴子的通称；cothurnus 特指古代悲剧演员所穿的高靴，与 buskin 的戏剧义最接近；tragedy 对应 buskin 的文学转喻义，不能替代其鞋靴义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boot is the general term for this kind of footwear; cothurnus specifically denotes the boot associated with ancient tragic actors; tragedy corresponds to the literary figurative meaning of buskin, not its footwear meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 悲剧演员脚上的高靴：由“舞台靴”联想到“悲剧”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a tragic actor's tall boots: the footwear becomes a symbol of tragedy.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 cachou，法语形式经葡萄牙语 cachu 通常被追溯至马拉雅拉姆语 kaccu，原指儿茶类植物提取物。由于这种提取物曾用于芳香含片，词义后来扩展到清新口气的小糖片。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French cachou, generally traced through Portuguese cachu to Malayalam kaccu, referring to catechu. Because the extract was used in aromatic lozenges, the name also came to denote small breath-freshening sweets.

morphology_enriched.zh: cachou 是整体借入的基本词，在现代英语中没有可可靠拆分的词根和词缀。糖片义的复数为 cachous；表示儿茶物质时通常不可数。没有常用的固定派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Cachou is a borrowed base with no transparent root-and-affix breakdown in modern English. The sweet has the plural cachous; the substance sense is normally uncountable. There is no established family of common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: breath mint 是现代常用说法，通常指薄荷味清新口气糖；lozenge 强调供慢慢含化的片状物，不一定用于清新口气；catechu 只对应植物提取物义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Breath mint is the usual modern term and normally suggests mint flavor; lozenge describes something dissolved slowly in the mouth and need not freshen breath; catechu corresponds only to the plant-extract sense.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Catechu goes into a scented lozenge: the ingredient's name becomes the sweet's name.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经晚期拉丁语 cacodaemon 借自希腊语 kakodaimōn，由 kakos“坏的、邪恶的”和 daimōn“灵、神灵”组成。希腊语 daimōn 本身并不必然表示邪恶，前面的成分明确限定了恶灵之义。
etymology_story.en: English received the word through Late Latin cacodaemon from Greek kakodaimōn, combining kakos, 'bad or evil,' with daimōn, 'spirit or divine power.' Daimōn was not inherently evil in Greek; the first element supplies that meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: caco-（坏、恶）+ demon（灵、魔）→ cacodemon。复数为 cacodemons；相关形容词有 cacodemonic 和 cacodemonical，均表示“恶魔的、邪灵的”，且都很少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Caco- ('bad or evil') + demon ('spirit or demon') forms cacodemon. The plural is cacodemons; related adjectives include cacodemonic and cacodemonical, both meaning 'relating to an evil spirit' and both rare.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: demon 是最常见的对应词；evil spirit 直接描述邪恶的灵体，适用范围较广；fiend 更强调凶恶残忍，也常用于比喻残暴的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Demon is the closest everyday equivalent; evil spirit is a broad descriptive expression; fiend emphasizes wickedness or cruelty and is also used figuratively for a brutal person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: caco- 表示“坏”：坏的灵，就是邪灵。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Caco- means 'bad': a bad spirit is an evil spirit.

etymology_story.zh: calcimine 是较早形式 kalsomine 的变体，其名称与拉丁语 calx“石灰”有关。它先指用于墙壁和天花板的白垩胶水涂料，随后也用作动词，表示涂刷这种材料。
etymology_story.en: Calcimine is an altered form of the earlier kalsomine, a name connected with Latin calx, 'lime.' The coating's name also became a verb meaning to apply it to walls or ceilings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 calcimine 为完整词基；其中的 calc- 可帮助联想到石灰，但不宜把全词强行分析为现代能产词缀的组合。名词可直接转为动词；动词形式为 calcimines、calcimined、calcimining；calcimine 去末尾 e 加 -er → calciminer“胶粉涂料粉刷工”。kalsomine 是异体拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats calcimine as a complete base; calc- suggests lime, but the whole word is not a transparent combination of productive modern affixes. The noun also functions as a verb, with forms calcimines, calcimined, and calcimining; dropping final e and adding -er gives calciminer, a person who applies it. Kalsomine is a spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: distemper 指用水和胶等黏结剂调制的一类传统涂料，与 calcimine 在材料和用途上接近；whitewash 通常指石灰水涂料，成分不同；paint 是涂料或涂刷动作的统称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Distemper denotes a related class of traditional water-based coatings using a binder such as glue; whitewash usually uses lime and differs in composition; paint is the broader term for either a coating or the act of applying one.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Let calc- suggest lime: white mineral powder becomes a coating, then an action—coating the wall.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源自希腊语 kallipygos，由 kalli-、即 kallos“美”的组合形式，与 pygē“臀部”构成。这个称号因阿佛洛狄忒，即罗马传统中的维纳斯的雕像而广为人知，后来也用于描写人的体态。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately derives from Greek kallipygos, combining kalli-, associated with kallos, 'beauty,' and pygē, 'buttocks.' The epithet became familiar through statues of Aphrodite, or Venus in Roman tradition, and was extended to descriptions of human figures.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作学术性分析：calli-（美）+ pyg-（臀部）+ -ean（形容词词尾）。同源形容词有 callipygian 和 callipygous，意思基本相同；这组词均属少见用语，没有常用的进一步派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: A learned morphological analysis is calli- ('beautiful') + pyg- ('buttocks') + the adjectival ending -ean. Related adjectives are callipygian and callipygous, with essentially the same meaning; all are uncommon, with no established family of further common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: callipygian 与 callipygous 是基本同义的少见词；shapely 更常用，表示身体或某个部位线条优美，并不专指臀部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Callipygian and callipygous are uncommon equivalents with essentially the same meaning; shapely is more usual and can describe an attractive body or body part without specifically referring to the buttocks.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: calli- 是“美”，pyg- 是“臀”：两个词根直接拼出“臀部优美”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Calli- means 'beautiful' and pyg- means 'buttocks': the roots state the meaning directly.

usage_note: 较少见的物理或描写用词，强调白热发亮的状态，不是任意颜色的光。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于 candescent 的词族，最终源于拉丁语 candescere，意为“开始发白或发亮”，由 candere（发白光、炽热发亮）发展而来。英语中的意义集中于物体受热后发出白光的状态。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the family of candescent and ultimately comes from Latin candescere, meaning 'to become white or begin to glow,' from candere, 'to shine white or glow.' Its English meaning centers on the white glow produced by intense heat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：candescent（白热的）中的 -ent 对应状态名词后缀 -ence，形成 candescence。词族包括 candescent、candescence、candescently；相关形式有 incandescent（白炽的）、incandescence（白炽）和 incandescently（白炽地；热烈地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphological relationship: the adjective ending -ent in candescent corresponds to the state-noun ending -ence in candescence. The family includes candescent, candescence, and candescently; related forms include incandescent, incandescence, and incandescently.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: incandescence（白炽）是更常用的近义词，强调高温引起的发光；glow（辉光）不一定呈白色，也不一定由高温产生；radiance（光辉）泛指明亮的光，不限定成因。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Incandescence is the more usual near-synonym and emphasizes light caused by high temperature; glow need not be white or heat-produced; radiance refers broadly to bright light without specifying its cause.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 cand- 联想到“发白光”，把 -escence 联想到“进入某种状态”：热到发白，就是白热。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cand- with shining white and -escence with entering a state: heat becomes intense enough to produce a white glow.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经解剖学拉丁语进入英语，源于希腊语 kanthos，意为“眼角”。英语保留了这一具体的解剖学含义。

morphology_enriched.zh: canthus 在现代普通英语中作为完整借词处理；医学构词使用 canth- 或 cantho-。复数为 canthi；相关形式有 canthal（眦的）、canthotomy（眦切开术）、canthoplasty（眦成形术）、canthopexy（眦固定术）、epicanthus（内眦赘皮）和 epicanthal（内眦赘皮的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Canthus is a complete loanword in ordinary modern English; medical formations use canth- or cantho-. Its plural is canthi. Related forms include canthal, canthotomy, canthoplasty, canthopexy, epicanthus, and epicanthal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: corner of the eye（眼角）是日常表达，但有时也指视野边缘；angle of the eye（眼角）是描述性近义表达；palpebral commissure（眼睑连合）更具体地强调上下眼睑连接的部位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Corner of the eye is the everyday equivalent, though it can also refer to peripheral vision; angle of the eye is a descriptive alternative; palpebral commissure more specifically emphasizes the junction of the eyelids.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 Cape 和 skin 组成，Cape 指非洲南端好望角及相关地区。名称最初与该地区出产的羊皮有关，后来也用于指这种柔软的制手套皮革。
etymology_story.en: The word combines Cape, referring to the Cape of Good Hope and its surrounding region, with skin. Originally associated with sheepskins from that region, the name also came to designate this soft glove leather.

morphology_enriched.zh: 透明复合词：Cape（开普地区）＋ skin（皮）→ capeskin。通常作物质名词；表示不同皮张或品类时可用 capeskins。没有常用的独立派生词；capeskin gloves 中的 capeskin 是作定语的名词。
morphology_enriched.en: A transparent compound: Cape + skin → capeskin. It is usually a material noun; capeskins can refer to individual skins or varieties. There are no common separate derivatives; in capeskin gloves, capeskin is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sheepskin leather（羊皮革）是更宽泛的上位词；lambskin（羔羊皮革）特指幼羊皮制成的皮革；nappa leather（纳帕软革）强调柔软的皮革类型，可采用不同动物的皮，三者不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sheepskin leather is the broader category; lambskin specifically comes from young sheep; nappa leather describes a soft leather type that can come from different animals. These terms overlap but are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Cape 地名＋ skin 皮革：记住“开普来的柔软羊皮手套”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cape names the place and skin names the material: picture soft sheepskin gloves from the Cape.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经法语借入此词，源头是意大利语 capriola（腾跃、翻跃），与 capriolo（狍）有关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 capreolus。动物轻快跳跃的形象后来成为这一马术动作的名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through French from Italian capriola, meaning a leap or tumble, related to capriolo, 'roe deer,' and ultimately Latin capreolus. The image of an animal's springing leap became the name of this equestrian movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，capriole 作为完整借词处理，并可通过零派生兼作名词和动词。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 caprioles；过去式和过去分词为 caprioled；现在分词为 caprioling，添加 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, capriole is treated as a complete loanword and functions as both noun and verb through conversion. Caprioles is the noun plural and third-person singular verb; caprioled is the past tense and past participle; caprioling drops the silent final e before -ing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leap（腾跃）强调跃入空中的动作；jump（跳跃）最宽泛；caper（雀跃、蹦跳）常带活泼嬉戏意味。作为马术术语，capriole 特指包含双后腿后踢的腾跃。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leap emphasizes springing into the air; jump is the broadest term; caper often suggests lively, playful movement. As an equestrian term, capriole specifically includes the backward kick of both hind legs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从小鹿跃起的画面，记住马“跃起＋后踢”的 capriole。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自葡萄牙语 carambola；这一果名通常被追溯到马拉地语 karambal，并进一步联系到梵语 karmaranga。该名称随热带水果及其种植传播，既指果实，也指果树。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed carambola from Portuguese; the fruit name is usually traced to Marathi karambal and further connected with Sanskrit karmaranga. As the fruit and its cultivation spread, the name came to denote both the fruit and its tree.

morphology_enriched.zh: carambola 是整体借词，现代英语中不宜强行拆分为词根和词缀；规则复数为 carambolas。没有常用的独立派生词；carambola tree、carambola juice 和 carambola-shaped 分别是名词短语或临时复合形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Carambola is a complete loanword with no useful modern English root-and-affix division; its regular plural is carambolas. It has no common separate derivatives; carambola tree, carambola juice, and carambola-shaped are phrases or freely formed compounds.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: star fruit（星形果，即杨桃）是日常英语中更直观的同义名称，也可连写为 starfruit；star-fruit tree（杨桃树）明确指植物本身。carambola 可同时指果实和果树。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Star fruit is the more transparent everyday name for the fruit and is also written starfruit; star-fruit tree explicitly names the plant. Carambola can denote either the fruit or the tree.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 不要硬拆外来词：把 carambola 与“横切一刀，出现五角星”的杨桃画面绑定。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Treat the borrowed name as a whole: connect carambola with a fruit that reveals a five-pointed star when sliced.

morphology.text: carb-（碳） + -uret（旧化合物名后缀） → carburet（旧名词“碳化物”），再用作动词“使与碳化合”。

etymology.text: 科学词汇由表示碳的 carb- 与旧化合物名后缀 -uret 组合而成，carb- 的源头是拉丁语 carbo（炭）。由碳化物的名称联想使物质与碳结合的动作。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由表示“碳”的 carb- 和旧化学命名后缀 -uret 构成；carb- 最终源自拉丁语 carbo，意为“炭”。它早期也作名词表示碳的化合物，后来动词用法表示使物质与碳结合，并扩展到使气体混入烃类蒸气。
etymology_story.en: The word combines carb-, referring to carbon and ultimately derived from Latin carbo, meaning charcoal, with the older chemical suffix -uret. It was also formerly a noun for a carbon compound; its verbal uses concern combining substances with carbon and enriching gases with hydrocarbon vapour.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 carburet 作为整体动词记忆；carb- + -uret 属于历史构词分析，-uret 已不是能自由使用的常用后缀。屈折形式有 carburets、carbureted/carbur­etted、carbureting/carburetting；相关词族包括 carburetion/carburation（汽化混合过程）和 carburetor/carburettor（化油器）。同根相关词还有 carbon（碳）、carburize/carburise（使渗碳）和 carburization/carburisation（渗碳）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, carburet is best treated as a whole verb; carb- + -uret is a historical analysis, and -uret is no longer a freely productive everyday suffix. Inflections include carburets, carbureted/carburetted, and carbureting/carburetting; the associated family includes carburetion/carburation and carburetor/carburettor. Related carbon-root words include carbon, carburize/carburise, and carburization/carburisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: carburize 指使材料增碳，尤其指钢铁表面渗碳；carbonize 指使物质炭化，通常涉及加热分解，并不等于增碳；enrich 是更宽泛的“富集、增热”，用于气体时可对应 carburet 的燃料混合义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Carburize means to introduce carbon into a material, especially the surface of iron or steel. Carbonize means to turn material into carbon or a carbon-rich residue, often through heating, rather than simply adding carbon. Enrich is broader and can describe increasing a gas's fuel value, matching the fuel-mixing sense of carburet.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 carb- 的“碳”：给材料加碳，或给气体加入含碳燃料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor carb- to carbon: add carbon to a material, or carbon-containing fuel to a gas.

morphology.text: cart(a)（意大利语“纸”） + -occio（名词后缀） → cartoccio（纸筒），经法语成为 cartouch；英语中作为独立词素整体记忆。

etymology_story.zh: cartouch 是 cartouche 的较少见拼写，经法语 cartouche 源自意大利语 cartoccio，意为“纸筒、纸卷”，最终与表示“纸”的 carta 有关。纸卷的形状引出了卷轴状框饰的含义，后来该名称也用于古埃及王名周围的椭圆框。
etymology_story.en: Cartouch is a less usual spelling of cartouche, borrowed through French from Italian cartoccio, meaning a paper roll or cone, ultimately related to carta, paper. The rolled-paper shape gave rise to the ornamental-frame sense, and the name was later applied to the oval enclosure around an ancient Egyptian royal name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cartouch 是不可再作常用词素切分的借词，不应拆成英语 cart + touch。复数为 cartouches；更常见的基本拼写为 cartouche，相关形式有 cartouched（饰有框饰的）以及描述性复合词 cartouche-shaped（王名圈形的、框饰形的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cartouch is an unanalysed loanword, not a combination of the English words cart and touch. Its plural is cartouches; the more usual base spelling is cartouche, with related forms such as cartouched, meaning decorated with a cartouche, and the descriptive compound cartouche-shaped.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cartouche 是同词的常见拼写，意义相同；name ring 在埃及学语境中可通俗地指王名圈，但不是所有装饰性框饰；ornamental panel 泛指装饰面板，不要求呈椭圆形或卷轴形。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cartouche is the usual spelling of the same word and has the same meanings. Name ring can describe the Egyptian enclosure in plain language, but does not cover every decorative use. Ornamental panel is broader and does not require an oval or scroll-like form.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“纸卷”想到“卷边框”：框住题字，也框住法老的名字。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a paper scroll becoming a decorative border: it frames an inscription or a pharaoh's name.

etymology_story.zh: casaba 来自土耳其城镇 Kasaba 的旧地名，该地今称 Turgutlu。这种甜瓜曾从那里运出，因此产地名称进入英语后成为瓜名。
etymology_story.en: Casaba comes from Kasaba, the former name of the Turkish town now called Turgutlu. Melons were shipped from there, and the place name became the English name of the fruit.

morphology_enriched.zh: casaba 是由地名转成的整体名词，没有可用于现代英语构词分析的常用前后缀。复数为 casabas；casaba + melon 构成同义名称 casaba melon；没有常用的单词式派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Casaba is a whole noun derived from a place name, with no productive modern English prefix or suffix to separate. Its plural is casabas; casaba + melon forms the equivalent name casaba melon. It has no common single-word derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: casaba melon 是完全对应的名称；muskmelon 是更宽泛的甜瓜类别名称；honeydew 指另一类甜瓜，通常外皮较光滑，与 casaba 相关但不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Casaba melon is an exact equivalent. Muskmelon is a broader category name. Honeydew is a related but distinct type of melon, usually with smoother skin, so it is not interchangeable with casaba.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“产地变瓜名”：Kasaba 运出的黄皱皮甜瓜，就是 casaba。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a place becoming a fruit name: the wrinkled yellow melon shipped from Kasaba became casaba.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借入 Catawba 作为卡罗来纳地区一个原住民族及其语言的名称，其更早的词源解释并不完全确定。葡萄品种名则来自 Catawba River（卡托巴河），随后又用于指这种葡萄酿成的酒。
etymology_story.en: English adopted Catawba as the name of an Indigenous people of the Carolinas and their language; accounts of the name's earlier origin are not fully certain. The grape variety was named after the Catawba River, and its name was then extended to the wine made from the grapes.

morphology_enriched.zh: Catawba 在现代英语中是整体名称，没有可自由拆分的英语词根或词缀。表示族人成员时复数可用 Catawbas 或 Catawba；语言名及葡萄酒名通常不可数；表示单颗葡萄时复数为 Catawbas。名词与形容词形式相同，相关复合表达有 Catawba-speaking（说卡托巴语的）、Catawba-language（卡托巴语的）和 Catawba grape（卡托巴葡萄）。
morphology_enriched.en: Catawba is a whole name in modern English, without separable productive English roots or affixes. For individual people, the plural can be Catawbas or Catawba; the language and wine names are normally uncountable, while individual grapes can be called Catawbas. The noun and adjective have the same form; related compounds include Catawba-speaking, Catawba-language, and Catawba grape.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Catawba people 明确指族群，Catawba Nation 强调民族或其政治共同体，二者不能在所有语境中互换；Catawba language 只对应语言义。这些是消除歧义的相关名称，不能替代葡萄或葡萄酒义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Catawba people explicitly names the ethnic group, while Catawba Nation emphasizes the nation or its political community, so the expressions are not interchangeable in every context. Catawba language identifies only the language sense. These are clarifying names rather than substitutes for the grape or wine senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分成两条线记：族名连接“人—语言—文化”；河名连接“葡萄—葡萄酒”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember two chains: the people's name links people, language, and culture; the river's name links the grape and its wine.

etymology_story.zh: catboat 是英语 cat 与 boat 组成的航海复合词，在19世纪已有使用。这里的 cat 属于表示单桅单帆帆装的航海用语，而不是说船与猫有关；该航海义更早的来源并不明确。
etymology_story.en: Catboat is an English nautical compound of cat and boat, in use by the nineteenth century. Here cat refers to a single-mast, single-sail arrangement rather than the animal; the earlier origin of this nautical use is uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: cat（航海用语中的帆装名称）+ boat（船）→ catboat；复数为 catboats。相关表达包括 cat rig（单桅单帆帆装）、cat-rigged（采用这种帆装的）和 cat-rigged boat（采用这种帆装的船）；没有常用的单词式派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Cat, in its nautical rigging sense, + boat forms catboat; the plural is catboats. Related expressions include cat rig, cat-rigged, and cat-rigged boat. There are no common single-word derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cat-rigged boat 是说明帆装特征的近义表达；sailboat 是包含 catboat 的上位词；dinghy 通常指小艇，可采用不同帆装，也可没有帆，因此不等同于 catboat。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cat-rigged boat is a close descriptive equivalent emphasizing the rig. Sailboat is the broader category containing catboats. Dinghy usually means a small boat that may have various rigs or no sail, so it is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 cat 当作帆装标签：一根桅杆靠船首，一面大帆带船走。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Treat cat as a rig label: one mast near the bow, one large sail driving the boat.

senses.meaning_zh: 牙骨质；覆盖牙根表面、供牙周韧带纤维附着的矿化组织
senses.meaning_en: The mineralized tissue covering a tooth root and providing attachment for periodontal ligament fibers.
senses.english_definition: Cementum is the hard tissue that covers the roots of your teeth and helps attach them to the surrounding supporting structures.
senses.collocation_en: root cementum; cellular cementum
senses.collocation_zh: 牙根牙骨质；细胞性牙骨质
senses.sentence_en: Periodontal ligament fibers attach to the cementum covering the tooth root.
senses.sentence_zh: 牙周韧带纤维附着在覆盖牙根的牙骨质上。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是由拉丁语 caementum 发展而来的医学拉丁语名称；caementum 原指用于建筑的碎石，后来也与胶结材料联系起来。牙科学借用这一名称，指覆盖牙根并为牙周附着提供支撑的硬组织。
etymology_story.en: This medical Latin term ultimately derives from Latin caementum, originally referring to broken stone used in building and later associated with cementing materials. Dentistry adopted the name for the hard tissue covering tooth roots and supporting periodontal attachment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 cementum 作为完整的专业名词记忆；形式上可辨认 cement- 与拉丁语中性名词词尾 -um，但这不是现代英语中自由使用的构词规则。相关词族包括 cemental（牙骨质的）、cementoblast（成牙骨质细胞）、cementocyte（牙骨质细胞）和 cementogenesis（牙骨质形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cementum is normally learned as a complete technical noun. Its form contains cement- and the Latin neuter noun ending -um, but this is not a freely productive English formation. Related terms include cemental, cementoblast, cementocyte, and cementogenesis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dental cementum（牙骨质）和 tooth cementum（牙齿的牙骨质）是明确所指的同义表达。dentine（牙本质）是相邻而不同的组织，不是同义词；dental cement（牙科水门汀或黏固剂）则通常指牙科材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dental cementum and tooth cementum are explicit equivalent expressions. Dentine is a neighboring but different tissue, whereas dental cement usually refers to a dental material rather than this natural tissue.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 cement 的“固定”作用：cementum 是牙根表面供支持纤维附着的硬组织。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of cement as something that secures: cementum gives supporting fibers an attachment surface on the tooth root.

senses.meaning_zh: 分；某些货币基本单位的百分之一，也指相应面额的硬币
senses.meaning_en: A monetary unit equal to one hundredth of certain currencies, or a coin representing that unit.
senses.english_definition: A centimo is a unit of money worth one hundredth of the main monetary unit in some countries, or a coin with that value.
senses.collocation_en: one centimo; a fifty-centimo coin
senses.collocation_zh: 一分；一枚五十分硬币

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自西班牙语 céntimo，意思是货币基本单位的“百分之一”。它与法语 centime 同源相关，最终可追溯至拉丁语中表示“一百”和“第一百”的词。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Spanish céntimo, meaning one hundredth of a main monetary unit. It is related to French centime and ultimately to Latin words meaning 'hundred' and 'hundredth.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 centimo 是借入的完整词，复数为 centimos；不宜把 -imo 当作可自由构词的英语后缀。cent- 可帮助联系“百”的概念；相关词包括 cent（分）、centime（分，见于另一些货币）和 centesimal（百分的），但这些不是由 centimo 直接派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: Centimo is a whole-word borrowing in English, with the plural centimos; -imo should not be treated as a productive English suffix. The element cent- provides a connection with 'hundred.' Related vocabulary includes cent, centime, and centesimal, though these are not direct derivatives of centimo.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cent、centime 和 centavo 都可指某种货币的百分之一，但分别属于不同货币的正式单位名称。它们概念相近，涉及具体金额时不能随意替换 centimo。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cent, centime, and centavo can also name one-hundredth monetary units, but they belong to different currency naming systems. They are conceptually similar and should not replace centimo indiscriminately in references to actual amounts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cent- 联想“一百”：一百个 centimos 构成一个相应的基本货币单位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cent- with 'hundred': one hundred centimos make one corresponding main currency unit.

senses.meaning_zh: 鲸类的；与鲸、海豚或鼠海豚有关的
senses.meaning_en: Of or relating to cetaceans, including whales, dolphins, and porpoises.
senses.english_definition: Something that is cetaceous belongs to or is connected with the group of mammals that includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises.
senses.collocation_en: cetaceous mammals; cetaceous species
senses.collocation_zh: 鲸类哺乳动物；鲸类物种
senses.sentence_en: The museum displays the skeletons of several cetaceous species.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家博物馆展出了几种鲸类动物的骨骼。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于拉丁语 cetus，意为“鲸”或“大型海兽”，而 cetus 又借自希腊语 kētos。英语用这一词干形成形容词，表示属于鲸类或与鲸类有关。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin cetus, meaning a whale or large sea creature, borrowed from Greek kētos. English formed an adjective from this stem to describe animals and features associated with cetaceans.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 cet-（鲸、海兽）+ -aceous（具有某类性质的、属于某类的）。相关词族包括 Cetacea（鲸类的分类名称）、cetacean（鲸类动物；鲸类的）、cetology（鲸类学）和 cetologist（鲸类学家）；现代英语通常更常用 cetacean。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as cet- ('whale' or 'sea creature') + -aceous ('belonging to or having the nature of'). Related terms include Cetacea, cetacean, cetology, and cetologist. Cetacean is generally the more usual term in modern English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cetacean 作形容词时是最直接的对应词，现代用法更常见；whale-related 表示“与鲸有关”，但可能不明确包括海豚和鼠海豚；marine mammalian 表示“海洋哺乳动物的”，范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cetacean, used adjectivally, is the closest equivalent and is more usual today. Whale-related may not clearly include dolphins and porpoises, while marine mammalian has a broader scope.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cet- 联想“鲸类”，-aceous 表示“属于这一类”：cetaceous 就是“鲸类的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link cet- with cetaceans and -aceous with belonging to a group: cetaceous means 'of the whale group.'

etymology_story.zh: 英语从西班牙语 chinche 借入此词；西班牙语词源可追溯至拉丁语 cimex（属格 cimicis），意为“臭虫”。英语保留了臭虫义，也把它用于另一类危害禾本科植物的小型半翅目昆虫，尤其见于 chinch bug。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from Spanish chinche, ultimately from Latin cimex, genitive cimicis, meaning 'bedbug.' English retained that meaning and also applied the name to small plant-feeding bugs, especially in the expression chinch bug.

morphology_enriched.zh: chinch 是完整的借入词，现代英语中没有需要拆分的词缀；复数为 chinches。常见相关形式是复合名词 chinch bug；chinch-infested（受长蝽或臭虫侵扰的）属于临时组合表达，不是独立的常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Chinch is an unsegmented borrowing with no productive internal affixes in modern English; its plural is chinches. The established related compound is chinch bug. Chinch-infested is a possible descriptive combination rather than a separate common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chinch bug 对应危害植物的长蝽义；bedbug 对应吸血的床虱义，两者不是同一种昆虫。bug 是更宽泛的称呼，不能表达具体种类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chinch bug corresponds to the plant-feeding sense, while bedbug corresponds to the blood-feeding sense; these are different insects. Bug is a much broader term and does not identify the particular kind.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记原义“臭虫”，再记 chinch bug 常指吸食草和谷物汁液的害虫；看语境区分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the original 'bedbug' meaning, then remember that chinch bug usually names a pest of grasses and grain; let context distinguish them.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自弗吉尼亚地区阿尔冈昆语中的植物名称，早期英语使用者借用它来称呼当地的矮栗及其坚果。后来，这个名称也用于其他结有类似坚果的近缘植物。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from a Virginia Algonquian plant name that early English speakers adopted for a local dwarf chestnut and its nuts. The name was later also applied to related plants producing similar nuts.

morphology_enriched.zh: chinquapin 是整体借入的植物名，不应按 chin、qua、pin 等英语拼写片段强行拆解；复数为 chinquapins。chinkapin 是常见异体拼写；相关复合名称包括 Allegheny chinquapin（阿勒格尼矮栗）和 golden chinquapin（金叶栲），这些名称不指同一种植物。
morphology_enriched.en: Chinquapin is a whole-word borrowed plant name and should not be divided into apparent English fragments such as chin, qua, and pin. Its plural is chinquapins, and chinkapin is a common spelling variant. Related compound names include Allegheny chinquapin and golden chinquapin, which name different plants.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chinkapin 是同一个词的异体拼写；dwarf chestnut 通常对应其中的矮栗类植物，范围较窄；chestnut 是相关但更宽泛的名称，不能在所有植物名称中替换 chinquapin。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chinkapin is a spelling variant of the same word. Dwarf chestnut usually refers more narrowly to the dwarf chestnut plants included under the name. Chestnut is related but broader and cannot replace chinquapin in every botanical name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词绑定“小栗树和小栗果”：chinquapin 既可指树，也可指它结的坚果。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to 'a little chestnut tree and its nut': chinquapin can name both the plant and its edible fruit.

etymology_story.zh: chiro 是 chiropractor 的非正式截短形式。完整词所属的 chiropractic 词族最终使用了希腊语中表示“手”和“实践、操作”的成分，体现徒手操作的特点。
etymology_story.en: Chiro is an informal clipping of chiropractor. The chiropractic word family ultimately uses Greek elements meaning 'hand' and 'practice or action,' reflecting its emphasis on manual treatment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chiropractor → chiro，属于截短构词；独立名词 chiro 不宜直接拆作“手＋词尾”。复数为 chiros；相关词族包括 chiropractor（整脊师）、chiropractic（整脊疗法；整脊的）和 chiropractically（以整脊方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: chiropractor → chiro by clipping; the independent noun should not be analyzed simply as 'hand + ending.' Its plural is chiros. Related family members include chiropractor, chiropractic, and chiropractically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chiropractor 是正式、完整的对应词；osteopath 指整骨医师，其资质和执业范围因国家而异；physiotherapist 指物理治疗师，通常使用运动、康复训练等方法，不能与 chiro 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chiropractor is the full, neutral equivalent. Osteopath refers to a practitioner whose qualifications and scope vary by country. Physiotherapist refers to a professional who commonly uses exercise and rehabilitation methods and is not interchangeable with chiro.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 chiropractor 缩成 chiro：名字变短，仍是那位用手操作的整脊师。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Shorten chiropractor to chiro: a shorter name for the same hands-on practitioner.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语传统追溯至希腊语 kheir（手）和与 graphein（书写）相关的成分，字面意思是“手写”。英语中用它表示手写、书写技艺或个人笔迹，如今主要见于正式或历史语境。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through the Latin tradition from Greek elements based on kheir, 'hand,' and graphein, 'to write,' literally expressing writing by hand. In English it denotes handwriting, penmanship, or an individual's written style and now occurs mainly in formal or historical contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：chiro-（手）＋-graphy（书写、记录）→ chirography。相关词族包括 chirographic、chirographical（手写的；笔迹的），以及罕用的 chirographer、chirographist（书写者；书法家）；chirograph 是相关历史词，可指手写文书，尤其某类法律文书。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphological analysis: chiro- ('hand') + -graphy ('writing or recording') → chirography. Related forms include chirographic and chirographical, plus the rare agent nouns chirographer and chirographist. Chirograph is a related historical noun for a handwritten document, especially a particular kind of legal instrument.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handwriting 是最普通的“手写字迹”；penmanship 更强调书写技能和字迹质量；calligraphy 强调具有审美设计的书法，不等于一般手写。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handwriting is the everyday term for writing produced by hand. Penmanship emphasizes writing skill and the quality of letter formation. Calligraphy specifically emphasizes aesthetically designed lettering rather than handwriting in general.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chiro- 是“手”，-graphy 是“写”：手留下的字，就是手写笔迹。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chiro- means 'hand' and -graphy means 'writing': the marks your hand writes are your chirography.

senses.english_definition: Chitlings are the intestines of an animal, usually a pig, that are cleaned and cooked as food.

etymology_story.zh: chitlings 是 chitterlings 的变体，后者可追溯到中古英语 chiterling，早期表示动物的肠子。其更早来源并不确定；现代用法主要保留了作为食物名称的含义。
etymology_story.en: Chitlings is a variant of chitterlings, which goes back to Middle English chiterling, referring to an animal's intestines. Its earlier origin is uncertain, and modern usage chiefly preserves the food meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：chitling＋复数词尾 -s，但日常使用通常采用复数整体形式 chitlings。相关形式包括 chitterlings（较完整的拼写）和 chitlins（反映口语发音的拼写）；这些是同一食物名称的变体，并非不同的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: chitling + plural -s, although ordinary usage favors the plural food name chitlings. Related forms include the fuller spelling chitterlings and the pronunciation-based spelling chitlins; these are variants of the same food name rather than separate derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chitterlings 与 chitlings 基本同义；chitlins 是更口语化的拼写；offal 泛指供食用的内脏，范围比猪肠更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chitterlings is essentially equivalent to chitlings. Chitlins is a more informal spelling. Offal is broader, covering edible internal organs rather than intestines alone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 chitlings、chitterlings、chitlins 连成一组：拼写有长短，都指餐桌上的肠类食物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link chitlings, chitterlings, and chitlins: different-length spellings for the same intestine-based food.

senses.meaning_zh: 金霉素；氯四环素，一种四环素类抗生素
senses.meaning_en: a chlorine-containing antibiotic of the tetracycline class
senses.english_definition: Chlortetracycline is an antibiotic in the tetracycline family that is used against certain bacterial infections.
senses.collocation_en: chlortetracycline hydrochloride; chlortetracycline resistance
senses.collocation_zh: 盐酸金霉素；对金霉素的耐药性

senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员检测了这些细菌分离株对金霉素的耐药性。

etymology_story.zh: 这一20世纪药物名称以表示“氯”的 chlor- 和 tetracycline（四环素）构成，反映其分子中的氯取代基及四环骨架。它也以商品名 Aureomycin 为人所知，中文通常称为“金霉素”。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century drug name combines chlor-, referring to chlorine, with tetracycline, reflecting its chlorine substituent and four-ring molecular framework. It is also known by the trade name Aureomycin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chlor-（氯）＋tetracycline（四环素）→ chlortetracycline；tetracycline 又可分析为 tetra-（四）＋cycl-（环）＋-ine（化学名称常见词尾）。相关词包括 tetracycline、oxytetracycline（土霉素）和 doxycycline（多西环素），后三者属于相关药物名称，不能当作 chlortetracycline 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: chlor- ('chlorine') + tetracycline → chlortetracycline. Tetracycline can further be analyzed as tetra- ('four') + cycl- ('ring') + -ine, a common chemical-name ending. Related vocabulary includes tetracycline, oxytetracycline, and doxycycline; these are related drug names, not direct derivatives of chlortetracycline.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Aureomycin（金霉素的商品名）指这种抗生素的命名或制剂；tetracycline 既可指四环素这一具体药物，也可用于相关药物类别的名称；oxytetracycline（土霉素）是同类中的另一种抗生素，并非同一种物质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aureomycin is a trade name associated with this antibiotic and its preparations. Tetracycline names a specific related antibiotic and also appears in the name of the broader drug class. Oxytetracycline is another antibiotic in that class, not the same substance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chlor 看“氯”，tetra 看“四”，cycl 看“环”：含氯的四环素，就是氯四环素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read chlor as 'chlorine,' tetra as 'four,' and cycl as 'ring': a chlorine-containing member of the four-ring antibiotic family.

etymology_story.zh: 腌菜义通常与早期中国沿海洋泾浜英语中表示混合物、杂货或食物的 chow-chow 联系起来，但其确切汉语来源并不确定。犬种名称也常被联系到这一贸易用语；印度英语中的佛手瓜义属于另一个地区用法，不宜仅凭拼写相同断定其来源。
etymology_story.en: The relish sense is usually linked to chow-chow in early Chinese Pidgin English, associated with mixtures, miscellaneous goods, or food, although its exact Chinese source is uncertain. The dog name is also often linked to that trading vocabulary; the regional Indian vegetable sense should not be assigned the same origin merely because its spelling matches.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式：chow＋chow，呈现重复结构，但各义应按整体词记忆，不能由现代 chow（食物）机械推导。常见拼写为 chowchow、chow-chow 和 chow chow；犬种义尤其常写作 chow chow，也可简称 chow，复数为 chowchows 或 chows；没有常用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern form: chow + chow, a repeated structure, but each sense should be learned as a whole rather than mechanically derived from modern chow meaning 'food.' Common spellings include chowchow, chow-chow, and chow chow. The dog sense is especially often written chow chow and shortened to chow, with plurals chowchows or chows. There is no common family of direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 腌菜义：relish 泛指佐餐酱菜，范围较广；piccalilli 是相关的什锦腌菜，通常突出芥末风味，配方因地区而异。佛手瓜义：chayote 是分布更广的对应名称；犬种义可用简称 chow，但不能与其他犬种名称互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the food sense, relish is a broader category, while piccalilli is a related mixed pickle typically distinguished by mustard seasoning, with regional recipe differences. For the vegetable sense, chayote is the more widely used equivalent. For the dog sense, chow is a shortened equivalent, not a label for other breeds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 重复的 chow 帮你联想“一样又一样蔬菜混合”：先记什锦腌酱，再把松狮犬和印度英语的佛手瓜作为独立义项挂上去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let the repeated chow suggest vegetable after vegetable mixed together; then attach the dog and regional chayote meanings as separate senses.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪初借入此词，其源头是希腊语 khrēstomatheia，结合了表示“有用的”的 khrēstos 和与“学习”有关的词干。它指有助于学习的选文集，后来也用于某一领域的代表性文章选集。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the early nineteenth century from Greek khrēstomatheia, combining khrēstos, meaning “useful,” with a stem connected with learning. It denotes selected readings useful for study and has also been extended to representative selections from a particular field.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可作学术构词分析：chresto-（有用）+ -mathy（学习）；这些是希腊语来源的构词成分，并非自由使用的现代英语单词。复数为 chrestomathies；相关形容词为 chrestomathic（文选的；与学习文选有关的），没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned morphological analysis: chresto- (“useful”) + -mathy (“learning”); these are Greek-derived combining elements rather than independent modern English words. The plural is chrestomathies, and the related adjective is chrestomathic; there are no commonly used derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reader（学习读本）最接近其教学用途；anthology（选集）强调作品的汇集，不一定用于语言教学；selection（选文集）含义更宽，不限定编选目的。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reader is closest when teaching is the purpose; anthology emphasizes a collection of works without necessarily implying language instruction; selection is broader and does not specify why the passages were chosen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “有用”+“学习”＝帮助学习的精选文章。
mnemonic_anchor.en: “Useful” + “learning” = selected passages that help you learn.

etymology_story.zh: Chrisom 与 chrism（圣油）同源，最终来自希腊语 khrisma（涂抹的油膏），与 khriein（涂油）有关。名称从洗礼时使用的圣油转指受洗婴儿披戴的白布；旧时也可指尚穿戴这种白布的婴儿。
etymology_story.en: Chrisom is historically related to chrism, ultimately from Greek khrisma, meaning an anointing substance, and khriein, “to anoint.” The name shifted from baptismal oil to the white cloth placed on a baptized infant and was also formerly applied to an infant still wearing that cloth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 chrisom 视为不可再作常用词缀拆分的整体名词；复数为 chrisoms。Chrisom cloth 是复合词组；chrism（圣油）、chrismal（圣油的）和 chrismation（傅油礼）是同源相关词，并非由 chrisom 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chrisom is treated as a whole noun without a productive prefix–suffix division; its plural is chrisoms. Chrisom cloth is a compound expression; chrism, chrismal, and chrismation are historically related words rather than direct derivatives of chrisom.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: baptismal cloth（洗礼用布）是最接近的描述性说法；christening robe（婴儿洗礼袍）强调完整衣袍，范围不完全相同；baptismal garment（洗礼服）更宽泛，也可指成人穿的洗礼服。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Baptismal cloth is the closest descriptive equivalent; christening robe specifically suggests a complete robe and is not always interchangeable; baptismal garment is broader and may also refer to clothing worn by adults.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从圣油 chrism 联想到洗礼，再联想到婴儿身上的白布。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link chrism, the sacred oil, to baptism and then to the baby's white cloth.

etymology_story.zh: Chuckhole 见于19世纪的美国英语，是以 hole（洞）为后半部分的合成词。前半部分 chuck 的确切来源并不确定，因此不宜把它解释为某个确定的“颠簸”词根。
etymology_story.en: Chuckhole is recorded in nineteenth-century American English as a compound ending in hole. The precise origin of chuck in this word is uncertain, so it should not be presented as an established root meaning “jolt.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分为 chuck + hole，其中 hole 是中心词；chuck 在此不具有明确且能自由类推的现代词义。复数为 chuckholes；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form divides into chuck + hole, with hole as the head; chuck does not have a clear, freely productive meaning in this compound. The plural is chuckholes, and there are no commonly used direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pothole（路面坑洞）是最通用、最接近的对应词；rut（车辙）指车轮反复碾压形成的长槽；depression（凹陷）范围更广，不一定是破损形成的坑洞。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pothole is the closest and most widely used equivalent; rut means an elongated groove made by repeated wheel traffic; depression is broader and need not involve a broken road surface.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 hole“洞”：车轮遇到路上的洞就会颠一下。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to hole: a hole in the road gives your wheels a jolt.

etymology_story.zh: Chuckwalla 经墨西哥西班牙语 chacahuala 进入英语，其更早来源通常追溯到卡维拉语等北美原住民语言中的蜥蜴名称。它是借入的动物名称，与英语 chuck（扔）或 wall（墙）没有构词关系。
etymology_story.en: Chuckwalla entered English through Mexican Spanish chacahuala, with its earlier source generally traced to an Indigenous lizard name associated with Cahuilla and neighboring languages. It is a borrowed animal name, unrelated in formation to English chuck or wall.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 chuckwalla 是不可按英语词根词缀拆分的借词；复数为 chuckwallas。它指 Sauromalus 属的蜥蜴，没有常用的直接派生词；chuckwalla-like 只是可临时构成的“像查克瓦拉鬣蜥的”，不是固定词族成员。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chuckwalla is a borrowed word without an English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is chuckwallas. It names lizards of the genus Sauromalus and has no commonly used direct derivatives; chuckwalla-like is a possible occasional formation rather than an established word-family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有同样精确的常用单词近义词。lizard（蜥蜴）是更宽泛的上位词；iguana（鬣蜥）可表示其所属的较大类群，但不专指查克瓦拉鬣蜥；desert iguana（沙漠鬣蜥）通常指另一种蜥蜴，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no equally precise everyday single-word synonym. Lizard is a broader category; iguana can describe its wider group but does not specifically identify a chuckwalla; desert iguana normally names a different lizard and is not interchangeable.

etymology_story.zh: Chugalug 是20世纪美国口语中的拟声词，也常写作 chug-a-lug。它以 chug 所模拟的咕嘟声为基础，通过押韵延长形式表现连续吞咽，并非由表示“拖拽”的 lug 按字面组合而成。
etymology_story.en: Chugalug is a twentieth-century American colloquial sound-imitating formation, also commonly written chug-a-lug. It expands the gulping sound suggested by chug through a rhyming ending, rather than literally combining it with lug meaning “drag.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分析为 chug + 拟声押韵延伸 -a-lug，不能把 a 当作冠词、把 lug 当作独立实义词来解释。词形为 chugalugs、chugalugged、chugalugging；连字符变体为 chug-a-lug、chug-a-lugs、chug-a-lugged、chug-a-lugging；相关基础动词为 chug（大口喝）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation is chug + the sound-symbolic rhyming extension -a-lug; a is not functioning as an article, and lug has no separate literal meaning here. Inflected forms are chugalugs, chugalugged, and chugalugging; hyphenated variants are chug-a-lug, chug-a-lugs, chug-a-lugged, and chug-a-lugging. The related base verb is chug, meaning to drink in gulps.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chug（咕嘟咕嘟地喝）最接近，形式更短、更常用；guzzle（狂饮）强调喝得多且急；gulp（大口吞饮）可只指一次吞咽，不一定连续喝完。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chug is the closest equivalent and is shorter and more usual; guzzle emphasizes drinking eagerly or in large quantities; gulp can describe a single large swallow without implying that the whole drink is finished.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 听见 chug-a-lug，就想象“咕嘟—咕嘟”连续喝下去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear chug-a-lug as the repeated gulping sound of a drink going down.

etymology_story.zh: 宗教用词 chumash 借自希伯来语 ḥumash，与表示“五”的词根有关，原指《托拉》五卷中的一卷，后来也指整部《摩西五经》的印刷读本。首字母大写的族名 Chumash 来自加利福尼亚原住民名称，与这个希伯来语词没有词源关系。
etymology_story.en: The religious word chumash comes from Hebrew ḥumash, related to the root meaning 'five'; it originally referred to one of the Torah's five books and also came to denote a printed edition of the whole Pentateuch. The capitalized ethnonym Chumash comes from an Indigenous Californian name and is etymologically unrelated to the Hebrew word.

morphology_enriched.zh: 宗教义 chumash 是整体借词，在现代英语中不拆分为能产的词根和词缀；复数为 chumashim，也可见 chumashes。chumash-based 可作临时复合修饰语，表示“以《摩西五经》读本为基础的”，但不是固定派生词。族名 Chumash 通常单复数同形，也用作形容词；相关词 Chumashan 表示“丘马什语系的”，也可指丘马什语系。
morphology_enriched.en: The religious noun chumash is an unanalyzed borrowing in modern English; its plurals include chumashim and chumashes. Chumash-based is a possible temporary compound modifier meaning 'based on a chumash,' rather than an established derivative. The ethnonym Chumash normally has the same singular and plural form and also functions adjectivally; the related form Chumashan refers to the Chumash language family or means 'relating to that family.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 宗教义相关词：Pentateuch（《摩西五经》）强调五卷经文本身；Torah（《托拉》）可指《摩西五经》，也可泛指更广的犹太教教导；chumash 特别强调供阅读、学习的印刷读本。族名和语言名称 Chumash 没有可直接替换的普通近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the religious sense, Pentateuch names the five biblical books as a text, while Torah can name those books or a broader body of Jewish teaching; chumash specifically emphasizes a printed volume used for reading or study. The ethnonym and language name Chumash have no ordinary interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 宗教义抓住“五”：五卷《托拉》合成手中的读本；大写且读作 /tʃ-/ 的 Chumash 则是独立的族名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the religious sense, anchor the word to 'five': the Torah's five books in a reading volume. Capitalized Chumash, beginning with /tʃ/, is a separate people's name.

etymology_story.zh: chyle 经晚期拉丁语 chylus 源自希腊语 khylos，意为“汁液”。它进入医学词汇后，专指肠道吸收脂肪时形成的乳白色淋巴液。
etymology_story.en: Chyle comes through Late Latin chylus from Greek khylos, meaning 'juice.' In medical usage, it became the name for the milky lymph produced during the intestinal absorption of fat.

morphology_enriched.zh: chyle 是整体借词；医学构词中使用词干 chyl- 和结合形式 chylo-。主要相关词有 chylous（乳糜的）、chylomicron（乳糜微粒）、chylothorax（乳糜胸）、chyluria（乳糜尿）和 chyliferous（输送乳糜的）；这些主要是医学派生词或复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Chyle is an unanalyzed borrowing, with chyl- and chylo- used in medical word formation. Its principal related forms include chylous ('containing or relating to chyle'), chylomicron (a particle that transports dietary fat), chylothorax (chyle in the pleural cavity), chyluria (chyle in the urine), and chyliferous ('carrying chyle'); these are chiefly medical derivatives or compounds.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lymph（淋巴液）是上位词，chyle 是富含肠道所吸收脂肪的一类淋巴液；intestinal lymph（肠淋巴液）侧重来源，在富含脂肪时与 chyle 所指接近。chyme（食糜）只是易混词，指消化道内部分消化的食物，不是乳糜。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lymph is the broader term: chyle is lymph rich in fat absorbed from the intestine. Intestinal lymph emphasizes its source and closely matches chyle when it is fat-rich. Chyme is a confusable word, not a synonym: it means partly digested food within the digestive tract.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源“汁液”加上脂肪造成的乳白色：肠道吸脂后的“乳白淋巴汁”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the original 'juice' with its milky appearance: chyle is lymph turned milky by absorbed dietary fat.

etymology_story.zh: cincture 借自拉丁语 cinctura，意为“束带、围束”，源于 cingere“围住、束起”。由腰间围束的带子，词义也扩展到环绕物，并产生了表示“围住、束住”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Cincture comes from Latin cinctura, meaning 'a girding or belt,' from cingere, 'to surround or gird.' Its meaning extended from a belt around the waist to something encircling an object, and it also developed a verb use meaning 'to encircle or gird.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 从历史形态看，可分析为拉丁语词干 cinct-（围束）加名词成分 -ure；现代英语通常把 cincture 作为整体词使用。名词和动词同形，屈折形式有 cinctures、cinctured、cincturing；相关拉丁语词族包括 cinch（肚带；束紧）和 succinct（简洁的，历史意象为“束紧”）。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the word contains the Latin stem cinct- ('gird') and the noun-forming element -ure; modern English generally treats cincture as a whole word. The noun and verb share a form, with inflections cinctures, cinctured, and cincturing. Related words from the same Latin family include cinch ('a girth; to tighten') and succinct ('concise,' historically associated with being girded up).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: belt（腰带）最通用，可指日常服饰或功能性带子；girdle（腰带、束带）较传统，也可表示环绕的一圈；sash（腰带、饰带）通常是较宽的布带。cincture 尤其用于宗教服饰，作动词时具有明显的文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Belt is the general word for an everyday or functional waist fastening; girdle is more traditional and can also mean an encircling band; sash usually means a broad fabric band. Cincture is especially associated with religious clothing, and its verb use is distinctly literary.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 cinct- 的“围束”：腰间围一圈是腰带，围住某物就是动词义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor cinct- to 'gird': a band girding the waist is the noun, and girding something is the verb.

etymology_story.zh: cislunar 由表示“在这一侧”的拉丁语前缀 cis- 与 lunar“月球的”构成，以地球为参照表示“在月球这一侧”。它原先侧重月球轨道以内的空间，现代航天语境也常用来概括地月之间及其附近的空间区域。
etymology_story.en: Cislunar combines the Latin prefix cis-, 'on this side of,' with lunar, 'relating to the Moon,' using Earth as the reference point. Originally emphasizing space within the Moon's orbit, it is also used in modern spaceflight for the broader Earth–Moon region.

morphology_enriched.zh: cis-（在这一侧）+ lunar（月球的）→ cislunar。lunar 与拉丁语 luna“月亮”有关；相关词包括 lunar（月球的）、sublunar（月下的；月球轨道以内的）和 translunar（月球轨道以外的）；cis-lunar 是带连字符的拼写变体。cislunar 本身没有常用的名词或动词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Cis- ('on this side of') + lunar ('relating to the Moon') forms cislunar. Lunar is related to Latin luna, 'moon'; related formations include lunar, sublunar ('beneath the Moon or within its orbit'), and translunar ('beyond the Moon's orbit'). Cis-lunar is a hyphenated spelling variant, and cislunar has no commonly used noun or verb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Earth–Moon（地月的）强调地球与月球组成的系统或二者的联系；sublunar（月下的）与其传统空间范围有重合，但常带古典宇宙观或文学色彩；near-Earth（近地的）侧重地球附近，范围不等同于整个地月空间。这些都是近义或相关表达，并非在所有语境中都可互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Earth–Moon emphasizes the system or relationship linking Earth and the Moon; sublunar overlaps with the traditional spatial meaning but often has classical or literary associations; near-Earth emphasizes proximity to Earth and does not necessarily cover the whole Earth–Moon region. These are related expressions rather than universally interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cis- 是“这一侧”，lunar 是“月球的”：站在地球看，月球这一侧就是核心空间意象。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cis- means 'this side' and lunar means 'Moon-related': picture the space on our side of the Moon, viewed from Earth.

etymology_story.zh: claymation 是 clay“黏土”与 animation“动画”的缩合词，名称直接描述其制作材料和表现形式。这个名称因动画师威尔·文顿及其工作室的使用而广为人知，并曾作为商标使用，后来也被广泛用来泛指黏土定格动画。
etymology_story.en: Claymation blends clay with animation, directly naming the material and the filmmaking technique. The name became widely known through animator Will Vinton and his studio, was used as a trademark, and also entered broader use as a term for clay-based stop-motion animation.

morphology_enriched.zh: clay（黏土）+ animation（动画，截取后半部分）→ claymation，属于缩合构词。通常用作不可数名词，也可在 claymation film 等短语中作名词定语；原料词及相关词族包括 clay、animate（使动起来；制作动画）、animation（动画）和 animator（动画制作人）。没有通行的 claymate 动词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Clay + a shortened portion of animation forms the blend claymation. It is normally an uncountable noun and can modify another noun in expressions such as claymation film. Its source words and related family include clay, animate ('bring to life or produce animation'), animation, and animator. There is no established derivative verb claymate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clay animation（黏土动画）是最直接的对应表达；stop-motion animation（定格动画）是上位概念，也可使用木偶、纸片或实物；model animation（模型动画）强调实体模型，模型不一定由黏土制成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clay animation is the closest equivalent; stop-motion animation is the broader technique and can use puppets, paper cutouts, or ordinary objects; model animation emphasizes physical models, which need not be made of clay.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 cling“黏附”和 stone“果核”合成，以果肉紧贴果核这一特征命名。它既可作形容词描述黏核特性，也可作名词指具有这种特性的果实。
etymology_story.en: The word combines cling, meaning 'adhere,' with stone, meaning the hard structure enclosing a fruit's seed. It describes flesh that adheres to the stone and also names a fruit with this characteristic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cling（黏附）+ stone（果核）→ clingstone（黏核的；黏核果）。名词复数为 clingstones；该复合词没有常用的进一步派生词。组成词 cling 的屈折形式包括 clings、clung、clinging，相关形容词有 clingy（黏人的；贴身的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cling ('adhere') + stone ('fruit stone') → clingstone. The noun plural is clingstones; the compound has no common further derivatives. The component cling has the forms clings, clung, and clinging, with the related adjective clingy.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Adhering-stone and stone-adhering are descriptive near-equivalents, but neither is as usual as clingstone. The contrasting term freestone describes fruit whose flesh separates readily from the stone.

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于20世纪形成的 cliometrics“计量史学”词族，将希腊神话中主管历史的缪斯 Clio 与表示测量的构词成分结合。其名称体现了把经济理论和定量分析引入历史研究的学术取向。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the twentieth-century cliometrics family, combining Clio, the Greek Muse of history, with an element referring to measurement. The name reflects the application of economic theory and quantitative analysis to historical research.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Clio（历史缪斯，代表历史）+ -metric（与计量有关的）→ cliometric。主要词族：cliometrics（计量史学）、cliometrician（计量史学研究者；复数 cliometricians）、cliometrically（以计量史学方法）。cliometrics 虽以 -s 结尾，表示学科时通常按单数处理。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Clio ('the Muse of history,' representing history) + -metric ('relating to measurement') → cliometric. The main family includes cliometrics, cliometrician (plural cliometricians), and cliometrically. Despite its final -s, cliometrics normally takes singular agreement when naming the discipline.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quantitative historical（定量历史研究的）范围更广，不一定采用经济理论；econometric（计量经济学的）强调经济数据的统计建模，不限于历史问题；economic-historical（经济史的）强调研究对象，不限定定量方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quantitative historical is broader and need not involve economic theory; econometric emphasizes statistical modeling of economic data without necessarily addressing history; economic-historical identifies the subject matter without specifying a quantitative method.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Clio 代表历史，metric 代表计量：让历史材料接受定量分析。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Clio supplies the history; metric supplies the measurement: analyze the past quantitatively.

etymology_story.zh: 该词以紧握的拳头比喻不肯拿出钱财，来自 close“紧闭的”、fist“拳头”和后缀 -ed。这里 close 表示“紧闭”，读音末尾为 /s/，而不是动词 close“关闭”中的 /z/。
etymology_story.en: The word uses the image of a tightly closed fist to suggest someone who will not release money, combining close, fist, and -ed. Here close means 'shut' and ends in /s/, unlike the verb close, which ends in /z/.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：close（紧闭的）+ fist（拳头）+ -ed（具有……特征的）→ closefisted。也常写作 close-fisted。主要派生词：closefistedly／close-fistedly（吝啬地）、closefistedness／close-fistedness（吝啬）。比较级和最高级通常用 more closefisted 和 most closefisted。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: close ('shut') + fist + -ed ('having the specified characteristic') → closefisted. The hyphenated spelling close-fisted is also common. Main derivatives are closefistedly or close-fistedly, and closefistedness or close-fistedness. Comparison normally uses more closefisted and most closefisted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stingy（吝啬的）是日常通用词，也可形容给出的数量太少；tightfisted（吝啬的）与 closefisted 几乎同义，同样突出不肯花钱；miserly（守财奴般的）贬义更强，常暗示极端爱财。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stingy is the everyday general term and can also describe an inadequate amount; tightfisted is almost interchangeable with closefisted and similarly emphasizes reluctance to spend; miserly is more strongly disapproving and suggests extreme attachment to money.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拳头攥得紧，钱就拿不出来：close + fist → 吝啬。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A tightly closed fist will not let money go: close + fist → unwilling to spend.

etymology_story.zh: 单数 coccyx 经拉丁语借自希腊语 kokkyx“布谷鸟”，因尾骨的形状被比作布谷鸟的喙而获得这一解剖学名称。复数 coccyges 沿用了经拉丁化的希腊语复数模式。
etymology_story.en: The singular coccyx came through Latin from Greek kokkyx, meaning 'cuckoo'; the anatomical name arose from a resemblance between the tailbone and a cuckoo's beak. Coccyges follows the Latinized Greek plural pattern.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：coccyx（尾骨，单数）→ coccyges（古典复数）；也可用规则复数 coccyxes。相关构词词干为 coccyg-，如 coccyg- + -eal → coccygeal（尾骨的）。主要相关词还有 coccygeus（尾骨肌）、coccydynia／coccygodynia（尾骨痛）、coccygectomy（尾骨切除术）、sacrococcygeal（骶尾部的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphology: coccyx (singular) → coccyges (classical plural); the regular plural coccyxes is also used. The related combining stem is coccyg-, as in coccyg- + -eal → coccygeal. Principal related terms include coccygeus, coccydynia or coccygodynia, coccygectomy, and sacrococcygeal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tailbones（尾骨）是通俗对应词；coccyxes（尾骨）是同一单数词的另一复数形式，意义完全相同；coccygeal vertebrae（尾椎）指构成尾骨的各节椎骨，并不等同于多块完整尾骨。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tailbones is the everyday equivalent; coccyxes is an alternative plural with exactly the same meaning; coccygeal vertebrae refers to the individual vertebrae making up a coccyx, rather than to multiple complete tailbones.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“布谷鸟喙形的尾骨”：一块 coccyx，多块 coccyges。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a cuckoo's beak at the base of the spine: one coccyx, several coccyges.

etymology_story.zh: 该词可追溯至中古英语的 colop、coloppe 等形式，早期用于指肉片或小块肉，其更早来源并不确定。现代用法主要保留在传统烹饪和地方菜名中，常见复数 collops。
etymology_story.en: The word goes back to Middle English forms such as colop and coloppe, referring to a slice or small piece of meat; its earlier origin is uncertain. Modern use survives mainly in traditional cookery and regional dish names, often as the plural collops.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 collop 是不可再作可靠词根词缀拆分的单纯词；collop + -s → collops（肉片）。没有常用的固定派生词族。collop-like 可临时表示“像肉片的”，但不是需要作为常用派生词收录的形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, collop is a simple word with no reliable productive root-and-affix division; collop + -s → collops. It has no common established derivative family. Collop-like can be formed descriptively, but it is not a standard common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slice（片）适用范围最广，不限于肉；escalope（薄肉片）通常指无骨、常经拍薄后烹调的肉片；cutlet（肉排）通常指供一人食用的一块肉，可带骨，也可指肉饼，范围与 collop 不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Slice is the broadest term and is not restricted to meat; escalope usually means a thin boneless piece of meat, often flattened before cooking; cutlet usually denotes a portion of meat, sometimes with a bone, or a shaped meat preparation, so its scope differs from collop.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 collop 当作老食谱里的“一小片肉”整体记忆，不强拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember collop as a small slice of meat in an old recipe; learn it whole rather than inventing a root.

etymology_story.zh: 源自新拉丁语科名 Colubridae，其基础是拉丁语 coluber，意为“蛇”。英语中的 colubrid 既可指这一科的成员，也可作形容词表示“游蛇科的”。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin family name Colubridae, based on Latin coluber, meaning “snake.” In English, colubrid names a member of the family and also functions as an adjective meaning “of that family.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词分析：colubr-（蛇，来自拉丁语）+ -id（动物分类中表示某科成员或与该科有关）；这不是日常英语中自由组合的构词形式。词族及相关形式：colubrid（名词、形容词）、colubrids（名词复数）、Colubridae（游蛇科）；colubrine（蛇的、似蛇的，亦可指游蛇亚科的）和 colubroid（游蛇总科的或其成员）是相关形式，并非 colubrid 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned morphological analysis: colubr- (“snake,” from Latin) + -id, used in zoology for family membership or association; this is not a freely productive everyday English formation. Family and related forms: colubrid, noun and adjective; colubrids, plural; and Colubridae, the family name. Colubrine, meaning snakelike or relating to snakes or Colubrinae, and colubroid, referring to Colubroidea or its members, are related formations rather than direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有同样精确的普通近义词。snake 是范围更广的“蛇”；serpent 通常是文学性的“蛇”；colubroid 是相关分类术语，通常涉及比游蛇科更大的分类范围，不能直接替换 colubrid。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no equally precise everyday synonym. Snake is the broader general term; serpent is usually literary; colubroid is a related taxonomic term generally covering a broader group than Colubridae and is not interchangeable with colubrid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: colubr- 表示“蛇”，-id 标示科属身份：一条“持游蛇科身份证的蛇”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect colubr-, “snake,” with the zoological family marker -id: a snake carrying a Colubridae identity card.

senses.meaning_zh: 合生；过程哲学中多种既有因素整合为一个新的现实实有的过程
senses.meaning_en: In process philosophy, the integration of many inherited factors into a new actual entity.
senses.english_definition: In Whitehead's philosophy, concrescence is the process through which many contributing factors become one new actual entity.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 concrescentia，源于 concrescere“共同生长、凝结”，其中 con- 表示“一起”，crescere 表示“生长”。“长成一体”的原义用于组织合生，后来也成为怀特海过程哲学中描述多者形成统一体的术语。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin concrescentia, from concrescere, “to grow together or solidify,” combining con-, “together,” with crescere, “to grow.” Its image of growing into a unity underlies its biological use and its later technical use in Whitehead's process philosophy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术词素分析：con-（共同）+ cresc-（生长）+ -ence（过程或状态）；也可联系 concrescent（合生的）与对应名词 concrescence。词族：concresce（合生，罕用动词）、concresces、concresced、concrescing、concrescent、concrescence、concrescences；concrete 和 concretion 是同源相关词，并非由 concrescence 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Learned analysis: con-, “together,” + cresc-, “grow,” + -ence, marking a process or state; compare the adjective concrescent with the corresponding noun concrescence. The family includes the rare verb concresce, its forms concresces, concresced, and concrescing, the adjective concrescent, and concrescence with plural concrescences. Concrete and concretion are etymologically related, not direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fusion 强调部分合为一体，未必涉及生长；coalescence 强调原本分开的部分逐渐汇合；accretion 强调附着、积累而增大。concrescence 特别突出“共同生长而结合”，在牙科学和过程哲学中有专门含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fusion emphasizes union without necessarily involving growth; coalescence emphasizes separate parts coming together; accretion emphasizes enlargement through accumulation or attachment. Concrescence specifically suggests growing together and has specialized meanings in dentistry and process philosophy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con-＝一起，cresc-＝生长：分开的部分“长到一起”，形成一个整体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means “together” and cresc- means “grow”: separate parts grow into one whole.

senses.meaning_zh: 惯例；习俗；长期形成的习惯，属罕用正式词

senses.english_definition: Consuetude is a custom or way of doing something that has become established through repeated use.
senses.collocation_en: long consuetude; established consuetude

senses.sentence_zh: 依照长期沿袭的习俗，村民们每年春天都会在广场上聚集。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 consuetudo“习惯、惯例”，与 consuescere“变得习惯”有关。它保留了拉丁词形的明显痕迹，在现代英语中主要见于罕用的正式、历史或法律语境。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin consuetudo, “habit or custom,” related to consuescere, “to become accustomed.” It retains a visibly Latin form and survives chiefly in rare formal, historical, or legal usage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 consuetude 作为整体词干学习，不宜机械拆成具有独立现代词义的 con- + sue- + -tude。历史上可联系 consuet-（习惯）与表示状态的拉丁名词词尾；词族及相关形式包括 consuetudes（复数，少用）、consuetudinal 和 consuetudinary（习惯的、习俗的，均罕用），以及相关的 desuetude（废而不用）；custom 也是历史同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, consuetude is best learned as a whole stem rather than mechanically divided into independently meaningful con-, sue-, and -tude. Historically, it relates to consuet-, “accustomed,” and a Latin noun ending expressing a state. Family and related forms include the uncommon plural consuetudes, the rare adjectives consuetudinal and consuetudinary, and the related noun desuetude, “disuse.” Custom is also historically cognate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: custom 多指群体沿袭的习俗；habit 多指个人反复形成的习惯；usage 强调惯常采用的做法，尤其用于语言或制度。consuetude 与 custom 最接近，但语体明显更古雅、更正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Custom usually refers to a practice shared by a community; habit often refers to an individual's repeated behavior; usage emphasizes an accepted practice, especially in language or institutions. Consuetude is closest to custom but sounds markedly more archaic and formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“习以为常”的逻辑：一件事反复做久了，就成为 consuetude。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to becoming accustomed: a practice repeated long enough becomes consuetude.

senses.meaning_zh: 伞房花序：下部花梗较长，使各花排列成近乎平顶的花序
senses.meaning_en: A roughly flat-topped flower cluster whose lower flower stalks are longer than its upper ones.
senses.english_definition: A corymb is a flower cluster in which the lower flowers have longer stalks, bringing the flowers to approximately the same level.
senses.collocation_en: a flat-topped corymb; flowers arranged in corymbs
senses.collocation_zh: 平顶的伞房花序；排列成伞房花序的花
senses.sentence_en: The flowers form a corymb, with the longer lower stalks bringing them level with the upper flowers.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些花形成伞房花序，下部较长的花梗使它们与上部的花处于同一高度。

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 corymbus，更早源于希腊语 korymbos，指“顶部”或“一簇花果”。植物学将这个表示顶端簇生的词用于花朵大致排列在同一平面上的花序。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin corymbus, ultimately from Greek korymbos, meaning a summit or a cluster of flowers or fruit. Botanical usage applies this image of a terminal cluster to flowers arranged at approximately the same level.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词干为 corymb，不宜再拆成日常英语词素。词族：corymbs（复数）；corymb + -ose → corymbose（伞房状的）；corymb + -ous → corymbous（伞房状的）；corymb + -iform → corymbiform（形似伞房花序的）；corymbosely（以伞房状方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is corymb, which should not be further divided into everyday English morphemes. Its family includes the plural corymbs; corymb + -ose → corymbose; corymb + -ous → corymbous; corymb + -iform → corymbiform, all describing a corymb-like form; and the adverb corymbosely.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相邻概念，并非严格同义词：raceme（总状花序）的花梗沿主轴着生，通常不形成平顶；umbel（伞形花序）的花梗从近乎同一点发出；panicle（圆锥花序）具有分枝。corymb 的关键是下部花梗较长，使花顶近乎齐平。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These are neighboring terms rather than exact synonyms: a raceme bears stalked flowers along an axis and is usually not flat-topped; an umbel has stalks arising from approximately one point; a panicle is branched. A corymb is distinguished by longer lower stalks that bring the flowers to nearly the same level.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“一簇花齐顶”：下面的花梗长一点，把花托到同一层。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a level-topped flower cluster: the lower stalks grow longer to lift their flowers to the same height.

senses.meaning_zh: 余割：正弦的倒数；直角三角形中为斜边与对边之比
senses.meaning_en: The reciprocal of sine; in a right triangle, the hypotenuse divided by the opposite side.
senses.english_definition: The cosecant of an angle is one divided by its sine; for an acute angle in a right triangle, it is the hypotenuse divided by the opposite side.
senses.collocation_en: the cosecant of an angle; the cosecant function
senses.collocation_zh: 一个角的余割；余割函数
senses.sentence_en: The cosecant of 30 degrees is 2 because the sine of 30 degrees is one half.
senses.sentence_zh: 30度的余割是2，因为30度的正弦是二分之一。

etymology_story.zh: 来自新拉丁语三角学术语 cosecans，表示“余角的正割”；其中 co- 与“余角”有关，secant 最终源于拉丁语 secare“切割”。名称反映了余割与余角正割之间的关系：csc θ = sec(90° − θ)，在两边均有定义时成立。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin trigonometric term cosecans, meaning the secant of the complementary angle; co- refers to the complement, while secant ultimately derives from Latin secare, “to cut.” The name reflects the identity csc θ = sec(90° − θ), wherever both sides are defined.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：co-（表示余角关系）+ secant（正割）→ cosecant（余割）。词形包括 cosecants（复数）；csc 和 cosec 是常见缩写，不是派生词。相关三角函数词有 sine（正弦）、cosine（余弦）、secant（正割）和 cotangent（余切），它们属于同一术语体系，并非全部由 cosecant 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: co-, marking a complementary-angle relationship, + secant → cosecant. The plural is cosecants; csc and cosec are common abbreviations, not derivatives. Related trigonometric terms include sine, cosine, secant, and cotangent; they belong to the same terminology system rather than all being derived from cosecant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reciprocal of sine（正弦的倒数）是精确的释义性同义表达；secant（正割）是余弦的倒数；cotangent（余切）是正切的倒数。后两者是相关函数，不能与 cosecant 互换；reciprocal sine 也不应与 inverse sine（反正弦）混淆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reciprocal of sine is an exact descriptive equivalent; secant is the reciprocal of cosine; cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent. The latter two are related functions, not interchangeable synonyms. Reciprocal sine must also be distinguished from inverse sine, meaning arcsine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记 sec＝1/cos，再用 co- 的余角关系连接：csc θ＝sec(90°−θ)＝1/sin θ，取各式有定义的角。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with sec = 1/cos, then use the complementary-angle link in co-: csc θ = sec(90° − θ) = 1/sin θ, wherever these expressions are defined.

senses.meaning_zh: （罕见或诙谐用语）饮酒或进食过量后的不适
senses.meaning_en: Illness or discomfort caused by excessive drinking or eating, expressed in a rare or humorous word.
senses.english_definition: Crapulence is the unpleasant feeling you have after drinking too much alcohol or eating too much food.
senses.collocation_en: suffer from crapulence; a bout of crapulence
