etymology_story.zh: 英语经新拉丁语 encephalon 借入此词，源自希腊语 enkephalos，意为“脑”，其历史构造包含 en-（在……内）和 kephalē（头）。这一“头内之物”的名称在解剖学中用于指整个脑，而非仅指大脑。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed encephalon through New Latin from Greek enkephalos, meaning 'brain,' historically built from en- ('in') and kephalē ('head'). This name for what lies within the head became an anatomical term for the whole brain rather than the cerebrum alone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词以 encephal-／encephalo- 表示“脑”；encephalon 的词尾 -on 是借入词保留的希腊语名词词尾，不宜当作普通英语的能产后缀。复数：encephala；主要词族包括 encephalic（脑的）、encephalitis（脑炎）、encephalitic（脑炎的）、encephalopathy（脑病）、encephalopathic（脑病的）、encephalogram（脑部检查记录或图像）、encephalography（脑部记录或成像技术），以及 electroencephalogram（脑电图）、electroencephalography（脑电描记术）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formations use encephal-/encephalo- to mean 'brain'; the ending -on in encephalon is an inherited Greek noun ending, not an ordinary productive English suffix. The plural is encephala; principal family members include encephalic ('relating to the brain'), encephalitis ('brain inflammation'), encephalitic ('relating to encephalitis'), encephalopathy ('brain disease or dysfunction'), encephalopathic ('relating to encephalopathy'), encephalogram ('a brain record or image'), encephalography ('brain recording or imaging'), electroencephalogram ('an electrical brain tracing'), and electroencephalography ('the recording of brain electrical activity').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brain：最直接的同义词，适用于日常和专业语境；cerebrum：指“大脑”，只是整个脑的一部分，不能完全替换；central nervous system：指“中枢神经系统”，包括脑和脊髓，范围更广。后两者是相关术语，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brain is the direct equivalent in both everyday and specialist usage. Cerebrum names only one major part of the brain, while central nervous system includes both the brain and spinal cord; these last two are related terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: en- 在内 + cephal- 头：位于头内的是“脑”；记住它指整个脑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: En- means 'in' and cephal- means 'head': the organ within the head is the whole brain.

etymology_story.en: This modern dental term combines Greek-derived elements meaning 'inside' and 'tooth' with the adjective suffix -ic. Its literal focus on the inside of a tooth underlies its specialized use for endodontics and associated treatment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：end-（endo- 在元音前的形式，内部）+ odont-（牙）+ -ic（……的）→ endodontic。词族：endodontics（牙髓病学，形式以 -s 结尾但作单数学科名词）、endodontist（牙髓病专科医生）、endodontically（以牙髓治疗方式；在牙髓治疗方面）、endodontology（牙髓病学，较少用的同义学科名）；endodontic 本身通常只作形容词。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Root-canal, used attributively, closely overlaps with endodontic in treatment contexts but is narrower. Pulpal relates specifically to dental pulp, whereas dental covers teeth or dentistry generally; these expressions are related rather than universally interchangeable.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在20世纪中叶由 endodontics（牙髓病学）的词干与表示专业人员的 -ist 构成。其核心成分最终来自希腊语 endon（内部）和 odous、属格 odontos（牙齿），体现这一专科关注牙齿内部组织的特点。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the mid-twentieth century from the stem of endodontics and the specialist suffix -ist. Its underlying elements come from Greek endon, meaning 'within,' and odous, with the stem odont-, meaning 'tooth,' reflecting the specialty's focus on the inside of teeth. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/endodontist)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：endo-（内部）+ odont-（牙）+ -ist（专业人员）→ endodontist。词族：endodontics（牙髓病学）、endodontic（牙髓病学的）、endodontically（以牙髓治疗方式）、endodontist（牙髓病专科医生）、endodontists（复数）；相关形式有 endodontology（牙髓病学）和 endodontologist（牙髓病学专家）。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: endo- ('within') + odont- ('tooth') + -ist ('specialist') → endodontist. The family includes endodontics ('the dental specialty'), endodontic ('relating to that specialty'), endodontically ('by endodontic methods'), endodontist, and the plural endodontists; related forms include endodontology and endodontologist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: endodontologist（牙髓病学专家）是较少见的近义名称；root canal specialist（根管治疗专家）是突出主要治疗项目的通俗说法；dentist（牙医）是上位词，并不表示接受过牙髓病专科训练。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Endodontologist is a less common alternative designation; root canal specialist is an everyday description emphasizing a major treatment; dentist is the broader term and does not itself imply specialist training in endodontics.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: endo- 内部 + odont- 牙 + -ist 专家：处理“牙齿内部问题”的专家。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inside + tooth + specialist: the expert who treats problems inside a tooth.

usage_note: 本课取化学中的吸热义，与 endothermic 对应；exothermic 表示放热。生物学中的内温义另作区分。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于现代科学英语的希腊语来源词族，由表示“内部”的 endo-、表示“热”的 therm- 和形容词后缀 -al 构成。它在物理化学中表示热量向系统内部输入，在动物生理学中则表示热量主要由体内产生。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific formation combines Greek-derived endo-, meaning 'within,' and therm-, meaning 'heat,' with the adjective suffix -al. Its established uses concern heat entering a physical or chemical system and heat being generated within an animal's body. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/endothermal)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：endo-（内部、向内）+ therm-（热）+ -al（……的）→ endothermal。词族：endothermally（以吸热或内温方式）、endothermic（吸热的；内温性的，更常用）、endothermically（以吸热或内温方式）、endotherm（内温动物）、endothermy（内温性）；endotherms 是 endotherm 的复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: endo- ('within, inward') + therm- ('heat') + -al ('relating to') → endothermal. The family includes endothermally, the more usual adjective endothermic, endothermically, endotherm ('an animal producing its own body heat'), endothermy ('internal heat production'), and the plural endotherms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: endothermic（吸热的；内温性的）通常更常用，具有相应的两种专业义；heat-absorbing（吸热的）只对应热量吸收义；warm-blooded（温血的）是动物生理学中的通俗近义词，但不能用于吸热反应，也不如“内温性”精确。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Endothermic is generally the more usual equivalent and has corresponding scientific senses; heat-absorbing applies only to heat uptake; warm-blooded is an everyday biological near-equivalent, but it cannot describe heat-absorbing reactions and is less precise than endothermal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: endo- 内 + therm- 热：化学看“热进入内部”，动物看“内部产生热”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inside + heat: in chemistry, heat moves in; in animals, heat is made within.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 enfeffen、enfeoffen 借自盎格鲁法语 enfeoffer，与古法语表示封地的 fief 属同一词族。它最初用于封建土地授予，后来也成为历史土地法中通过封授使人取得地产权利的术语。
etymology_story.en: Middle English enfeffen and enfeoffen were borrowed from Anglo-French enfeoffer, belonging to the same family as Old French fief. The word described feudal land grants and also became a historical property-law term for putting someone in legal possession of an estate. [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/enfeoff)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词可分析为 en-（使进入某种状态）+ feoff（授予封地），但 feoff 本身现已罕见。屈折形式：enfeoffs、enfeoffed、enfeoffing；派生词：enfeoffment（封授；封授行为）；相关法律词族：feoffment（封授）、feoffor（授地产者）、feoffee（受地产者），以及历史相关词 fief（封地）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure can be analyzed as en- ('cause to enter a state') + feoff ('grant a fief'), although feoff is itself now rare. Inflections are enfeoffs, enfeoffed, and enfeoffing; the derivative enfeoffment names the act or grant. Related legal forms include feoffment, feoffor ('the grantor'), feoffee ('the recipient'), and the historically related fief.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: feoff（封授）是罕见的直接近义词；grant（授予）适用范围更广，不限定封建关系或特定地产权利；invest someone with an estate（使某人取得地产权利）突出正式赋予权利，仍需上下文说明具体法律形式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Feoff is a rare direct equivalent; grant is broader and does not specify feudal tenure or a particular property interest; invest someone with an estate emphasizes formally conferring property rights, with the exact legal mechanism supplied by context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect feoff with fief: put someone into possession of a landed estate.

It became a specialist term for curved indentations on heraldic edges and decorative markings around coins and similar objects. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/engrail)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 engrail 作为整体动词词干学习，其历史上的 en- + 法语词干结构已不透明。屈折形式：engrails、engrailed、engrailing；派生词：engrailment（弧齿边饰；制作这种边饰的行为）；engrailed 也用作形容词，表示“有内凹弧齿边的”，如 an engrailed cross（弧齿边十字纹）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, engrail is best learned as a whole verb stem; its historical en- plus French-base structure is no longer transparent. Inflections are engrails, engrailed, and engrailing; engrailment names the ornamentation or the act of producing it. Engrailed also functions as an adjective meaning 'having an edge with concave curves,' as in an engrailed cross.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scallop（做成扇贝状边缘）同样突出连续弧形，但未必遵循纹章学对凹凸方向的规定；notch（刻缺口）不限定缺口为弧形；serrate（做成锯齿状）通常强调较尖的齿形，与 engrail 的内凹弧形不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scallop likewise suggests repeated curves but does not necessarily follow heraldic conventions about their direction; notch does not specify curved indentations; serrate usually suggests sharper, sawlike teeth rather than the concave curves characteristic of engrailing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：eno-（葡萄酒；变体 oeno-）+ -logy（学科）→ enology。词族：enologist（葡萄酒学专家）、enologic／enological（葡萄酒学的）、enologically（从葡萄酒学角度）；对应的 oeno- 拼写形式有 oenology、oenologist、oenologic、oenological、oenologically；enologists 和 oenologists 为人员名词的复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: eno- ('wine'; variant oeno-) + -logy ('field of study') → enology. The family includes enologist ('a wine scientist'), enologic and enological ('relating to wine science'), and enologically ('from an enological perspective'). Corresponding oeno- forms are oenology, oenologist, oenologic, oenological, and oenologically; the personal nouns have the plurals enologists and oenologists.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oenology（葡萄酒学）是意义相同的另一拼写；wine science（葡萄酒科学）是透明易懂的近义表达；winemaking（葡萄酒酿造）主要指实际生产活动，而 enology 强调相关知识体系与科学研究。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oenology is an alternative spelling with the same meaning; wine science is a transparent near-equivalent; winemaking primarily names the practical activity, whereas enology emphasizes its body of knowledge and scientific study.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eno- 酒 + -logy 学：把葡萄酒如何酿成当作一门科学来研究。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Wine + study: the science of how wine is made.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 esculentus，意为“可食用的”，其基础词 esca 意为“食物”，与 edere“吃”同源。英语保留了形容词用法，也曾将它用作名词，指食物，尤其是可食用植物。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin esculentus, meaning 'edible', based on esca, 'food', which is related to edere, 'to eat'. English retained the adjective and also used it as a noun for food, especially edible plants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 esculent 视为不可再作能产拆分的借词；历史上可联系拉丁语 esca“食物”和形容词后缀 -ulentus。主要词族形式为形容词 esculent 及同形名词 esculent；名词复数为 esculents，没有常用的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, esculent is normally treated as an established borrowing rather than a productively divisible formation; historically, it connects Latin esca, 'food', with the adjectival suffix -ulentus. Its principal family forms are the adjective esculent and the identical noun esculent, with plural esculents; it has no common modern derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: edible 是“可食用的”最普通、中性的表达；eatable 常强调某物尚能入口，语体较口语化；comestible 也表示“可食用的”，但较正式。esculent 如今罕用，常带植物学或旧式书面语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Edible is the ordinary, neutral word for something suitable to eat; eatable often suggests that something is acceptable to eat and is more conversational; comestible is formal. Esculent is now uncommon and often has a botanical or older literary flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 esca“食物”：能作为食物的，就是 esculent。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to Latin esca, 'food': something fit to become food is esculent.

etymology_story.zh: 由化学名词 ester“酯”加表示“使成为”的后缀 -ify 构成。ester 本身借自德语 Ester，是对 Essigäther“乙酸乙酯，字面为醋醚”一词的缩合命名。
etymology_story.en: Esterify was formed from the chemical noun ester and the suffix -ify, meaning 'to make or become'. Ester itself was borrowed from German Ester, a contracted name based on Essigäther, 'ethyl acetate', literally 'vinegar ether'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ester“酯”＋-ify“使成为／变成”→ esterify。屈折形式：esterifies、esterified、esterifying；主要相关词：ester“酯”、esterification“酯化”、esterifiable“可酯化的”、de-esterify“使脱酯化”、de-esterification“脱酯化”、transesterify“使发生酯交换”、transesterification“酯交换”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: ester + -ify, 'to make or become' → esterify. Inflected forms are esterifies, esterified, and esterifying; principal related forms include ester, esterification, esterifiable, de-esterify, de-esterification, transesterify, and transesterification.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: form an ester“形成酯”和 convert into an ester“转化为酯”是释义性近义表达；前者侧重产物形成，后者侧重原料转化。acylate“酰化”是相关化学术语，但范围不同，不能与 esterify 普遍互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Form an ester and convert into an ester are explanatory equivalents: the first emphasizes product formation, while the second emphasizes conversion of the starting material. Acylate is a related chemical term with a different scope and is not generally interchangeable with esterify.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ester“酯”＋-ify“变成”：让物质变成酯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ester + -ify, 'make or become': make a substance into an ester.

senses.meaning_zh: 优境学；通过改善环境和生活条件增进人类福祉的研究

senses.sentence_zh: 优境学强调改善营养、卫生、住房和教育条件。

etymology_story.zh: 这一学科名称于20世纪初进入英语，取自希腊语 euthēnein“兴盛、生活良好”，并采用学科后缀 -ics。它尤其与埃伦·斯沃洛·理查兹倡导的环境改善理念相联系，强调生活条件对人的发展的作用。
etymology_story.en: This disciplinary name entered English in the early twentieth century, drawing on Greek euthēnein, 'to flourish or thrive', and the disciplinary suffix -ics. It is particularly associated with Ellen Swallow Richards's emphasis on improving the conditions in which people live and develop.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词结构：euthen-，源于希腊语中“兴盛、生活良好”的词干，＋-ics“学科”→ euthenics。主要相关形式：euthenic“优境学的；改善生活环境的”、euthenist“优境学倡导者／研究者”；这两个派生词也较罕见。词尾 -s 是学科名称的一部分，不表示普通名词复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: euthen-, a Greek-derived stem expressing flourishing or living well, + -ics, denoting a field of study → euthenics. Principal related forms are euthenic, 'relating to euthenics or improved living conditions', and euthenist, 'an advocate or student of euthenics'; both are uncommon. The final -s belongs to the disciplinary name and does not mark an ordinary plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用词。environmental improvement“环境改善”侧重改善行动；public health“公共卫生”侧重群体健康；social reform“社会改革”涉及更广泛的制度与社会变革。euthenics 特指通过改善生活环境促进人的福祉这一研究取向。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Environmental improvement emphasizes practical changes to surroundings; public health focuses on population health; social reform covers broader institutional and social change. Euthenics specifically names an approach to human well-being through improved living conditions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eu- 联想“好”，全词抓住“让人生活得好”：改善环境，促进人的发展。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Associate eu- with 'good' and the whole word with 'living well': improve people's surroundings so that they can flourish.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 excurs- 这一词干，它来自 excurrere“向外跑”，由 ex-“向外”和 currere“跑”构成。“跑出原来的路线”既可表示实际漫游，也可比喻言谈或思路偏离主题。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin excurs-, the stem associated with excurrere, 'to run out', formed from ex-, 'out', and currere, 'to run'. Leaving an original route developed both into physical wandering and into a figurative departure from the main topic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词结构：excurs-“向外跑；偏离”＋-ive“具有……性质或倾向的”→ excursive。直接派生词：excursively“离题地；漫游地”、excursiveness“离题；漫游性”；同源相关词：excursion“短途旅行；涉足其他领域”、excursus“附论；插论”，它们并非由 excursive 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: excurs-, 'run out or depart', + -ive, expressing a quality or tendency → excursive. Direct derivatives are excursively and excursiveness. Related words from the same historical base include excursion and excursus; these are not derivatives of excursive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: digressive 最直接地表示偏离主旨；discursive 常指论述广泛展开、涉及多个相关话题；rambling 常带贬义，暗示言谈冗长且缺乏条理。excursive 强调思路向外延伸或游移，本身不一定表示表达混乱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Digressive most directly means departing from the main subject; discursive often describes a discussion that ranges across several related topics; rambling commonly criticizes speech or writing as lengthy and poorly organized. Excursive emphasizes outward movement or wandering of thought without necessarily implying confusion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex-“向外”＋“跑”：脚跑出路线是漫游，话跑出主题是离题。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'run out': feet leave the route and wander; thoughts leave the topic and digress.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 extrados，由 extra-“外部”和 dos“背”构成；dos 可追溯至拉丁语 dorsum“背”。这个名称把拱的外凸面形象地看作拱的“外背部”。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed extrados from French, where it combines extra-, 'outside', with dos, 'back'; dos ultimately comes from Latin dorsum, 'back'. The name pictures the outer convex surface as the arch's external back.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借词内部结构：extra-“外部”＋dos“背，法语词”→ extrados；dos 不是能在英语中自由构词的常用词根。复数通常为 extradoses；相关形容词 extradosed 常见于 extradosed bridge“矮塔斜拉桥／部分斜拉桥”。对应的反义术语为 intrados“拱腹；内凹曲面”。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure within the borrowing: extra-, 'outside', + French dos, 'back' → extrados; dos is not a common freely productive English root. The usual plural is extradoses. The related adjective extradosed occurs especially in extradosed bridge. The contrasting technical term is intrados, the inner concave surface.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: outer surface of an arch“拱的外表面”和 back of an arch“拱背”是释义性近义表达；前者较通俗，后者保留“背部”的形象。extrados 是精确的建筑学术语，专指外凸曲面；intrados 指内凹面，是反义词而非近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Outer surface of an arch and back of an arch are explanatory equivalents: the former is plain language, while the latter preserves the image of a back. Extrados is the precise architectural term for the outer convex surface; intrados denotes the inner concave surface and is an antonym, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: extra“外”＋dos“背”：拱的外背面就是 extrados。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Extra means 'outside' and dos means 'back': the outside back of an arch is its extrados.

etymology_story.zh: 这是一个现代医学构词，由表示“向外”的拉丁语来源前缀 ex- 与表示“管”的词干及动词后缀组成。它与 intubate（插管）相对应，表示将已置入的导管拔出。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical formation combines the Latin-derived prefix ex-, meaning 'out,' with a stem meaning 'tube' and a verbal suffix. It contrasts with intubate, describing the removal of a tube that has been inserted.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ex-（向外）+ tub(e)（管）+ -ate（动词后缀）。屈折形式：extubates、extubated、extubating；名词：extubation（拔管）。相关对应词：intubate（插管）、intubation（插管操作），二者不是 extubate 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: ex- ('out') + tub(e) ('tube') + -ate (verb-forming suffix). Inflected forms: extubates, extubated, extubating; derived noun: extubation. Related counterparts are intubate and intubation, which are not derivatives of extubate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: remove a tube（移除导管）是范围较广的普通表达；remove an endotracheal tube（拔除气管导管）明确限定气管导管；decannulate（拔除套管）通常用于套管，尤其是气管切开套管，不能在所有场合与 extubate 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Remove a tube is a broad, plain-language equivalent; remove an endotracheal tube specifies the airway device; decannulate usually concerns a cannula, especially a tracheostomy tube, and is not interchangeable with extubate in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex- 向外 + tube 管：把管拔出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- means 'out': take the tube out.

etymology_story.en: The word arose in the twentieth century from exurb plus -ia, following the pattern of suburbia. Exurb combines ex-, meaning 'outside,' with urb-, from Latin urbs, 'city,' to name residential areas beyond the established suburbs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 直接构词：exurb（远郊居住区）+ -ia（地区或集合后缀）；进一步可分析为 ex-（在外）+ urb-（城市）+ -ia。通常作不可数集合名词；相关词族：exurb／exurbs（远郊居住区）、exurban（远郊的）、exurbanite／exurbanites（远郊居民）、exurbanization（远郊化）。
morphology_enriched.en: Immediate structure: exurb + -ia, an area-forming or collective suffix; more deeply, ex- ('outside') + urb- ('city') + -ia. It is normally an uncountable collective noun. Related forms include exurb/exurbs, exurban, exurbanite/exurbanites, and exurbanization.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Outer suburbs emphasizes the outer parts of the suburbs, which may still belong to the continuous built-up area; commuter belt is defined by commuting links and can include both suburbs and exurbs; rural–urban fringe emphasizes transitional land use rather than residential settlement alone.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- means 'outside' and urb- means 'city': homes beyond the suburbs.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 fainéant；其较早形式与 feignant（假装的，后来也指偷懒的）有关，并受到 fait néant（什么也不做）这一解释的影响而改变词形。英语保留了“懒人”和“懒散的、无所作为的”两种用法，现多见于文学或历史语境。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French fainéant, whose earlier form was associated with feignant, 'pretending' or 'shirking,' and was reshaped under the influence of fait néant, 'does nothing.' English retained both the noun and adjective, now chiefly in literary or historical contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜视为完整的法语借词，不应机械拆成英语词根与词缀；fait + néant 是影响其历史词形的再分析。名词复数：fainéants；常见无重音符号拼写：faineant；罕见相关抽象名词：fainéantise（懒散、无所作为）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat this as a whole French loanword rather than a productive combination of English roots and affixes; fait + néant represents a historical reinterpretation. The noun plural is fainéants; faineant is the unaccented spelling; the rare related abstract noun fainéantise means idleness or inactivity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: idler（闲人、懒汉）是较中性的名词；sluggard（懒汉）更明确地责备懒惰，且同样带文学色彩；indolent（懒散的）是近义形容词，强调不愿费力。fainéant 常带讽刺意味，尤其适合形容养尊处优却无所作为的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Idler is a relatively neutral noun for someone who does little work; sluggard is more openly reproachful and also literary; indolent is an adjective emphasizing unwillingness to exert oneself. Fainéant often adds a mocking suggestion of privileged inactivity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用历史再分析 fait néant“什么也不做”记：不做事的人，也可形容无所作为。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical reinterpretation 'does nothing': a do-nothing person, or someone described as do-nothing.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源自新拉丁语科名 Felidae，而科名以猫属名称 Felis 为基础，最终可追溯到拉丁语 feles／felis（猫）。因此，felid 的范围涵盖整个猫科，不只指家猫。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin family name Felidae, based on the genus name Felis and ultimately Latin feles or felis, meaning 'cat.' Felid therefore covers the whole cat family rather than domestic cats alone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分类学构词可分析为 fel-（猫，见于 Felis、Felidae）+ -id（某动物科的成员或与该科有关的）；也可直接视为 Felidae 对应的普通名词和形容词。复数：felids；相关词族：feline（猫科的；猫科动物）、Felidae（猫科）、Felis（猫属）、feliform（猫型的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In taxonomic word formation, fel- ('cat,' as in Felis and Felidae) combines with -id, denoting a family member or association with that family; felid also functions as the ordinary noun and adjective corresponding to Felidae. The plural is felids. Related forms include feline, Felidae, Felis, and feliform.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: feline 作名词时可近指猫科动物，作形容词时还可表示“像猫的”；cat 在日常英语中通常指家猫，在动物学语境中也可泛指猫科成员；member of the family Felidae（猫科成员）是分类意义最明确的释义。felid 尤其适用于科学语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Feline can denote a cat-family animal, but its adjective also means 'catlike'; cat usually means a domestic cat in everyday speech, though it can have a broader zoological meaning; member of the family Felidae is the most explicit taxonomic equivalent. Felid is particularly suited to scientific contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fel- 联结 feline：家猫、狮子、老虎都是猫科成员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link fel- with feline: domestic cats, lions, and tigers all belong to the same family.

senses.meaning_en: A synthetic radioactive metallic element with atomic number 100 and symbol Fm.
senses.english_definition: Fermium is a radioactive chemical element that scientists produce in nuclear reactions and that has the atomic number 100.

senses.collocation_zh: 镄同位素；镄-257

etymology_story.zh: 镄于1952年首次热核武器试验产生的残留物中被发现，后来为纪念物理学家恩里科·费米而命名为 fermium。词尾 -ium 沿用了许多金属元素名称的构词惯例。
etymology_story.en: Fermium was discovered in material from the first thermonuclear weapon test in 1952 and was later named in honor of the physicist Enrico Fermi. Its ending -ium follows a familiar naming pattern for metallic elements.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：Fermi（费米，人名）+ -ium（元素名后缀）。fermium 通常为不可数名词，没有常用的普通英语派生词；化学符号为 Fm，同位素名称采用 fermium- 加质量数，如 fermium-257。fermi、fermion 等也与费米的人名有关，但不是 fermium 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: Fermi, the physicist's surname, + -ium, an element-name suffix. Fermium is normally uncountable and has no common everyday derivatives. Its chemical symbol is Fm, and isotope names add a mass number, as in fermium-257. Fermi and fermion also commemorate Fermi but are not derivatives of fermium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: element 100（100号元素）是同一元素的编号称呼；Fm 是其化学符号，属于等值标记而非普通近义词；actinide（锕系元素）是其所属类别，范围更广，不能当作镄的专名替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Element 100 is an equivalent numerical designation; Fm is its chemical symbol rather than an ordinary synonym; actinide names the broader class to which fermium belongs and cannot replace its specific name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Fermi + -ium：用费米的人名记镄；符号 Fm，序号100。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fermi + -ium: Fermi's commemorative element, Fm, number 100.

senses.meaning_en: an alloy of iron and manganese used mainly in steelmaking
senses.english_definition: Ferromanganese is an alloy containing iron and a high proportion of manganese, which is added to steel to adjust its composition and help remove oxygen and sulfur.
senses.collocation_en: high-carbon ferromanganese; ferromanganese production
senses.collocation_zh: 高碳锰铁；锰铁生产
senses.sentence_en: The plant produces high-carbon ferromanganese for the steel industry.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家工厂为钢铁行业生产高碳锰铁。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在19世纪由 ferro-（铁）与 manganese（锰）组合而成，用来命名炼钢所用的铁锰合金。ferro- 源自拉丁语 ferrum，意为“铁”。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from ferro- and manganese to name an iron–manganese alloy used in steelmaking. Ferro- comes from Latin ferrum, meaning “iron.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：ferro-（铁）+ manganese（锰）→ ferromanganese（锰铁）。通常作不可数名词，也可前置修饰名词，如 ferromanganese production（锰铁生产）；没有常用的直接派生词。相关词包括 manganese（锰）、ferroalloy（铁合金）和 ferrosilicon（硅铁），后两者属于相关构词系列。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ferro- “iron” + manganese → ferromanganese. It is normally an uncountable noun and can modify another noun, as in ferromanganese production; it has no common direct derivatives. Related vocabulary includes manganese, ferroalloy, and ferrosilicon, with the latter two belonging to the same combining-form series.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无常用的完全同义词。iron–manganese alloy（铁锰合金）是解释性近义表达；ferroalloy（铁合金）范围更广；spiegeleisen（镜铁）指一种含锰、含碳的特定铁合金，不能泛指所有锰铁。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Iron–manganese alloy is a descriptive equivalent; ferroalloy is a broader category; spiegeleisen denotes a particular manganese- and carbon-containing iron alloy rather than ferromanganese generally.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ferro- 是铁，manganese 是锰：铁与锰合在一起，就是锰铁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ferro- means iron and manganese supplies the other metal: iron plus manganese makes ferromanganese.

senses.sentence_zh: 摄影师将这些照片贴板上光，使其表面呈现高光泽。

etymology_story.zh: 该词出现于19世纪，由表示“铁”的 ferro- 与表示“印痕、图像”的 -type 构成，最初指以铁片为底材的摄影工艺及其照片。后来，动词也用于指通过接触抛光表面使相纸获得光泽的工序。
etymology_story.en: Formed in the nineteenth century from ferro- “iron” and -type “impression or image,” the word originally named an iron-plate photographic process and its photographs. The verb also came to describe giving photographic paper a glossy finish through contact with a polished surface.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：ferro-（铁）+ -type（印痕、图像）→ ferrotype。名词与动词通过词类转换共用同一形式；词族包括 ferrotypes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、ferrotyped（过去式、过去分词）和 ferrotyping（现在分词；照片贴板上光工艺）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: ferro- “iron” + -type “impression or image” → ferrotype. The noun and verb share their form through conversion; the word family includes ferrotypes, ferrotyped, and ferrotyping, which can also name the print-glazing process.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词义：tintype（铁版照片）是常用同义词，名称虽含 tin，却通常使用铁片；melainotype（黑底铁版照片）是历史上的相关名称。动词义：glaze（给照片上光）是近义词，但用途更广，不限于这种摄影工序。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the noun, tintype is the usual synonym, although its plate is generally iron despite the name; melainotype is a related historical name. For the verb, glaze is a near-synonym with broader uses beyond this photographic process.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 铁片承载图像，是铁版照片；照片贴着光滑表面干燥，就能上光。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An image on iron gives the noun; drying a print against a smooth surface gives the glossy-finish verb.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由医学新拉丁语进入英语，将源自拉丁语 fibra（纤维）的词干与源自希腊语的 -oma（肿瘤、肿块）结合起来。其名称依据组织构成，表示主要由纤维组织形成的肿瘤。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through medical New Latin, combining a stem from Latin fibra “fiber” with Greek-derived -oma “tumor or swelling.” It names the tumor by its predominantly fibrous tissue.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：fibr-（纤维）+ -oma（肿瘤）→ fibroma；相关复合词通常使用连接形式 fibro-。词族包括 fibromas／fibromata（复数）、fibromatous（纤维瘤性的）和 fibromatosis（纤维瘤病，指一组纤维组织增生性病变，并非 fibroma 的复数）；同根相关词有 fibrous（纤维的）、fibrosis（纤维化）和 fibrotic（纤维化的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: fibr- “fiber” + -oma “tumor” → fibroma; related compounds commonly use the combining form fibro-. The family includes the plurals fibromas and fibromata, fibromatous, and fibromatosis, which names a group of fibrous proliferative conditions rather than the plural of fibroma. Related words include fibrous, fibrosis, and fibrotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fibrous tumor（纤维性肿瘤）是近义描述，但未必明确良恶性；benign tumor（良性肿瘤）是范围更广的上位词；fibroid（通常指子宫肌瘤）在常用医学语境中一般指平滑肌瘤，不能直接等同于 fibroma。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fibrous tumor is a descriptive near-equivalent but does not necessarily specify benign behavior; benign tumor is a broader category. Fibroid usually refers to a uterine leiomyoma in ordinary medical usage and should not be treated as an exact synonym of fibroma.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fibr- 是纤维，-oma 是肿瘤：纤维组织形成的瘤，就是纤维瘤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fibr- supplies fiber and -oma supplies tumor: a fibroma is a fibrous-tissue tumor.

etymology_story.zh: forb 于20世纪进入英语生态学术语，其词源可追溯到希腊语 phorbē（牧草、饲料），与 pherbein（喂养、放牧）有关。现代用法强调植物的生长型，用它区别阔叶草本植物与禾草状植物，而非表示某个植物分类群。
etymology_story.en: Forb entered English ecological terminology in the twentieth century and ultimately derives from Greek phorbē “pasture or fodder,” related to pherbein “to feed or graze.” Its modern meaning identifies a plant growth form distinct from grasses and other grasslike plants, rather than a taxonomic group.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 forb 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的简单名词；复数为 forbs。常见复合形式包括 forb-rich（阔叶草本植物丰富的）、forb-dominated（以阔叶草本植物为主的）和 forb cover（阔叶草本植物盖度）；这些形式不构成独立的常用新词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, forb is a simple noun without a productive internal prefix–root–suffix breakdown; its plural is forbs. Common combinations include forb-rich, forb-dominated, and forb cover; these do not establish a separate common part of speech for forb itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: herb（草本植物）范围更广，可包括禾草状植物；wildflower（野花、野生开花植物）强调野生和开花，不与 forb 完全重合；broad-leaved herb（阔叶草本植物）是常见的解释性近义表达，但并非每种 forb 的叶片都宽阔。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Herb is broader and can include grasslike plants; wildflower emphasizes wild occurrence and flowers, so its scope differs from forb. Broad-leaved herb is a useful descriptive near-equivalent, although not every forb has conspicuously broad leaves.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 观察草甸：把禾草、莎草和灯心草分开，其余非木本开花植物就是 forb 的核心范围。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a meadow: set aside grasses, sedges, and rushes; the remaining nonwoody flowering plants form the core forb group.

etymology_story.zh: 钫由玛格丽特·佩雷于1939年发现，后来以其祖国法国命名。francium 将表示法国的 Franc- 与元素名称中常见的 -ium 结合起来。
etymology_story.en: Francium was discovered by Marguerite Perey in 1939 and later named after her home country, France. Its name combines Franc-, referring to France, with the familiar element-name ending -ium.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：Franc-（法国）+ -ium（元素名后缀）→ francium（钫）。通常作不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词；Fr 是化学符号，francium-223（钫-223）等是同位素名称，均不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: Franc- “France” + -ium, an element-name suffix, → francium. It is normally an uncountable noun with no common direct derivatives; Fr is its chemical symbol, and forms such as francium-223 are isotope names rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的词汇性同义词。Fr（钫的化学符号）与 element 87（87号元素）指同一元素，但分别是符号和描述性名称；alkali metal（碱金属）是上位类别，不能单独替代 francium。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common lexical synonym. Fr and element 87 identify the same element but function as a chemical symbol and a descriptive designation respectively; alkali metal is a broader category and cannot replace francium by itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: France（法国）加元素名尾缀 -ium：以法国命名的元素 francium，就是钫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect France with the element ending -ium: francium is the element named after France.

senses.meaning_en: The portion of a solid, especially a cone or pyramid, remaining after its top is cut off parallel to its base.
senses.english_definition: A frustum is the part of a cone or pyramid that remains when its pointed top is cut off by a plane parallel to its base.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 frustum，意为“一块、碎块”，经数学拉丁语进入英语。其几何意义把立体被截切后留下的部分看作原物体的一块。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin frustum, meaning “a piece” or “a fragment,” through mathematical Latin. Its geometrical meaning treats the remaining portion of a cut solid as a piece of the original body.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作常规词缀拆分的借入名词 frustum；复数为 frustums 或 frusta。相关构词形式 frusto- 表示“截头的”，见 frustoconical（截圆锥形的、圆台形的）和 frustopyramidal（截棱锥形的、棱台形的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, frustum is a borrowed noun without a productive internal affix breakdown; its plurals are frustums and frusta. The related combining form frusto-, meaning “truncated,” appears in frustoconical and frustopyramidal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: truncated solid（截切后的立体）范围更广，不一定专指平行截面形成的截头体；truncated cone（截圆锥、圆台）和 truncated pyramid（截棱锥、棱台）分别是 frustum 的具体类型。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Truncated solid is broader and does not necessarily specify a parallel cut; truncated cone and truncated pyramid name particular types of frustum.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语本义是“一块”：锥顶切掉，留下的那块就是 frustum。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “a piece”: cut off the pointed top, and the remaining piece is the frustum.

senses.meaning_zh: 暗褐色的；褐灰色的，尤用于动植物颜色描述
senses.meaning_en: Dark brown or brownish gray, especially in descriptions of plants and animals.
senses.english_definition: Something that is fuscous is a dull, dark brown or brownish-gray colour.

senses.collocation_zh: 暗褐色斑纹；褐灰色的翅膀

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 fuscus，意为“暗的、深褐色的”。进入英语后主要保留为描述暗褐色或褐灰色的书面用语，尤见于自然史和物种描述。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin fuscus, meaning “dark” or “dusky brown.” In English it has remained chiefly a descriptive term for dark brown or brownish-gray colouring, particularly in natural history.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 fusc-（暗色、褐色）+ -ous（形容词后缀），但它属于拉丁语来源的既有词，而不是现代英语中常用的自由构词。相关同根词有 infuscate（使变暗、使变褐）和 infuscation（变暗、褐化）；这一词族主要用于专业描述。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analysed as fusc- (“dark” or “brown”) + the adjective suffix -ous, although it is an established Latin-derived word rather than a freely productive modern formation. Related words include infuscate (“to darken or make brown”) and infuscation (“darkening or brown coloration”); this family is chiefly technical.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dusky（暗沉的）强调光线或颜色偏暗，不限定褐色；brownish-gray（褐灰色的）直接说明色相，适合一般表达；somber（暗淡的、阴沉的）还可传达沉郁气氛，而 fuscous 主要客观描述颜色。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dusky emphasizes darkness without specifying brown; brownish-gray states the hue plainly; somber can suggest a gloomy mood as well as a dark colour, whereas fuscous chiefly describes coloration objectively.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fusc- 抓住“暗褐色”：想象蛾翅上低调、暗沉的褐灰斑纹。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor fusc- to “dusky brown”: picture the muted brown-gray markings on a moth.

senses.english_definition: Galluses are straps that go over your shoulders and attach to your trousers to keep them up.

etymology_story.zh: galluses 来自 gallus，后者是 gallows（绞刑架）的地区性变体。名称从“悬吊”的概念转用于托住裤子的背带，如今主要保留在地区性或旧式表达中。
etymology_story.en: Galluses comes from gallus, a regional variant of gallows. The idea of suspension was extended to straps that hold up trousers, and the clothing term now survives mainly in regional or old-fashioned usage.

morphology_enriched.zh: gallus（背带；地区性形式）+ -es（复数后缀）→ galluses。表示这种衣物时通常使用复数 galluses，也可说 a pair of galluses（一副背带）；gallows 是其历史相关词，不是由 galluses 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Gallus, a regional form referring to a suspender, + plural -es gives galluses. The garment is normally referred to in the plural, including in a pair of galluses; gallows is historically related, not a derivative of galluses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: suspenders 是美式英语中“裤子背带”的常用词；braces 是英式英语中的常用对应词。galluses 所指基本相同，但地区性和旧式色彩更强；英式英语中的 suspenders 通常指吊袜带。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Suspenders is the usual American term, and braces is the usual British equivalent. Galluses refers to essentially the same item but has a stronger regional or old-fashioned flavour; in British English, suspenders usually means straps that hold up stockings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 gallows 的“吊住”联想：galluses 把裤子吊住。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with the suspension idea in gallows: galluses keep trousers hanging in place.

etymology_story.zh: 形成于以意大利科学家 Luigi Galvani 姓氏命名的电学词族，词尾属于源自希腊语 metron（度量）的测量词族。其含义由早期电现象研究发展为“与检流计及其测量有关的”。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the electrical vocabulary named after the Italian scientist Luigi Galvani, combined with measurement terminology ultimately derived from Greek metron, “measure.” Its meaning developed within that vocabulary to describe galvanometers and measurements made with them.

morphology_enriched.zh: galvano-（与伽伐尼电现象或电流有关）+ -metric（测量的）→ galvanometric；对应名词有 galvanometer（检流计）和 galvanometry（检流测量法），副词为 galvanometrically（用检流计测量地）。较广的同源词族包括 galvanic（原电池的、电流的）、galvanism（电流作用）、galvanize（镀锌；激励）和 galvanization（镀锌；激励）。
morphology_enriched.en: Galvano- (“relating to galvanic electricity or current”) + -metric (“relating to measurement”) forms galvanometric. Corresponding nouns are galvanometer and galvanometry, and the adverb is galvanometrically. The wider related family includes galvanic, galvanism, galvanize, and galvanization.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: galvanometer-based（基于检流计的）是强调所用仪器的直接释义；electrical（电的）范围更广；amperometric（安培测量的、电流测量的）常用于通过测量电流进行分析的技术语境，不一定涉及检流计。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Galvanometer-based is a direct paraphrase emphasizing the instrument; electrical is much broader; amperometric often describes analytical techniques based on measuring current and does not necessarily imply the use of a galvanometer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Galvani 关联电流，metric 关联测量：用检流计测电流。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Galvani suggests electricity; metric suggests measurement: measuring current with a galvanometer.

senses.english_definition: Geotropism is the growth of a plant part in a particular direction in response to gravity, either towards or away from its pull.
senses.collocation_en: positive geotropism; negative geotropism

etymology_story.zh: 英语词通常追溯至德语植物学术语 Geotropismus，由希腊语来源的“地”和“转向”成分构成。名称原以“地”标示方向，实际指植物对重力的定向生长反应，既包括顺重力方向生长，也包括逆重力方向生长。
etymology_story.en: The English word is generally traced to German Geotropismus, a botanical term built from Greek-derived elements meaning “earth” and “turning.” Although its name refers to the earth, it describes directional growth in response to gravity, including growth both with and against its pull.

morphology_enriched.zh: geo-（地）+ trop-（转向）+ -ism（过程或现象）→ geotropism。主要派生词有 geotropic（向地性的）和 geotropically（以向地性方式）；gravitropism（向重力性）是使用 gravi-（重力）构成的对应术语。
morphology_enriched.en: Geo- (“earth”) + trop- (“turning”) + -ism (“process or phenomenon”) forms geotropism. Its main derivatives are geotropic and geotropically; gravitropism is the corresponding term formed with gravi-, referring explicitly to gravity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gravitropism（向重力性）与 geotropism 基本同义，并更明确地指出刺激来自重力；geotropic response（向地性反应）和 gravitropic response（向重力性反应）通常侧重某次具体反应，而 geotropism 可指整体生长现象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gravitropism is essentially synonymous and identifies gravity more explicitly as the stimulus. Geotropic response and gravitropic response often emphasize a particular response, whereas geotropism can name the general growth phenomenon.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo 是“地”，trop 是“转向”：重力给生长定方向，根常向下，茎常向上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo means “earth” and trop means “turn”: gravity directs growth, with roots commonly growing down and shoots growing up.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 glaber，意为“无毛的、光滑的”，其词干为 glabr-。英语将它用于植物学和解剖学，描述天然不生毛的表面，而不一定指脱毛后变光滑的表面。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin glaber, meaning 'hairless' or 'smooth,' with the stem glabr-. In English botanical and anatomical descriptions, it identifies surfaces without hairs, rather than necessarily surfaces made smooth by removing hair.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：glabr-（光滑、无毛的拉丁语词干）+ -ous（形容词后缀）。主要词族：glabrousness（无毛性）；同源专业词有 glabrescent（逐渐变无毛的）和 glabrescence（逐渐脱毛或变无毛的过程），后两者并非直接在 glabrous 后加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Morphological analysis: glabr- (a Latin stem meaning smooth or hairless) + -ous (an adjective suffix). The principal derivative is glabrousness; related technical formations include glabrescent, meaning becoming hairless, and glabrescence, the process of becoming hairless. These last two share the stem rather than being direct suffixations of glabrous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hairless（无毛的）是通用表达；bald（秃的）多描述头部缺发，也可指缺少通常应有的覆盖物；smooth（光滑的）强调触感，不能单独保证表面无毛。glabrous 专门描述表面无毛这一生物学特征。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hairless is the general equivalent; bald usually describes a head lacking hair or a surface lacking its usual covering; smooth describes texture and does not itself establish that hairs are absent. Glabrous specifically identifies the biological absence of surface hairs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: glabr-＝光滑无毛：用手掌没有毛这一特征记住 glabrous。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Glabr- means smooth or hairless: picture the hairless surface of your palm.

etymology_story.zh: gloam 属于一个古老的英语暮色词族，与古英语 glōm（薄暮）以及苏格兰语 gloaming（薄暮）密切相关。动词 gloam 通常被解释为从 gloaming 逆构而来；不宜因此把整个词族都解释为现代逆构产物。
etymology_story.en: Gloam belongs to an old English twilight word family associated with Old English glōm and Scots gloaming. The verb gloam is commonly explained as a back-formation from gloaming; that explanation should not be extended to the entire historical word family.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 gloam 作为不可再拆的词基；动词变化为 gloams、gloamed、gloaming。相关名词 gloaming 意为“薄暮”；从现代形式看可分析为 gloam + -ing，但历史上的构词方向不能仅凭这一外形判断。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gloam is an unsegmented base; its verb forms are gloams, gloamed, and gloaming. The related noun gloaming means twilight. Although its modern shape suggests gloam + -ing, that surface analysis alone does not establish the historical direction of formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: twilight（曙暮光）可指日出前或日落后的微光；dusk（黄昏、薄暮）通常侧重傍晚渐暗的阶段；gloaming（薄暮）与 gloam 最接近，同样带文学或苏格兰色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Twilight can refer to the dim light before sunrise or after sunset; dusk usually emphasizes the darkening period in the evening; gloaming is the closest equivalent to gloam and shares its literary or Scottish associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 gloam 与 gloaming 连在一起：太阳落下，暮色渐浓。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link gloam with gloaming: the sun sets and the evening light fades.

senses.meaning_en: Speech-like vocalization that is generally unintelligible to listeners, especially during religious worship.
senses.english_definition: Glossolalia is an activity in which someone produces sounds that resemble speech but are not generally understood as an identifiable language, especially during religious worship.
senses.collocation_en: practice glossolalia; glossolalia in worship
senses.collocation_zh: 进行说方言活动；礼拜中的说方言现象

etymology_story.zh: 这个近代学术词由希腊语 glōssa（舌、语言）和 lalia（言语、说话）组成，与基督教传统中的“说方言”概念有关。这里的中文“方言”是宗教译语，并不等于日常所说的地方方言。
etymology_story.en: This modern scholarly term combines Greek glōssa, meaning tongue or language, with lalia, meaning speech, and is associated with the Christian concept of speaking in tongues. The conventional Chinese religious translation uses 方言, which here does not mean an ordinary regional dialect.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：glosso-（舌、语言）+ -lalia（言语活动）。主要词族：glossolalic（说方言的）、glossolalist（说方言者）；相关组合形式 glosso- 也见于 glossopharyngeal（舌咽的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: glosso- (tongue or language) + -lalia (speech activity). Principal family members include glossolalic, meaning relating to glossolalia, and glossolalist, a person who practices it. The combining form glosso- also occurs in glossopharyngeal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: speaking in tongues（说方言）是宗教语境中的常用对应表达；ecstatic speech（狂喜状态下的言语）范围更广，强调说话时的状态；xenolalia（异语现象）特指据称说出本人未学过的真实语言，不能与 glossolalia 完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Speaking in tongues is the usual religious equivalent; ecstatic speech is broader and emphasizes the speaker's state; xenolalia specifically concerns the claimed use of an actual language the speaker has not learned and is not interchangeable with glossolalia.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: glosso-＝舌，-lalia＝说话：舌头发出似语言的话语。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Glosso- means tongue and -lalia means speech: picture the tongue producing speech-like sounds.

senses.meaning_en: To disguise or explain away something objectionable with smooth or misleading language.
senses.english_definition: If someone glozes over a fault or an unpleasant fact, they use pleasing or misleading explanations to make it seem less serious.

etymology_story.zh: 源自中古英语 glosen（解释、注解，也可指奉承），与 glose（注释、解释）有关，最终可追溯到希腊语 glōssa（舌、语言及需解释的词语）。词义从“作解释”发展为“作有利或似是而非的解释”，继而表示粉饰、掩盖。
etymology_story.en: Gloze comes from Middle English glosen, meaning to explain, annotate, or flatter, associated with glose, an explanatory note, and ultimately Greek glōssa. Its meaning developed from providing an explanation to offering a favorable or specious explanation, and hence to disguising faults.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 gloze 作为完整词基，不作伪词根拆分。变化形式：glozes、glozed、glozing；加 -ing 时去掉末尾不发音的 e。glozing 也可作形容词，表示“花言巧语的、粉饰的”；相关历史词有 gloss（注释；粉饰）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gloze is a complete base rather than a combination of smaller productive elements. Its forms are glozes, glozed, and glozing, with the silent final e dropped before -ing. Glozing can also function adjectivally, meaning flattering or deceptively explanatory; gloss is historically related.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gloss over（轻描淡写、掩饰）强调略过令人不快的细节；whitewash（粉饰、掩盖）强调掩盖过错或责任；sugarcoat（把话说得好听）强调让坏消息较易接受，未必完全隐瞒事实。gloze 尤其带有花言巧语或诡辩式解释的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gloss over emphasizes passing lightly over unpleasant details; whitewash emphasizes concealing wrongdoing or responsibility; sugarcoat emphasizes making bad news easier to accept, without necessarily hiding it entirely. Gloze particularly suggests smooth language or specious explanation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“解释”滑向“粉饰”：把过错解释得太好听，就是 gloze over。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the shift from explanation to excuse: explaining a fault too smoothly becomes glozing over it.

etymology_story.zh: 由希腊语 gnathos（颌）与形容词后缀 -ic 构成，进入英语后用于解剖学等专业描述。词义始终围绕颌及其结构，并未发展出常见的日常引申义。
etymology_story.en: Gnathic was formed from Greek gnathos, meaning jaw, with the adjective suffix -ic, and entered English as an anatomical term. Its meaning has remained centered on the jaws and their structure, without a common everyday figurative extension.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：gnath-（颌）+ -ic（……的）。主要同根词族：gnathology（颌学，研究颌及咀嚼系统）、gnathological（颌学的）、gnathologist（颌学研究者或专家）、prognathic／prognathous（颌前突的）和 prognathism（颌前突）；这些词共享 gnath- 词根，并非都由 gnathic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: gnath- (jaw) + -ic (relating to). Principal related formations include gnathology, the study of the jaws and masticatory system; gnathological; gnathologist; prognathic or prognathous, describing projecting jaws; and prognathism. These share gnath- rather than all deriving directly from gnathic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jaw-related（与颌有关的）是通俗释义；maxillary（上颌的）通常专指上颌；mandibular（下颌的）专指下颌。gnathic 可泛指颌部，因此后两词的适用范围通常更窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jaw-related is the plain-language equivalent; maxillary usually refers specifically to the upper jaw; mandibular refers to the lower jaw. Gnathic can refer to the jaws generally, so the latter two terms usually have narrower applications.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gnath-＝颌，-ic＝有关的；开头 g 不发音，联想咀嚼时活动的颌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gnath- means jaw and -ic means relating to; the initial g is silent. Picture your jaw moving as you chew.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 gonfalon 与意大利语 gonfalone、古法语 gonfalon 相承，最终源于日耳曼语中表示“战斗”和“旗帜、布”的成分。原来的战旗名称后来也用于城邦标志旗及宗教游行中的横悬旗。[《柯林斯词典》词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/gonfalon)
etymology_story.en: English gonfalon came through Italian gonfalone and French forms, ultimately from Germanic elements meaning 'battle' and 'banner or cloth.' The battle-banner name also came to describe civic standards and crossbar banners carried in religious processions. [Collins etymology and definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/gonfalon)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 gonfalon 作为完整的借入词干记忆，不强拆为现代英语词根。关联构词：gonfalon + -ier（表示担任某种职务的人）→ gonfalonier（旗手；历史上的城邦执政官）；相关异体有 gonfanon、gonfalone；复数为 gonfalons。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat gonfalon as a complete borrowed stem rather than dividing it into productive English roots. Related formation: gonfalon + -ier, an occupational suffix, → gonfalonier, 'banner bearer; historical civic magistrate.' Related variant forms include gonfanon and gonfalone; the plural is gonfalons.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: banner（旗帜、旗幡）范围较广，不限定悬挂结构；standard（军旗、仪仗旗）强调其代表军队、统治者或团体的身份；flag（旗）是最普通的统称。gonfalon 尤其突出旗面从横杆垂挂的形制及其礼仪、历史背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Banner is broad and does not specify how the cloth is mounted; standard emphasizes a flag's role in representing an army, ruler, or organization; flag is the general everyday term. Gonfalon particularly suggests a banner hanging from a crossbar in a ceremonial or historical setting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 战斗中的标志布 → 横杆上垂挂的仪仗旗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A identifying cloth in battle → a ceremonial banner hanging from a crossbar.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 gonfalonier 经法语借自意大利语 gonfaloniere，后者以 gonfalone“旗帜”为基础构成，原指执旗者。由于旗帜象征公共权力，这一称号也成为意大利某些共和国高级官职的名称。[《柯林斯词典》词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/gonfalonier)
etymology_story.en: English gonfalonier came through French from Italian gonfaloniere, formed from gonfalone, 'banner,' and originally denoting its bearer. Because the banner represented civic authority, the title also designated senior public offices in certain Italian republics. [Collins etymology and definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/gonfalonier)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代记忆公式：gonfalon（横悬旗）+ -ier（担任某种职务的人）→ gonfalonier（旗手；执政官）；这是对借入词的形态分析，并非断言它最初在英语中组合而成。词族核心为 gonfalon、gonfalonier；gonfaloniere 是相关意大利语形式，复数 gonfaloniers 是英语屈折形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: gonfalon, 'crossbar banner,' + -ier, an occupational suffix, → gonfalonier, 'banner bearer; magistrate.' This analyzes a borrowed word rather than claiming that it was first assembled in English. The core family is gonfalon and gonfalonier; gonfaloniere is the related Italian form, and gonfaloniers is the English plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: standard-bearer（旗手）可指各种旗帜的执持者，也可比喻事业的领军人物；banner-bearer（执旗者）直接描述持旗职责；magistrate（行政长官、司法官）只与其历史官职义近似，不能体现特定的意大利制度背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Standard-bearer covers bearers of various flags and can figuratively mean a leading representative of a cause; banner-bearer directly describes the flag-carrying role. Magistrate approximates the historical office sense but does not identify the particular Italian institution.

senses.collocation_zh: 贪吃油腻丰盛的食物；在宴席上大吃大喝
senses.sentence_en: The guests gormandized on roast meat and rich desserts.
senses.sentence_zh: 宾客们贪婪地大吃烤肉和浓腻的甜点。

senses.meaning_zh: 贪食；对饮食享受的嗜好（罕见，亦作 gourmandise）
senses.meaning_en: Gluttonous eating or indulgence in the pleasures of food; a rare variant of gourmandise.
senses.english_definition: Gormandize is the habit or pleasure of eating indulgently, often to excess.
senses.collocation_en: indulge in gormandize; a taste for gormandize
senses.collocation_zh: 沉溺于饮食享受；对美食享受的嗜好
senses.sentence_en: The essay contrasts plain living with the pleasures of gormandize.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇随笔将朴素生活与纵情饮食的乐趣加以对照。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在十六世纪中叶进入英语，其历史与法语 gourmand“贪食者”和 gourmandise“贪食、饮食享受”有关；法语名词词尾 -ise 后来被重新理解为英语动词后缀 -ize。动词保留了贪婪大吃的意味，名词用法如今十分罕见。[《柯林斯词典》词源、词性与读音](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/gormandize)
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the mid-sixteenth century and is historically connected with French gourmand, 'glutton,' and gourmandise, 'gluttony or enjoyment of food'; the French noun ending -ise was subsequently interpreted as the English verb suffix -ize. The verb retains the idea of greedy eating, while the noun is now very rare. [Collins etymology, parts of speech, and pronunciations](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/gormandize)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代动词分析：gormand（gourmand 的异体，贪食者）+ -ize（动词后缀）→ gormandize；gormandize + -er → gormandizer（贪食者）；gormandizing 可作动名词，表示贪食。相关形式包括 gourmand、gormand、gourmandize、英式异体 gormandise，以及名词 gourmandise、gormandism、gourmandism（贪食或对饮食的嗜好）；动词屈折形式为 gormandizes、gormandized、gormandizing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern verbal analysis: gormand, a variant of gourmand meaning 'glutton,' + the verb suffix -ize → gormandize; gormandize + -er → gormandizer, 'greedy eater.' Gormandizing can function as a gerund denoting greedy eating. Related forms include gourmand, gormand, gourmandize, British gormandise, and the nouns gourmandise, gormandism, and gourmandism, referring to gluttony or enjoyment of food. Verb inflections are gormandizes, gormandized, and gormandizing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gorge（大吃、塞饱）强调吃得很多、直到很饱；devour（狼吞虎咽地吃）强调速度快、胃口急切；overeat（吃得过量）只说明超过适量，不一定带贪婪或文学色彩。gormandize 较书面，常带诙谐或批评意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gorge emphasizes eating a large quantity until very full; devour emphasizes speed and eagerness; overeat simply means eating too much and need not imply greed. Gormandize is more literary and often humorous or disapproving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gormand 是贪食者，加上动词化的 -ize：把“贪吃的人”变成“贪吃的动作”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A gormand is a greedy eater; verbal -ize turns the eater's characteristic into the action of eating greedily.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 grandame、graundame 源于盎格鲁法语及古法语中相当于 grand dame 的形式，其中 dame 指女士或母亲。英语用它称祖母，也可泛指老妇人；今天主要保留在古典或仿古文体中。[《柯林斯词典》词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grandam)
etymology_story.en: Middle English grandame and graundame developed from Anglo-French and Old French forms corresponding to grand dame, with dame meaning 'lady' or 'mother.' English used the word for a grandmother and, more broadly, an old woman; it now survives chiefly in older or deliberately archaic writing. [Collins etymology and definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grandam)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代记忆分析：grand-（表示祖辈关系）+ dam（与旧称“母亲”的 dame 有历史联系）→ grandam；不宜把现代动物繁育义的 dam“母兽”直接当作此词的唯一解释。grandame 是拼写异体；grandams 是复数。grandmother（祖母、外祖母）、grandmaternal（祖母的、外祖母的）在意义上相关，但不是由 grandam 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: grand-, marking a grandparent relationship, + dam, historically connected with dame in the sense 'mother,' → grandam. Its formation should not be explained solely through modern dam meaning 'female animal parent.' Grandame is a spelling variant, and grandams is the plural. Grandmother and grandmaternal are semantically related but are not direct derivatives of grandam.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grandmother（祖母、外祖母）是现代中性标准词；granny（奶奶、姥姥）亲昵而口语化；old woman（老妇人）只对应其泛指年长女性的义项，并不说明亲属关系。grandam 自带古语或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grandmother is the neutral modern standard; granny is affectionate and informal; old woman matches only the broader elderly-woman sense and implies no family relationship. Grandam has an inherently archaic or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: grand- 指向祖辈，dame 的旧义连着母亲：向上一代的母亲称呼 → 祖母。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Grand- points to the grandparent generation, and historical dame connects with 'mother': a mother's-generation term extended upward to grandmother.

senses.meaning_zh: 流行性感冒；流感（旧称）
senses.meaning_en: Influenza; an old-fashioned name for the flu.
senses.english_definition: Grippe is an old-fashioned name for influenza, an infectious illness that can cause fever, body aches, and a cough.
senses.collocation_en: an attack of grippe; suffer from grippe
senses.collocation_zh: 一次流感发作；患流感
senses.sentence_en: In her diary, she wrote that an attack of grippe had kept her in bed for several days.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在日记中写道，一场流感使她卧床了好几天。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在十八世纪借入法语 grippe“流感”，该词通常与 gripper“突然抓住”联系起来，其更早来源属日耳曼语。疾病名称体现了病症仿佛突然攫住人的形象，后来英语日常表达更多使用 influenza 或 flu。[《柯林斯词典》词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grippe)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French grippe, 'influenza,' in the eighteenth century; it is generally connected with gripper, 'to seize suddenly,' of Germanic origin. The disease name evokes an illness suddenly taking hold of someone, while modern English generally uses influenza or flu. [Collins etymology and definitions](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grippe)

morphology_enriched.zh: grippe 是完整的借入词干，不能分析为现代英语 grip + 有意义的后缀 -pe。相关派生：grippe 去末尾 e + -al → grippal（流感的，罕见）；grippe 去末尾 e + -y → grippy（患流感的，旧用）；grippe + -like → grippelike（类似流感的）。la grippe 是保留法语冠词的旧式名称，influenza 和 flu 是同义词而非派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Grippe is a complete borrowed stem, not modern English grip plus a meaningful suffix -pe. Related derivatives are grippe minus final e + -al → grippal, 'relating to influenza,' rare; grippe minus final e + -y → grippy, 'affected with influenza,' dated; and grippe + -like → grippelike, 'resembling influenza.' La grippe retains the French article; influenza and flu are synonyms rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: influenza（流行性感冒）是正式及医学名称；flu（流感）是现代日常名称；la grippe（流感）是保留法语形式的旧称。grippe 同样陈旧；普通感冒 cold 与流感并非同一种疾病，不能作为严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Influenza is the formal and medical term; flu is the usual modern everyday name; la grippe is an older name retaining the French form. Grippe is likewise dated. A cold is a different illness and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“突然抓住”联想到流感突然缠身；记作流感的旧称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of an illness suddenly gripping you: grippe is an old name for influenza.

senses.meaning_zh: 陀螺罗盘；利用陀螺原理和地球自转指示真北的导航仪器
senses.meaning_en: A navigational compass that uses gyroscopic action and Earth's rotation to indicate true north.
senses.english_definition: A gyrocompass is an instrument that uses a spinning gyroscope and Earth's rotation to show the direction of true north, especially on a ship.
senses.collocation_en: gyrocompass heading; gyrocompass error
senses.collocation_zh: 陀螺罗盘航向；陀螺罗盘误差
senses.sentence_en: The officer compared the gyrocompass heading with the reading from the magnetic compass.
senses.sentence_zh: 值班驾驶员将陀螺罗盘航向与磁罗盘的读数进行了比较。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在二十世纪初由 gyro- 和 compass 组合而成，用于命名利用陀螺原理寻找真北的仪器。gyro- 与 gyroscope（陀螺仪）有关，最终源于表示“圆、旋转”的希腊语 gyros。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the early twentieth century from gyro- and compass to name an instrument that uses gyroscopic action to find true north. The element gyro- is associated with gyroscope and ultimately comes from Greek gyros, meaning a circle or turn.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gyro-（陀螺、旋转）+ compass（罗盘）。复数为 gyrocompasses；相关词有 gyroscope（陀螺仪）、gyroscopic（陀螺的）和 gyroscopically（以陀螺方式）；gyrocompass 本身没有常用的加后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: gyro- (gyroscope or rotation) + compass. The plural is gyrocompasses; related words include gyroscope, gyroscopic, and gyroscopically. Gyrocompass itself has no common suffixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: compass（罗盘）是上位词；north-seeking gyro（寻北陀螺仪）强调寻找真北的功能，但不一定指完整的罗盘装置；magnetic compass（磁罗盘）是相关仪器，指向磁北，不能与 gyrocompass 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Compass is the broader term. North-seeking gyro emphasizes the true-north-seeking mechanism and does not necessarily denote a complete compass installation. Magnetic compass names a related instrument that indicates magnetic north, so it is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gyro- 想“旋转陀螺”，compass 想“罗盘”：靠旋转原理寻找真北。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a spinning gyro inside a compass: gyroscopic action helps it find true north.

morphology.text: habilit-（能力，来自拉丁语 habilitas） + -ate（动词后缀） → habilitate（使具备能力）；派生名词 habilitation 表示能力培养。

etymology.text: 来自晚期拉丁语 habilitare 的过去分词 habilitatus，词根与拉丁语 habilitas“能力”相连。记忆重点是帮助一个人具备做事的能力。

usage_note: 正式用语；本课取使人具备能力的及物义。与 rehabilitate 强调恢复已有能力有所区别。

senses.sentence_zh: 获得博士学位后，她在一所德国大学取得了哲学学科的高级任教资格。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 habilitare（使适合、使具备资格），其基础是 habilis（适合的、能干的），与 habere（拥有、持有）有关。英语保留了“使具备能力或资格”的核心意义，并发展出能力培养和大学任教资格认证等专业用法。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin habilitare, meaning to make fit or qualified, based on habilis, meaning suitable or capable, and ultimately related to habere, to have or hold. English retained the idea of making someone capable or qualified in specialist uses involving skill development and academic qualification.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 habilit-（表示能力或资格的黏着词干）+ -ate（动词后缀）；它是借入词，不能把 habilit- 当作独立英语单词。词形有 habilitates、habilitated、habilitating；主要派生词有 habilitation（能力培养；高级任教资格认证）和 habilitative（能力培养的）；同源相关词有 rehabilitate（使康复、恢复能力）、rehabilitation（康复）和 rehabilitative（康复的）。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is habilit- (a bound stem associated with ability or qualification) + -ate (a verb-forming suffix); the word was borrowed, and habilit- is not an independent English word. Inflections are habilitates, habilitated, and habilitating. Principal derivatives are habilitation and habilitative; related words include rehabilitate, rehabilitation, and rehabilitative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: enable（使能够）泛指提供条件或能力；qualify（使具备资格）强调达到任职或从业要求；rehabilitate（使康复、恢复能力）通常强调恢复失去的能力，而临床语境中的 habilitate 通常强调获得尚未形成的能力。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Enable broadly means to provide the means or ability to do something. Qualify emphasizes meeting requirements for a role or activity. Rehabilitate usually emphasizes restoring lost abilities, whereas clinical habilitate typically concerns developing abilities not previously acquired.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“使具备”：生活中具备能力，学术上具备任教资格。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the idea 'make qualified': develop practical abilities or gain academic teaching qualifications.

pronunciation.note: 采用本词条列出的IPA读法，ˈ 后的音节为主重音，ˌ 后的音节为次重音。

forms: 通常作抽象名词；复数 haecceities 可表示不同个体各自的独特性。
family: thisness n. 此性，是相关哲学说法。

morphology.text: haecce-（拉丁语“这个”的成分） + -ity（性质） → haecceity（使“这个”成为独一无二个体的性质）。

etymology.text: 来自中世纪拉丁语 haecceitas，其中 haecce 与拉丁语“这个”有关，-itas 表示性质。通俗地说，就是追问“为什么偏偏是这一个”。

usage_note: 哲学专门用语，常译“此性”或“这个性”；强调某一个体之所以是这个个体。
sentence: The philosopher used haecceity to explain what makes this tree a unique individual.
translation: 这位哲学家用个体独特性来解释是什么让这棵树成为独一无二的个体。
scenario: 哲学讨论区分某个个体与同类事物。
cloze: The philosopher used _____ to explain what makes this tree a unique individual.
collocation:
discuss personal haecceity 讨论个人的个体独特性
the haecceity of an object 某件物体的独特个体性
context_hint: Focus on what makes this particular tree different from every other tree.
hint: Focus on what makes this particular tree different from every other tree.

teaching.contrast: haecceity 强调“是这一个”，quiddity 强调“是什么”。
teaching.sentence: In the seminar, haecceity meant the individuality of this particular person.
teaching.translation: 研讨课上，个体独特性指的是这个特定的人所具有的个体性。

comprehension_check.sentence: Haecceity concerns what makes one individual uniquely itself, rather than what a whole group shares.

senses.meaning_zh: 此性；使某一个体成为“这一个”而非其他个体的独特性
senses.meaning_en: The individual particularity that makes something this specific thing rather than another.
senses.english_definition: The haecceity of something is the particular individuality that makes it this very thing rather than any other thing.
senses.collocation_en: the haecceity of an individual; the concept of haecceity
senses.collocation_zh: 个体的此性；此性概念
senses.sentence_en: The philosopher distinguished the properties shared by all people from the haecceity of each individual.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位哲学家区分了所有人共有的属性与每一个体独有的此性。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自中世纪拉丁语 haecceitas，其基础是带有强调意味、表示“这一个”的拉丁语 haecce。它与邓斯·司各脱的个体化哲学密切相关，用来表达使某物成为特定个体的“此性”。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from medieval Latin haecceitas, based on the emphatic Latin demonstrative haecce, meaning this particular thing. Closely associated with Duns Scotus's account of individuation, it expresses the 'thisness' that makes something a particular individual.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可作学术性分析：haecce-（“这一个”的借入词干）+ -ity（性质、状态）；haecce- 不是可自由使用的英语词。相关专业派生词有 haecceitism（此性主义）和 haecceitist（此性主义者）；讨论多个个体的此性时可用复数 haecceities。
morphology_enriched.en: A learned modern analysis is haecce- (a borrowed stem meaning 'this particular') + -ity (a suffix denoting a quality or state); haecce- is not a free-standing English word. Specialist derivatives include haecceitism and haecceitist. The plural haecceities can refer to the individual particularities of multiple things.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thisness（此性）是最接近的直白对应词；individuality（个体性）范围更广，也可指性格或风格上的独特；particularity（特殊性、个别性）强调具体差异，未必涉及哲学上的个体化根据。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thisness is the closest plain-language equivalent. Individuality is broader and can describe distinctive character or style. Particularity emphasizes specific differences without necessarily referring to the philosophical basis of individuation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 不是泛泛的“一个”，而是眼前的“这一个”：这份不可替代性就是此性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Point to 'this very one': its being this individual is its haecceity.

pronunciation.note: 采用本词条列出的IPA读法，ˈ 后的音节为主重音，ˌ 后的音节为次重音。

forms: 可数名词；复数可用 halfbeaks。
family: half n./adj. 一半；beak n. 喙。

morphology.text: half（一半） + beak（喙） → halfbeak（鱵鱼）；下颌长、上颌短，看起来像只长出半边长喙。

usage_note: 鱼类名称；本课指具有伸长下颌的鱵鱼，不把 halfbeak 当成鸟类的名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 鱵鱼；通常下颌显著长于上颌的细长鱼类
senses.meaning_en: A slender fish typically having a much longer lower jaw than upper jaw.
senses.english_definition: A halfbeak is a slender fish whose lower jaw usually projects well beyond its upper jaw.
senses.collocation_en: freshwater halfbeak; halfbeak fry
senses.collocation_zh: 淡水鱵鱼；鱵鱼幼鱼

etymology_story.zh: 该词在十九世纪由 half（一半）和 beak（喙）组合而成。名称来自这种鱼常见的颌部形态：下颌向前伸长，而上颌较短，看起来只有半边长喙。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the nineteenth century from half and beak. It refers to the fish's characteristic unequal jaws: the lower jaw projects forward while the upper jaw remains short, suggesting half of a long beak.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：half（一半）+ beak（喙），属于名词复合词。复数为 halfbeaks；halfbeak 本身没有常用派生词，beak 的相关词有 beaked（有喙的）、beakless（无喙的）和 beaklike（似喙的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: half + beak, forming a compound noun. The plural is halfbeaks. Halfbeak has no common derivatives of its own; words related to beak include beaked, beakless, and beaklike.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hemiramphid（鱵科鱼）是分类学相关称呼，但不能覆盖所有俗称 halfbeak 的鱼；garfish 在某些地区也可指鱵鱼，但另有其他指称；needlefish（颌针鱼）是相关鱼类，通常上下颌都伸长，并非 halfbeak 的准确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hemiramphid is a taxonomic term for a member of Hemiramphidae, but it does not cover every fish commonly called a halfbeak. Garfish can denote halfbeaks regionally, though it also has other referents. Needlefish names related fish whose two jaws are usually elongated, so it is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: half + beak：只有下半边“喙”特别长，认准长下颌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Half a beak: picture an elongated lower jaw beneath a short upper jaw.

senses.meaning_zh: 𬭶；元素符号 Hs、原子序数为108的人造放射性金属元素
senses.meaning_en: A synthetic radioactive metallic element with symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
senses.english_definition: Hassium is a radioactive chemical element that has atomic number 108 and is produced artificially in nuclear reactions.
senses.collocation_en: hassium isotopes; hassium atoms
senses.collocation_zh: 𬭶的同位素；𬭶原子
senses.sentence_en: The researchers identified hassium atoms by studying their radioactive decay.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员通过研究放射性衰变鉴定出了𬭶原子。

etymology_story.zh: hassium 得名于 Hassia，即德国黑森州的拉丁名称，以纪念该元素在当地达姆施塔特的实验室首次合成。它于1984年首次制得，名称体现的是发现地点，而非某种化学性质。
etymology_story.en: Hassium was named after Hassia, the Latin name of the German state of Hesse, to recognize its first synthesis at a laboratory in Darmstadt. First produced in 1984, the element takes its name from a place rather than a chemical property.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Hass-（取自地名 Hassia）+ -ium（常见元素名后缀）。hassium 通常作不可数名词，没有常用的独立派生词；hassium-270（𬭶-270）等是同位素名称，Hs 是元素符号。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Hass- (from the place name Hassia) + -ium (a common element-name suffix). Hassium is normally uncountable and has no common independent derivatives. Forms such as hassium-270 are isotope designations, and Hs is its chemical symbol.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: element 108（108号元素）是按原子序数给出的等指称名称；Hs 是化学符号，并非另一个普通词汇同义词。两者都指 hassium，没有其他通用的日常同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Element 108 is an equivalent designation based on atomic number. Hs is the chemical symbol rather than a separate ordinary lexical synonym. Both refer to hassium, which has no other common everyday synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Hassia（黑森）+ -ium（元素）：记住“黑森命名的108号元素”，符号 Hs。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hassia plus -ium: the element named for Hesse is number 108, symbol Hs.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读法；音标按词典注音转写为IPA。

forms: 抽象名词，通常不可数。
family: hebetudinous adj. 迟钝的；hebetate v. 使迟钝。

morphology.text: hebetude 作为独立词素记忆；hebetude（去末尾 e） + -inous → hebetudinous（迟钝的）。

etymology.text: 来自晚期拉丁语 hebetudo“迟钝”，与拉丁语 hebes“钝的”相连。从刀刃不锋利的“钝”，联想到头脑不灵敏的状态。

usage_note: 罕见、书面用语，常描述精神不振、反应迟缓的状态。

senses.meaning_zh: 精神迟钝；昏沉；思维不敏锐的状态
senses.meaning_en: Mental dullness or sluggishness.
senses.english_definition: Hebetude is a state in which you feel mentally dull and find it difficult to think clearly or respond quickly.
senses.collocation_en: mental hebetude; a state of hebetude
senses.collocation_zh: 精神迟钝；昏沉的状态
senses.sentence_en: After a sleepless night, she struggled to shake off her hebetude.
senses.sentence_zh: 一夜未眠后，她努力摆脱昏昏沉沉的状态。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 hebetudo，意为“迟钝”，与 hebes“钝的、不敏锐的”有关。表示刀刃或感官不锐利的“钝”，也被用于描述思维迟缓。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin hebetudo, meaning dullness, related to hebes, meaning blunt or lacking sharpness. The idea of a blunt edge or dulled senses also applies to a mind that responds slowly.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 hebetude 作为整体词学习，不宜机械拆成能自由组合的词根和词缀。相关词族包括 hebetudinous（精神迟钝的）、hebetate（使迟钝）和 hebetation（迟钝化）；hebetudinous 使用拉丁语延伸词干 hebetudin-，不是简单去掉末尾 e 再加 -inous。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hebetude is normally learned as a whole word rather than as a freely productive root-and-suffix combination. Its related family includes hebetudinous, meaning mentally dull, hebetate, meaning to make dull, and hebetation, meaning dulling; hebetudinous uses the extended Latin stem hebetudin-, rather than simply dropping the final e and adding -inous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dullness（迟钝）最宽泛，可指智力、感官或事物缺乏生气；lethargy（困倦、无精打采）更强调精力不足；torpor（麻木、迟缓）强调身心活动明显减弱。hebetude 是罕见的正式用词，尤其突出精神不敏锐。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dullness is broad and can describe limited mental sharpness, weakened sensation, or lack of interest; lethargy emphasizes low energy; torpor suggests markedly reduced physical or mental activity. Hebetude is a rare, formal word emphasizing mental dullness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“钝”的共同逻辑：刀刃钝了切不动，头脑钝了想不快。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the shared idea of bluntness: a blunt blade cuts poorly, and a dulled mind thinks slowly.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读法；音标按词典注音转写为IPA。

forms: 可数名词；复数 hectograms；单位符号 hg。
family: gram n. 克；kilogram n. 千克。

morphology.text: hecto-（一百） + gram（克） → hectogram（百克）。

usage_note: 质量单位，1 hectogram = 100 grams；不要与 kilogram（一千克）混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 百克；等于一百克的质量单位
senses.meaning_en: A metric unit of mass equal to 100 grams.
senses.english_definition: A hectogram is a unit of mass equal to one hundred grams, or one tenth of a kilogram.
senses.collocation_en: one hectogram of cheese; price per hectogram
senses.collocation_zh: 一百克奶酪；每百克的价格
senses.sentence_en: The shop lists the price of cheese per hectogram.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家商店按每百克标示奶酪的价格。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 hectogramme，是公制单位命名体系中的词。hecto- 最终源自希腊语 hekaton“一百”，gramme 则最终与希腊语表示小重量单位的 gramma 有关。
etymology_story.en: Hectogram was borrowed from French hectogramme as part of the metric naming system. Hecto- ultimately comes from Greek hekaton, meaning a hundred, while gramme ultimately relates to Greek gramma, a small unit of weight.

morphology_enriched.zh: hecto-（一百倍）+ gram（克）→ hectogram（百克），单位符号为 hg。复数为 hectograms；hectogramme 是另一种拼写，复数为 hectogrammes；该词没有常用的动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Hecto-, meaning one hundred times, + gram forms hectogram, with the unit symbol hg. The plural is hectograms; hectogramme is an alternative spelling, with the plural hectogrammes. There are no common verb or adjective derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hectogramme（百克）只是拼写变体；100 grams（一百克）和 one tenth of a kilogram（十分之一千克）是数值完全相同的表达。它们没有质量大小上的差别，只是单位和表达方式不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hectogramme is simply a spelling variant; 100 grams and one tenth of a kilogram express exactly the same mass. The difference lies only in spelling or the choice of units.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hecto- 锁定“一百”：1 hectogram = 100 grams。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let hecto- signal one hundred: 1 hectogram = 100 grams.

morphology.text: hee（拟声） + haw（拟声） → heehaw（驴叫声）；两段声音合起来模仿驴叫。

senses.english_definition: When a donkey heehaws, it makes its characteristic loud cry.
senses.collocation_en: a donkey heehawing; heehaw loudly

etymology_story.zh: 这是模仿驴叫声形成的英语拟声词，hee 和 haw 对应叫声中交替出现的两段声音。后来也用于形容或表示像驴叫一样响亮、粗放的笑声。
etymology_story.en: Heehaw is an English imitative formation whose two parts reproduce the alternating sounds of a donkey's bray. It was also extended to a loud, coarse laugh resembling that cry.

morphology_enriched.zh: hee + haw 是拟声组合，不是普通的词根加词缀结构；也写作 hee-haw。名词复数和动词第三人称单数为 heehaws，过去式及过去分词为 heehawed，现在分词为 heehawing；带连字符的拼写相应为 hee-haws、hee-hawed、hee-hawing。
morphology_enriched.en: Hee + haw is an imitative combination rather than an ordinary root-and-affix structure; the word is also written hee-haw. Its noun plural and third-person singular verb are heehaws, its past tense and past participle are heehawed, and its present participle is heehawing; the hyphenated forms are hee-haws, hee-hawed, and hee-hawing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bray（驴叫；发出驴叫般的声音）是描述驴叫的常规词；guffaw（放声大笑）强调笑声响亮、奔放；cackle（咯咯笑）强调尖锐、断续的声音。heehaw 特别保留了驴叫的声音形象，用于人的笑声时常带揶揄意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bray is the standard word for a donkey's cry; guffaw emphasizes a loud, unrestrained laugh; cackle suggests sharp, broken laughter. Heehaw specifically evokes a donkey's sound and often sounds mocking when applied to human laughter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 读出“hee—haw”：先听见驴叫，再联想到同样粗响的笑声。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Say hee—haw aloud: hear the donkey first, then picture a laugh with the same rough sound.

forms: 可数名词；复数 hemidemisemiquavers。

morphology.text: hemi-（一半） + demisemiquaver（三十二分音符） → hemidemisemiquaver（六十四分音符），时值再减半。

etymology.text: 十九世纪英语在 demisemiquaver 前加上希腊语来源的 hemi-“一半”，用来命名更短一半的音符。沿着不断减半的时值记忆。

usage_note: 主要用于英式音乐术语；美式通常说 sixty-fourth note。时值是全音符的六十四分之一。

senses.meaning_zh: 六十四分音符
senses.meaning_en: A sixty-fourth note.
senses.english_definition: A hemidemisemiquaver is a musical note that lasts one sixty-fourth as long as a semibreve, or whole note.

senses.sentence_zh: 这一乐段以一串快速的六十四分音符结束。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在英语中由 hemi-“一半”加在 demisemiquaver“三十二分音符”之前构成，表示时值再减半。词中的 hemi-、demi- 和 semi- 都有“一半”的含义，依次把 quaver“八分音符”的时值减至六十四分音符。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in English by adding hemi-, meaning half, to demisemiquaver, a thirty-second note, to indicate another halving of duration. Hemi-, demi-, and semi- each mean half, successively reducing a quaver, or eighth note, to a sixty-fourth note.

morphology_enriched.zh: hemi-（一半）+ demisemiquaver（三十二分音符）→ hemidemisemiquaver（六十四分音符）。完整命名链为 quaver（八分音符）→ semiquaver（十六分音符）→ demisemiquaver（三十二分音符）→ hemidemisemiquaver（六十四分音符）；复数为 hemidemisemiquavers，没有常用的其他词性派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Hemi-, meaning half, + demisemiquaver, a thirty-second note, forms hemidemisemiquaver, a sixty-fourth note. The naming sequence is quaver, eighth note → semiquaver, sixteenth note → demisemiquaver, thirty-second note → hemidemisemiquaver, sixty-fourth note. The plural is hemidemisemiquavers, and there are no common derivatives belonging to other parts of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sixty-fourth note（六十四分音符）是同一音符的美式英语名称；64th note 是数字拼写形式。两者与主要用于英式英语的 hemidemisemiquaver 时值完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sixty-fourth note is the American English name for the same note; 64th note is its numerical spelling. Both have exactly the same duration as hemidemisemiquaver, which is chiefly British usage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 quaver 的八分之一开始，semi、demi、hemi 连续减半：1/8 → 1/16 → 1/32 → 1/64。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a quaver at one eighth and halve it for semi, demi, and hemi: 1/8 → 1/16 → 1/32 → 1/64.

forms: 修辞手法名称，本课作抽象名词使用。

morphology.text: hen（一个） + dia（通过） + dyoin（两个） → hendiadys（二词一意）；这是希腊语短语形成的修辞术语。

etymology.text: 经晚期拉丁语进入英语，源头是希腊语 hen dia dyoin，字面为“一个意思通过两个词表达”。把两个词看成合力说清一件事。

senses.meaning_zh: 重言法；用两个并列词表达一个整体意思的修辞手法
senses.meaning_en: The expression of a single idea through two coordinated words.
senses.english_definition: Hendiadys is a way of expressing one idea with two words joined by 'and', often instead of using one word to modify the other.

senses.sentence_zh: 用“杯与金”来表达“金杯”的说法，体现了重言法。

etymology_story.zh: 经拉丁语修辞术语传入英语，最终源自希腊语短语 hen dia dyoin，字面意思是“通过两个表达一个”。这个名称直接概括了其修辞机制：两个并列的词共同表达一个整体概念。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Latin rhetorical terminology and ultimately comes from the Greek phrase hen dia dyoin, literally one through two. Its name describes the device itself: two coordinated words convey a single combined idea.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 hendiadys 作为整体借词使用；hen（一个）+ dia（通过）+ dyoin（两个）属于历史来源分析，不是现代英语的自由构词公式。相关形容词为 hendiadic（重言法的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats hendiadys as a whole borrowed word; hen, meaning one, + dia, meaning through, + dyoin, meaning two, explains its historical source rather than a productive English formation. The related adjective is hendiadic, meaning involving hendiadys.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该术语没有完全等义的常用近义词。coordination（并列）只说明语法关系，不一定表达一个概念；periphrasis（迂说）指用较长表达替代简短说法；hendiadys 特指以两个并列词表达一个整体意思。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Coordination names a grammatical relationship without necessarily expressing a single concept; periphrasis uses a longer expression in place of a shorter one; hendiadys specifically conveys one combined idea through two coordinated words.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住词源的“一通过二”：两个词，一层意思。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the source phrase one through two: two words, one combined idea.
