etymology_story.zh: tamoxifen 是现代药物命名中创造的通用名，并非由普通英语词自然演变而来。其名称有时被推测与 trans-、含氧相关片段及 clomiphene 等药名的片段有关，但这种解释不宜当作已确定的逐段词源。
etymology_story.en: Tamoxifen is a coined modern generic drug name rather than a word inherited through ordinary English usage. Its formation has been tentatively associated with trans-, oxygen-related elements, and fragments resembling those in clomiphene, but this should not be presented as a certain element-by-element derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 tamoxifen 作为不可进一步作普通构词分析的完整药名处理，没有常用的直接派生词族。相关复合形式有 tamoxifen + resistant → tamoxifen-resistant（对他莫昔芬耐药的）、tamoxifen + induced → tamoxifen-induced（他莫昔芬诱导的）；这些是复合修饰语，并非药名内部的词根、词缀拆解。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tamoxifen is treated as a complete drug name without a productive everyday root-and-affix analysis or a common direct derivational family. Related compounds include tamoxifen + resistant → tamoxifen-resistant and tamoxifen + induced → tamoxifen-induced; these are compound modifiers, not internal analyses of the drug name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可完全互换的普通近义词。anti-oestrogen（抗雌激素药）强调药理作用；selective oestrogen receptor modulator（选择性雌激素受体调节剂，SERM）表示其所属药物类别；breast cancer medicine（乳腺癌治疗药物）表示更宽泛的用途类别，三者均不专指他莫昔芬。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no fully interchangeable everyday synonym. Anti-oestrogen emphasizes its pharmacological action; selective oestrogen receptor modulator, or SERM, identifies its drug class; breast cancer medicine describes a broader treatment category. None uniquely identifies tamoxifen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记药名：tamoxifen → 他莫昔芬 → 在乳腺组织中阻断雌激素作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole drug name: tamoxifen → blocking oestrogen effects in breast tissue.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第一音节；英式读法词尾不读 r，美式常带 /r/ 音。

forms: 可数名词；复数 monickers。更常见拼写 moniker，复数 monikers。
family: moniker 同义拼写；monickered 被冠以某个名号的。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆，monicker 和 moniker 是同一词的两种拼写。相关动词可构成 monicker + -ed → monickered（被冠以某个名号的）；词尾 -er 在这里不表示“做某事的人”。

etymology.text: monicker 是 moniker 的拼写变体。它很可能经谢尔塔语 mŭnnik 传入英语，并与爱尔兰语 ainm（名字）有关；抓住“名字”这条线，就能记住它在口语里表示外号、绰号。

usage_note: 非正式可数名词；moniker 更常见，monicker 也正确。常与 earn、give、use 连用；本课用来指外号，不表示签名笔迹。

senses.meaning_zh: 名字；外号；绰号，属非正式用语，是 moniker 的拼写变体
senses.meaning_en: an informal name or nickname; a variant spelling of moniker
senses.english_definition: A person's monicker is a name or nickname by which people know them.
senses.collocation_en: earn the monicker; an unusual monicker
senses.collocation_zh: 获得某个绰号；一个不寻常的名字或绰号
senses.sentence_en: His speed on the football field earned him the monicker 'Lightning'.
senses.sentence_zh: 他在足球场上的速度为他赢得了“闪电”的绰号。

etymology_story.zh: monicker 是 moniker 的拼写变体，后者见于十九世纪英国俚语，表示名字或别名。其确切来源不明；谢尔塔语以及与爱尔兰语 ainm（名字）的联系，均属于被提出过的解释，而非定论。
etymology_story.en: Monicker is a variant spelling of moniker, recorded in nineteenth-century British slang for a name or alias. Its exact origin is uncertain; connections with Shelta and with Irish ainm, meaning 'name', are proposed explanations rather than established facts.

morphology_enriched.zh: monicker 在现代英语中是单纯词，不能拆成有明确意义的 moni- + -cker，词尾也不是表示人的 -er。复数为 monickers；常见拼写为 moniker，复数 monikers；monickered、monikered 可表示“被冠以某名号的”，属于较少见的动词或分词形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Monicker is a simple lexical base in modern English, not a meaningful combination of moni- and -cker, and its ending is not the agent suffix -er. Its plural is monickers; the usual spelling is moniker, with plural monikers. Monickered and monikered occur as less common verbal or participial forms meaning 'given a particular name'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nickname（绰号）是最直接、最日常的近义词；alias（别名、化名）常强调另一身份或替代姓名；sobriquet（绰号、雅号）较书面，常带描述人物特点的意味。monicker 更口语化，也可以泛指名字。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nickname is the closest everyday equivalent; alias often suggests an alternative identity or assumed name; sobriquet is more literary and often describes a person's characteristics. Monicker is informal and can also refer simply to someone's name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 monicker 想成贴在人身上的“名字标签”：既可以是真名，也可以是绰号。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a name tag attached to someone: their monicker may be their name or their nickname.

meaning: 痴迷某领域的人；技术迷

pronunciation.note: 英式读法不读 r，元音 /ɜː/ 要读足；美式常读 /nɝːd/。

forms: 可数名词；复数 nerds。
family: nerdy 痴迷某领域的；nerdish 书呆子气的；nerdishness 书呆子气。

morphology.text: nerd 在现代英语中作为不可再拆的独立词素记忆。nerd + -y → nerdy（痴迷某领域的、书呆子气的）；-y 把名词变为描述这种特点的形容词。

etymology.text: nerd 在二十世纪中期的英语里流行起来，词典把它与苏斯博士故事中的生物名 nerd 联系起来，认为这可能是它的来源。如今可用它形容对技术或某门知识特别入迷的人。

relations.meaning: 痴迷某领域的；书呆子气的

usage_note: 非正式用语，常说 a computer nerd、a science nerd；可带贬义，也可用于自嘲或亲昵赞许，取决于语气。本课聚焦“某领域的痴迷者”。

senses.meaning_zh: 书呆子；被认为过于用功、拘谨或不善社交的人，有时含贬义
senses.meaning_en: someone regarded as overly studious or socially awkward, sometimes used disapprovingly
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a nerd, they may mean that the person studies a lot or seems awkward in social situations.
senses.collocation_en: a school nerd; a stereotypical nerd
senses.collocation_zh: 学校里的书呆子；刻板印象中的书呆子

senses.sentence_zh: 上学时，因为他更喜欢读书而非参加聚会，别人就叫他书呆子。

senses.meaning_zh: 对某一领域极为痴迷且颇有研究的人；某领域的迷
senses.meaning_en: someone with an intense interest in and detailed knowledge of a particular subject
senses.english_definition: A nerd is someone who is very interested in a particular subject and enjoys learning a great deal about it.
senses.collocation_en: a computer nerd; a science nerd
senses.collocation_zh: 计算机迷；科学迷
senses.sentence_en: I'm a bit of a history nerd, so I could spend hours in this museum.
senses.sentence_zh: 我算是个历史迷，所以在这座博物馆里待上几个小时也不会腻。

senses.meaning_zh: 痴迷地钻研或兴奋地谈论某事，通常用于非正式短语 nerd out
senses.meaning_en: to become enthusiastically absorbed in a subject, usually in the informal phrase nerd out
senses.english_definition: If you nerd out about or over something, you enthusiastically discuss or explore its details because you find it fascinating.
senses.collocation_en: nerd out about technology; nerd out over the details
senses.collocation_zh: 兴致勃勃地钻研或谈论科技；痴迷于各种细节
senses.sentence_en: We spent the evening nerding out over old maps.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们整个晚上都兴致勃勃地研究旧地图。

etymology_story.zh: nerd 在二十世纪中期成为英语俚语；苏斯博士于 1950 年出版的《If I Ran the Zoo》中使用过 Nerd 作为虚构生物的名字，但它与后来的俚语之间是否存在直接传承关系仍不确定。词义后来从带贬义的“书呆子”扩展为也可带自豪意味的“某领域痴迷者”。
etymology_story.en: Nerd became English slang in the mid-twentieth century; Dr. Seuss used Nerd as the name of an imaginary creature in his 1950 book If I Ran the Zoo, though a direct connection with the later slang is uncertain. Its meaning later broadened from a disparaging label for a bookish or awkward person to a sometimes proud description of a dedicated enthusiast.

morphology_enriched.zh: nerd 是单纯词，也可由名词零派生为动词，常见于 nerd out。词族包括 nerd + -y → nerdy（书呆子气的；痴迷某领域的），nerdy + -ness → nerdiness（书呆子气；痴迷特质），nerdy + -ly → nerdily（带书呆子气地）；另有较非正式的 nerddom（书呆子或爱好者群体及其文化）。屈折形式包括 nerds、nerded、nerding、nerdier、nerdiest。
morphology_enriched.en: Nerd is a simple base and can also become a verb through conversion, commonly in nerd out. Its family includes nerd + -y → nerdy, nerdy + -ness → nerdiness, and nerdy + -ly → nerdily; the informal nerddom refers to nerds collectively or their culture. Inflected forms include nerds, nerded, nerding, nerdier, and nerdiest.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: geek（极客、迷）与 nerd 高度重叠，常突出技术或特定兴趣；enthusiast（爱好者）语气中性，不暗示社交特点；bookworm（书虫）专指爱读书的人。nerd 可强调深入钻研，也可能保留“不善社交”的刻板印象，具体语气取决于上下文。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Geek overlaps strongly with nerd and often highlights technology or a specialized interest; enthusiast is neutral and implies nothing about social skills; bookworm specifically describes someone who loves reading. Nerd can emphasize deep knowledge but may retain a stereotype of social awkwardness, depending on context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个核心画面：沉浸在喜欢的领域里的人；nerdy 描述这种特质，nerd out 表示进入这种状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone absorbed in a favourite subject: nerdy describes the trait, and nerd out means entering that enthusiastic state.

pronunciation.note: 采用 Merriam-Webster 名词读音 /vɪs/，不按岛名读 /viːs/。

forms: 名词复数为 vires；不是英语规则复数 vises。
family: vis viva 活力（历史物理学术语）；vires 力量（复数形式）

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。借助真实复合术语识别：vis（力） + viva（活的） → vis viva（活力，历史物理学用语）。

etymology.text: 英语直接借入拉丁语 vis，原义就是“力、力量”。看到这个短词，可联想拉丁语留在英语书面表达中的“力”。

usage_note: 罕见的书面名词，日常通常说 force 或 power。小写 vis 表示力；大写 Vis 可指地名，不属于本课。

senses.meaning_zh: 力；力量；作用力，属罕见或历史性用语，常见于拉丁语术语
senses.meaning_en: force, power, or operative strength, chiefly in rare or historical Latin expressions
senses.english_definition: Vis is an uncommon word for force or power, usually encountered in expressions borrowed from Latin.
senses.collocation_en: vis viva; vis inertiae
senses.collocation_zh: 活力，历史物理学术语；惯性力，亦可比喻惰性或抗拒改变的倾向
senses.sentence_en: The historian explained how the term vis viva was used in early mechanics.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位历史学者解释了早期力学中如何使用 vis viva 这一术语。

etymology_story.zh: vis 直接借自拉丁语 vīs，原义是“力、力量”。它在英语中主要保留于学术或历史性的拉丁语表达，如 vis viva，而没有发展成日常常用词。
etymology_story.en: Vis was borrowed directly from Latin vīs, meaning 'force' or 'strength'. In English it survives chiefly in learned or historical Latin expressions such as vis viva rather than as an everyday word.

morphology_enriched.zh: vis 是整体借入的单纯词，不宜在现代英语中继续拆分。相关表达包括 vis + viva（活的）→ vis viva（历史力学中的“活力”），以及 vis + inertiae（惯性的）→ vis inertiae（惯性力；比喻惰性）；这些是拉丁语短语，不是英语后缀派生，也不存在常用的英语直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Vis is a simple borrowed word without a further productive breakdown in modern English. Related expressions include vis + viva ('living') → vis viva, a historical mechanics term, and vis + inertiae ('of inertia') → vis inertiae, referring to inertia or figurative resistance to change. These are Latin phrases, not English suffix formations, and there is no common direct English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: force（力、作用力）是最接近的现代对应词；strength（力量、强度）强调具有多大的力或抵抗能力；power（力量、能力）范围更广，在物理学中还专指功率。具体历史术语中的 vis 不一定能用这些词直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Force is the closest modern equivalent; strength emphasizes the degree of force or capacity to resist; power has a broader sense of capacity and a specific technical meaning in physics. These words are not automatically interchangeable within historical expressions containing vis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vis 的真实拉丁语核心就是“力”；看到 vis viva，就抓住“活的力”这一历史命名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The actual Latin core is 'force'; vis viva literally supplies the historical image of 'living force'.

pronunciation.note: 采用 Collins 所列英语读音 /blæŋk/；法语读音另有鼻化元音。

forms: 可数用法复数为 blancs；表示烹煮用汤汁时常作物质名词。
family: blancmange 牛奶冻；vin blanc 白葡萄酒（法语借入的表达）

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。词源助记（法语历史组合）：blanc（白） + manger（食物） → blancmange（牛奶冻）。

etymology.text: 来自法语 blanc，承自古法语，原义是“白色的”。英语把它用于法式烹饪的清煮汤汁；联想浅色汤汁，可帮助记住这个借词。

senses.meaning_zh: 法式白煮液；通常加入面粉和柠檬汁、用于帮助食材保持浅色的烹煮液
senses.meaning_en: a cooking liquid, typically containing flour and lemon juice, used to help ingredients retain a pale colour
senses.english_definition: A blanc is a cooking liquid usually made with water, flour, and lemon juice, in which food is cooked to help keep it pale.
senses.collocation_en: prepare a blanc; cook in a blanc
senses.collocation_zh: 调制白煮液；在白煮液中烹煮
senses.sentence_en: The chef cooked the artichoke hearts in a blanc to help preserve their colour.
senses.sentence_zh: 厨师用白煮液烹煮洋蓟心，以帮助保持其原有的浅色。

etymology_story.zh: blanc 借自法语 blanc，意思是“白色的”，英语中的这一烹饪用法与保持食材浅色有关。法语中的形容词身份并不意味着 blanc 在普通英语中也具有常用的独立形容词用法。
etymology_story.en: Blanc was borrowed from French blanc, meaning 'white', and its English culinary use relates to keeping food pale. Its status as an adjective in French does not make it a commonly used independent adjective in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: blanc 在英语中是整体借入的单纯词，没有常用的直接派生词族。blancmange（牛奶冻）是有历史联系的另一借词，源于古法语表示“白色食物”的组合；它不宜当作现代英语中自由使用的 blanc + mange 构词公式。
morphology_enriched.en: Blanc is a simple borrowed base in English and has no common direct derivational family. Blancmange is a historically related borrowing from an Old French expression meaning 'white food'; it should not be treated as a freely productive modern English combination of blanc and mange.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的日常近义词。cooking liquid（烹煮液）是上位词；poaching liquid（水波煮或温和浸煮用液体）强调烹煮方法；court bouillon（法式酸味香料煮汁）通常含酸和芳香配料，与常含面粉、用于保色的 blanc 配方及用途不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Cooking liquid is the broader category; poaching liquid emphasizes the cooking method; court bouillon is typically an acidic, aromatic cooking liquid and differs in preparation and purpose from the often flour-containing blanc used to preserve pale colour.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 法语 blanc＝白：白煮液的记忆重点是“帮助食材保持浅色”，并非“清澈的汤”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: French blanc means 'white': remember a cooking liquid that helps food stay pale, rather than picturing a clear broth.

meaning: （非正式提醒）你的裤子拉链开了

pronunciation.note: 按 American Heritage 所列美式字母名连读：X、Y、Z；重音落在最后的 Z。

forms: 固定字母缩略语；不变形，不加复数或时态词尾。
family: examine 检查；zipper 拉链；二者是缩略表达的组成词，不是 XYZ 的派生词。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；这是英语字母缩略表达。ex(amine) + y(our) + z(ipper) → XYZ（检查你的拉链），X 取 examine 中的 /eks/ 提示。

etymology.text: 由英语 examine your zipper（检查你的拉链）缩略而来：用 X 提示 examine，再取 your 和 zipper 的首字母 Y、Z，成为提醒裤子拉链未拉好的暗号。

usage_note: 常写成大写 XYZ；用于熟人之间委婉提醒裤子拉链开了。这里不教坐标轴或占位字母义；说话时仍应留意场合和对方感受。

morphology_enriched.en: Formation: X [suggesting examine] + Y [your] + Z [zipper] → XYZ; it is pronounced as separate letters rather than formed from a root and affixes. etymology_story.en: The verb comes from Middle English fryggen, meaning to wriggle, and later acquired sexual and other vulgar uses; its deeper origin is uncertain. The refrigerator noun independently abbreviates refrigerator and has a different pronunciation; see [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frig) and [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/frig).

morphology_enriched.zh: 动词 frig 是现代英语中的简单词干：frigs（第三人称单数）、frigged（过去式及过去分词）、frigging（现在分词及动名词），加 -ed、-ing 时双写 g；frigging 另可作不礼貌的语气加强词。冰箱名词 frig 是 refrigerator 的截短形式，复数 frigs，通常拼作 fridge，复数 fridges；两组形式属于不同来源。此词没有可靠的统一 CEFR 定级或固定考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: The verb frig is a simple modern stem: frigs is the third-person singular, frigged the past tense and past participle, and frigging the present participle and gerund; g doubles before -ed and -ing. Frigging also functions as an impolite intensifier. The refrigerator noun frig is a clipping of refrigerator, with plural frigs; the usual spelling is fridge, plural fridges, and this family has a separate origin. No reliable uniform CEFR level or examination classification is established.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Have sex is neutral where the corresponding sense of frig is vulgar; masturbate is neutral and suitable in medical contexts for the other sexual sense; mess around corresponds to frig around but is generally milder.

etymology_story.zh: Pommy 在二十世纪初的澳大利亚英语中已有记录，但确切来源尚无定论；一种常见解释把它与 immigrant（移民）及 pomegranate（石榴）的谐音或文字游戏联系起来。不能把 Jimmy Grant → pomegranate → Pommy 的完整链条当作已证实的历史，参见 [Oxford 词条](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/pommy)。
etymology_story.en: Pommy is recorded in Australian English from the early twentieth century, but its exact origin remains uncertain; a familiar explanation connects it with wordplay involving immigrant and pomegranate. The full Jimmy Grant → pomegranate → Pommy sequence should not be presented as established history; see [Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/pommy).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可联系 Pom + -y → Pommy，拼写双写 m；这种分析不证明各形式在历史上出现的先后。相关形式：Pom、复数 Poms；Pommy、复数 Pommies；异体 Pommie、复数 Pommies；也常小写。形容词通常不分级，没有常用的进一步派生词族；无可靠的标准 CEFR 定级或固定考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, the form can be related to Pom + -y → Pommy, with doubled m; this analysis does not establish the historical order of the forms. Related forms are Pom, plural Poms; Pommy, plural Pommies; and the alternative Pommie, plural Pommies; lowercase spellings also occur. The adjective is normally ungraded, and there is no common extended derivative family or reliably established CEFR or examination classification.

etymology_story.zh: 爱尔兰组织成员义由 Provisional（临时派的）截短并加非正式称呼后缀 -o 构成；欧洲抗议者义则与 provocateur（挑衅者、鼓动者）的缩略形式有关。美国城市名另源于皮毛商 Étienne Provost 的姓氏，这三个来源应分别处理，参见 [Collins 词条](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/provo)。
etymology_story.en: The Irish membership term clips Provisional and adds the informal ending -o, whereas the European protester term is associated with a shortened form of provocateur. The American city name separately derives from the surname of fur trader Étienne Provost; these origins should be kept distinct, as reflected in [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/provo).

morphology_enriched.zh: 爱尔兰成员义：Prov-〔Provisional 的截短形式〕+ -o → Provo，复数 Provos；相关名称为 Provisional IRA。欧洲抗议者义：与 provocateur 的截短有关，单数 provo 或 Provo，复数 provos 或 Provos；城市名 Provo 是不可按普通词缀拆解的专名。无可靠的标准 CEFR 定级或固定考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Irish membership sense: Prov- [clipped from Provisional] + -o → Provo, plural Provos; the associated organizational name is Provisional IRA. The European protester sense is a clipping associated with provocateur, with singular provo or Provo and plural provos or Provos. The city name Provo is a proper name without a productive affix analysis. No reliable standard CEFR level or examination classification is established.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Provisional IRA member（爱尔兰共和军临时派成员）是该组织成员义的中性、明确表达；IRA member（爱尔兰共和军成员）范围较宽，不限定临时派；Irish republican（爱尔兰共和主义者）表示政治立场，不必然表示任何组织成员身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Provisional IRA member is the neutral, explicit equivalent of the Irish membership sense; IRA member is broader and does not specify the faction; Irish republican describes a political position and does not necessarily imply organizational membership.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 爱尔兰语境看 Prov-，想到 Provisional（临时派）；欧洲历史语境想到抗议运动；犹他州语境想到城市。
mnemonic_anchor.en: In an Irish context, connect Prov- with Provisional; in European history, think of the protest movement; in Utah, think of the city.

pronunciation.note: 英式读音；重音符号 ˈ 表示主重音。

forms: 第三人称单数 smithereens；过去式、过去分词 smithereened；现在分词 smithereening。注意名词 smithereens（碎片）也以 s 结尾。
family: smithereens（名词，细小碎片）；动词 smithereen 表示使物体成为这样的碎片。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆，不拆成 smith（铁匠）。smithereen + -ing → smithereening（动名词：打碎这一动作）；保留词尾 n 后接 -ing。

etymology.text: 这个词与 smithereens（细小碎片）相连：smithereens 源自爱尔兰盖尔语 smidirīn，可追到 smiodar（碎片）。可以从“一地细碎残片”的画面记住英语动词 smithereen 的“打碎”义。

usage_note: smithereen 是少见的及物动词，表示把某物打碎，日常更常用 smash 或 shatter。smithereens 是复数名词，表示细小碎片，常见于 smash something to smithereens（把某物砸得粉碎）。

senses.meaning_en: A tiny fragment; the singular is rare, and the usual form is smithereens.
senses.english_definition: Smithereens are the very small pieces left when something has been smashed or blown apart; the singular smithereen is rare.
senses.collocation_en: smash something to smithereens; blow something to smithereens
senses.collocation_zh: 把某物砸得粉碎；把某物炸得粉碎

etymology_story.zh: smithereen 与常见复数名词 smithereens（细碎片）相联系，动词表达把东西变成这些碎片的动作。smithereens 通常被认为来自爱尔兰语 smidirín（小碎片），与 smiodar（碎片）及指小后缀 -ín 有关；参见 [Collins 动词词条](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/smithereen)及 [Oxford 词源说明](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/smithereens)。
etymology_story.en: Smithereen is related to the familiar plural noun smithereens, and the verb expresses the action of reducing something to such fragments. Smithereens is generally traced to Irish smidirín, a small fragment, associated with smiodar and the diminutive suffix -ín; see the [Collins verb entry](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/smithereen) and [Oxford's origin note](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/smithereens).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 smithereen 作为整体词干，不拆成 smith（铁匠）加其他部分。名词通常用复数 smithereens；罕用动词的屈折形式为 smithereens、smithereened、smithereening，词尾 n 不双写；smithereened 也可作分词性形容词。-een 的指小联系属于历史来源，不是此词中可自由替换的现代后缀；无可靠的标准 CEFR 定级或固定考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats smithereen as a whole stem rather than smith plus additional elements. The noun normally appears as smithereens; the rare verb has the inflections smithereens, smithereened, and smithereening, without doubling n, and smithereened can also serve as a participial adjective. The diminutive association of -een belongs to its history rather than a freely interchangeable modern suffix here. No reliable standard CEFR level or examination classification is established.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shatter（使碎裂）强调突然破裂成许多片；smash（砸碎、撞毁）强调猛烈撞击，未必形成细屑；pulverize（使粉碎、磨成粉）强调碎得极细。smithereen 强调变成细碎残片，但远不如这些动词常用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shatter emphasizes sudden breakage into many pieces; smash emphasizes forceful impact without necessarily producing tiny fragments; pulverize emphasizes reduction to extremely fine particles or powder. Smithereen emphasizes tiny broken fragments but is much rarer than these alternatives.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记 to smithereens＝碎成一地小片，再把罕用动词 smithereen 记成“使变成这些碎片”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with to smithereens, meaning into tiny pieces, then remember the rare verb smithereen as making those pieces.

forms: 第三人称单数 conks；过去式、过去分词 conked；现在分词 conking。
family: conk（俚语名词，可指鼻子）；conk out（另一动词搭配，可指机器停止运转或人睡着）。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。英语俚语名词 conk（头）转为动词，表示敲击头部。conk + -ing → conking（动名词：敲打这一动作），不是把 con- 当成前缀；conk out 是另一个常见搭配。

etymology.text: 表示“敲头”的动词来自英语俚语名词 conk（头）：从身体部位的名字转成敲击这一部位的动作。把“脑袋挨了一下”的画面和这个短促的词联系起来。

usage_note: 非正式用语，常见 conk someone on the head。本卡教及物的敲打义；conk out 表示机器坏掉或人睡着，是另一种用法。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“敲头”的动词来自俚语 conk“脑袋”，而“鼻子”义可能与 conch“海螺壳”有关；表示停机、睡着等的用法可能另有拟声来源。真菌义可能也是 conch 的变体，而拉直头发义可能由拉直剂名称 congolene 缩略变形而来，这些同形词不能全部归为同一条语义演变链。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/conk)
etymology_story.en: The hitting verb comes from slang conk meaning 'head,' while the nose noun may be related to conch; the stopping and sleeping verb may have a separate imitative origin. The fungal noun may also be an alteration of conch, whereas the hair-straightening use probably shortens and alters congolene, a hair-straightening preparation, so these forms do not all share one established origin. [Etymological reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/conk)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 conk 作为不可再分的词基，不拆成 con- + k。动词屈折：conks、conked、conking；可数名词复数：conks；短语动词：conk out，也见表示睡着的 conk off。派生词 conky 可表示带有层架状菌体或受相关腐朽影响的；历史文化表达 conked hair 指经化学拉直的头发。[词形与义项参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/conk)
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, conk is an indivisible base, not con- + k. Verb forms are conks, conked, and conking; count nouns take conks. Phrasal verbs include conk out and, for falling asleep, conk off. The derivative conky describes wood bearing conks or affected by associated decay; conked hair means chemically straightened hair. [Forms and senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/conk)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hit（击打）最宽泛；whack（猛击）强调用力且常带口语色彩；break down（发生故障）对应机器 conk out 的意思。conk 的击打义常突出头部，停机义则比 break down 更随意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hit is the broadest term for striking; whack suggests a forceful, informal blow; break down corresponds to the mechanical sense of conk out. Conk often suggests a hit to the head, while conk out sounds more casual than break down.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记两幅画面：“咚”一下敲中头；“咚”一下人或机器停下来。声音联想只是助记，不能解释全部同形词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a sudden 'bonk' to the head, then a person or machine abruptly stopping. This sound association is a memory aid, not an explanation of every homonym.

meaning: 把……收拾整齐；把……打扮漂亮（常与 up 连用）

pronunciation.note: 英式读音，单音节。

forms: 第三人称单数 spiffs；过去式、过去分词 spiffed；现在分词 spiffing。常见搭配 spiff up。
family: spiffy（形容词，漂亮整洁的）；spiffing（英式非正式形容词，极好的，也可作 spiff 的现在分词）。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。spiff + -y → spiffy（漂亮整洁的）；动词 spiff 常与 up 连用，表示收拾得更好看。

etymology.text: 这个动词来自英语方言形容词 spiff，原义是“衣着讲究的”。从“穿得漂亮”转为“使人或物更整洁漂亮”，就形成了常见的 spiff up。

usage_note: 非正式用语，通常用 spiff up。可用于人的装扮，也可用于房间或物品的外观改善；不等于彻底重建或修复所有故障。代词放中间，如 spiff it up。

senses.meaning_en: Informally, to make someone or something look smarter, usually with up.
senses.english_definition: If you spiff something up, you improve its appearance, and if you spiff up, you make yourself look smarter.
senses.collocation_en: spiff up the house; spiff yourself up
senses.collocation_zh: 把房子收拾漂亮；把自己打扮整齐
senses.sentence_en: We spiffed up the spare room before our guests arrived.
senses.sentence_zh: 客人到来之前，我们把客房收拾得漂漂亮亮。

senses.meaning_zh: （商业非正式用语）销售特定商品所得的额外奖金
senses.meaning_en: An extra payment to a salesperson for selling a particular product.
senses.english_definition: A spiff is an additional reward that a salesperson receives for selling a particular product.
senses.collocation_en: pay a spiff; earn sales spiffs
senses.collocation_zh: 支付销售奖励金；赚取额外销售奖金
senses.sentence_en: The manufacturer offered a spiff for every unit sold.
senses.sentence_zh: 制造商承诺，每售出一件产品，就支付一笔额外销售奖金。

senses.meaning_zh: （商业俚语）向销售人员支付额外销售奖金
senses.meaning_en: In sales jargon, to reward a salesperson with an extra sales payment.
senses.english_definition: If a company spiffs a salesperson, it gives them an extra reward for making a particular sale.
senses.collocation_en: spiff salespeople; spiff the sales staff
senses.collocation_zh: 向销售人员发放额外奖金；给销售团队发销售奖励金
senses.sentence_en: Some suppliers spiff salespeople who recommend their products.
senses.sentence_zh: 有些供应商会向推荐其产品的销售人员支付额外奖金。

etymology_story.zh: 表示修饰外观的 spiff 在十九世纪已有记录，可能与方言形容词 spiff“衣着讲究的”及 spiffy 有关，但更早的来源并不确定。销售奖金义也见于十九世纪，其起源及与打扮义的关系尚不明确，不宜把现代流行的字母展开式当作已证实的词源。[词源参考](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/spiff)
etymology_story.en: The appearance-improving verb is recorded in the nineteenth century and may be connected with dialect spiff meaning 'well-dressed' and with spiffy, but its deeper origin is uncertain. The sales-bonus noun also dates from the nineteenth century; its origin and relationship to the appearance sense remain uncertain, so modern acronym expansions should not be treated as established etymology. [Etymological reference](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/spiff)

morphology_enriched.zh: spiff 是现代不可再分的词基；动词形式为 spiffs、spiffed、spiffing，名词复数为 spiffs。相关词族：spiffy（漂亮整洁的）、spiffier、spiffiest、spiffily（漂亮整洁地）、spiffiness（整洁漂亮）；spiffing 还可独立作英式非正式形容词，意为“极好的”。常见结构为 spiff up；商业名词也拼作 spif。[商业义参考](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/spiff)
morphology_enriched.en: Spiff is an indivisible modern base; its verb forms are spiffs, spiffed, and spiffing, and its noun plural is spiffs. Related family members include spiffy, spiffier, spiffiest, spiffily, and spiffiness; spiffing also functions independently as an informal British adjective meaning 'excellent.' The usual construction is spiff up, and the commercial noun also has the spelling spif. [Commercial sense](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/spiff)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spruce up（收拾漂亮）最接近外观改善义；tidy up（整理整齐）更强调秩序和清洁；bonus（奖金）范围更广，而商业义 spiff 特别指推动特定销售的额外奖励。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spruce up closely matches the appearance-improving sense; tidy up emphasizes order and cleanliness; bonus is broader than the commercial spiff, which specifically rewards particular sales.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: spiff up → 看起来更 spiffy（漂亮整洁）；销售义另记“一笔额外奖金”，不要强行与外观义串成同一词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Spiff up means 'make it look spiffy'; remember the sales sense separately as an extra payment, without assuming a shared historical origin.

meaning: 二巯丙醇（英国抗路易氏剂）

pronunciation.note: 逐个读出字母 B、A、L，最后的 L 读完整的 /el/。

forms: 药物名称，通常作不可数名词；按三个字母 B、A、L 分别读出。
family: British Anti-Lewisite 为全称；dimercaprol 为同一药物的通用名。

morphology.text: British + Anti-Lewisite → British Anti-Lewisite，取三个词的首字母组成 BAL。整词作为独立词素记忆，这里是英语首字母词。

etymology.text: 英语 British Anti-Lewisite 的首字母缩写，原意是“英国抗路易氏剂”。名称保留了这项药物与路易氏剂之间的历史联系。

usage_note: 药物缩写必须全大写 BAL；小写 bal 还可缩写 balance，本课只学药物名。按字母读，不读成 ball。
sentence: The museum label identifies BAL as an antidote developed during the war.
translation: 博物馆标签把BAL介绍为战争期间研发的一种解毒剂。
scenario: 你在医学史展览中读到一种解毒药的名称。
cloze: The museum label identifies _____ as an antidote developed during the war.
collocation:
wartime research on BAL 战时对BAL的研究
BAL in a pharmacology textbook 药理学教材中的BAL条目
context_hint: Look for the name of the antidote on the museum label.
hint: Look for the name of the antidote on the museum label.

teaching.contrast: BAL 是一种具体药物的名称，不是泛指所有解毒剂，也不是小写的余额缩写 bal。
teaching.sentence: The pharmacology textbook lists BAL under its other name, dimercaprol.
teaching.translation: 药理学教材以另一名称dimercaprol列出了BAL。

comprehension_check.sentence: The exhibit describes BAL as a medicine rather than a piece of laboratory equipment.
comprehension_check.question: 请选择句中目标词的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 句中直接把 BAL 归为 medicine，所以它指药物，而非实验仪器。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（一种药物／一种实验仪器）
fields.wrong_reason: 句中直接把 BAL 归为 medicine，所以它指药物，而非实验仪器。

senses.pos: n. 名词（首字母缩略词）
senses.meaning_zh: （药学）二巯丙醇；英国抗路易氏剂
senses.meaning_en: Dimercaprol, also called British anti-Lewisite.
senses.english_definition: BAL is another name for dimercaprol, a medicine developed to counter the effects of the arsenic-containing chemical agent Lewisite.
senses.collocation_en: BAL treatment; BAL injection
senses.collocation_zh: 二巯丙醇治疗；二巯丙醇注射剂
senses.sentence_en: The historical report describes the development of BAL.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份历史报告介绍了二巯丙醇的研发过程。

senses.pos: n. 名词（医学首字母缩略词）
senses.meaning_zh: 支气管肺泡灌洗
senses.meaning_en: Bronchoalveolar lavage.
senses.english_definition: BAL is a procedure in which fluid is introduced into a small part of the lung and collected again to obtain material for examination.
senses.collocation_en: perform BAL; BAL fluid
senses.collocation_zh: 进行支气管肺泡灌洗；支气管肺泡灌洗液
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory examined the BAL fluid for signs of infection.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室检查了支气管肺泡灌洗液，以寻找感染迹象。

senses.pos: n. 名词（医学首字母缩略词）
senses.meaning_zh: 血液酒精浓度
senses.meaning_en: Blood alcohol level.
senses.english_definition: Someone's BAL is the concentration of alcohol in their blood.
senses.collocation_en: an elevated BAL; measure BAL
senses.collocation_zh: 升高的血液酒精浓度；测量血液酒精浓度
senses.sentence_en: The study measured each participant's BAL.
senses.sentence_zh: 该研究测量了每位参与者的血液酒精浓度。

etymology_story.zh: 药物名称 BAL 取自 British anti-Lewisite“英国抗路易氏剂”，保留了它最初用于对抗路易氏剂的历史背景。现代医学还独立使用同一组字母缩写 bronchoalveolar lavage“支气管肺泡灌洗”和 blood alcohol level“血液酒精浓度”，这些含义并非由药名演变而来。[药名来源](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/BAL)；[灌洗义](https://www.tabers.com/tabersonline/view/Tabers-Dictionary/737009/all/BAL)；[血液酒精浓度义](https://healthcenter.indiana.edu/health-answers/substance-abuse-addiction/alcohol.html)
etymology_story.en: The drug name BAL takes its letters from British anti-Lewisite, preserving its original connection with countering Lewisite. Medical English independently uses the same letters for bronchoalveolar lavage and blood alcohol level; these meanings did not develop from the drug name. [Drug-name origin](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/BAL), [lavage sense](https://www.tabers.com/tabersonline/view/Tabers-Dictionary/737009/all/BAL), [blood-alcohol sense](https://healthcenter.indiana.edu/health-answers/substance-abuse-addiction/alcohol.html)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词方式为首字母缩略：B(ritish) + A(nti-) + L(ewisite)；另有 B(roncho-) + A(lveolar) + L(avage)，以及 B(lood) + A(lcohol) + L(evel)。通常逐字母读作 B–A–L；BAL 本身没有常用的加缀派生词族。BAL treatment（二巯丙醇治疗）、BAL fluid（支气管肺泡灌洗液）、BAL measurement（血液酒精浓度测量）属于不同义项下的搭配。
morphology_enriched.en: BAL is formed by initial letters: B(ritish) + A(nti-) + L(ewisite); independently, B(roncho-) + A(lveolar) + L(avage), or B(lood) + A(lcohol) + L(evel). It is normally pronounced letter by letter as B–A–L and has no common affix-derived word family. BAL treatment, BAL fluid, and BAL measurement are combinations belonging to different senses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dimercaprol（二巯丙醇）与药物义 BAL 同指一种药；bronchoalveolar washing（支气管肺泡灌洗）对应操作义；blood alcohol concentration / BAC（血液酒精浓度）对应浓度义。这三组表达分别属于不同概念，不能相互替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dimercaprol names the same drug as medicinal BAL; bronchoalveolar washing corresponds to the lavage procedure; blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, corresponds to the alcohol-level sense. These equivalents belong to separate concepts and are not interchangeable across senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先展开字母，再确定含义：anti-Lewisite 指药物，lavage 指灌洗，level 指浓度。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand the letters before choosing the meaning: anti-Lewisite identifies the drug, lavage the washing procedure, and level the alcohol concentration.

meaning: 费尔（部分阿拉伯国家的辅币单位）

pronunciation.note: 只有一个音节；/ɪ/ 是短元音，结尾读出 /l/。

forms: 单数 fil，也写 fils；复数 fils。不要把单数 fils 末尾的 s 一律当成复数标记。
family: fils 同一货币单位的另一种单数拼写，也用作复数。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆；fil + -s → fils（复数）。这里的 -s 表示数量变化，不是新词根。

etymology.text: 英语从阿拉伯语借入这个小额货币名称；阿拉伯语较早的形式 fals 指小额硬币。把它和口袋里一枚很小的零钱联系起来记忆。

usage_note: 本课只学货币单位。不同国家的换算比例不同，不能把 fil 一律换算成同样金额；英文单数也可写 fils。
sentence: The collector found a one fil coin in the box.
translation: 收藏者在盒子里找到了一枚一费尔硬币。
scenario: 你在辨认旧硬币的面额。
cloze: The collector found a one _____ coin in the box.
collocation:
a one fil coin 一枚一费尔硬币
a charge of one fil 一费尔的收费
context_hint: The collector is reading the denomination of a small coin.
hint: The collector is reading the denomination of a small coin.

teaching.sentence: The price list gives the smallest charge as one fil.
teaching.translation: 价目表将最低收费列为一费尔。

comprehension_check.question: 请选择句中目标词的意思。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（货币单位／长度单位）
fields.wrong_reason: 硬币的 value 以 fil 表示，因此这里是货币单位，不是长度单位。

senses.meaning_zh: 费尔，部分阿拉伯国家的辅币单位；fils 的异体
senses.meaning_en: A variant of fils, a small monetary unit used in several Arab countries.
senses.english_definition: A fil is a small unit of money used in some Arab countries, more usually written fils even in the singular.
senses.collocation_en: one fil; five fils
senses.collocation_zh: 一费尔；五费尔
senses.sentence_en: The coin catalogue lists its face value as one fil.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本钱币目录将它的面值记为一费尔。

etymology_story.zh: 货币名 fil 是英语 fils 的异体，后者借自阿拉伯语的小额货币名称。应注意，英语货币名 fils 本身也可作单数，不能把所有词尾 s 都解释成英语复数后缀。[fil 词条](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fil)；[fils 词源与词形](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fils)
etymology_story.en: The monetary term fil is a variant of English fils, which was borrowed from Arabic as the name of a small monetary unit. English fils is itself also singular, so its final s should not automatically be interpreted as an English plural ending. [Fil entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fil), [fils origin and forms](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fils)

morphology_enriched.zh: 货币义 fil 作为一个完整借词词基处理，无可用的现代英语前缀或后缀拆分；复数为 fils。更常用的词形 fils 则单复数同形：one fils、five fils；没有常用的英语加缀派生词族。本词不应与表示“丝、线”的拉丁来源词根 fil- 混为一谈。[词形参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/fils)
morphology_enriched.en: Monetary fil is a whole borrowed base with no useful modern English prefix–suffix division; its plural is fils. The more usual form fils has the same singular and plural: one fils, five fils. There is no common English affix-derived family, and this word should not be confused with the Latin-derived element fil- meaning 'thread.' [Forms reference](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/fils)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fils（费尔）是同一货币名更常见的词形；monetary subunit（辅币单位）是上位概念；small change（零钱）泛指小额钱币。后两者便于解释，却不是可以精确替换 fil 的同义单位名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fils is the more usual form of the same currency name; monetary subunit is a broader category; small change refers generally to low-value money. The latter two explain the concept but are not exact alternative names for the unit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一枚小辅币：fil；常用拼法 fils，一个也可带 s。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one tiny coin: a fil; remember that the usual spelling fils can name just one.

pronunciation.note: 只有一个音节；按这里的英式读音，元音 /ɒ/ 要短促。

forms: 可数名词，复数 noms。
family: nomination 提名；nominate 提名某人。

morphology.text: 英语 nomination 截短为 nom，整词作为独立词素记忆；nom + -s → noms（多项提名）。

etymology.text: 来自英语 nomination 的口语截短：把长词前面的 nom 留下来，仍指“提名”。娱乐新闻里常把长名称缩短，用 nom 快速谈论奖项提名。

usage_note: 非正式用语，常见于影视奖项报道；正式文件写 nomination。与表示好吃的感叹词 nom 是不同义项。
sentence: The actor received a nom for best supporting actor.
translation: 这名演员获得了最佳男配角提名。
scenario: 你在读电影奖项的候选名单报道。
cloze: The actor received a _____ for best supporting actor.
collocation:
a best actor nom 最佳男演员提名
a nom for club president 社团主席候选人提名
context_hint: The actor is on the shortlist, but the winner has not been announced.
hint: The actor is on the shortlist, but the winner has not been announced.

teaching.contrast: nom 表示获得提名，不保证获奖；winner 才指已经获胜的人。
teaching.sentence: Her first award nom brought new attention to the small documentary.
teaching.translation: 她的首次奖项提名让那部小成本纪录片受到新的关注。

comprehension_check.sentence: The film earned a nom, but another film won the prize.
comprehension_check.question: 请选择句中目标词的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: but 后面说另一部影片获奖，所以 nom 是提名，尚不是获奖。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（奖项提名／最终获奖）
fields.wrong_reason: but 后面说另一部影片获奖，所以 nom 是提名，尚不是获奖。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式）提名，尤指奖项提名
senses.meaning_en: An informal shortening of nomination, especially for an award.
senses.english_definition: A nom is a nomination, especially one received by a film, performer, or other possible award winner.
senses.collocation_en: an Oscar nom; earn a nom
senses.collocation_zh: 一项奥斯卡提名；获得提名
senses.sentence_en: The film picked up three Oscar noms.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影获得了三项奥斯卡提名。

senses.meaning_zh: （诙谐或网络用语）好吃；啊呜，表示享受美食
senses.meaning_en: A playful expression of enjoyment when eating or thinking about delicious food.
senses.english_definition: You say or write nom, often repeatedly, to show that food tastes good or looks delicious.
senses.collocation_en: nom nom; nom nom nom
senses.collocation_zh: 啊呜啊呜，真好吃；啊呜啊呜啊呜
senses.sentence_en: "Nom nom!" she wrote beneath the photo of her homemade cookies.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在自制饼干的照片下写道：“啊呜啊呜，真好吃！”

senses.pos: v. 动词（及物或不及物）
senses.meaning_zh: （诙谐或网络用语）津津有味地吃
senses.meaning_en: Playfully, to eat something with enjoyment.
senses.english_definition: If you nom something or nom on it, you eat it with obvious enjoyment.
senses.collocation_en: nom on snacks; nom a sandwich
senses.collocation_zh: 津津有味地吃零食；美滋滋地吃三明治
senses.sentence_en: We spent the evening nomming on popcorn and watching films.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们一晚上都在津津有味地吃爆米花、看电影。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“提名”的 nom 是 nomination 的非正式截短形式，其较远的词源涉及拉丁语 nomen“名字”。表示吃东西的感叹词及动词则来自模仿进食声音的表达，与“提名”义不是同一条词源。[提名义与拟声义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/nom)；[进食动词义](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/nom?topic=eating)
etymology_story.en: Nom meaning 'nomination' is an informal clipping of nomination, whose more distant ancestry involves Latin nomen, 'name.' The eating interjection and verb instead come from an imitation of eating sounds and do not share the nomination sense's origin. [Nomination and imitative senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/nom), [eating verb](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/nom?topic=eating)

morphology_enriched.zh: 提名义：nomination → 截短为 nom，复数 noms；相关完整词族有 nominate（提名）、nomination（提名）、nominee（被提名者）、nominator（提名者），它们不是由短词 nom 再加后缀直接生成的。进食义：拟声表达 nom 或重复形式 nom nom → 转作动词；动词形式为 noms、nommed、nomming，后两者双写 m。另须区别书面缩写 nom.，它可代表 nominal 或 nominative。
morphology_enriched.en: For nomination, nomination is clipped to nom, with plural noms; the related full-word family includes nominate, nomination, nominee, and nominator, rather than being formed by directly adding suffixes to nom. For eating, imitative nom or repeated nom nom also functions as a verb, with forms noms, nommed, and nomming; m doubles before -ed and -ing. Distinguish the written abbreviation nom., which can stand for nominal or nominative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nomination（提名）是奖项义 nom 的完整、中性表达；yum（真好吃）与感叹词 nom 接近，但 nom 更像模仿吃东西的声音；munch（大嚼、咀嚼）与动词 nom 接近，但更突出咀嚼动作或声音。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nomination is the full, neutral equivalent of the award noun; yum resembles the interjection, though nom more strongly imitates eating; munch resembles the verb, but emphasizes chewing or its sound.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 奖项语境：nom 是 nomination 的短版；食物语境：nom nom 是嘴巴“啊呜啊呜”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: With awards, nom is nomination cut short; with food, nom nom imitates a happily eating mouth.

pronunciation.note: 这里采用非卷舌读音 /nɑː/，拉长 /ɑː/，词尾不另读 /r/。

forms: 本课作方言副词，无复数或动词时态变化；标准英语对应 near。
family: near 标准英语形式；nearness 接近。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；nar 是 near 的方言形式。相关标准词的派生：near + -ness → nearness（接近），不要据此另造 nar 的派生词。

etymology.text: 由英语 near 的方言读音和拼写演变而来。把 nar 放回 near“靠近”的意思中记，读到地方口音对白时更容易理解。

etymology_story.zh: nar 与 near 同源，其历史可追溯至中古英语及古诺尔斯语中表示“更近”的形式；这些地域用法并非仅由现代 near 简单改写而来。[《苏格兰语词典》](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/nar)
etymology_story.en: Nar shares its history with near, through Middle English and Old Norse comparative forms meaning “nearer.” [Dictionaries of the Scots Language](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/nar)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代按单一词素处理；地域词形包括 naur、naar，比较级包括 naarer、narder，最高级包括 nardest。相关地域复合词有 narby（附近）；nearness（接近）属于标准英语 near 的词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat nar as one morpheme. Regional forms include naur, naar, comparative naarer/narder, superlative nardest, and compound narby. Nearness belongs to standard English near.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: near（近）是标准对应词；nearby（在附近）主要表示位置；almost（几乎）只对应其表示程度接近的用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near is the standard equivalent; nearby expresses location; almost corresponds only to the approximation sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 nar 连到 near：距离近，或程度接近。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link nar with near: close in distance or degree.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第一音节；/ŋk/ 先发鼻音 /ŋ/，再接 /k/。

forms: 复数 honkies，也可见 honkeys；异体拼写 honkey、honkie。
family: honkey、honkie 为同一蔑称的拼写变体。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆，不拆成 honk 与 -y；honky + 复数词尾 -s → honkies（y 改为 ies）。

senses.meaning_zh: 对白人的侮辱性称呼（主要用于美国俚语）
senses.meaning_en: An offensive slang term for a white person, chiefly in American English.
senses.english_definition: Honky is an offensive word used to refer contemptuously to a white person.
senses.collocation_en: call someone a honky; use the slur honky
senses.collocation_zh: 用 honky 辱称某人；使用 honky 这一侮辱性称呼
senses.sentence_en: The article explains why calling someone a honky is offensive.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章解释了为什么用 honky 称呼他人具有侮辱性。

etymology_story.zh: honky 很可能由旧蔑称 Hunky 变形而来，后者曾用于贬称来自中东欧的移民；其对白人的侮辱义在二十世纪中叶已有记录。具体来源仍有不确定性。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/honky)
etymology_story.en: Honky probably developed from Hunky, an older derogatory name for immigrants from east-central Europe; its insulting use for white people is recorded by the mid-twentieth century. The precise derivation remains uncertain. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/honky)

morphology_enriched.zh: 此侮辱义的 honky 在现代英语中按单一词素处理，不分析为 honk（鸣笛）加 -y。复数为 honkies，即去掉 y 再加 -ies；异体拼写包括 honkie、honkey，后者也有复数 honkeys。没有需要补造的常用派生词族；honky-tonk 是另一个独立词项。
morphology_enriched.en: For this insulting sense, treat honky as a single morpheme rather than honk plus -y. Its plural is honkies, formed by replacing y with -ies; spelling variants include honkie and honkey, with honkeys also recorded. There is no established common derivative family to expand artificially; honky-tonk is a separate lexical item.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: white person（白人）是中性对应表达；whitey（对白人的蔑称）同样带侮辱性；cracker（对白人的蔑称）常另外含有美国南部、乡村或阶层方面的刻板印象，不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: White person is the neutral equivalent; whitey is another derogatory label; cracker often adds stereotypes involving the American South, rural identity, or social class, so it is not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旧蔑称变体 → 对白人的辱称；连同侮辱语域一起记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An altered older slur became a slur for white people: remember the offensive register with the meaning.

meaning: 法式蔬菜烤菜（常用浅陶盘烹制）

pronunciation.note: 这里读一个音节，/t/ 后紧接 /j/，再接短元音 /æ/。

forms: 可数或不可数，按一道菜或这种食物理解；复数 tians。
family: 同一词 tian 也可指烹制它的浅陶盘。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆；tian + -s → tians（多道这种菜）。词尾变化不改变法式菜肴这一核心意思。

etymology.text: 经法语借入英语，来自普罗旺斯语中“无柄陶盘”的名称，更早可追溯到希腊语 tēganon“煎锅”。先有容器名，再用它称呼盘中烤出的菜。

usage_note: 本课学菜肴义，不是汉语拼音或山名。通常由切片蔬菜烹制；这里采用 Collins 的英式读音 /tjæn/。

etymology_story.zh: tian 经法语借入英语，来自普罗旺斯语的陶制烹饪容器名称，更早可追溯至希腊语 tēganon（煎锅）。词义由容器扩展到其中烹制的食物。[《柯林斯英语词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/tian)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed tian through French from a Provençal name for an earthenware cooking vessel, ultimately traced to Greek tēganon, meaning a frying pan. The vessel's name was extended to the food cooked in it. [Collins English Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/tian)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 tian 作为不可再拆分的借词词干；tian + -s → tians，复数可指多道菜或多个烤盘。没有常用的英语派生词族；vegetable tian（蔬菜烤菜）等是名词短语，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tian is an unanalyzed borrowed stem: tian + -s → tians, referring to multiple dishes of food or cooking vessels. It has no established common English derivative family; combinations such as vegetable tian are noun phrases rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gratin（焗菜）强调烤出的表面焦壳；casserole（烤炖菜；烤炖锅）范围更广；ratatouille（普罗旺斯杂蔬）通常指混合蔬菜炖菜。tian 更突出特定浅陶盘及其中烹制的菜肴，三者并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gratin emphasizes a browned surface; casserole is broader and can name either food or its vessel; ratatouille usually denotes a mixed vegetable stew. Tian more specifically evokes the shallow earthenware vessel and its contents, so these are related terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先有浅陶盘，再有盘中菜：一个词记住容器与食物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: First the shallow dish, then its contents: one name connects vessel and food.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第二音节 /ɡæn/，最后的 /ə/ 轻读。

forms: 通常作不可数名词；计量可说 a metre of organza（一米欧根纱）。
family: organdy 是另一种相似的薄硬织物名称，不是本词的词形变化。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆；可用形容词组合 organza + -like → organza-like（像欧根纱的），描述轻薄而挺括的质感。

etymology.text: 英语织物名称，词典认为很可能由商标名 Lorganza 改变而来。把它想成从商品名称变成了衣料名称：一层能透光、又能撑起轮廓的薄纱。

usage_note: 常用于礼服、装饰或包装，轻薄透明而较挺括；可由丝或合成纤维制成。不要把它当成 organ 的派生词。

senses.meaning_zh: 欧根纱；轻薄透明、质地挺括的平纹织物
senses.meaning_en: A thin, transparent, crisp plain-weave fabric used especially for formal clothing.

etymology_story.zh: organza 在十九世纪初已有英语记录，很可能由商标名 Lorganza 变形而来。它成为一种透明而挺括的服装面料的通用名称。[《牛津高阶英语词典》](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/organza)
etymology_story.en: Organza is recorded in English from the early nineteenth century and probably developed from the trademark Lorganza. It became the generic name for a transparent, crisp dress fabric. [Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/organza)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代按单一借词词干 organza 处理，不拆成 organ 与 -za。通常是不可数名词；organzas 可在专业语境中表示不同品种；organza-like（像欧根纱的）是可自由构成的比较性形容词。organza dress 中 organza 是名词作定语，不据此另立常用形容词词性；organdy（蝉翼纱）是相关织物名称，不是其现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat organza as a single borrowed stem, not organ plus -za. It is normally uncountable; organzas can denote varieties in specialist usage, and organza-like is a freely formed comparative adjective. In organza dress, organza is a noun modifier, which does not establish a separate common adjective entry; organdy names a related fabric rather than a modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: organdy（蝉翼纱）通常指经过硬挺整理的透明棉织物；chiffon（雪纺）更柔软、垂坠；tulle（薄纱网）具有网眼结构。organza 的核心特点是透明而挺括，这些面料名称不能直接互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Organdy usually denotes a sheer cotton fabric with a stiff finish; chiffon is softer and more flowing; tulle has an open net structure. Organza combines transparency with crispness, so these fabric names are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看得透，却撑得起：透明加挺括就是 organza 的质感。
mnemonic_anchor.en: See through it, yet it holds its shape: transparency plus crispness recalls organza.

meaning: 暗中勾结；共谋（常用于in cahoots）

pronunciation.note: 重音在第二音节，/uː/ 拉长，词尾 /ts/ 连读。

forms: 通常使用复数形式 cahoots；常见结构 be in cahoots with somebody。单数 cahoot 很少单独使用。
family: cahoot 较少见的单数形式；in cahoots 暗中串通。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆；cahoot + -s → cahoots。英语惯常保留这个复数形式，用在 in cahoots 中表示暗中联手。

etymology.text: 英语中的 cahoot 通常以复数 cahoots 出现；词典认为它可能来自法语 cahute“小屋”。可以把“躲在小屋里密谋”当作助记画面，这只是帮助记义的联想。

usage_note: 非正式表达，常含暗中串通或可疑合作的意味；用 in cahoots with，不单独用 cahoots 代替动词 conspire。

hint: The cashier and thief secretly worked together.

senses.meaning_zh: 暗中联手；勾结；共谋（通常用于 in cahoots）
senses.meaning_en: A secret partnership or alliance, often involving dishonest activity.
senses.english_definition: If people are in cahoots, they are working or planning together secretly, often to do something dishonest.

senses.sentence_zh: 调查人员怀疑，这家供应商与公司的一名员工暗中勾结。

etymology_story.zh: cahoot 在十九世纪的美国英语中已有记录，可能来自法语 cahute（小屋），但词源尚未完全确定。原有的“合伙、联手”含义如今主要保留在 in cahoots 中，并常带有秘密勾结的意味。[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cahoot)
etymology_story.en: Cahoot is recorded in nineteenth-century American English and may come from French cahute, meaning a hut, although its origin remains uncertain. Its partnership sense now survives chiefly in in cahoots, often suggesting secret or dishonest cooperation. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cahoot)

morphology_enriched.zh: cahoot + 复数词尾 -s → cahoots；现代通常将复数形式连同固定结构 in cahoots（暗中联手）整体学习。单数 cahoot 有词典记录，但远不如该固定结构常见；没有常用派生词族，不拆成 ca- 与 hoots，也不与 hoot（鸣叫）建立构词联系。
morphology_enriched.en: Cahoot + plural -s → cahoots; modern learners should usually treat the plural together with the fixed expression in cahoots. Singular cahoot is recorded but is much less common than the expression. There is no established common derivative family; do not split it into ca- and hoots or connect its formation with hoot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: collusion（勾结、串通）较正式，通常明确涉及欺骗；conspiracy（阴谋、共谋）强调共同策划，尤其是非法或有害行为；in league（结盟、联手）侧重联合关系。in cahoots 更口语化，通常暗示可疑合作，也可用于玩笑语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Collusion is more formal and usually implies deception; conspiracy emphasizes a shared plan, especially an unlawful or harmful one; in league emphasizes an alliance. In cahoots is more conversational, usually suggests suspicious cooperation, and can also be used playfully.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture people planning together inside a hut: a memory image, not a proven account of the word's development.

senses.english_definition: If you call someone a dolt, you mean that they are stupid or slow to understand things.

etymology_story.zh: dolt 的确切来源尚不确定，通常认为它与 dull“迟钝的；愚笨的”有关，可能由表示“使迟钝”的旧动词形式发展而来。其意义由“迟钝、愚笨”落实为“迟钝或愚笨的人”。
etymology_story.en: The exact origin of dolt is uncertain, but it is generally connected with dull and may have developed from an old verb form meaning to make dull. The meaning became a person who is slow-witted or stupid.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再拆的词基 dolt。词族：dolt → dolts（名词复数）；dolt + -ish → doltish（愚笨的）；doltish + -ly → doltishly（愚笨地）；doltish + -ness → doltishness（愚笨）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dolt is an unanalyzable base. Its family includes dolts, the noun plural; dolt + -ish → doltish, meaning stupid; doltish + -ly → doltishly; and doltish + -ness → doltishness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fool（傻瓜）范围较广，也可指判断失当的人；idiot（白痴、笨蛋）通常是更强烈的直接辱骂；dunce（笨学生）尤其强调学习或理解能力差。dolt 往往带有较书面或略显老派的嘲讽色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool is broader and can describe someone who shows poor judgment; idiot is usually a stronger direct insult; dunce especially suggests difficulty learning or understanding. Dolt often sounds literary or somewhat old-fashioned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用 dull“迟钝的”作联想：脑子迟钝的人 → dolt“笨蛋”。这是记忆联系，不是现代构词拆分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect dolt with dull: a dull-witted person is a dolt. This is a memory association, not a modern morphological breakdown.

meaning: 对非洲黑人的严重侮辱性称呼

pronunciation.note: 重音在第一音节，/æ/ 是短元音；这里采用非卷舌读音，末尾 /ə/ 轻读。

forms: 复数 kaffirs；也有 kafir 拼写。这里只辨认种族蔑称这一义项。
family: kafir 为相关拼写变体，含义须结合历史和语境判断。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆；kaffir + -s → kaffirs（复数形式）。不要把词尾误当成可随意替换的英语派生词缀。

etymology.text: 源自阿拉伯语 kāfir，原指伊斯兰教立场下的“不信者／非穆斯林”，也可能包括信奉其他宗教的人。借入英语后，在南非等历史语境中被用于种族贬称；现代文本中应辨认它的侮辱性，不能沿用来称呼人。

usage_note: 极具冒犯性的种族蔑称，只供阅读历史材料或辨认歧视性语言；不能用作对人的日常称呼。本义常小写 kaffir，历史文本也会大写；中性描述可用 Black African。

senses.meaning_zh: 对非洲黑人的极严重种族侮辱性称呼，尤见于南非语境
senses.meaning_en: An extremely offensive racial slur for a Black African person, especially in South African contexts.
senses.english_definition: Kaffir is an extremely offensive word used to insult a Black African person, especially in South Africa.

senses.meaning_zh: 用于贬称非洲黑人的或其相关事物的；极具种族侮辱性，多见于旧文本
senses.meaning_en: An extremely offensive, chiefly historical adjective referring to Black African people or things associated with them.
senses.english_definition: In older racist language, kaffir was used before a noun to describe Black African people or things associated with them.
senses.collocation_en: 'kaffir' as a racial adjective; historical uses of 'kaffir'
senses.collocation_zh: 用作种族贬称形容词的“kaffir”；“kaffir”的历史用法
senses.sentence_en: The dictionary labels the adjective 'kaffir' as extremely offensive.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部词典将形容词“kaffir”标注为极具侮辱性。

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源于阿拉伯语 kāfir，意为“不信者”，在伊斯兰教语境中指不信奉伊斯兰教的人，并经欧洲语言传播。它在南部非洲被用于称呼当地黑人，后来成为极严重的种族辱称；宗教原义不能代表这一英语用法的现代含义。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Arabic kāfir, meaning an unbeliever in an Islamic context, and spread through European languages. In southern Africa it was applied to Black African people and became an extremely offensive racial slur, distinct from its original religious meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整体借词处理，不拆成英语词根与词缀。名词复数为 kaffirs，形容词通常不分级；它也保留在 kaffir lime（箭叶橙，又称 makrut lime）和 kaffir corn（旧称，指某类高粱）等固定名称中，不能据此推导出可自由使用的中性称人义。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat it as a whole loanword rather than an English root-plus-affix formation. The noun plural is kaffirs, and the adjective is normally ungradable; it also survives in fixed names such as kaffir lime, also called makrut lime, and kaffir corn, an older name for a type of sorghum, but these compounds do not make it a neutral term for people.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Black African（非洲黑人）是中性的身份描述，并不保留原词的侮辱意味；racial slur（种族辱称）说明其语言性质；racial epithet（种族性称谓、种族辱称）较正式，在此语境中指侮辱性的种族标签。后两者是类别名称，不是可替换的称人词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Black African is a neutral identity description and does not preserve the insult; racial slur identifies the kind of abusive language involved; racial epithet is more formal and, in this context, means an insulting racial label. The latter two describe the expression rather than the person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住语义路径：“不信者”的宗教标签 → 南部非洲的种族标签 → 极严重的种族辱称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the semantic path: a religious label for an unbeliever → a racial label in southern Africa → an extremely offensive racial slur.

usage_note: 非正式、较活泼的说法，常指规模较大或很热闹的聚会；正式活动名称通常用 reception、celebration 等，视场合选择。

etymology_story.zh: shindig 出现于十九世纪的英语口语中，通常被认为是 shindy 的变体；shindy 可表示喧闹、争闹或热闹的聚会。shindig 后来主要用于表示欢乐而热闹的社交聚会，其更早来源仍不确定。
etymology_story.en: Shindig appeared in nineteenth-century informal English and is usually considered an alteration of shindy, which could mean a commotion, a quarrel, or a lively gathering. Shindig came to refer mainly to a festive social event, while its deeper origin remains uncertain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 shindig 作为不可再拆的词基；shindig + -s → shindigs（复数）。没有常用的标准派生词族，也不应把它按 shin“胫骨”+ dig“挖”作历史构词分析。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, shindig is an unanalyzable base; shindig + -s → shindigs forms the plural. It has no established common family of derivatives, and shin plus dig is not a supported historical analysis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: party（聚会）最中性，规模和气氛不限；bash（盛大热闹的派对）同样口语化，常突出庆祝气氛；knees-up（热闹的歌舞聚会）主要用于英式口语，尤其让人想到唱歌跳舞。shindig 常带轻松、诙谐的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Party is neutral and does not specify size or atmosphere; bash is informal and often suggests a substantial celebration; knees-up is chiefly British and particularly suggests singing and dancing. Shindig often has a playful, light-hearted tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 shindig 记成“一屋子人随着音乐热闹庆祝”的完整画面，无须硬拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a room full of people celebrating noisily to music: that is a shindig. Remember the whole scene rather than inventing roots.

etymology_story.zh: pelmet 的来源不完全确定，通常被认为可能是法语 palmette 的变体；palmette 指棕榈叶形的装饰图案。这个词后来在英语中专指窗帘顶部的装饰遮盖物。
etymology_story.en: The origin of pelmet is not completely certain, but it is often considered a possible alteration of French palmette, a palm-leaf-shaped ornament. In English, the word came to designate a decorative covering above curtains.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pelmet 是不可再拆的词基；pelmet + -s → pelmets（复数）。常见复合形式有 pelmet board（窗帘盒板）和 pelmet box（盒式窗帘顶部遮盖物）；没有常用的标准派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pelmet is an unanalyzable base; pelmet + -s → pelmets forms the plural. Common compounds include pelmet board and pelmet box; there is no established common family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: valance（短帘幔）通常指布制的装饰垂幔，也可出现在床沿等位置；cornice（窗帘顶部装饰檐板）在窗饰语境中常指硬质装饰结构，但也可指建筑檐口。pelmet 主要是英式用词，强调窗帘顶部的装饰遮盖功能，材料不一定是木板。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Valance usually suggests a short decorative fabric hanging and can also occur around a bed; cornice, in a window-treatment context, often means a rigid decorative structure, but it also has architectural meanings. Pelmet is chiefly British and emphasizes the decorative covering above curtains, which need not be wooden.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把窗帘顶部想成戴了一顶遮住轨道的“装饰帽”：这顶帽子就是 pelmet。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine the curtains wearing a decorative cap that hides their track: that cap is the pelmet.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。bacon + rasher → bacon rasher（培根薄片）；rasher 在这里是整词，不按形容词 rash 的比较级理解。

etymology.text: rasher 可能来自已经不用的英语动词 rash（切），再往前可追到中古英语 rashen。想象切下的一薄片培根，有助于记住它表示食物薄片；“切”这一来源仍属可能的解释。

usage_note: 常见结构为 a rasher of bacon，数片时用 rashers。本课是食物名词，不是 rash（鲁莽的）的比较级。

senses.meaning_zh: 更鲁莽的；更欠考虑的
senses.meaning_en: More reckless or less careful about possible consequences.
senses.english_definition: If a person or decision is rasher than another, they show less thought about possible dangers or consequences.
senses.collocation_en: a rasher decision; even rasher
senses.collocation_zh: 更鲁莽的决定；更加鲁莽

senses.sentence_zh: 不查看天气就出发，本来会是一个更加鲁莽的决定。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“培根薄片”的名词 rasher 自十六世纪已有记录，来源不确定，可能与表示“切、划”的旧动词 rash 有关。表示“更鲁莽的”的 rasher 则是形容词 rash 的规则比较级，不能因为拼写相同就把两者视为同一构词来源。
etymology_story.en: The noun rasher, recorded since the sixteenth century, has an uncertain origin and may be connected with an obsolete verb rash meaning to cut or slash. The adjective rasher is the regular comparative of rash, meaning reckless, and its identical spelling does not establish a shared formation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名词 rasher 在现代英语中整体记忆，复数为 rashers，不分析成 rash + 表示人的 -er。形容词则明确为 rash（鲁莽的）+ 比较级 -er → rasher；同族形式包括 rashest（最鲁莽的）、rashly（鲁莽地）和 rashness（鲁莽）。bacon rasher（培根片）是名词复合形式。
morphology_enriched.en: The noun rasher is a whole base in modern English, with the plural rashers; its ending is not the person-forming suffix -er. The adjective is transparently rash, meaning reckless, + comparative -er → rasher; related forms include rashest, rashly, and rashness. Bacon rasher is a noun compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slice（薄片）适用于多种食物，rasher 则主要专指培根或火腿的一片；more reckless（更不顾后果的）强调对危险或后果的漠视；more impetuous（更冲动的）强调一时冲动、未经思考。后两者与形容词 rasher 接近，不能替换其食物名词义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Slice applies to many foods, whereas a rasher is specifically a slice of bacon or ham; more reckless emphasizes disregard for danger or consequences; more impetuous emphasizes acting on sudden impulse without thinking. The latter two overlap with the adjective rasher, not the food noun.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 两条记忆线：盘里的 a rasher 是“一片培根”；比较行为时，rash + -er 就是“更鲁莽”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two tracks: a rasher on a plate is a slice of bacon; when comparing behavior, rash + -er means more reckless.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。dilly + -s → dillies（多个出色的人或事物，y 变 i 再加 -es）；这是名词数量变化，不把整词拆成 dill 与 -y。

etymology.text: 这个名词来自英语中已废弃的形容词 dilly，意思是“令人愉快的”。该形容词可能由 delightful 缩短、变形而来；可以把它与“让人眼前一亮的好东西”联系起来。

usage_note: 非正式、较老派的赞赏用语；常见 a dilly of a ...。本课不教旧时马车义，也不采用与此名词无关的动词变形。

senses.meaning_en: A remarkable or unusual person or thing, especially in informal American English.

etymology_story.zh: dilly 这一名词通常被认为来自现已过时的形容词 dilly，意为“令人愉快的”，而该形容词可能是 delightful 的缩略变体。它后来用于指令人印象深刻或非同寻常的人和事物，有时也包括格外棘手的事情。
etymology_story.en: The noun dilly is generally traced to an obsolete adjective meaning 'delightful,' possibly an altered shortening of delightful. It came to describe impressive or unusual people and things, sometimes including exceptionally difficult situations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 dilly 作为不可进一步分析的词基，不拆成 dill + -y。复数为 dillies，即辅音字母后的 y 变为 -ies；没有常用的派生词族，dilly-dally 也不是它的常规派生词。本条 CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估计，并非官方定级。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dilly is an unanalyzed base, not dill + -y. Its plural is dillies, formed by replacing consonant-final y with -ies; it has no common productive derivative family, and dilly-dally is not a regular derivative. The CEFR-C2 tag here is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official rating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wonder（奇才；奇物）突出惊叹和赞赏；marvel（令人惊叹的人或事物）更强调卓越；humdinger（非凡的人或事物）与 dilly 一样口语化，但语气往往更强烈。dilly 也可诙谐地形容格外难办的事情。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wonder emphasizes admiration and amazement; marvel more strongly suggests exceptional excellence; humdinger is similarly informal but often more emphatic. Dilly can also humorously describe something exceptionally troublesome.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借可能的 delightful 联系记忆：让人眼前一亮，或让人直呼“真不一般”的，就是 a dilly。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the possible delightful connection: a dilly makes you think 'What a remarkable one!'

etymology.text: harridan 可能由法语 haridelle 变形而来，原词指老马，也曾用来贬称瘦削的女人；进入英语后成为对尖刻女人的贬称。这个来源可以帮助理解它为什么带有明显恶意，但不宜拿来称呼别人。

etymology_story.zh: harridan 的来源尚不完全确定，通常认为它可能是法语 haridelle 的变形；后者指瘦弱、衰老的马，也曾被用来贬称女人。进入英语后，它发展为对脾气暴躁、尖刻专横的女人的辱称。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 harridan 作为不可进一步分析的借入词基，不拆成 harri + dan。复数为 harridans；没有需要作为常用词族掌握的派生词。本条 CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估计，并非官方定级。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shrew emphasizes an argumentative, bad-tempered woman; termagant is more dated or literary and suggests noisy aggression; nag emphasizes repeated complaints or demands and need not refer to a woman. These terms can all be derogatory, while harridan particularly evokes a hostile caricature of an older woman.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool is broad and can emphasize poor judgment; idiot is usually more direct and cutting; prat is another British informal insult for someone foolish or irritating. Burk has a distinctly British colloquial flavor and can range from teasing to insulting.

mnemonic_anchor.en: First link the spellings: burk = berk. Then picture someone being called a fool after a silly mistake; historically, the word is a shortened rhyming-slang expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 momento 作为整体词形，不分析为 moment + -o；通常复数为 momentos。它与标准拼写 memento 是变体关系；标准词的复数为 mementos 或 mementoes，没有常用的派生词族。正式写作宜用 memento；本条 CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估计，并非官方定级。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, momento is treated as a whole form, not moment + -o; its usual plural is momentos. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Memento is the standard spelling with the same meaning; keepsake emphasizes personal affection or a gift relationship; souvenir commonly relates to travel, a place, or an event and may be a purchased item. Momento differs chiefly in spelling status, not meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住拉丁语“记住”的意思：纪念物让记忆留下来；同时记牢标准拼写 memento，第二个元音是 e。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the Latin idea 'remember': the object keeps a memory alive. Remember the standard spelling memento, with e as its second vowel.

etymology_story.en: Anaconda is generally traced to Sinhala henakandayā, originally the name of a Sri Lankan snake, although the exact route of transmission is uncertain. In English, the name was later transferred to large aquatic boas of South America.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作有效词缀分析的借词：anaconda + -s → anacondas（复数）。没有常用的派生动词或形容词；green anaconda（绿森蚺）等是物种名称中的名词短语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, anaconda is a borrowed base without a productive internal prefix–root–suffix analysis: anaconda + -s → anacondas. It has no common derived verb or adjective; expressions such as green anaconda are noun phrases used as species names.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boa is a broader term that includes anacondas; constrictor describes a snake by its method of killing prey rather than its species; python refers to a different group of snakes with a similar appearance and hunting method.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借来的蛇名，后来落在南美水中巨蛇身上：anaconda → 森蚺。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A borrowed snake name acquired a new home: picture anaconda as a huge South American water snake.

senses.sentence_zh: 最后一首歌响起时，我们到前排跳了一场冲撞舞。

etymology_story.zh: mosh 在20世纪80年代的硬核朋克等音乐场景中流行起来，通常被认为是 mash 或 mush 的变体，但具体来源仍有不确定性。它逐渐专指观众随强烈音乐跳跃、互相推挤的舞蹈方式。
etymology_story.en: Mosh became established in hardcore punk and related music scenes during the 1980s and is usually treated as a variant of mash or mush, although its precise origin remains uncertain. It came to denote dancing that involves jumping and pushing against other people.

morphology_enriched.zh: mosh 是现代英语中的整体词根：mosh + -es → moshes（第三人称单数）；mosh + -ed → moshed（过去式、过去分词）；mosh + -ing → moshing（现在分词，也可指冲撞舞活动）；mosh + -er → mosher（跳冲撞舞的人）。复合词 mosh pit 指演出中供观众跳冲撞舞的区域；mosh 也可不加词缀转作名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Mosh functions as a whole modern base: mosh + -es → moshes; mosh + -ed → moshed; mosh + -ing → moshing, a participle and an activity noun; mosh + -er → mosher, a participant. The compound mosh pit names the area where people mosh; mosh also functions as a noun through conversion.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slam-dance（跳冲撞舞）：最接近，强调身体碰撞；pogo（直上直下地蹦跳）：强调反复垂直跳跃，不一定互相推挤；headbang（甩头）：强调随音乐猛烈摆头，可以站在原地进行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Slam-dance is the closest equivalent and emphasizes bodily collisions; pogo emphasizes repeated vertical jumping without necessarily pushing others; headbang means moving the head vigorously to music and can be done while standing in place.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 mash 的“挤成一团”：人群随重拍跳跃推挤，就是 mosh；这一联想不代表词源已确定。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of people being mashed together as they jump to a heavy beat: that is moshing. This association is a memory aid, not a claim of certain origin.

pronunciation.note: 英式读音，重音在第一音节；x 读 /ks/。

forms: 形容词，不加名词复数或动词时态词尾。oxo- 也用作化学构词成分。
family: oxoacid 含氧酸；ox- / oxo- 表示氧的构词成分。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。相关构词：oxo-（含氧） + acid（酸） → oxoacid（含氧酸）；这里的 oxo- 表示与氧有关，不是 ox（牛）。

etymology.text: 英语化学用语 oxo 来自表示氧的 ox-；这一构词成分借自法语 oxygène（氧）。沿着“氧的名称 → 含氧的化学用语”这条线记忆。

usage_note: 用于化学名称或描述，常见于 oxo compound、oxo group。此处学习形容词“含氧的、氧代的”；OxO 等品牌字样不属于这个义项。普通句中小写。

senses.meaning_zh: 氧代的；含有与另一原子形成双键的氧原子的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to an oxygen atom doubly bonded to another atom.
senses.english_definition: An oxo group contains an oxygen atom joined to another atom by a double bond.
senses.collocation_en: an oxo group; an oxo compound
senses.collocation_zh: 一个氧代基团；一种氧代化合物
senses.sentence_en: The structure contains an oxo group attached to the central metal atom.
senses.sentence_zh: 该结构含有一个与中心金属原子相连的氧代基团。

senses.pos: combining form 构词成分（写作 oxo-；化学）
senses.meaning_zh: 表示氧或氧代基团；用于某些含氧化合物名称
senses.meaning_en: A chemical word-forming element indicating oxygen or an oxo group.
senses.english_definition: Oxo- is used in chemical names to indicate oxygen, especially an oxygen atom attached by a double bond.
senses.collocation_en: 2-oxopropanoic acid; an oxoacid
senses.collocation_zh: 2-氧代丙酸；一种含氧酸
senses.sentence_en: The prefix oxo- in 2-oxopropanoic acid identifies a doubly bonded oxygen atom.
senses.sentence_zh: 2-氧代丙酸名称中的前缀 oxo- 标明了一个以双键连接的氧原子。

etymology_story.zh: oxo 是由氧的名称发展出的化学构词形式，与 oxygen 以及法语 oxygène 有关。其更早的希腊语构词背景表示“生酸”，反映了早期化学家对氧与酸之间关系的认识；后来 oxo 在化学命名中获得了专门用途。
etymology_story.en: Oxo developed as a chemical word-forming element associated with oxygen and French oxygène. The earlier Greek elements conveyed the idea of producing acid, reflecting an early theory about oxygen; oxo later acquired specialized uses in chemical nomenclature.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词中可分析为表示氧的 ox- 加连接元音 -o-，形成 oxo-；它不是 ox（牛）的派生词。常见相关构词有 oxo- + acid → oxoacid（含氧酸）、oxo- + anion → oxoanion（含氧阴离子）；oxygen（氧）、oxide（氧化物）和 oxidation（氧化）属于相关术语，并非都由 oxo 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern chemical word formation, oxo- can be analyzed as oxygen-related ox- plus the linking vowel -o-; it is unrelated to ox, the animal. Related formations include oxo- + acid → oxoacid and oxo- + anion → oxoanion. Oxygen, oxide, and oxidation are related terms, not all direct derivatives of oxo.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oxygen-containing（含氧的）：范围最广，不限定成键方式；carbonyl（羰基的）：专指碳氧双键，范围比 oxo 窄；keto（酮基的、酮式的）：用于与酮有关的结构或命名语境，不能替代所有 oxo 用法。这些词是相关术语，并非完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oxygen-containing is broader and does not specify bonding; carbonyl specifically concerns a carbon–oxygen double bond and is narrower than oxo; keto applies in ketone-related structural or naming contexts and cannot replace every use of oxo. These are related terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 oxo，先想到氧 O；在氧代命名中，再想到双键连接的氧。
mnemonic_anchor.en: See oxo, think oxygen, O; in oxo nomenclature, picture an oxygen atom attached by a double bond.

pronunciation.note: 采用非卷舌英式标法 /dʒʊə/；卷舌读音末尾可带 /r/。开头是 /dʒ/，与 job、judge 的首音相同，不是 yes 的 /j/。

forms: 第三人称单数 jures；过去式、过去分词 jured；现在分词 juring（去掉末尾 e）。
family: juror 陪审员；jury 陪审团。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。词形对应可记作 jure（去末尾 e） + -or（人） → juror（陪审员）。历史顺序是先有 juror，再逆构出动词 jure，不能把这个记忆公式当成历史先后。

etymology.text: 英语动词 jure 从 juror（陪审员）逆构而来：人们把表示人的词尾去掉，得到“使人成为陪审员”的动词。记住“陪审员 → 任命为陪审员”的方向即可。

usage_note: 罕用法律动词，后接被任命的人。日常通常说 appoint someone as a juror。de jure 是另一条拉丁语短语，不能把这里的动词直接解释成“法律上的”。

sentence: The court will jure the selected citizens before the trial begins.
translation: 法庭将在审判开始前任命选中的公民为陪审员。
scenario: 阅读描述旧时法庭程序的文字，确认选中的公民将承担什么角色。
cloze: The court will _____ the selected citizens before the trial begins.
collocation:
jure citizens for a criminal trial 为刑事审判任命公民担任陪审员
jure a replacement for a civil case 为民事案件任命替补陪审员
context_hint: The selected citizen will become a member of the jury.
hint: The selected citizen will become a member of the jury.

teaching.contrast: jure 是动词，指任命某人为陪审员；juror 指这个人，jury 指整个陪审团。它不表示任命辩护律师。
teaching.sentence: The court needed to jure another citizen after a panel member withdrew.
teaching.translation: 一名陪审团成员退出后，法庭需要另任命一位公民为陪审员。

comprehension_check.sentence: The court will jure Mara so that she can serve on the jury.
comprehension_check.question: 句中目标词表示哪一个意思？
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: serve on the jury 表示加入陪审团，因此 jure 指任命为陪审员；不是让她担任辩护律师。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（任命为陪审员／任命为辩护律师）
fields.wrong_reason: serve on the jury 表示加入陪审团，因此 jure 指任命为陪审员；不是让她担任辩护律师。

senses.meaning_zh: 使宣誓就任陪审员；使成为陪审员
senses.meaning_en: To swear someone in as a juror.
senses.english_definition: If an official jures someone, the official swears that person in to serve as a juror.
senses.collocation_en: jure a person; be jured as a juror
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人宣誓就任陪审员；经宣誓成为陪审员
senses.sentence_en: The selected citizens were jured before the trial began.
senses.sentence_zh: 审判开始前，获选的公民宣誓就任了陪审员。

etymology_story.zh: 这个罕用动词通常解释为由 juror（陪审员）逆构而成，即去掉被理解为表示人的词尾，形成“使成为陪审员”的动词。juror 的更早来源与古法语及拉丁语中“宣誓”的词有关。
etymology_story.en: This rare verb is generally explained as a back-formation from juror, created by removing what was interpreted as a person-denoting ending. Juror ultimately belongs to an Old French and Latin word history involving the act of swearing an oath.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词方向是 juror → jure，而不是先有 jure 再加 -or。动词变化为 jures、jured、juring；相关词有 juror（陪审员）和 jury（陪审团），但不能把这些都说成 jure 的派生词。常见短语 de jure 中的 jure 是拉丁语词形，与这个英语动词的用法不同。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical word-formation direction is juror → jure, rather than jure + -or → juror. Its inflected forms are jures, jured, and juring; related words include juror and jury, which should not all be described as derivatives of jure. The jure in the familiar phrase de jure is a Latin form with a different grammatical role.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: swear in（使宣誓就职）：最自然的现代替换，但适用对象不限于陪审员；empanel（选任、组成陪审团）：侧重选定或组建陪审团，不一定专指宣誓步骤；appoint（任命）：意义更宽，不包含宣誓这一要求。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Swear in is the most natural modern equivalent but applies to offices beyond jury service; empanel emphasizes selecting or constituting a jury and does not necessarily identify the oath-taking step; appoint is broader and does not imply an oath.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 juror“陪审员”倒推：jure 就是“使人成为宣誓就任的陪审员”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Work backward from juror: to jure someone is to make that person a sworn juror.

pronunciation.note: 英式读音；末尾 q 在这个法语借词中读 /k/。美式常读 /kɑːk/。

forms: 复数 coqs；另有拼写 coque。
family: coque 同一羽饰词的另一拼写；coquet 与其法语词根相关，指卖弄风情者。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。法语中 coq（公鸡） + -et（指小词尾） → coquet，后来也用来形容卖弄风情的人；这条同根线索帮助记住 coq 的“公鸡羽毛”形象。

etymology.text: 英语 coq 借自法语 coq（公鸡），法语形式又来自古法语 coc。公鸡的羽毛被用来装饰帽子，英语便用这个名称指这种羽饰。

usage_note: 罕见服饰用语，本课专指公鸡羽毛制成的帽饰。英语日常说公鸡通常用 rooster 或 cock；菜名 coq au vin 中则保留法语“鸡”的意思，不是帽饰。

senses.meaning_zh: 公鸡羽毛制成的女帽饰物；公鸡羽毛帽饰材料（罕见制帽术语）
senses.meaning_en: A woman's hat trimming made from rooster feathers, or the feathers used for it; a rare millinery term.
senses.english_definition: Coq is a decoration made from rooster feathers that is attached to a woman's hat.
senses.collocation_en: black coq; coq feathers (historical millinery combinations rather than high-frequency general English)
senses.collocation_zh: 黑色公鸡羽饰；制帽用公鸡羽毛（历史制帽用语，并非普通英语高频搭配）
senses.sentence_en: The vintage hat was trimmed with black coq.
senses.sentence_zh: 这顶古董女帽饰有黑色公鸡羽毛。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 coq“公鸡”，上溯古法语 coc；英语制帽用语把鸟的名称转用于其羽毛制成的帽饰。[来源：韦氏词典](https://scrabble.m-w.com/dictionary/coq)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French coq, meaning 'rooster', from Old French coc, the word acquired a specialized millinery meaning for hat trimming made from the bird's feathers. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://scrabble.m-w.com/dictionary/coq)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的借词词基 coq，无可识别的英语前缀或后缀。可数用法的复数为 coqs，另有拼写变体 coque；没有常用的英语派生词族。coquet、coquette、coquetry 与它有法语词源联系，但不是现代英语直接由 coq 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, coq is an unanalyzable borrowed base with no identifiable English prefix or suffix. Its countable plural is coqs, and coque is a spelling variant; it has no common English derivative family. Coquet, coquette, and coquetry are historically related through French, rather than direct modern English derivatives of coq.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cock-feather trimming（公鸡羽毛饰边）是最准确的释义性替换；plume（装饰羽毛、羽饰）范围更广；aigrette（簇状羽饰）强调直立或喷散的形状，不限定使用公鸡羽毛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cock-feather trimming is the closest descriptive equivalent; plume is broader and can denote other decorative feathers; aigrette emphasizes an upright or spray-shaped ornament without specifying rooster feathers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 法语“公鸡” → 公鸡羽毛 → 帽上的羽饰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: French 'rooster' → rooster feathers → a feather ornament on a hat.

pronunciation.note: 采用苏格兰词典列出的 /fuː/ 读音；ou 在这里读长音 /uː/。

forms: 形容词，没有动词时态变化；常置于 be、get 等动词后。另可见方言拼写 fu'、foo、fow。
family: full 满的，同源的普通英语形式；fullness 满的状态、充实。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。fou 是 full 的苏格兰形式；用同源词的真实派生关系 full + -ness → fullness（满的状态）记住“满”这条线索。本课的 fou 则指饮酒后“醉了”的状态。

etymology.text: 来自中古英语苏格兰形式 fow（满的），它又来自中古英语 full。词义从“满”转到“喝得满了、醉了”，就能把形式和意思连起来记。

usage_note: 苏格兰用语，多见于地方对话、诗歌或旧作品。普通英语表达醉酒通常用 drunk。法语 fou 可表示“疯的”，不要把那个法语义项带到本课。

senses.sentence_zh: 到了午夜，他已酩酊大醉，正扯着嗓子唱歌。

senses.meaning_zh: 满的；吃饱的（苏格兰用语）
senses.meaning_en: Full or having eaten enough; Scots usage.
senses.english_definition: If something is fou, it is full, and if a person is fou after eating, they have had enough food.
senses.collocation_en: fou o' (Scots: full of); a fou man
senses.collocation_zh: 充满……；一个吃饱的人
senses.sentence_en: The bairns were warm and fou after their supper.
senses.sentence_zh: 孩子们吃过晚饭后，身上暖和，肚子也饱了。

senses.meaning_zh: 很；十分；完全地（传统苏格兰方言用法）
senses.meaning_en: Very, quite, or fully; traditional Scots dialect usage.
senses.english_definition: In traditional Scots, fou can be used before another expression to emphasize its degree.
senses.collocation_en: fou weel; fou lang (traditional dialect combinations)
senses.collocation_zh: 十分好；很久（传统方言搭配）
senses.sentence_en: Ye ken fou weel why I came.
senses.sentence_zh: 你很清楚我为什么来。

etymology_story.zh: 苏格兰语 fou 与英语 full 同源，可追溯至古英语 full；“醉”义由“满的”，尤其“满肚子酒”，发展而来。[来源：苏格兰语词典](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/fou)
etymology_story.en: Scots fou shares its origin with English full, ultimately from Old English full; its drinking sense developed from being full, especially full of liquor. [Source: Dictionaries of the Scots Language](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/fou)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式 fou 是独立词基，不宜拆成英语词根与词缀；常见变体有 fu'、foo 和 fow。词典另收 fou + -ish → fouish“微醉的”，但该派生词罕见。full、fully、fullness 属于同源的标准英语词族，并非直接由 fou 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern fou is an independent base rather than a combination of English root and affixes; variants include fu', foo, and fow. Dictionaries also record fou + -ish → fouish, meaning slightly drunk, although this derivative is rare. Full, fully, and fullness belong to the cognate standard English family, rather than being derived directly from fou.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: drunk（醉的）是“醉酒”义的中性标准英语对应词；tipsy（微醉的）程度较轻；full（满的、饱的）对应其基本义，也说明“喝得满满的”这一语义联系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drunk is the neutral standard English equivalent of the intoxication sense; tipsy indicates milder intoxication; full corresponds to the basic sense and explains the semantic connection with being full of drink.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 full 联想 fou：肚子装满食物是“饱”，装满酒则可能“醉”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fou with full: full of food means satisfied; full of drink can mean drunk.

meaning: 达尔拉迪岩系的（主要形成于前寒武纪，并延伸至寒武纪）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号标出重读音节；本卡采用美式读音。

forms: 地质专名形容词，不作常规比较级变化。
family: Dalriada 苏格兰古地区名。

morphology.text: Dalrad-（古地名 Dalriada 的变形）+ -ian（属于……的）→ Dalradian（达尔拉迪岩系的）。专名作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语地质名称取自苏格兰古地区名 Dalriada，再接表示“属于某地”的 -ian。把古地名与当地的古老岩层一起记。

relations.meaning: 前寒武纪（涵盖该岩系的主要形成时期，但不是其完整年代范围）

usage_note: 地质学专门用语。Dalradian 首字母大写，常修饰 rocks、strata 或 Supergroup；本卡只教形容词。
sentence: The geologist mapped the Dalradian rocks along the valley.

context_hint: Look at the geological rock unit being mapped.

teaching.contrast: Dalradian 指特定岩系，主要形成于前寒武纪，并延伸至寒武纪；Precambrian 只表示前寒武纪这一时间范围，不能涵盖整个岩系。
teaching.sentence: The museum displays a sample of Dalradian schist.
