etymology_story.zh: 经南非荷兰语传入英语，源自科伊科伊语中与“干燥、干硬地面”有关的词。这个描述地表特征的名称后来用于南非内陆大片半干旱地区。
etymology_story.en: English acquired karoo through South African Dutch from a Khoekhoe word associated with dryness or hard, dry ground. This description of the landscape became the name of a large semiarid region in inland South Africa.

morphology_enriched.zh: karoo 是完整借词，karroo 是异体拼写；作为地名通常写作 Karoo。相关罕见形容词 karroid 表示“卡鲁式的、具有卡鲁特征的”，可理解为经词干拼写调整后加 -oid“类似……的”；Karoo vegetation 等结构中的 Karoo 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Karoo is a whole borrowing, with karroo as a variant spelling; the geographical name is normally capitalized as Karoo. The rare related adjective karroid means 'resembling or characteristic of the Karoo' and reflects an adjusted stem plus -oid, 'resembling'; Karoo in expressions such as Karoo vegetation is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: semidesert（半荒漠）最接近其气候和植被特征；dryland（旱地）是更宽泛的环境类别；vel d 通常写作 veld（南部非洲开阔原野），不一定同样干旱。Karoo 还具有明确的地域指向，不能与这些普通地貌词完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Semidesert most closely describes its climatic and vegetation conditions; dryland is a broader environmental category; veld means open country in southern Africa and need not be equally dry. Karoo also identifies a particular region, so these landscape terms are not exact substitutes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字抓住地表：干、硬、少雨 → 南非卡鲁高原。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let the name evoke the ground: dry, hard, and rain-starved → South Africa's Karoo.

etymology.text: 本课法庭义来自盎格鲁法语 lete 或中世纪拉丁语 leta。把村民到地方小法庭解决纠纷的场景与词义连起来记；不是网络上的 elite 缩写。

etymology_story.zh: 历史法律义与盎格鲁法语 lete、中世纪拉丁语 leta 等形式有关，更早的来源不确定。网络义则独立产生于 elite“精英的”的缩略和变体拼写，后来也指以数字、符号替换字母的书写方式，与旧法庭义没有词源联系。
etymology_story.en: The historical legal word is associated with Anglo-French lete and Medieval Latin leta, although its earlier origin is uncertain. The internet word arose independently as a shortening and respelling of elite and came to denote writing that replaces letters with numbers or symbols; it is unrelated to the old court term.

morphology_enriched.zh: 法律义 leet 是现代英语中不可再分析的历史词基；leet + -man → leetman，指受该法庭管辖的人，复数为 leetmen，属罕见历史用词。网络义来自 elite 的截短；leet + speak → leetspeak，另有 l33t、1337 等变体拼写；elite、elitist、elitism 是来源相关词，不是由 leet 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: The legal leet is an unanalyzed historical base in modern English; leet + -man forms the rare historical leetman, a person subject to the court's jurisdiction, with the plural leetmen. Internet leet is clipped from elite; leet + speak forms leetspeak, and l33t and 1337 are alternative spellings; elite, elitist, and elitism are source-related words, not direct derivatives of leet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: court leet 明确表示历史法庭，local court 只是较宽泛的描述；网络名词 leetspeak 与 leet 基本同义；elite 对应其形容词义，语域更广，而 leet 带有网络社群色彩，常用于戏谑或炫技。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Court leet specifies the historical institution, while local court is only a broader description; leetspeak is essentially synonymous with the internet noun leet; elite matches the adjective's meaning but has a wider register, whereas leet signals internet culture and is often playful or boastful.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分成两条记忆线：古代 leet 是地方小法庭；网络 elite 截短成 leet，再变写成 1337。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two separate hooks: historical leet is a local court; online elite shortens to leet and becomes 1337.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经现代希腊语 mousakas 和土耳其语 musakka 借入；《韦氏词典》将其进一步追溯至埃及阿拉伯语 musaggaʽa，字面义为“冷却的”。这个历史名称并不表示今天的菜必须冷食。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/moussaka)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the name through Modern Greek mousakas and Turkish musakka; Merriam-Webster traces it further to Egyptian Arabic musaggaʽa, literally meaning chilled. This historical name does not require the modern dish to be served cold. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/moussaka)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作常规词根、词缀拆分的借词。可作不可数菜名，也可作可数名词表示不同份数或种类：moussaka + -s → moussakas；另有较少见拼写 mousaka。没有常用的派生词族；moussaka dish 是名词短语，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed base without a productive root-and-affix breakdown. It can be uncountable as a food name or countable for portions or varieties: moussaka + -s → moussakas; mousaka is a less common spelling. There is no established common derivational family; moussaka dish is a noun phrase, not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格同义词。casserole（烤制炖菜）和 bake（烤菜）是较宽泛的菜肴类别；aubergine bake（茄子烤菜）只说明主要食材和烹饪方式，不保证采用穆萨卡的配方。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Casserole and bake name broader categories of dishes; aubergine bake identifies an ingredient and cooking method without specifying a moussaka recipe.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借词按菜名整块记：茄子、肉末，希腊式常盖白酱；历史上的“冷却”不等于今天冷食。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the borrowed dish name as one unit: aubergines and mince, often topped with white sauce in Greece; its historical cooling sense does not dictate serving temperature.

etymology_story.zh: 来自印地语、乌尔都语 pakkā，含“煮熟的、成熟的、坚实的”等义，其历史来源是梵语 pakva。“成熟、做得到位”的含义在英语中发展为“正宗、可靠、优质”，也用于表示合乎传统上流社会标准。[词源及义项依据：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pukka)
etymology_story.en: Pukka comes from Hindi and Urdu pakkā, meaning cooked, ripe, or solid, historically from Sanskrit pakva. The idea of being mature or properly finished developed into English meanings involving authenticity, reliability, quality, and conventional upper-class respectability. [Source for history and senses: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pukka)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按完整借词处理，不拆成 puk + -ka。相关拼写有 pucka、pukkah，以及南亚建筑语境常见的 pucca；这些是拼写变体，不是派生词。没有常用的副词、动词或抽象名词派生；pukkaness 即使偶见，也不宜作为核心常用词族教授。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat pukka as a complete borrowed base, not as puk + -ka. Related spellings include pucka, pukkah, and pucca, which is frequent in South Asian building contexts; these are spelling variants, not derivatives. There are no common adverbial, verbal, or abstract-noun derivatives; occasional pukkaness should not be taught as a core family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: genuine（真正的）强调并非假冒；first-rate（一流的）强调质量优秀；posh（上流派头的）强调阶层、口音或生活方式。pukka 可随语境表达这些不同含义，南亚建筑义则强调材料和结构的耐久性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Genuine emphasizes authenticity; first-rate emphasizes excellent quality; posh emphasizes social class, accent, or lifestyle. Pukka can express these different ideas according to context, while its South Asian building sense concerns durable materials and construction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “熟了、成了、做扎实了”→ 正宗、优质、牢靠；这是语义联系，不是英语词缀拆分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cooked, complete, and solid → authentic, excellent, and dependable: a semantic connection, not an English affix analysis.

In English it names the particular pouch worn at the front of a kilt in traditional Scottish Highland dress. morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是完整借词：sporran + -s → sporrans（复数）。没有常用的派生词族；sporran-maker（苏格兰腰袋制作人）是透明复合词。sporraned 一类“佩戴腰袋的”形式即使出现，也属于少见构词，不构成常用形容词义项。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English this is an intact borrowed base: sporran + -s → sporrans, the plural. There is no common derivational family; sporran-maker is a transparent compound. Forms such as sporraned, meaning equipped with a sporran, are uncommon formations rather than established common adjective senses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pouch（小袋）强调袋子的形状和功能；purse（钱袋）强调装钱；belt pouch（腰带袋）强调佩戴方式。sporran 则专指与苏格兰短裙搭配的传统腰袋。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pouch describes a small bag; purse emphasizes carrying money; belt pouch describes how a bag is worn. Sporran specifically identifies the traditional pouch worn with a Scottish kilt.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Fix the Gaelic purse meaning to one image: a small pouch hanging in front of a kilt.

etymology_story.zh: 扫帚义经中古英语传自古英语 besma、besema，与德语 Besen 同源。方言中称呼女人的义项词源存在争议，不宜断言它必定由“扫帚”引申而来。[词源及义项依据：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/besom)
etymology_story.en: The broom word descends through Middle English from Old English besma or besema and is cognate with German Besen. The origin of the dialect term for a woman is disputed; it should not confidently be presented as a simple extension of broom. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/besom)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按完整词基处理，不拆成 be- + som。名词复数 besoms；罕见动词由名词零派生，屈折形式为 besoms、besomed、besoming。透明复合词有 besom-maker（枝条扫帚制作人）；不把未经充分确立的 besomer 列为核心词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat besom as a complete modern base, not be- + som. The noun plural is besoms; the rare verb is formed by conversion and inflects as besoms, besomed, and besoming. Besom-maker is a transparent compound; insufficiently established besomer is excluded from the core family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: broom（扫帚）是一般名称，besom 通常特指枝条扎成的传统扫帚；brush（刷子）范围更广，也用于扫冰工具；sweep（清扫）是普通动词，而动词 besom 罕见且限定所用工具。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Broom is the general term, while besom usually specifies a traditional twig broom. Brush is broader and also applies to curling equipment. Sweep is the ordinary verb; verbal besom is rare and specifies the implement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一束细枝扎成扫帚；把动作也叫 besom，就是“用这种扫帚扫”。方言人物称呼另记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture twigs tied into a broom; using the same word as a verb means sweeping with it. Learn the dialect personal term separately.

etymology.text: 经中古法语 grotte 追到意大利语 grotta，意思是“洞穴”。想象花园里一个清凉的小洞窟，记住这一文学性词语。

senses.meaning_en: a grotto or small cave, in poetic or literary usage

etymology_story.zh: 文学性的“洞窟”义来自法语 grotte，进一步来自意大利语 grotta。现代俚语“污垢”义则由 grotty（脏兮兮的、糟糕的）缩略而来，不能直接解释成“洞穴变脏了”。[词源及义项依据：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grot)
etymology_story.en: The literary cave word comes from French grotte, ultimately from Italian grotta. The modern slang word for dirt was shortened from grotty, meaning dirty or unpleasant; it should not be explained as a cave becoming dirty. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/grot)

morphology_enriched.zh: 两义在现代英语中都按完整词基处理。文学义为可数名词：grot + -s → grots，与 grotto（洞窟）相关；污垢义通常不可数，其构词方向是 grotty → grot，而不是先有 grot 再加 -y。相关形式有 grotty → grottier、grottiest，以及 grotty + -ness → grottiness（肮脏、糟糕的状态）。
morphology_enriched.en: Both meanings function as complete modern bases. The literary noun is countable: grot + -s → grots, and is related to grotto. The dirt noun is normally uncountable and was formed in the direction grotty → grot, rather than grot + -y. Related forms include grottier, grottiest, and grotty + -ness → grottiness, meaning dirtiness or unpleasantness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grime（积垢）强调积聚、附着的污垢；filth（污秽）强调肮脏和令人厌恶，二者对应现代俚语义；grotto（小洞窟）对应文学义，通常比 grot 更中性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grime emphasizes accumulated, adhering dirt; filth emphasizes disgusting dirtiness, and both correspond to the modern slang sense. Grotto corresponds to the literary cave sense and is generally more neutral than grot.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 双画面分开记：诗里的 grot 是小洞窟；厨房里的 grot 是脏垢，联系 grotty 记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two pictures separate: a poetic grot is a little cave; kitchen grot is dirt, remembered through grotty.

etymology_story.zh: Luminol 是现代化学名称，以拉丁语 lumen（光）的词干 lumin- 加上化学名称中使用的词尾 -ol 构成。名称中的“光”对应它在适当化学反应中发光的性质。
etymology_story.en: Luminol is a modern chemical name formed from lumin-, the stem of Latin lumen, meaning 'light', and the chemical naming ending -ol. The reference to light reflects its ability to glow during suitable chemical reactions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学命名结构：lumin-（光）+ -ol → luminol。现代英语通常将全词作为一个化学名称使用；这里的 -ol 不能据此理解为该物质属于醇类。相关构式有 luminol-based（以鲁米诺为基础的）和 luminol-enhanced（经鲁米诺增强的），没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific naming structure: lumin- ('light') + -ol → luminol. Modern English generally treats it as a single chemical name; the ending -ol does not mean that the substance is an alcohol. Related formations include luminol-based and luminol-enhanced, but there is no common independent derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 3-aminophthalhydrazide（3-氨基邻苯二甲酰肼）是同一物质的化学名称；chemiluminescent reagent（化学发光试剂）是范围更广的类别名称；isoluminol（异鲁米诺）是相关异构体，不能作为同义词互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 3-Aminophthalhydrazide is a chemical name for the same substance; chemiluminescent reagent names a broader category; isoluminol is a related isomer and is not an interchangeable synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect lumin- with light: picture the blue glow of a luminol reaction.

etymology.text: 英语从法语 natron 借入，经阿拉伯语 naṭrūn 追到希腊语 nítron，指“硝碱”。把这个古老的矿物名与天然碱联系起来记。

senses.meaning_zh: 天然碱；矿物学上指十水碳酸钠，也指以碳酸钠为主的天然盐类混合物
senses.meaning_en: Hydrated sodium carbonate, or a natural salt mixture rich in sodium carbonate.
senses.english_definition: Natron is a naturally occurring mineral or salt mixture containing sodium carbonate that was historically used for cleaning and preserving bodies.
senses.collocation_en: natron deposits; natron crystals
senses.collocation_zh: 天然碱矿床；天然碱晶体
senses.sentence_en: Ancient Egyptian embalmers used natron to dry the body before wrapping it.
senses.sentence_zh: 古埃及的遗体防腐师用天然碱使遗体干燥，然后再进行包裹。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 natron 借自法语，其词源链涉及西班牙语和阿拉伯语 naṭrūn，并可追溯到希腊语 nitron，指天然碱性盐。这个古老的物质名称后来成为含水碳酸钠矿物的名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed natron from French, with a borrowing history involving Spanish and Arabic naṭrūn and reaching back to Greek nitron, a name for natural alkaline salts. The old substance name later became a mineralogical term for hydrated sodium carbonate.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：natron 是不可再按常用英语词缀拆分的借词，通常作不可数名词。natron deposits（天然碱矿床）中的 natron 是名词作定语；它没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生系列。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphology: natron is a borrowed word with no productive breakdown into ordinary English affixes and is normally uncountable. In natron deposits, natron is an attributive noun; it has no common series of derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: washing soda（洗涤碱）通常指作为清洁用品使用的含水碳酸钠；soda ash（纯碱）指无水碳酸钠；soda（碱、苏打）含义较宽且依语境变化。三者都与 natron 有关，但不能在所有矿物学或历史语境中替换它。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Washing soda usually means hydrated sodium carbonate used for cleaning; soda ash means anhydrous sodium carbonate; soda is broader and context-dependent. All three are related terms, but none replaces natron in every mineralogical or historical context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 natron 记成古埃及用来吸走水分的天然碱盐。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture natron as the natural alkaline salt used to draw moisture out of Egyptian mummies.

senses.meaning_zh: 神经酰胺；由鞘氨醇类碱基与脂肪酸通过酰胺键连接形成的一类脂质
senses.meaning_en: A lipid consisting of a sphingoid base joined to a fatty acid by an amide bond.
senses.english_definition: A ceramide is a type of fat molecule found in cell membranes that also helps the outer layer of the skin retain moisture.
senses.collocation_en: ceramide synthesis; ceramide-containing moisturizer
senses.collocation_zh: 神经酰胺合成；含神经酰胺的保湿霜
senses.sentence_en: Ceramides help the skin retain moisture and maintain its protective barrier.

etymology_story.zh: Ceramide 是由 cerebroside（脑苷脂）的开头部分与 amide（酰胺）组合而成的现代生化名称。这个名称反映了它与脑苷脂的化学关系，以及分子中的酰胺键。
etymology_story.en: Ceramide is a modern biochemical name combining the opening of cerebroside with amide. The name reflects its chemical relationship to cerebrosides and the amide bond in its molecular structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：cer-（截取自 cerebroside）+ amide（酰胺）→ ceramide；复数为 ceramides。主要相关词有 ceramidase（神经酰胺酶，分解神经酰胺的酶）、ceramide synthase（神经酰胺合酶）和 glycosylceramide（糖基神经酰胺）；ceramide-rich 表示“富含神经酰胺的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cer- (clipped from cerebroside) + amide → ceramide; the plural is ceramides. Major related terms include ceramidase, an enzyme that breaks down ceramides; ceramide synthase; and glycosylceramide. Ceramide-rich means containing a high proportion of ceramides.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: N-acylsphingoid base（N-酰基鞘氨醇类碱基）是结构性的对应名称；sphingolipid（鞘脂）是包含神经酰胺在内的更大类别；cerebroside（脑苷脂）是带有单糖基团的相关脂质，不能与 ceramide 混称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: N-Acylsphingoid base is a structural equivalent; sphingolipid names the larger class that includes ceramides; cerebroside is a related lipid bearing a single sugar unit and is not interchangeable with ceramide.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: amide 锚定“酰胺键”：把神经酰胺想成皮肤屏障中帮助封住水分的脂质。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let amide anchor the amide bond, then picture ceramides helping seal moisture into the skin barrier.

etymology_story.zh: Milch 经中古英语 milche 传自古英语表示“产奶的”的词形，与 milk（奶；挤奶）同源。它后来在 milch cow 中产生比喻义，把可持续挤奶的母牛比作不断被榨取利益的人或事物。
etymology_story.en: Milch comes through Middle English milche from an Old English form meaning 'giving milk' and is historically related to milk. The expression milch cow later developed a figurative meaning for a person or thing repeatedly exploited for money or benefits.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 milch 视为整体形容词，不能拆成 milk 加词缀。Milchy 是罕见的历史性派生词；常见相关词族以同源词 milk 为中心，包括 milking（挤奶）、milker（挤奶者；产奶牲畜）、milky（奶状的）和 milkiness（奶状性质），这些都不是由 milch 直接派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats milch as a whole adjective, not as milk plus an affix. Milchy is a rare historical derivative. The common related family centres on the cognate milk: milking, milker, milky, and milkiness; these are not direct derivatives of milch.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Milk-producing（产奶的）直接描述产奶能力；dairy（乳用的）强调饲养用途，如 dairy cattle；lactating（泌乳的）强调当前正在分泌乳汁的生理状态。Milch 带有传统农业用语色彩，现代普通英语通常更常用 dairy。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Milk-producing directly describes the ability to produce milk; dairy emphasizes agricultural purpose, as in dairy cattle; lactating describes the current physiological state of producing milk. Milch has a traditional agricultural flavour, while dairy is more usual in general modern English.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Link milch to milk: a literal cow supplies milk; a figurative one supplies money.

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆，核心是“独自”。semi- + solus → semi-solus（半独占式的）；这是广告用语，指版面上只与另一则广告共处，semi- 表示“半、部分”。

etymology.text: 直接借自拉丁语 solus，意思是“独自的”。剧本里其他角色都离场，只留一个角色在台上，就是这个词的典型场景。 拉丁语原词中的 sol- 是词干，-us 是阳性单数词尾；这是原语词形。

etymology_story.zh: Solus 直接借自拉丁语 sōlus，意为“独自的”。它先用于舞台说明，后来也用于广告业，表示广告在指定位置单独出现。
etymology_story.en: Solus was borrowed directly from Latin sōlus, meaning 'alone'. It was used in stage directions and later also in advertising to describe an advertisement appearing by itself in a designated position.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形态：solus 是整体拉丁语借词，没有常用英语派生系列；原拉丁语形式可分析为词干 sōl- 加阳性单数词尾 -us，但这不是现代英语的能产构词方式。广告术语 semi-solus 由 semi-（半、部分）加 solus 构成，通常表示与另一则广告共享位置；solo、solitary、solitude 是历史相关词，并非 solus 的现代英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphology: solus is a whole Latin borrowing with no common English derivational series. The Latin form contains the stem sōl- and masculine singular ending -us, but this is not productive English word formation. The advertising term semi-solus combines semi- ('half, partly') with solus and usually describes a position shared with one other advertisement. Solo, solitary, and solitude are historical relatives, not modern English derivatives of solus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Alone（独自的；独自地）最通用；solo（独自的；独自进行）常强调表演或活动由一人完成；unaccompanied（无人陪同的）强调没有同伴或伴奏。Solus 的使用范围更窄，主要属于舞台说明和广告术语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alone is the general term; solo often emphasizes a performance or activity carried out by one person; unaccompanied emphasizes the absence of companions or accompaniment. Solus is much more restricted, chiefly belonging to stage directions and advertising terminology.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用 solo 联想 solus：舞台只剩一人，广告位置只放一则。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect solus with solo: one person on stage, or one advertisement in its allotted space.

etymology_story.zh: guid 是苏格兰语中与标准英语 good 对应的本族词形式，两者都承续古英语 gōd。它不是现代英语 good 的随意错拼；其读音和拼写反映苏格兰语自身的历史发展。
etymology_story.en: Guid is the Scots counterpart of standard English good, and both continue Old English gōd. Its spelling and pronunciations reflect the historical development of Scots rather than an accidental misspelling of modern English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：guid 是不可进一步拆分的基本词，形容词、名词和副词用法不需要添加词缀；读音随方言变化。相关形式包括 guidness（善良；美好，对应 goodness）和 guidwill（善意，对应 goodwill）；标准英语对应词族有 good、goodness、goodwill，比较等级对应 better、best。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: guid is a simple base, with adjective, noun, and adverb uses requiring no added affix; pronunciation varies by dialect. Related Scots formations include guidness, corresponding to goodness, and guidwill, corresponding to goodwill; the standard English counterparts include good, goodness, and goodwill, with better and best supplying the comparative and superlative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: good 是标准英语中最直接的对应词；fine 常侧重质量优良或情况令人满意；well 对应副词 guid，强调动作完成得好，而不是事物本身的品质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Good is the direct standard English equivalent; fine often emphasizes high quality or a satisfactory condition; well corresponds to adverbial guid and describes how successfully an action is performed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 guid 与 good 成对记忆：同一历史根源，苏格兰语形式；再由“好”联想到“好处”和“做得好”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair guid with good: a shared historical source expressed through Scots, extending from being good to doing good and performing well.

etymology_story.zh: lempira 经洪都拉斯西班牙语进入英语，以十六世纪抵抗西班牙征服的伦卡族首领 Lempira 命名。人名成为货币单位名称后，英语中的普通名词通常写作小写。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed lempira from Honduran Spanish, where the currency was named after Lempira, a sixteenth-century Lenca leader associated with resistance to Spanish conquest. As a common noun naming a monetary unit, it is normally written with a lowercase initial.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：lempira 是以人名为来源的完整借词，英语中不拆作词根和词缀；复数为 lempiras。lempira note（伦皮拉纸币）和 lempira exchange rate（伦皮拉汇率）是名词组合，不是派生词；没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: lempira is an intact borrowed word derived from a personal name, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is lempiras. Lempira note and lempira exchange rate are noun combinations rather than derivatives, and there is no established common English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Honduran currency（洪都拉斯货币）是概括性表达；monetary unit（货币单位）是上位概念，两者都不是严格同义词。HNL 是该货币的代码，L 常用作金额前的符号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Honduran currency is a broader descriptive expression, while monetary unit names the general category; neither is a strict synonym. HNL is the currency code, and L is commonly used before an amount.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 首领 Lempira 的名字，成为洪都拉斯钱币 lempira 的名字。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the naming link: the leader Lempira gave his name to Honduras's lempira.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“情妇；妓女”的 doxy 出现于早期现代英语，其来源不确定，常被认为可能与荷兰语中表示“玩偶”的 docke 有关。现代医疗语境中的 doxy 则是 doxycycline 的截短形式，与这个旧式贬称没有词源联系。
etymology_story.en: Doxy meaning a mistress or prostitute arose in Early Modern English; its origin is uncertain, though a connection with Dutch docke, meaning a doll, is often proposed. The modern medical use is a clipping of doxycycline and is etymologically separate from the older derogatory word.

morphology_enriched.zh: 旧义 doxy 在现代英语中作为不可再拆的词使用，复数为 doxies；doxy-like 是可以临时构成的“像情妇的”，不是常用派生词。药名简称的构词为 doxycycline → doxy，属于截短；不要把独立词 doxy 与 orthodoxy 等词中的 -doxy 混为一谈。
morphology_enriched.en: The older doxy is synchronically a simple word, with the plural doxies; doxy-like is a possible occasional formation rather than a common established derivative. The medical shortening follows doxycycline → doxy by clipping; the independent word should not be confused with the element -doxy in words such as orthodoxy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 旧义近义词：mistress 强调与已有伴侣的男子保持婚外关系，不必涉及金钱；prostitute 指提供有偿性服务的人；harlot 是旧式且带贬义的称呼。药名义对应完整名称 doxycycline。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the older sense, mistress emphasizes an extramarital relationship and does not necessarily imply payment; prostitute refers to someone providing sexual services for money; harlot is archaic and derogatory. In the medical sense, the full equivalent is doxycycline.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分语境记忆：旧故事中的 doxy 是贬称；医疗语境中的 doxy 是 doxycycline 的短称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use context as the anchor: doxy in an old story is a derogatory label; doxy in medical conversation is shortened doxycycline.

etymology_story.en: Shrike is usually traced to Old English scrīc, a name for a thrush, through a partly reconstructed Middle English form. The bird name changed its reference over time and now denotes a shrike.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：shrike 是不可再拆的基本名词，复数为 shrikes；shrikelike 或 shrike-like 表示“像伯劳的”，属于透明构词，但并非常用词。常见组合包括 red-backed shrike（红背伯劳）和 great grey shrike（灰伯劳）；没有丰富的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: shrike is a simple noun, with the plural shrikes; shrikelike or shrike-like is a transparent but uncommon formation meaning resembling a shrike. Common combinations include red-backed shrike and great grey shrike, and there is no extensive family of common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: butcherbird 是伯劳的俗称，突出其悬挂猎物的习性，但也可指其他鸟类；predatory songbird（捕食性鸣禽）是描述性上位表达；bird（鸟）范围最广，不能替代精确鸟名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Butcherbird is an informal name for a shrike that highlights its prey-impaling habit, but it also names other birds; predatory songbird is a broader descriptive expression; bird is the broadest category and does not identify the species group precisely.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the distinctive behavior: a hooked bill catches prey, and a sharp thorn holds it.

etymology_story.zh: fatso 是现代英语中的体型侮辱词，明显与 fat 有关；一种词源解释认为它可能由胖人的昵称 Fats 加上 -o 形成。具体形成路径并不完全确定，昵称式外形也不意味着这个词语气温和。
etymology_story.en: Fatso is a modern English insult transparently associated with fat; one proposed explanation derives it from the nickname Fats plus -o. Its precise formation is not entirely certain, and its nickname-like shape does not make it a mild expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：以 fat 为语义基础形成的非正式人物称呼；历史上可能是 Fats + -o，但不宜把 -so 当作可普遍使用的后缀。复数为 fatsoes 或 fatsos；相关基础词族有 fat、fatter、fattest、fatness、fatty、fatten、fattening，这些词并非都具有 fatso 的侮辱语气。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: an informal personal label based semantically on fat; historically it may represent Fats + -o, but -so should not be treated as a generally productive suffix. Plurals include fatsoes and fatsos; the related base-word family includes fat, fatter, fattest, fatness, fatty, fatten, and fattening, which do not all carry fatso's insulting force.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fatty 也可用作冒犯性的称呼；fat person 是直接描述体型的表达，其是否冒犯取决于语境；overweight person 较为正式，但不是适用于所有个体的中性替换，仍可能带有评价意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fatty can also function as an offensive personal label; fat person directly describes body size, with its reception depending on context; overweight person is more formal but is not a universally neutral substitute and can still sound evaluative.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fat 联想到体型；fatso 是把体型变成侮辱性称呼，主要用于识别冒犯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect fat with body size, then recognize fatso as an insulting label built around that feature.

etymology_story.zh: 该词可能经孔卡尼语 vindalu 和印度葡萄牙语传入英语，最终源于葡萄牙语 vinho de alho，字面意思是“蒜味酒”。菜名保留了酒与蒜的历史联系，现代咖喱版本则通常使用醋。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vindaloo)
etymology_story.en: The word probably reached English through Konkani vindalu and Indo-Portuguese, ultimately from Portuguese vinho de alho, literally 'wine of garlic.' The name preserves the historical connection with wine and garlic, while modern curry versions commonly use vinegar. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vindaloo)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可进一步分析为英语词根和词缀的借词：vindaloo。表示若干份或若干种时可用复数 vindaloos；常见组合有 vindaloo sauce（文达卢咖喱酱）、vindaloo paste（文达卢咖喱膏）和 chicken vindaloo（文达卢鸡肉咖喱）。没有常用的派生词族；词尾不是印地语 aloo（土豆）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, vindaloo is a borrowed base without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. The plural vindaloos can refer to portions or varieties; established combinations include vindaloo sauce, vindaloo paste, and chicken vindaloo. There is no common derivational family, and the ending is not Hindi aloo, meaning 'potato.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: curry（咖喱菜）是上位词，涵盖许多不同做法；Goan curry（果阿咖喱）强调地域，范围比 vindaloo 更广；hot curry（辣咖喱）只说明辣度，不能体现文达卢特有的蒜醋风味。三者都不是完全等义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Curry is the broader category; Goan curry identifies a regional tradition that includes more than vindaloo; hot curry describes heat without specifying vindaloo's garlic-and-vinegar character. None is an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史配方“酒＋蒜”，再联想到如今常见的“醋香辣咖喱”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical pairing 'wine + garlic,' then connect it with today's tangy, spicy curry.

etymology.text: 英语中的拟声词，模仿四足动物低沉喷鼻的声音。把声音 whoof 与动物突然喷出鼻息的画面连起来记。

senses.meaning_zh: 低沉的喷鼻声；呼哧声
senses.meaning_en: A deep snorting or forceful puffing sound.

senses.meaning_zh: 呼哧地喷气；发出低沉的喷鼻声；用力喷出
senses.meaning_en: To make a deep snorting sound or blow something out forcefully.
senses.english_definition: If an animal or person whoofs, they force air out with a deep sound; if they whoof something out, they expel it with a forceful puff.
senses.collocation_en: whoof softly; whoof through the nostrils

etymology_story.zh: whoof 是模仿低沉喷鼻声或喷气声形成的拟声词，名词指声音本身，动词指发出这种声音或喷气的动作。它没有需要拆解的古典词根。[词源与词性依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/whoof)
etymology_story.en: Whoof is an imitative formation representing a deep snort or puff; the noun names the sound, and the verb describes making it or blowing forcefully. It has no classical root that needs to be reconstructed. [Source for origin and parts of speech: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/whoof)

morphology_enriched.zh: whoof 是独立的拟声词基，名词和动词同形。名词复数为 whoofs；动词变化为 whoofs、whoofed、whoofing。该词本身较少见，没有需要作为常用词族掌握的派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Whoof is a free imitative base used as both a noun and a verb. Its noun plural is whoofs, and its verb forms are whoofs, whoofed, and whoofing. The word itself is uncommon and has no established common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: snort（喷鼻息）突出空气从鼻腔猛然喷出；puff（喷气、噗声）突出短促的一股气，不一定低沉；woof（汪汪声、吠叫）通常指狗叫。whoof 更侧重低沉、带气流感的“呼哧”声。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Snort emphasizes air forced through the nose; puff emphasizes a short burst of air without necessarily suggesting a deep sound; woof usually denotes a dog's bark. Whoof particularly suggests a deep, breathy rush of air.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 whoof 读成一口低沉的“呼哧”：声音是名词，喷出这口气就是动词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear whoof as a deep burst of breath: the sound is the noun, and producing it is the verb.

etymology.text: 来自法语 sauce béchamelle，以法国廷臣 Louis de Béchamel 的姓氏命名。这个人名如今成了一种奶香白酱的名字。

senses.meaning_zh: 贝沙梅尔白酱；以黄油、面粉和牛奶制成的白酱
senses.meaning_en: A white sauce made from butter, flour, and milk.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 sauce béchamelle，酱名取自法国廷臣 Louis de Béchamel 的姓氏。它是由人名转成的食物名称，名称本身并不能证明此人发明了这种酱。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bechamel)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the name from French sauce béchamelle, named after the French courtier Louis de Béchamel. A personal name thus became a culinary term, although the naming alone does not establish that he invented the sauce. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bechamel)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可按英语词根、词缀拆分的借词。bechamel 与 béchamel 是拼写变体；通常作不可数名词，指不同种类或若干份时可用 bechamels 或 béchamels。常见组合是 bechamel sauce（贝沙梅尔白酱）；没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed base without an English root-and-affix breakdown. Bechamel and béchamel are spelling variants; the noun is usually uncountable, although bechamels or béchamels can denote varieties or portions. Bechamel sauce is an established combination, and there is no common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: white sauce（白酱）在许多烹饪语境中可直接指 bechamel，但也可能泛指其他白色酱汁；cream sauce（奶油酱）强调奶油，并不一定采用相同配方；velouté（丝绒酱）通常以高汤而非牛奶调制。后两者是相关酱汁，不是严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: White sauce often means bechamel, though it can describe other pale sauces; cream sauce emphasizes cream and need not follow the same recipe; velouté typically uses stock rather than milk. The latter two are related sauces rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “人名变酱名”：Béchamel → 黄油、面粉、牛奶做成的白酱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A person's name became a sauce name: Béchamel → butter, flour, and milk → white sauce.

etymology_story.zh: blotto 在二十世纪初已有使用记录，可能是 blot 的不规则变体，但确切形成过程并不确定。它后来固定为表示“烂醉”的俚语形容词。[词源依据：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/blotto)
etymology_story.en: Blotto is recorded from the early twentieth century and is probably an irregular alteration of blot, although its precise formation is uncertain. It became established as a slang adjective meaning extremely drunk. [Etymological source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/blotto)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习时宜将 blotto 作为完整的俚语词基记忆；可暂时联想为 blot + 表口语色彩的 -o，但这不是已经确定的规则构词过程。它通常用于 be、get 等词之后，没有常用的规则比较级、最高级或派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern vocabulary learning, treat blotto as a complete slang base. A tentative association with blot plus colloquial -o is possible, but this is not a securely established regular formation. It normally follows verbs such as be and get and has no common regular comparative, superlative, or derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: drunk（醉的）是程度范围较广的普通用词；intoxicated（醉酒的）更正式，常见于医学或法律语境；plastered（烂醉的）与 blotto 一样是强调醉酒程度的俚语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drunk is the ordinary term and covers a range of severity; intoxicated is more formal and common in medical or legal contexts; plastered, like blotto, is slang emphasizing heavy drunkenness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想“酒精把清醒抹掉了”：blotto＝烂醉；这是记忆联想，不是确定词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine alcohol blotting out clear thinking: blotto means extremely drunk. This is a memory association, not a proven etymology.

etymology_story.en: Ern and erne continue a Middle English bird name derived from Old English earn, meaning 'eagle.' This old name is uncommon in modern English and generally refers to a sea eagle, especially the white-tailed eagle. morphology_enriched.zh: ern 是不可进一步拆分的独立词基；ern 与 erne 是拼写变体，不是派生关系。复数分别为 erns 和 ernes。现代通用英语中没有常用的派生词族；不应将它与表示“挣得”的 earn 混为一词。
morphology_enriched.en: Ern is an indivisible free base. Ern and erne are spelling variants rather than derivatives, with the plurals erns and ernes respectively. There is no common derivational family in general modern English, and the bird name should not be confused with earn, meaning to receive through work.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sea eagle（海雕）是更常见的名称，可指多种海雕；white-tailed eagle（白尾海雕）明确指这一物种；eagle（雕、鹰）范围更广。ern 是较少见的传统鸟名，常与白尾海雕对应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sea eagle is the more usual term and can cover several species; white-tailed eagle identifies the particular species; eagle is broader still. Ern is an uncommon traditional name often referring specifically to the white-tailed eagle.

senses.meaning_en: Extremely good or impressive, in informal American English.
senses.english_definition: If you describe something as bodacious, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive.
senses.collocation_en: a bodacious burger; bodacious waves
senses.collocation_zh: 超棒的汉堡；令人赞叹的海浪
senses.sentence_en: That little beach café serves some bodacious burgers.
senses.sentence_zh: 那家海边小咖啡馆供应的汉堡棒极了。

senses.meaning_zh: （美式非正式）大胆的；敢作敢为的；放肆的
senses.meaning_en: Bold, daring, or impudently confident.
senses.english_definition: A bodacious person or action shows great confidence and a willingness to take risks or break rules.
senses.collocation_en: a bodacious move; a bodacious claim
senses.collocation_zh: 大胆的举动；大胆甚至放肆的断言
senses.sentence_en: Challenging the champion in her first season was a bodacious move.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在参赛的第一个赛季就挑战冠军，实在是大胆之举。

senses.meaning_zh: （美式俚语）性感迷人的；身材惹眼的
senses.meaning_en: Sexually attractive, especially in physical appearance.
senses.english_definition: If someone describes a person or their body as bodacious, they mean that the person is very sexually attractive.
senses.collocation_en: a bodacious body; bodacious curves
senses.collocation_zh: 性感迷人的身材；惹眼的身体曲线
senses.sentence_en: The magazine used the slang phrase “a bodacious body” in its headline.
senses.sentence_zh: 那本杂志在标题中使用了“性感迷人的身材”这一俚语表达。

etymology_story.zh: 该词通常被认为由方言词 boldacious 演变而来，后者可能混合了 bold（大胆的）和 audacious（大胆的；放肆的）。它早期突出大胆、放肆，后来在美国俚语中扩展为“极棒的”和“性感迷人的”。
etymology_story.en: Bodacious is generally traced to dialectal boldacious, probably a blend of bold and audacious. Its earlier emphasis on boldness or impudence later broadened in American slang to enthusiastic praise and physical attractiveness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 bodacious 为完整词基，不宜机械拆成具有独立意义的 bod- 和 -acious。常见派生关系：bodacious + -ly → bodaciously（大胆地；极出色地）；bodacious + -ness → bodaciousness（大胆；出众的特质），两种派生词均不如原形常见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bodacious functions as a whole adjective base; it should not be mechanically divided into independently meaningful bod- and -acious. Its regular derivatives are bodacious + -ly → bodaciously, meaning boldly or impressively, and bodacious + -ness → bodaciousness, meaning boldness or impressive quality; both are less frequent than the adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: awesome（极棒的）侧重强烈赞赏；audacious（大胆的；放肆的）侧重冒险或挑战规矩；sexy（性感的）直接强调性吸引力。bodacious 可覆盖这些不同义项，但语气更夸张，且带明显的美式俚语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Awesome emphasizes enthusiastic approval; audacious emphasizes risk-taking or disregard for convention; sexy directly emphasizes sexual attraction. Bodacious can express these different meanings, with a more exaggerated and distinctly American slang tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 bold + audacious 联想到“大胆得惹眼”，再连接“棒得惹眼”和“性感惹眼”；这是记忆线索，并非现代词素拆分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link bold + audacious to “bold enough to stand out,” then extend that image to outstanding quality and striking attractiveness; this is a memory aid, not a modern morpheme analysis.

forms: 本课作副词，不变形；也常写作 mañana。
family: 本课集中记这个整词；同一词的变化见词形栏。

morphology.text: manana + attitude → manana attitude（明日复明日的拖延态度）。整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆，表示明天再说、改天再办。

etymology.text: 借自西班牙语 mañana，原义“明天”。进入英语的这类口语用法中，它常成为把事情推到改天的说法。

usage_note: 来自西班牙语 mañana；英语口语中常带拖延意味，不一定承诺确切的明天。英语也保留带 ñ 的拼写。
sentence: Asked when he would fix the gate, he shrugged and said, "manana".
translation: 有人问他何时修门，他耸耸肩说：“改天吧。”
scenario: 有人问他何时修门，他耸耸肩说：“改天吧。”

collocation:
a manana attitude 凡事改天再办的态度
leave the repairs till manana 把修理拖到改天
context_hint: The reply puts the task off to an unspecified later time.

teaching.contrast: 来自西班牙语 mañana；英语口语中常带拖延意味，不一定承诺确切的明天。英语也保留带 ñ 的拼写。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式，亦写作 mañana）明天；以后再说
senses.meaning_en: Tomorrow, or at some unspecified later time.
senses.english_definition: If someone says that something will happen manana, they mean tomorrow or at some later time, often suggesting that they are putting it off.
senses.collocation_en: do it manana; come back manana
senses.collocation_zh: 明天再做；明天再来
senses.sentence_en: “I'll fix it manana,” he said, putting the tools away.
senses.sentence_zh: “我明天再修吧，”他说着，把工具收了起来。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式）遥遥无期的明天；不确定的将来
senses.meaning_en: An indefinite future time to which something is postponed.
senses.english_definition: Manana is an unspecified future time when someone says they will do something that they keep delaying.
senses.collocation_en: leave it until manana; put it off until manana
senses.collocation_zh: 留到明天再说；推到以后再办
senses.sentence_en: For him, manana never seems to arrive.
senses.sentence_zh: 对他来说，那个承诺办事的“明天”似乎永远不会到来。

etymology_story.zh: 借自西班牙语 mañana，意为“明天”，其历史可追溯至表示“早晨”的通俗拉丁语形式。英语借用后，除表示“明天”外，还常带有把事情推到不确定将来的戏谑意味。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Spanish mañana, meaning “tomorrow,” whose history goes back to a Vulgar Latin form referring to the morning. In English, the borrowing also developed a humorous suggestion of postponing things to an indefinite future.

morphology_enriched.zh: manana 是借词 mañana 的无变音符号拼写，在现代英语中作为完整词基使用，没有常用的前后缀派生词。manana attitude（凡事明天再说的态度）和 manana mentality（拖延心态）属于短语组合，不是派生词；这类组合中的名词可作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Manana is the spelling of the borrowing mañana without its diacritic and functions as a whole base in English, with no established common affixal derivatives. Manana attitude and manana mentality are phrase combinations rather than derivatives; the noun can function attributively in such expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tomorrow（明天）通常明确指次日；later（以后）只说明时间较晚；someday（将来某一天）强调日期未定。manana 可表示明天，但在英语中常额外暗示拖延或漫不经心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tomorrow normally identifies the following day; later simply indicates a subsequent time; someday leaves the date unspecified. Manana can mean tomorrow but often adds a suggestion of procrastination or casual unconcern.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 mañana 想成口头禅“明天吧”：既能指真正的明天，也能指一推再推的以后。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear mañana as the repeated promise “tomorrow”: it can mean the next day or a future that keeps being postponed.

forms: 第三人称 skedaddles；过去式、过去分词 skedaddled；现在分词 skedaddling。
family: 本课集中记这个整词；同一词的变化见词形栏。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。skedaddle + -er → skedaddler（赶紧溜走的人）；加 -er 时去掉词尾不发音的 e。

etymology.text: 英语词典提出，它可能由方言 scaddle 扩展而来，后者与“受惊逃跑”有关。把看到危险就赶紧溜走的画面与这个词相连。

usage_note: 非正式、不及物动词，重在迅速离开；通常不直接接表示人的宾语。
sentence: We had to skedaddle when the angry dog ran towards us.
translation: 那只生气的狗朝我们跑来时，我们只好赶紧溜走。
scenario: 那只生气的狗朝我们跑来时，我们只好赶紧溜走。
cloze: We had to _____ when the angry dog ran towards us.
collocation:
skedaddle from danger 赶紧逃离危险
skedaddle before dark 天黑前赶紧离开
context_hint: The people leave quickly rather than stay where they are.

teaching.contrast: 非正式、不及物动词，重在迅速离开；通常不直接接表示人的宾语。
teaching.sentence: The children decided to skedaddle before the guard spotted them.

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的 skedaddle 表示“赶紧溜走”；结合句中场景，不能解释为“留下等待”。

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式）赶紧溜走；仓促逃离
senses.meaning_en: To leave or run away quickly.
senses.english_definition: If you skedaddle, you leave a place quickly, especially to avoid trouble or being caught.
senses.collocation_en: skedaddle out of the room; skedaddle home
senses.collocation_zh: 赶紧溜出房间；赶紧溜回家
senses.sentence_en: We'd better skedaddle before the storm reaches us.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们最好在暴风雨到来之前赶紧离开。

senses.meaning_zh: （较少见，非正式）仓促离开；匆忙逃走
senses.meaning_en: A hurried departure or escape.
senses.english_definition: A skedaddle is a quick departure, especially when someone wants to escape trouble.
senses.collocation_en: a quick skedaddle; a hasty skedaddle
senses.collocation_zh: 迅速溜走；仓促逃离
senses.sentence_en: Their quick skedaddle left us to explain the mess.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们匆匆溜走，留下我们来解释这一团糟的局面。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在美国南北战争时期广为流传，起初常用于描述士兵仓促逃跑或溃逃，确切来源尚无定论。一种解释认为它与英国方言 scaddle（受惊逃跑）有关，后来泛指带有诙谐色彩的“赶紧溜走”。
etymology_story.en: Skedaddle became widely known during the American Civil War, especially for soldiers fleeing or retreating in haste, but its exact origin is uncertain. One proposed connection is with British dialect scaddle, meaning to run off in fright; it later broadened into a humorous word for leaving quickly.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 skedaddle 作为完整动词词基记忆，不宜拆成没有依据的前缀和词根。屈折形式为 skedaddles、skedaddled、skedaddling；加 -ing 时去掉词尾 e。名词 skedaddle 与动词同形；较少见的施事名词 skedaddler 表示“仓促逃走的人”，由 skedaddle 去 e 加 -er 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats skedaddle as a whole verb base, without a securely identifiable productive prefix or root division. Its inflected forms are skedaddles, skedaddled, and skedaddling, with final e dropped before -ing. The noun skedaddle has the same form as the verb; the uncommon agent noun skedaddler means someone who runs away and is formed by dropping final e and adding -er.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flee（逃离）常暗示真实危险；bolt（突然冲走）强调动作突然而迅速；scram（赶紧走开）常用于命令，语气较生硬。skedaddle 通常更诙谐、随意，强调赶快溜走。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flee often suggests genuine danger; bolt emphasizes a sudden, rapid movement; scram is frequently used as a blunt command to leave. Skedaddle is usually more playful and informal, emphasizing a quick getaway.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把这个节奏急促的词配上“脚底抹油、赶紧开溜”的画面；这是声音联想，不是词源解释。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair the word's lively rhythm with the image of feet hurrying away: skedaddle means “make a quick getaway.” This is a sound association, not an etymology.

forms: 第三人称 futzes；过去式、过去分词 futzed；现在分词 futzing。
family: 本课集中记这个整词；同一词的变化见词形栏。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。futz + -y → futzy（瞎忙的、反复试弄的）；-y 构成形容词，把胡乱摆弄的动作与做事方式联系起来。

etymology.text: 词典认为它可能部分改译自意第绪语 arumfartsn zikh，字面是一个粗俗的“到处放屁”的说法。英语里用来表示漫无目的地瞎忙，原意不等于现义。

usage_note: 美式非正式用语，常接 around 或 with；强调瞎忙或无成效地摆弄，不等于认真修理。
sentence: Stop trying to futz with the settings and start the presentation.
translation: 别再瞎摆弄设置了，开始演示吧。
scenario: 别再瞎摆弄设置了，开始演示吧。
cloze: Stop trying to _____ with the settings and start the presentation.
collocation:
futz with the settings 瞎摆弄设置
futz around in the workshop 在工坊里瞎忙
context_hint: The activity wastes time without achieving anything useful.

teaching.contrast: 美式非正式用语，常接 around 或 with；强调瞎忙或无成效地摆弄，不等于认真修理。
teaching.sentence: We do not have time to futz around in the workshop today.
teaching.translation: 我们今天没时间在工坊里瞎忙。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（瞎忙；无目的地摆弄／专心高效地工作）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的 futz 表示“瞎忙；无目的地摆弄”；结合句中场景，不能解释为“专心高效地工作”。

senses.meaning_zh: （美式非正式）瞎忙；磨蹭；无所事事地消磨时间
senses.meaning_en: To waste time doing unimportant things.
senses.english_definition: If you futz around, you spend time doing things that are unimportant or achieve very little.
senses.collocation_en: futz around; futz about
senses.collocation_zh: 瞎忙；磨蹭闲混
senses.sentence_en: Stop futzing around and finish packing.
senses.sentence_zh: 别再磨蹭了，赶快把行李收拾好。

senses.meaning_zh: （美式非正式）反复摆弄；胡乱调整
senses.meaning_en: To fiddle with something, often without making useful progress.
senses.english_definition: If you futz with something, you keep handling or adjusting it, often without a clear purpose or useful result.
senses.collocation_en: futz with the settings; futz around with a computer
senses.collocation_zh: 反复摆弄设置；瞎折腾电脑
senses.sentence_en: I spent an hour futzing with the settings and still couldn't get any sound.
senses.sentence_zh: 我折腾了一个小时的设置，还是弄不出声音。

etymology_story.zh: 该词的确切来源存在争议，一种常见解释把它与意第绪语 arumfartsn zikh 联系起来，该表达字面涉及“到处放屁”，引申为瞎混或瞎折腾。英语 futz 通常指浪费时间或反复摆弄，并不保留这一字面意义。
etymology_story.en: The exact origin is disputed, but one common explanation connects futz with Yiddish arumfartsn zikh, an expression literally involving farting around and figuratively suggesting aimless activity. English futz normally means wasting time or fiddling with something, without retaining that literal meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: futz 在现代英语中是完整动词词基，没有可独立分析的常用词缀。屈折形式为 futzes、futzed、futzing；futz around、futz about 和 futz with 是常见搭配。相关形容词 futzy 较少见，可表示“繁琐费事的；需要反复摆弄的”，不宜简单理解为“瞎忙的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Futz is a whole verb base in modern English, without a productive internal affix analysis. Its inflected forms are futzes, futzed, and futzing; common constructions include futz around, futz about, and futz with. The less common related adjective futzy can mean fussy, fiddly, or requiring troublesome small adjustments, rather than simply “busy doing nothing.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fiddle（摆弄）强调小动作或细微调整；tinker（修修弄弄）往往带有尝试改进的目的；mess around（瞎折腾）范围更广，可指胡闹或无效忙碌。futz 尤其突出费了时间却没多少进展。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fiddle emphasizes small movements or adjustments; tinker often suggests an attempt to improve something; mess around covers a wider range of playful or unproductive activity. Futz particularly suggests spending time without making much progress.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“手一直在动，事情没推进”：闲着瞎忙是 futz around，拿着东西瞎调是 futz with。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture busy hands with little progress: futz around means waste time, while futz with means fiddle with something.

forms: 通常作食品物质名；多份或多种可用 granitas。
family: 本课集中记这个整词；同一词的变化见词形栏。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。granita + -like → granita-like（像格兰尼塔碎冰甜点的）；-like 表示“像……的”，常用于描述粗颗粒冰晶质地。

etymology.text: 来自意大利语 granita，是 granito 的阴性形式，并与 granire 有历史联系。用甜点中粗颗粒的冰晶来记住名称，不把它等同于顺滑冰淇淋。

usage_note: 意大利式颗粒较粗的冰冻甜点，常用水果制作；不同于顺滑的冰淇淋。
sentence: The cafe serves lemon granita on hot afternoons.
translation: 这家咖啡馆在炎热的午后供应柠檬碎冰甜点。
scenario: 这家咖啡馆在炎热的午后供应柠檬碎冰甜点。
cloze: The cafe serves lemon _____ on hot afternoons.
collocation:
lemon granita 柠檬碎冰甜点
scrape the granita 刮松碎冰甜点
context_hint: Think of a frozen dessert with coarse ice crystals.

teaching.contrast: 意大利式颗粒较粗的冰冻甜点，常用水果制作；不同于顺滑的冰淇淋。

teaching.translation: 碎冰甜点冷冻时，用叉子刮松冰晶。

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的 granita 表示“格兰尼塔碎冰甜点”；结合句中场景，不能解释为“热布丁”。

senses.meaning_zh: 格兰尼塔冰沙；意式颗粒状冰晶甜点
senses.meaning_en: An Italian frozen dessert made of coarse, flavored ice crystals.
senses.english_definition: Granita is an Italian frozen dessert made by freezing a sweetened, flavored liquid and breaking it into small ice crystals.
senses.collocation_en: lemon granita; coffee granita
senses.collocation_zh: 柠檬格兰尼塔冰沙；咖啡格兰尼塔冰沙
senses.sentence_en: For dessert, we shared a bowl of lemon granita.
senses.sentence_zh: 甜点时，我们分吃了一碗柠檬格兰尼塔冰沙。

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 granita，该形式与表示“使成颗粒”的 granire 及其过去分词 granito 有关，最终与意为“谷粒”的 grano 相联系。名称突出甜点中一粒粒的冰晶，后来直接作为这种意式冷冻甜点的名称进入英语。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian granita, a form related to granire, meaning to make granular, and its past participle granito, ultimately connected with grano, meaning grain. The name evokes the dessert's separate grains of ice and entered English as the name of this Italian frozen dessert.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 granita 是完整的外来名词，不宜拆成英语词根 gran- 加后缀 -ita。它可作物质名词，也可指一种口味或一份甜点，英语复数为 granitas；没有常用的固定派生词。granita-like（像格兰尼塔冰沙的）是可临时构成的形式；lemon granita、coffee granita 是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, granita is a whole borrowed noun, not an English root gran- plus a suffix -ita. It can be a mass noun or refer to a variety or serving, with the English plural granitas; it has no common established derivatives. Granita-like is a freely formed description meaning resembling granita, while lemon granita and coffee granita are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sorbet（雪葩）通常冰晶更细、口感更顺滑；shaved ice（刨冰）通常先把冰刨碎，再加入糖浆等调味；Italian ice（意式冰品）是相关的水基冷冻甜点名称，其质地和用法因地区而异。granita 的典型特点是将调味液冷冻后形成并刮散的颗粒状冰晶。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sorbet generally has finer crystals and a smoother texture; shaved ice is typically made by shaving ice before adding syrup or other flavorings; Italian ice names a related water-based frozen dessert whose texture and usage vary by region. Granita characteristically consists of granular crystals formed by freezing and scraping a flavored liquid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用历史上的“谷粒”意象记住一粒粒冰晶：granita 的辨识点是颗粒感。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical image of grains to remember separate grains of ice: granita is recognizable by its granular texture.

senses.meaning_en: A cooked grain dish, especially one made from buckwheat.
senses.english_definition: Kasha is a dish of cooked grains, especially buckwheat, eaten as porridge or as an accompaniment to other food.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 kasha 借自俄语 ка́ша，原指用各种谷物煮成的粥或饭。进入英语后，其含义通常收窄为荞麦食品，也可指用来制作这种食品的烘烤去壳荞麦粒。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed kasha from Russian ка́ша, a word for porridge or a cooked grain dish. In English, its meaning usually narrowed to buckwheat dishes and extended to the roasted buckwheat grains used to make them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有效词根、词缀拆分的借词：kasha。通常用作不可数名词，没有常用的派生词；相关组合有 buckwheat kasha（荞麦粥或饭）、kasha porridge（荞麦粥）、kasha varnishkes（荞麦蝴蝶面）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kasha is a borrowed base with no productive internal root-and-affix breakdown. It is normally uncountable and has no common derived forms; related combinations include buckwheat kasha, kasha porridge, and kasha varnishkes, a dish combining buckwheat with bow-tie pasta.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关表达：buckwheat groats（去壳荞麦粒）强调原料，未必经过烘烤；porridge（谷物粥）强调煮成的粥状食品，原料范围更广；gruel（稀粥）强调稀薄的质地。这些词不能在所有语境中替换 kasha。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: buckwheat groats emphasizes the grain ingredient, which need not be roasted; porridge covers a wider range of cooked cereal dishes; gruel specifically suggests a thin consistency. None replaces kasha in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“同一碗荞麦，两种指称”：下锅前的荞麦粒、煮好后的荞麦粥或饭，都可以叫 kasha。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one bowl of buckwheat at two stages: kasha can name the grains before cooking or the dish afterward.

senses.meaning_en: An American plover with two black breast bands and a loud, distinctive call.
senses.english_definition: A killdeer is a brown-and-white American bird with two black bands across its breast that often lives and nests on open ground.

etymology_story.zh: killdeer 是模仿这种鸟尖亮鸣叫声而形成的英语鸟名，叫声听起来近似“kill-deer”。它的名称并不表示“杀鹿”，也不是由这种行为引申而来。
etymology_story.en: Killdeer arose as an English imitation of the bird's loud call, heard as something like “kill-deer.” Its name does not describe killing deer or derive from such behavior.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是词汇化的拟声鸟名，不宜按 kill（杀）＋deer（鹿）的字面意义分析。复数可用 killdeer 或 killdeers；变体名称有 killdee 和 killdeer plover，没有常用的派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, killdeer is a lexicalized imitative bird name, rather than a semantically transparent combination of kill + deer. Its plural is killdeer or killdeers; alternative names include killdee and killdeer plover, and there are no common derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: killdeer plover（双领鸻）是同一物种较完整的名称；killdee（双领鸻）是较少见的名称变体；plover（鸻）是范围更广的鸟类名称，不能精确替代物种名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Killdeer plover is a fuller name for the same species; killdee is a less common alternative name; plover is a broader bird-group term and does not identify this particular species.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 听声记鸟名：它仿佛在叫“kill-deer”；看胸记中文名：两道黑带就是“双领”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear “kill-deer” in its call, then picture its two black breast bands to remember the bird.

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆，不拆成英语词根。现代复合词组：sambal + sauce → sambal sauce（参巴酱）。

etymology.text: 英语从马来语借入 sambal，原指这种辣椒调味酱。记住饭旁一小碟红辣酱，就能把名称和食物连起来。

usage_note: 食品名通常小写。多指配米饭、咖喱等食物的辣味调料，各地配方不同；本课不教大写 Sambal 的族群或语言名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 参巴辣酱，东南亚常见的辣椒调味酱或佐料
senses.meaning_en: A Southeast Asian chili-based condiment or relish.
senses.english_definition: Sambal is a spicy condiment made with chilies and other ingredients that is eaten with food, especially in Indonesian and Malaysian cooking.

senses.sentence_en: Stir a spoonful of sambal into the noodles for extra heat.
senses.sentence_zh: 往面条里拌入一匙参巴辣酱，可以增加辣味。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 sambal 借自马来语 sambal，指辣椒制成的调味酱或佐料。英语保留了它的烹饪含义，用于多种印度尼西亚、马来西亚及邻近地区的辣椒调味品。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed sambal from Malay sambal, referring to a chili-based condiment or relish. English retains this culinary meaning for various chili preparations associated with Indonesia, Malaysia, and neighboring regions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的词基 sambal，没有可有效拆分的英语词根或词缀。作食品总称时通常不可数，指不同种类或不同份的参巴酱时可用复数 sambals；相关组合有 sambal sauce（参巴酱）、sambal paste（参巴辣椒糊）和 sambal oelek（参巴辣椒酱），没有常用的英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sambal is a borrowed base without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. It is normally uncountable as a food name, but sambals can refer to varieties or servings; related combinations include sambal sauce, sambal paste, and sambal oelek, with no common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关表达：chili paste（辣椒糊）强调糊状质地；chili sauce（辣椒酱）范围更广，也可能较稀；relish（佐餐调味料）强调配餐用途，未必含辣椒。sambal 则带有特定的东南亚烹饪背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: chili paste emphasizes a thick texture; chili sauce is broader and may be more liquid; relish emphasizes use as an accompaniment and need not contain chilies. Sambal additionally identifies a Southeast Asian culinary tradition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 sambal 与饭旁那一小碟辣椒佐酱绑定：记住用途和食物形象，不硬拆音节。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor sambal to the small dish of chili condiment beside a meal; remember the food and its function as one unit.

pronunciation.note: 按词典美式重拼读音转写为 IPA；重音符号在重读音节之前。

forms: 指酒液通常不可数；不同酒款可用复数 zinfandels。葡萄品种名也写作 Zinfandel。
family: zinfandel grape 仙粉黛葡萄（复合词组）；zinfandels 不同的仙粉黛酒款（复数）。

morphology.text: 整词作为外来借词独立词素记忆。现代复合词组：zinfandel + grape → zinfandel grape（仙粉黛葡萄）；不要把名称的音节当成英语词根。

etymology.text: 这个酒名很可能改自匈牙利语旧葡萄名 tzinifándli 或 czirifandli，后者源于德语 Zierfandler。这个名称原指一种白葡萄，后来误用于另一葡萄品种；它在英语里成了如今的葡萄和酒名。

usage_note: 本课教这种葡萄酿制的干红葡萄酒；同一名称还可指葡萄。通常可小写，也常见首字母大写 Zinfandel；white zinfandel 是另一种酒款名称，不能一概理解成干红。

etymology_story.zh: Zinfandel 这一名称的确切来源尚不确定，通常被认为与匈牙利语葡萄名及德语 Zierfandler 有关，但具体的名称转移过程仍有争议。它在美国成为这一深色葡萄品种的名称，随后也用于该葡萄酿成的酒。
etymology_story.en: The precise origin of Zinfandel is uncertain; it is generally associated with Hungarian grape names and German Zierfandler, although the exact transfer of the name remains disputed. In the United States, it became the name of this dark-skinned grape variety and then of wines made from it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可按英语词根、词缀有效拆分的品种名 zinfandel，也常写作 Zinfandel。葡萄酒总称通常不可数，表示不同酒款时可用复数 Zinfandels；非正式缩略形式为 Zin 或 zin，相关组合有 Zinfandel grape（仙粉黛葡萄）和 white Zinfandel（白仙粉黛桃红葡萄酒）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, zinfandel, also written Zinfandel, is a varietal name without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. The wine name is normally uncountable, but Zinfandels can denote different wines; Zin or zin is an informal shortening, and related combinations include Zinfandel grape and white Zinfandel.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Zin（仙粉黛）是非正式简称；Primitivo（普里米蒂沃）和 Tribidrag（特里比德拉格）是同一葡萄品种的其他名称。葡萄品种相同不意味着不同产地、使用这些名称的葡萄酒具有完全相同的风格。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zin is an informal shortening; Primitivo and Tribidrag are other names for the same grape variety. Identity of grape variety does not make wines from different regions or sold under these names identical in style.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 沿着“葡萄藤→葡萄→酒杯”记忆 Zinfandel：一个品种名连接葡萄和葡萄酒；white Zinfandel 通常呈粉红色。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 ancho 来自墨西哥西班牙语 chile ancho，字面意思是“宽辣椒”，其中 ancho 意为“宽的”。这个名称描述辣椒宽大的外形；英语借入后通常专指成熟波布拉诺辣椒的干制品。
etymology_story.en: English ancho comes from Mexican Spanish chile ancho, literally “wide chili,” with ancho meaning “wide.” The name describes the pepper's broad shape; in English, it normally identifies the dried, ripe form of the poblano.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是从西班牙语短语 chile ancho 缩略借入的名词，不作英语词根、词缀拆分。单数 ancho，复数 anchos；没有常用的英语派生词，相关组合有 ancho chile（安乔辣椒）、ancho powder（安乔辣椒粉）和 ancho paste（安乔辣椒糊）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ancho is a noun borrowed from the shortened Spanish phrase chile ancho, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Its plural is anchos; it has no common English derivatives, while related combinations include ancho chile, ancho powder, and ancho paste.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ancho chile（安乔辣椒）是完整同义名称；dried poblano（干制波布拉诺辣椒）是说明性的近义表达；poblano（波布拉诺辣椒）单独使用时通常指鲜椒，而 ancho 特指成熟后干制的形态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ancho chile is the fuller equivalent name; dried poblano is a descriptive near-equivalent; poblano alone usually refers to the fresh pepper, whereas ancho specifically identifies its dried, ripe form.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 西班牙语 ancho＝“宽”：想象一枚宽扁、起皱的干辣椒，就能连起名称、形状和食材。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Spanish ancho means “wide”: picture a broad, flattened, wrinkled dried chili to connect its name, shape, and culinary identity.

etymology.text: cootie 的更早来源尚不确定。一战时期的英语军人记录里已有它和相近形式，用来谈战壕里的虱子；后来复数 cooties 也用于儿童游戏中假想的“会传染的脏东西”。记住从真虱子到游戏用语的变化。

usage_note: 口语或俚语。本课教单只虱子的意思。儿童说 someone has cooties 时，常是玩笑中的假想传染物，不一定是在说真的长虱子。一般小写。

senses.meaning_en: Imaginary germs or contamination in children's play, usually called cooties.

etymology_story.zh: cootie 在第一次世界大战时期的军人俚语中指虱子；它常被认为可能与马来语 kutu（虱子）有关，但具体来源和传播路径尚不确定。后来，复数 cooties 又用于儿童游戏，表示通过接触传染的假想病菌。
etymology_story.en: Cootie appeared in First World War military slang for a louse; it is often tentatively connected with Malay kutu, meaning 'louse,' although its precise origin and route into English remain uncertain. The plural cooties later developed a children's-play meaning involving imaginary germs passed through contact.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按单一词干 cootie 处理，没有可明确拆分的能产前后缀；复数为 cooties。常见组合有 cootie catcher（折纸占卜玩具）和 cootie shot（儿童游戏中预防假想病菌的打针）；没有常用的标准动词、副词或派生形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cootie is a single stem without clearly productive prefixes or suffixes; its plural is cooties. Established combinations include cootie catcher, a folded-paper fortune-telling toy, and cootie shot, a pretend protective injection in children's play; there are no common standard verb, adverb, or derived adjective forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: louse 是实际寄生虫“虱子”的中性名称；body louse 专指体虱；germs 指病菌，在儿童的假想传染语境中接近 cooties，但不自带游戏或取笑意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Louse is the neutral term for the actual parasite; body louse identifies the particular kind that lives mainly in clothing; germs overlaps with the imaginary-contamination sense of cooties but does not itself imply children's play or teasing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 真虱子让人躲，假病菌也让孩子躲：从寄生虫联想到游戏中的接触传染。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Real lice make people avoid contact; imaginary cooties make children do the same.

etymology.text: loblolly 很可能来自英语方言 lob（煮沸）和旧方言 lolly（汤），合起来让人想到熬得浓稠的汤粥。这个来源并非完全确定；“稠粥”义在16世纪末已有记录。

usage_note: “稠粥”是方言、旧时用法，日常英语更常说 porridge 或 gruel。loblolly 也可指泥沼或火炬松，读句子时要结合食物、地形或树木语境。一般小写。

etymology_story.zh: loblolly 在16世纪末已有“稠粥”义的记录，通常被分析为方言 lob（冒泡、煮沸）与 lolly（汤或粥）的组合，但构词来源并非完全确定。由于泥浆像稠粥，这个词后来也指泥沼，并进入常生于潮湿低地的火炬松名称 loblolly pine。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the late sixteenth century for thick porridge, loblolly is usually explained as a combination of dialectal lob, associated with bubbling or boiling, and lolly, meaning broth or porridge, though the formation is not entirely certain. Its resemblance to thick mud led to a swampy-ground sense and then to loblolly pine, a tree associated with moist lowlands.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 loblolly 当作不可再作实用拆分的词干，不能把词尾 -ly 当作副词后缀。可数义的复数为 loblollies，粥食义通常不可数；固定组合有 loblolly pine（火炬松）和历史用语 loblolly boy（船医助手），没有常用的标准派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats loblolly as an unanalyzed stem; its final -ly is not an adverb-forming suffix. Count uses have the plural loblollies, while the food sense is normally uncountable; established combinations include loblolly pine and the historical loblolly boy, meaning a ship's surgeon's assistant, with no common standard derived verb or adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: porridge 是粥食的普通名称，适合替换旧时食物义；bog 强调潮湿松软的地面，常涉及泥炭，与泥沼义部分重合；loblolly pine 是树木义更完整、明确的名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Porridge is the ordinary term corresponding to the historical food sense; bog overlaps with the wet-ground sense but often suggests peat and persistently waterlogged ground; loblolly pine is the fuller, more explicit name for the tree.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 稠粥像泥浆，泥浆形成湿地，湿地上长火炬松。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Thick porridge suggests thick mud; muddy lowlands lead you to loblolly pine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习中宜把 lunker 作为整体词干记忆，不能可靠地把它解释为某个常用动词加表示施事者的 -er。复数为 lunkers；常见组合有 lunker bass（特大黑鲈）和 lunker fishing（以钓大鱼为目标的垂钓），没有常用的标准派生词族。

etymology.text: 这是现代英语用 nano- 和 wire 组成的科技词。nano- 经国际科学词汇来自希腊语 nanos（侏儒），后来用来表示极小尺度；wire 则从古英语 wīr 经中古英语流传下来。记作“纳米尺度的细线”。

usage_note: 科技语境，通常小写。指极细的线状材料，常用于电子器件和传感器；不能仅凭这个词推断具体材料或精确直径。

etymology_story.zh: nanowire 是现代科技英语用 nano- 与 wire 构成的词。nano- 经科学术语体系源自希腊语 nanos（侏儒），在计量中表示十亿分之一，而 wire 可追溯到古英语 wīr。
etymology_story.en: Nanowire is a modern scientific formation combining nano- and wire. Through scientific terminology, nano- derives from Greek nanos, meaning 'dwarf,' and denotes one billionth in measurement, while wire descends from Old English wīr.

morphology_enriched.zh: nano-（纳米尺度；计量中为十亿分之一）+ wire（线）→ nanowire；nano- 是黏着构词成分，wire 是自由词根。复数为 nanowires，常见组合有 nanowire array（纳米线阵列）和 nanowire-based（基于纳米线的）；nanotube（纳米管）、nanofiber（纳米纤维）是共享 nano- 的相关构词，属于平行词而非 nanowire 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Nano- ('nanoscale'; one billionth in measurement) + wire → nanowire; nano- is a bound formative and wire is a free root. The plural is nanowires, with combinations such as nanowire array and nanowire-based; nanotube and nanofiber are parallel formations sharing nano-, rather than derivatives of nanowire.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nanofiber（纳米纤维）强调纤维形态，常见于聚合物等材料；nanorod（纳米棒）通常较短粗，长径比较小；nanotube（纳米管）强调中空管状结构。这些都是相关术语，不能在所有语境中与 nanowire 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nanofiber emphasizes a fibrous form and is often used for polymers and other materials; nanorod generally suggests a shorter, stouter structure with a smaller aspect ratio; nanotube specifically indicates a hollow tubular structure. These are related terms rather than universally interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nano- 定尺度，wire 定形状：横向细到纳米级的“线”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nano- gives the scale; wire gives the shape: a wire-shaped structure only nanometres across.

etymology.text: 借自美洲西班牙语 ranchera，它是 ranchero（牧场的）的阴性形式，与西班牙语中阴性的“歌曲”或“音乐”相呼应。把它联想成从牧场和乡村走来的民歌。

etymology_story.zh: ranchera 借自墨西哥西班牙语，是 ranchero（牧场的、乡村的）的阴性形式，在 canción ranchera（乡村歌曲）等表达中与阴性名词配合。这个名称保留了该音乐与墨西哥牧场、乡村文化的历史联系。
etymology_story.en: Ranchera was borrowed from Mexican Spanish, where it is the feminine form of ranchero, meaning 'of the ranch' or 'rural,' as in canción ranchera, 'rural song.' The name preserves the music's historical association with Mexican ranch and rural culture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中把 ranchera 作为完整借词处理，不把 -era 当作英语后缀；指一首歌曲时，复数为 rancheras，指音乐风格时通常不可数。常见组合有 ranchera singer（兰切拉歌手）和 ranchera music（兰切拉音乐）；西班牙语 rancho、ranchero 及英语 ranch 与其有词源联系，但不是英语 ranchera 的派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: English treats ranchera as a whole borrowed word, not as an English stem plus an English suffix -era; individual songs take the plural rancheras, while the musical style is normally uncountable. Common combinations include ranchera singer and ranchera music; Spanish rancho and ranchero and English ranch are etymologically related, rather than derivatives of English ranchera.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Mexican folk song（墨西哥民歌）是范围更广的概括；corrido（墨西哥叙事歌谣）主要通过歌词讲述人物和事件；mariachi（马里亚奇音乐或乐队）主要指一种演奏传统及其乐队，常伴奏兰切拉歌曲，但两者并不同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mexican folk song is a broader description; corrido is a narrative song that chiefly tells stories about people and events; mariachi refers to an instrumental and performance tradition or its ensemble, which often accompanies rancheras but is not synonymous with them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 ranch“牧场”想到牧场乡村的歌声：ranchera。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect ranch with the sound of rural Mexico: ranchera is the song that comes with the landscape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作生产性拆分的地名转用名词：Stilton。没有常用派生词；Blue Stilton、White Stilton 和 Stilton cheese 是名称组合；通常作不可数名词，Stiltons 可指多个品种或整块奶酪。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Stilton is an indivisible noun transferred from a place name. It has no common derivatives; Blue Stilton, White Stilton, and Stilton cheese are name combinations. It is normally uncountable, while Stiltons can refer to varieties or whole cheeses.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blue cheese（蓝纹奶酪）是包含蓝纹斯蒂尔顿的上位词，但不包括白色品种；Roquefort（罗克福奶酪）和 Gorgonzola（戈尔贡佐拉奶酪）是其他蓝纹奶酪的名称，不能与 Stilton 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blue cheese is a broader term covering Blue Stilton but not White Stilton. Roquefort and Gorgonzola name other blue cheeses and are related alternatives rather than exact synonyms.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自马来语 sado，其名称最终来自法语 dos-à-dos，意思是“背对背”。原来的法语表达描述座位排列，后来成为这种马车的名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Malay sado, a name ultimately derived from French dos-à-dos, meaning 'back to back'. The original expression described the seating arrangement and became a name for the carriage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可拆分的借词 sado；复数为 sados，末尾 -do 不是英语后缀。没有常用英语派生词；sado driver 和 sado ride 是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sado is an indivisible loanword; its plural is sados, and final -do is not an English suffix. It has no common English derivatives; sado driver and sado ride are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: carriage（马车）是上位词；cart（大车、两轮车）常强调简单结构或载货用途；dos-à-dos（背对背座式马车）突出座位布局，但不专指印度尼西亚的 sado。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Carriage is the general category. Cart often suggests a simpler vehicle or one used for carrying goods. Dos-à-dos emphasizes back-to-back seating without specifically identifying the Indonesian vehicle.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 背对背坐，想到 sado：座位布局就是名称的历史线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Back-to-back seats identify the sado: the seating arrangement explains its historical name.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 luzerne，通常追溯到奥克语或普罗旺斯语的相关形式。更早的来源尚不确定；一种解释将其与表示“萤火虫”的方言词及种子的光泽联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French luzerne, generally traced to a related Occitan or Provençal form. Its earlier origin is uncertain; one explanation connects it with a dialect word for a glow-worm and the seeds' sheen.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词为不可再拆分的植物名单纯词 lucerne，通常不可数；没有常用派生词族。lucerne hay、lucerne seed 和 lucerne field 均为名词组合，不能据此把 lucerne 拆成英语词根词缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Lucerne is an indivisible plant name in modern English and is normally uncountable. It has no common derivative family; lucerne hay, lucerne seed, and lucerne field are noun combinations, not evidence of internal English roots or affixes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alfalfa（紫花苜蓿）是同一种植物的名称，尤常见于美式英语；medick（苜蓿属植物）范围更广；clover（三叶草）属于相关但不同的植物，不能当作精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alfalfa names the same plant and is especially usual in American English. Medick is broader, covering plants of its genus. Clover refers to related but different plants and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 lucerne hay：紫花苜蓿晒成干草，用来喂牲畜。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor lucerne in lucerne hay: a purple-flowered crop dried to feed livestock.

etymology_story.zh: Edam 以荷兰的埃丹镇命名，该镇长期与奶酪贸易联系密切。地名由此成为一种奶酪的通用名称。
etymology_story.en: Edam is named after the Dutch town of Edam, which has long been associated with the cheese trade. The place name became the general name of a type of cheese.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为地名转用的不可拆分名词 Edam，没有常用派生词；Edam cheese 是名词组合。通常不可数，Edams 可用于指多个整只奶酪或不同品种。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Edam is an indivisible noun transferred from a place name, with no common derivatives; Edam cheese is a noun combination. It is normally uncountable, while Edams can refer to whole cheeses or different varieties.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Dutch cheese（荷兰奶酪）是更宽泛的称呼；Gouda（豪达奶酪）是另一种荷兰奶酪，通常更显乳脂感；Cheddar（切达奶酪）是不同类型，熟成后往往味道更浓，二者都不是 Edam 的精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dutch cheese is a broader description. Gouda is another Dutch cheese and is generally creamier. Cheddar is a different type that often develops a stronger flavour as it matures; neither name is an exact synonym for Edam.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 埃丹镇 → 埃丹奶酪；用常见的红色蜡皮圆奶酪形象辅助记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Edam the town → Edam the cheese; picture its familiar round shape and red wax coating.

senses.meaning_en: A castle, palace, or grand country house in a German-speaking region.
senses.english_definition: A schloss is a castle, palace, or large country house, especially in Germany or Austria.
senses.collocation_en: a Bavarian schloss; a lakeside schloss
senses.collocation_zh: 巴伐利亚的一座城堡；湖畔的一座宫邸

etymology_story.zh: 借自德语 Schloss，意思包括“锁”和“城堡、宫殿”，历史上与表示“关闭”的动词 schließen 同源。建筑义源于封闭、设防的住所，后来也用于气派的宫殿和庄园大宅。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from German Schloss, meaning both “lock” and “castle or palace,” and historically related to schließen, “to close.” The architectural meaning developed from an enclosed, fortified residence and later extended to grand palaces and country houses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再分析的借词词干 schloss，不应拆成英语词根和词缀。复数为 schlosses，也可保留德语复数 Schlösser；没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, schloss is an unanalyzed borrowed stem, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Its plural is schlosses, or the retained German form Schlösser; it has no established family of common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: castle（城堡）通常突出防御性；palace（宫殿）突出王室或显贵住所；château（法国城堡或庄园大宅）带法国文化背景。schloss 则突出德语地区的建筑与文化背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Castle usually emphasizes fortification; palace emphasizes a royal or otherwise grand residence; château suggests a French castle or country estate. Schloss specifically evokes a German-speaking architectural and cultural setting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“关闭、锁住”联想到封闭设防的大宅，再联想到德式城堡。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect “close and lock” with an enclosed, fortified residence: a German castle.

etymology_story.zh: 澳大利亚的“木棒”义借自悉尼地区的达鲁格语，通常追溯至 wadi，随后在英语中转用为表示“用棒击打”的动词。美国西部的“牛仔”义来源不确定，不能直接认定与澳大利亚词义同源。
etymology_story.en: The Australian word for a club was borrowed from Dharug, a language of the Sydney region, usually traced to wadi; English subsequently used the noun as a verb meaning “strike with a club.” The origin of the western American sense “cowboy” is uncertain and should not automatically be linked to the Australian word.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名词 waddy 为整体词干，末尾 -y 不是这里可独立分析的英语后缀；名词零派生为动词 waddy。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 waddies，过去式和过去分词为 waddied，现在分词为 waddying；没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The noun waddy is a single stem; its final -y is not a separately meaningful English suffix here. The verb is formed by conversion from the noun: waddies is the noun plural and third-person singular verb, waddied is the past tense and past participle, and waddying is the present participle; there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: club（棍棒）是用途更广的上位词；cudgel（粗短棍棒）突出用于击打；cowboy（牛仔）对应其独立的美国西部义。waddy 的木棒义具有澳大利亚原住民文化背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Club is the broader term for a heavy stick used as a weapon; cudgel emphasizes a stout stick for striking; cowboy corresponds to the separate western American sense. The club sense of waddy carries a specifically Aboriginal Australian cultural association.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记一根结实的澳洲木棒：名词是“棒”，转成动词就是“用棒打”；美国“牛仔”义另记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a sturdy Australian wooden club: the noun names the club, and the verb means using it to strike. Learn the American “cowboy” sense separately.

senses.collocation_zh: 哄骗某人做某事；骗走某人的钱
senses.sentence_en: He cozened her into signing away her share of the property.
senses.sentence_zh: 他哄骗她签字放弃了自己应得的那份财产。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于16世纪进入英语，确切来源尚无定论。一种传统解释将其联系到意大利语 cozzonare“做马匹交易”和 cozzone“马贩”，但不能把这一推测当作确定词源。
etymology_story.en: Cozen entered English in the sixteenth century, but its precise origin remains uncertain. One traditional explanation connects it with Italian cozzonare, “to trade horses,” and cozzone, “horse dealer,” though this connection is not established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cozen 是整体动词词干，不宜拆成 co- 和其他部分。屈折形式为 cozens、cozened、cozening；派生词包括 cozen + -er → cozener“骗子”和 cozen + -age → cozenage“欺骗、骗术”，两者均较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cozen is an unanalyzed verb stem, rather than co- plus another element. Its inflected forms are cozens, cozened, and cozening; derivatives include cozen + -er → cozener, “a deceiver,” and cozen + -age → cozenage, “deception or trickery,” both uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deceive（欺骗）含义最广；beguile（诱骗）突出魅力、讨好或迷惑；defraud（诈骗）突出以不诚实手段剥夺财物或权利。cozen 常带花言巧语和假意亲近的色彩，语体较古雅。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deceive is the broadest term; beguile emphasizes charm, flattery, or misleading attraction; defraud emphasizes dishonestly depriving someone of money or rights. Cozen often suggests persuasive talk or false friendliness and has a literary, old-fashioned tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 cozen 记成“嘴甜，手里有骗术”：先取得信任，再哄骗对方。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “sweet talk with a hidden trick”: gain someone's trust, then deceive them.

senses.meaning_en: Served with a garnish or accompanying vegetables, usually after a dish name.
senses.english_definition: A dish described as garni is served with a garnish or accompanying vegetables.
senses.collocation_en: steak garni; choucroute garni

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 garni，是 garnir“装备、装饰、配备”的过去分词。在英语烹饪用语中，它保留了“已配好配料或装饰食材”的意思，并常沿用法语式后置位置。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French garni, the past participle of garnir, “to equip, adorn, or furnish.” In English cookery, it retains the meaning “provided with a garnish or accompaniments” and often follows the dish name, as in French.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 garni 是不变形的整体借入形容词，不能拆成英语词缀；法语中的分词结构不等于英语构词结构。没有常用的英语派生词；garnish、garnished、garnishing 属于相关词族，与 garni 有共同的法语来源，但不是由英语 garni 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, garni is an invariant borrowed adjective, with no English affix breakdown; its French participial structure is not an English morphological construction. It has no common English derivatives; garnish, garnished, and garnishing are related through their French source, rather than derived from English garni.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: garnished（加有装饰食材的）最接近，突出摆盘或点缀；accompanied（配有……的）突出另有配菜；decorated（装饰过的）侧重外观，也可用于非食品。garni 是较专门的菜单用语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Garnished is the closest equivalent and emphasizes added presentation elements; accompanied emphasizes food served alongside a dish; decorated focuses on appearance and also applies outside cookery. Garni is a more specialized menu term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 菜名后加 garni：这道菜已经“配好了”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Garni after a dish name means the dish comes “already furnished” with accompaniments.

senses.meaning_en: The trifoliate orange, a thorny citrus relative with leaves composed of three leaflets.
senses.english_definition: Trifoliata is a thorny shrub or small tree with three leaflets to each leaf, often grown as a hedge or used as citrus rootstock.

etymology_story.zh: 来自植物学拉丁语名称 Poncirus trifoliata 中的种加词 trifoliata，意为“三叶的”，指其每片复叶通常由三片小叶组成。英语园艺用法把这一种加词单独用作树名。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the botanical Latin epithet trifoliata in Poncirus trifoliata, meaning “three-leaved” and referring to its leaves, each normally composed of three leaflets. English horticultural usage adopted the epithet as a standalone plant name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可辨认的学术构词成分为 tri-（三）+ foli-（叶，源自拉丁语 folium）+ -ata（拉丁语形容词词尾）；末尾不是现代英语中的能产后缀。英语中作为植物名称整体使用；相关形式有 trifoliate“三叶的、三出复叶的”和 trifoliolate“由三片小叶组成的”，但它们不是从英语名词 trifoliata 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Its recognizable learned elements are tri-, “three,” + foli-, “leaf,” from Latin folium, + -ata, a Latin adjectival ending rather than a productive modern English suffix. English uses the whole form as a plant name; related formations include trifoliate, “three-leaved,” and trifoliolate, “having three leaflets,” rather than direct derivatives of the English noun trifoliata.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: trifoliate orange（三叶橙、枳）是较透明的英语通名；hardy orange（耐寒橙、枳）突出耐寒性。两者在这里均指同一种植物，而 trifoliata 更带园艺和植物名称色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Trifoliate orange is the more transparent descriptive common name; hardy orange emphasizes the plant's cold tolerance. Both name the same plant here, while trifoliata has a more horticultural or botanical flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri- 是“三”，foli- 是“叶”：看见三片小叶，就想到枳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means “three” and foli- means “leaf”: three leaflets point to the trifoliate orange.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 domine，即 dominus（主人、主）的呼格，原用于当面尊称他人；牧师义另经荷兰语 dominee 传入英语。这些意义均带有历史色彩，不能当作现代日常称呼使用。参见[《韦氏词典》词源及用法](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/domine)。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin domine, the vocative of dominus, meaning 'lord' or 'master'; the minister sense also entered through Dutch dominee. Both uses are historical rather than ordinary modern forms of address. See [Merriam-Webster's etymology and usage](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/domine).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再按常用词缀拆分的借词：domine + -s → domines（复数）。相关形式 dominie 常用于苏格兰的“教师”义，也有牧师义；不应把其全部用法直接移给 domine。同源词包括 dominate（支配）、domination（支配）、dominant（占主导的）、dominance（优势）、dominion（统治权）、domineer（专横行事）、domineering（专横的），它们并非由现代英语 domine 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, domine is an unsegmented loanword: domine + -s → domines, its plural. The related form dominie commonly has a Scottish schoolmaster sense as well as a minister sense; its uses should not all be transferred to domine. Historical relatives include dominate, domination, dominant, dominance, dominion, domineer, and domineering; these are not direct modern derivatives of domine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: master（主人）突出权威或主仆关系；sir（先生）是仍通用的礼貌称呼；minister（牧师）表示宗教职务。domine 的区别在于其古旧尊称或特定教会背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Master emphasizes authority or a master–servant relationship; sir remains a general polite form of address; minister names a religious office. Domine adds an obsolete respectful register or a particular church background.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin 'O master!' → a respectful address → a historical title for a minister.
