etymology_story.zh: calkin 可追溯到中古英语的相关词形，用来指马蹄铁上的凸起。其更早来源并不完全确定；这个词的意义始终围绕帮助马蹄抓地的突出部分。
etymology_story.en: Calkin goes back to related Middle English forms denoting a projection on a horseshoe. Its earlier origin is not entirely certain; its meaning has remained centered on the projecting part that helps a hoof grip the ground.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：calkin 通常作为整体词处理，不宜把 -kin 机械解释为现代指小后缀；复数为 calkins。相关术语有 calk（蹄铁防滑凸起）和 calked（装有防滑凸起的），但不构成以 calkin 为基础的常用派生词族。该专业词没有可靠的统一 CEFR 定级或通行考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: calkin is normally treated as a whole base; its ending should not automatically be analyzed as the modern diminutive suffix -kin. Its plural is calkins. Related terminology includes calk and calked, but these do not form a common derivational family based on calkin. This specialist word has no reliably established general CEFR level or standard examination tags.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: calk 可与 calkin 同指蹄铁防滑凸起；horseshoe stud（蹄铁防滑钉）常指另行安装、尤其可拆卸的钉；cleat（防滑齿）用途更广，也可用于鞋底等部位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Calk can denote the same horseshoe projection; horseshoe stud often suggests a separately fitted, especially removable, component; cleat is broader and can refer to gripping projections on footwear and other equipment.

etymology_story.zh: calthrop 是 caltrop 的较少见异体，历史上与中古英语 calketrappe、古法语及中古拉丁语中的相关词形相联系。这一词群曾用于带刺植物和尖刺障碍物，二者通过“扎脚的尖刺”这一共同特征发生语义联系。
etymology_story.en: Calthrop is a less common variant of caltrop, historically connected with Middle English calketrappe and related Old French and medieval Latin forms. The word group has denoted both prickly plants and spiked obstacles, linked by their foot-piercing points.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：calthrop 是整体词，不宜按现代英语拆分；复数为 calthrops，常见异体为 caltrop，复数 caltrops。water + calthrop → water calthrop（菱）；没有常用的现代派生词族。该少见词形没有可靠的统一 CEFR 定级或通行考试标签。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: calthrop is an unanalyzed base, with the plural calthrops; the more usual variant is caltrop, plural caltrops. Water + calthrop forms water calthrop. There is no common modern derivational family, and this uncommon spelling has no reliably established general CEFR level or standard examination tags.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: caltrop 是较常见的同义拼写，可指尖刺障碍物或相关植物；puncture vine 专指蒺藜 Tribulus terrestris；water caltrop 指菱属水生植物，不能与陆生蒺藜混同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Caltrop is the more usual synonymous spelling for the device and the associated plant names; puncture vine specifically denotes Tribulus terrestris; water caltrop denotes aquatic Trapa plants and should be distinguished from terrestrial puncture vine.

senses.meaning_zh: 隶农：罗马帝国后期被束缚于土地、须缴纳地租的佃农
senses.meaning_en: A tenant farmer bound to an estate in the later Roman Empire
senses.english_definition: A colonus was a farmer in the later Roman Empire who had to remain on an estate and pay rent, often with part of the harvest.

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用拉丁语 colonus，原指农民或耕种者，与表示“耕作、居住”的 colere 有关。在英语历史研究中，该词专指罗马帝国后期依附于土地的佃农。[词源与历史义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/colonus)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin colonus, meaning a farmer or cultivator, related to colere, meaning to cultivate or inhabit. In English historical writing, it specifically denotes an estate-bound tenant of the later Roman Empire. [Origin and historical meaning](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/colonus)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借入词处理，不宜机械拆成具有现代英语意义的词根和后缀。单数 colonus，拉丁式复数 coloni；相关历史名词 colonate 指“隶农制”。colony（殖民地）、colonist（殖民者）、colonial（殖民的）、colonize（殖民）和 colonization（殖民化）属于同源词群，并非由现代英语 colonus 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, colonus is a whole borrowed stem rather than a productive combination of English roots and suffixes. Its Latin plural is coloni; the related historical noun colonate names the tenancy system. Colony, colonist, colonial, colonize, and colonization belong to the same etymological family rather than being direct modern derivatives of colonus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tenant farmer（佃农）是较宽泛的职业与租佃身份，不一定受土地束缚；serf（农奴）通常指中世纪等其他历史制度下依附土地的农民；peasant（农民）强调农业劳动者的社会身份，不说明具体法律地位。colonus 专指罗马历史中的特定身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tenant farmer is a broader term that does not necessarily imply being bound to the land; serf usually describes a land-bound peasant under medieval or other historical systems; peasant identifies a rural agricultural worker without specifying legal status. Colonus names a particular Roman historical status.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“耕种者”到“被土地拴住的耕种者”：耕地谋生，也受土地束缚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From cultivator to land-bound cultivator: the farmer works the land and is tied to it.

senses.meaning_zh: 环孢素：用于预防移植排斥等的环状多肽免疫抑制药
senses.meaning_en: A cyclic peptide drug that suppresses immune activity
senses.english_definition: Cyclosporine is a medicine that reduces the activity of the immune system, especially to help prevent the body from rejecting a transplanted organ.

senses.sentence_zh: 肾移植后，她接受了环孢素治疗，以帮助预防排斥反应。

etymology_story.zh: 这是国际科学词汇，由表示“环”的 cycl-、表示“孢子”的 spor- 和化学物质名称后缀 -ine 构成。名称联系其环状多肽结构与真菌来源，后来成为这种免疫抑制药的通用名称。[词源与药物释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cyclosporine)
etymology_story.en: This scientific name combines cycl-, meaning circle, spor-, meaning spore, and the chemical suffix -ine. It connects the compound's cyclic peptide structure with its fungal origin and became the generic name of the immunosuppressive medicine. [Origin and drug definition](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cyclosporine)

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词公式为 cyclo-（环状）+ spor-（孢子）+ -ine（化学物质名称后缀）；-ine 本身不表示“免疫抑制药”。相关名称包括 cyclosporin（异拼）、ciclosporin（国际通用名称）和 cyclosporine A／cyclosporin A（环孢素A）；这些主要是名称变体，并非独立派生词。常见组合有 cyclosporine-induced（环孢素引起的）和 cyclosporine-resistant（对环孢素耐药的）；无常用动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation is cyclo- meaning cyclic + spor- meaning spore + -ine, a suffix used in chemical names; -ine does not itself mean immunosuppressant. Related names include the spelling variant cyclosporin, the international nonproprietary name ciclosporin, and cyclosporine A or cyclosporin A. These are chiefly naming variants rather than separate derivatives. Established combinations include cyclosporine-induced and cyclosporine-resistant; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ciclosporin 与 cyclosporin 是同一药物的名称或拼写变体，基本没有词义差别；immunosuppressant（免疫抑制药）是上位词，涵盖环孢素及许多其他药物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ciclosporin and cyclosporin are alternative names or spellings for the same medicine, with essentially no semantic difference. Immunosuppressant is the broader category containing cyclosporine and many other drugs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cyclo- 想“环”，spor- 想“真菌孢子”：真菌来源的环状药物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cyclo- suggests a ring and spor- suggests fungal spores: a fungus-derived medicine with a ring structure.

etymology_story.zh: 名称来自十七世纪日本陶工酒井田柿右卫门及其传承的名号，后来由陶工之名转指相关瓷器与装饰风格。这一传统在有田发展，以乳白瓷地上的精巧釉上彩装饰闻名。[柿右卫门基金会历史介绍](https://kakiemon.or.jp/en/kakiemon/history/)
etymology_story.en: The name comes from the seventeenth-century Japanese potter Sakaida Kakiemon and the artistic name inherited by his successors; it came to designate their porcelain and its decorative style. The tradition developed in Arita and became known for refined overglaze enamels on a milky white body. [Kakiemon Foundation history](https://kakiemon.or.jp/en/kakiemon/history/)

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是由日语人名转成的英语借词，现代英语中不拆作英语词根与词缀。另见小写形式 kakiemon；作为瓷器类别通常用作不可数名词。Kakiemon ware（柿右卫门瓷器）、Kakiemon porcelain（柿右卫门瓷）和 Kakiemon-style decoration（柿右卫门风格装饰）是组合表达；名词放在另一名词前修饰，不必另立形容词词性。无常用独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: This is an English loanword formed from a Japanese personal name, with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. The lowercase spelling kakiemon also occurs; the porcelain category is normally uncountable. Kakiemon ware, Kakiemon porcelain, and Kakiemon-style decoration are combinations. Its use before another noun does not require a separate adjective entry. There is no common independent derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Kakiemon ware（柿右卫门瓷器）是近乎同义的完整表达；Arita ware（有田烧）按产地命名，范围更广；Imari ware（伊万里瓷）传统上联系经伊万里港输出的瓷器，范围与风格也更广，不能与 Kakiemon 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kakiemon ware is a virtually equivalent expanded expression. Arita ware is a broader geographical category. Imari ware traditionally refers to porcelain associated with shipment through Imari and encompasses a wider range of styles, so it is not interchangeable with Kakiemon.

mnemonic_anchor.en: The potter's name becomes the porcelain's name: Kakiemon evokes colourful birds and flowers against generous white space.

senses.sentence_zh: 那篇旧记述描写了海边高处的一堆岩石。

etymology_story.zh: 旧词典将 karn 追溯至康沃尔语，原义与石堆或岩石有关；它与源于盖尔语的 cairn 有亲缘关系，现代词典也将其列作 cairn 的变体。因此，不宜直接把 cairn 经苏格兰语传入英语的路径完全套用于 karn。[旧词典词源](https://classic.net.bible.org/lexicon.php/xml/xml/lexicon.php?word=karn)；[现代变体标注](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/karn)
etymology_story.en: Older dictionaries trace karn to Cornish and associate it with heaps of rocks; it is related to Gaelic-derived cairn and is also listed as a variant of cairn in modern dictionaries. Cairn's transmission through Scots should therefore not simply be assumed to be the exact history of karn. [Historical etymology](https://classic.net.bible.org/lexicon.php/xml/xml/lexicon.php?word=karn); [modern variant entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/karn)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可进一步分析的借入词干：karn + -s → karns（复数）。cairn（石堆、堆石标）是相关的标准常用形式；cairned（堆有石标的）等属于 cairn 的词族，不宜作为 karn 的直接派生词。karn 无常用独立派生词；所列搭配是罕见词的典型组合，不代表高频日常表达。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, karn is an unanalyzable borrowed stem: karn + -s gives the plural karns. Cairn is the related standard and much more usual form; words such as cairned belong to the cairn family rather than being direct derivatives of karn. Karn has no common independent derivatives. The listed combinations illustrate its rare usage rather than high-frequency everyday expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cairn（堆石标、纪念石堆）是最接近且更常用的词；rock pile（岩石堆）只说明岩石聚集，不暗示标记用途；marker（标记、界标）强调功能，但不限定材料。karn 带有明显的旧用或地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cairn is the closest and more usual equivalent, often suggesting a marker or memorial. Rock pile merely describes accumulated rocks without implying a marking function. Marker emphasizes purpose without specifying material. Karn has a distinctly dated or regional character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 karn 与 cairn 配成一对：看到石堆，先想到常用词 cairn。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair karn with cairn: picture a heap of stones and recall cairn as the usual modern word.

senses.meaning_zh: 夸希奥科病：以水肿为特征的严重营养不良，多见于儿童
senses.meaning_en: A severe form of malnutrition characterized by oedema, especially in children
senses.english_definition: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition, especially in children, in which fluid collects in the body's tissues and causes swelling.
senses.collocation_en: children with kwashiorkor; treatment of kwashiorkor
senses.collocation_zh: 患夸希奥科病的儿童；夸希奥科病的治疗
senses.sentence_en: The child with kwashiorkor had swelling in both feet.
senses.sentence_zh: 这名患夸希奥科病的儿童双脚都有水肿。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自加纳的加语，其名称通常解释为与“新生儿到来后被替代、断奶的孩子所患的病”有关。西塞莉·威廉斯于二十世纪三十年代将这一当地病名引入医学文献；这一命名背景不等于对所有病例病因的完整解释。[名称背景与医学史](https://www.icrc.org/sites/default/files/external/doc/en/assets/files/other/icrc_002_0820.pdf)
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Ga in Ghana and is commonly explained as referring to the illness of a child displaced or weaned when another baby arrives. Cicely Williams introduced the local name into medical literature in the 1930s; this naming background is not a complete explanation of the causes of every case. [Naming background and medical history](https://www.icrc.org/sites/default/files/external/doc/en/assets/files/other/icrc_002_0820.pdf)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借词记忆，不宜根据字母片段臆造英语词根或后缀。通常为不可数病名，没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生形式。kwashiorkor-associated oedema（夸希奥科病相关水肿）等是组合表达；marasmic kwashiorkor 指同时具有明显消瘦与营养性水肿的混合表现，并非本词的形态派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a whole borrowed word, not a combination of recognizable productive English roots and suffixes. It is normally an uncountable disease name, with no common derived verb, adjective, or adverb. Expressions such as kwashiorkor-associated oedema are combinations; marasmic kwashiorkor denotes a mixed presentation with marked wasting and nutritional oedema rather than a morphological derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oedematous malnutrition（水肿型营养不良）是最接近的描述性名称；protein-energy malnutrition（蛋白质－能量营养不良）范围更广；marasmus（消瘦型营养不良）是相关但不同的类型，突出严重消瘦，典型情况下没有营养性水肿。不能仅凭“蛋白质缺乏”四字概括 kwashiorkor 的全部病因。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oedematous malnutrition is the closest descriptive equivalent. Protein-energy malnutrition is a broader category. Marasmus is a related but distinct form characterized by severe wasting and typically no nutritional oedema. Protein deficiency alone should not be treated as a complete account of kwashiorkor's causes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借“新生儿到来，较大的孩子断奶”的命名故事记词，再抓住临床关键词“营养不良＋水肿”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the naming story of an older child weaned when a new baby arrives, then attach the defining image: malnutrition with swelling.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古拉丁语 marcasita 和法语相关形式传入英语，通常进一步追溯至阿拉伯语中的矿石名称。早期名称涵盖的矿物范围较宽；现代矿物学将其限定为白铁矿，但首饰行业仍常用它称呼黄铁矿装饰石。
etymology_story.en: The word reached English through Medieval Latin marcasita and related French forms, and is generally traced further back to an Arabic mineral name. The older name covered a broader range of minerals; modern mineralogy restricts it to marcasite, while jewellery usage commonly refers to pyrite.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整体借词分析，没有可独立释义的常用词根 marcas-；词尾形式与矿物名称后缀 -ite 相同。主要词族：marcasite（白铁矿；首饰装饰石）、marcasites（复数）、marcasitic（白铁矿的；含白铁矿的）；marcasite brooch 是名词作前置修饰语的短语，不构成独立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, marcasite is best treated as a whole borrowed base, without a familiar independently meaningful root marcas-; its ending matches the mineral suffix -ite. The main family comprises marcasite, plural marcasites, and marcasitic, meaning relating to or containing marcasite; marcasite in marcasite brooch is an attributive noun, not a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: white iron pyrites（白铁矿）是其传统矿物名称；pyrite（黄铁矿）是成分相同而晶体结构不同的矿物，不能在矿物学中直接互换；iron pyrites（硫铁矿，通常指黄铁矿）在旧式或宽泛用法中范围较模糊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: White iron pyrites is a traditional name for marcasite. Pyrite has the same chemical composition but a different crystal structure, so it is not an interchangeable mineralogical synonym. Iron pyrites usually means pyrite, although older or broader usage can be less precise.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住两个标签：矿物学是“白铁矿”，银饰柜台上的 marcasite 通常是“黄铁矿装饰石”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two labels in mind: mineralogical marcasite is its own mineral, while jewellery-counter marcasite is usually sparkling pyrite.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 maund 借自南亚语言中表示重量单位的 man，如印地语和乌尔都语中的相应形式。它随南亚贸易和行政计量进入英语，所表示的实际重量在不同地方和历史时期并不统一。
etymology_story.en: English maund was borrowed from the South Asian weight name man, represented in languages such as Hindi and Urdu. It entered English through trade and administrative measurement in South Asia, without acquiring one universal value across regions and periods.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：maund 为不可进一步拆解的借词词干；maund + -s → maunds（复数）。没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词；maund weight（以莫恩德计的重量）等属于名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: maund is an unanalyzable borrowed base; maund + -s gives the plural maunds. It has no common derived verb, adjective, or adverb; expressions such as maund weight are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: man（当地名称的转写）可指同一单位；seer（锡尔）是相关计量体系中的较小单位；hundredweight（英担）属于另一套重量体系。后二者只是相关计量词，不能不经换算就替代 maund。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Man is a transliteration of the local unit name and can refer to the same measure. Seer is a smaller unit in related measurement systems, while hundredweight belongs to a different system; neither is an interchangeable synonym without conversion.

etymology_story.en: Mool is a Scots and northern English form of mould meaning earth or soil, belonging to a Germanic word family represented by Old English molde, meaning earth or dust. The soil meaning also extends to grave earth, especially in the literary plural mools.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：mool 是单一词干；mool + -s → mools，后者既可表示土块，也常特指坟土。相关地区形式有 moul、mools；标准英语中的对应形式为 mould，美式拼写为 mold，此处均指“土”，不是“霉菌”。没有需要补列的常用现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: mool is a simple base; mool + -s gives mools, used for particles of earth and often specifically for grave earth. Related regional forms include moul and mools; the standard English counterpart is mould, spelled mold in American English, in its earth sense rather than its fungus sense. There are no common modern derivatives requiring a separate family listing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soil（土壤）侧重植物生长的介质；earth（泥土、大地）范围较广；mould（松软的土，尤指富含有机质的表土）保留了与 mool 最接近的传统词义。Mool 另外带有鲜明的地区或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soil emphasizes the material in which plants grow; earth is broader and can mean ground or its substance; mould retains the closely related traditional sense of loose earth, especially organic surface soil. Mool adds a distinctly regional or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 mool 看作苏格兰泥土里的 mould：根扎在土中，mools 还可指覆盖墓穴的土。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect mool with earthy mould: roots grow in it, and the mools can cover a grave.

etymology_story.zh: Musca 直接采用拉丁语 musca，原义为“苍蝇”。这个昆虫名称分别进入天文学命名和动物分类命名，用来指苍蝇座以及家蝇属。
etymology_story.en: Musca directly adopts Latin musca, meaning fly. The insect name entered both astronomical naming and zoological classification, becoming the name of a constellation and a genus of flies.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 Musca 是整体借入的拉丁语专名，没有英语式前后缀。拉丁语属格 Muscae 用于恒星名称，如 Alpha Muscae（苍蝇座α星）；同源的科学词汇包括 muscid（蝇科昆虫；蝇科的）和 muscoid（蝇状的；蝇类的），它们不是由星座名派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Musca is a whole borrowed Latin proper name, without English prefixes or suffixes. The Latin genitive Muscae appears in star names such as Alpha Muscae; cognate scientific vocabulary includes muscid, a member of or relating to the family Muscidae, and muscoid, meaning flylike or relating to certain flies. These are not derivatives of the constellation name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: the Fly（苍蝇座的英语意译名称）可对应星座义；fly（苍蝇）是广义普通名称；housefly（家蝇）通常指 Musca domestica。后两者不能与属名 Musca 完全等同，因为属包含物种，而普通名称的分类范围不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The Fly is an English rendering of the constellation name. Fly is a broad common noun, while housefly normally refers to Musca domestica. Neither common noun is an exact substitute for the genus name Musca, since a genus contains species and common names have different scopes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语 musca＝苍蝇：画上星图就是苍蝇座，写进分类表就是家蝇属。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin musca means fly: place it on a star map for the constellation, or in a classification table for the genus.

senses.english_definition: An omphalos is a sacred stone that represents the centre of the world, especially the stone associated with the ancient Greek sanctuary at Delphi.

senses.meaning_zh: 中心；核心；枢纽，常带文学色彩
senses.meaning_en: A central point, hub, or symbolic centre, especially in literary usage
senses.english_definition: If a place is described as the omphalos of something, it is regarded as its central or most significant point.
senses.collocation_en: the omphalos of the world; a cultural omphalos
senses.collocation_zh: 世界的中心；文化中心
senses.sentence_en: For the young writers, the café became the omphalos of their literary world.
senses.sentence_zh: 对这些年轻作家而言，这家咖啡馆成了他们文学世界的中心。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自希腊语 omphalos，原义为“肚脐”，也可引申为中心。古希腊人将德尔斐的圣石视为世界的“肚脐”，这一象征又支持了英语中“中心、枢纽”的比喻义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Greek omphalos, meaning navel and, by extension, centre. The ancient Greek association of the sacred stone at Delphi with the world's navel also supports the English figurative meaning of a centre or hub.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 omphalos 是整体借词；-os 是保留的希腊语词尾，不是有独立英语意义的后缀。复数可用 omphaloi 或 omphaloses；相关构词成分为 omphal-／omphalo-（脐），同源词包括 omphalic（脐的）、omphalitis（脐炎）和 omphalocele（脐膨出）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, omphalos is a whole borrowed word; -os is a retained Greek ending, not an independently meaningful English suffix. Plurals include omphaloi and omphaloses; the related combining forms omphal- and omphalo- mean navel, as in omphalic, relating to the navel, omphalitis, inflammation of the navel, and omphalocele, a congenital protrusion of abdominal organs at the umbilicus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: navel（肚脐）对应字面身体部位；centre（中心）是最中性的比喻替换词；hub（枢纽）强调活动或联系的汇聚。Omphalos 通常额外带有神圣中心、自我认定的中心或文学典故色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Navel matches the literal body part; centre is the most neutral figurative equivalent; hub emphasizes converging activity or connections. Omphalos often adds the idea of a sacred centre, a self-proclaimed centre, or a literary allusion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“身体的肚脐”想到“世界的肚脐”，再记住“中心、枢纽”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from the body's navel to the world's navel, then to any symbolic centre or hub.

senses.meaning_zh: 再生草；第二茬牧草

senses.english_definition: Rowen is grass that grows again after a field has been mown, especially when it is harvested as a second crop of hay.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经盎格鲁法语 rewain 等形式进入中古英语，与法语 regain（第二茬草）有词源联系。其历史构成包含表示“再、重新”的成分，指割草之后重新长出的牧草。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through Anglo-French forms such as rewain and is related to French regain, meaning a second growth of grass. Its historical formation includes an element meaning “again,” referring to grass growing back after mowing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 rowen 作为不可再分析的借入词根，不拆成 row + -en。它通常是不可数名词，没有常用的派生词；rowen hay（第二茬干草）和 rowen crop（再生牧草作物）是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, rowen is an unanalyzed borrowed base, not row + -en. It is normally a mass noun and has no common derivatives; rowen hay and rowen crop are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aftermath（割后再生草）在农业义上最接近，但日常英语中通常表示事件的后果；regrowth（再生、生长恢复）适用于各种重新长出的植物；second-cut hay（第二茬干草）强调已收割的第二茬干草。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aftermath is a close agricultural synonym, although its everyday meaning concerns the consequences of an event. Regrowth applies broadly to renewed plant growth, while second-cut hay specifically emphasizes hay harvested at the second cutting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“割过，又长”：rowen 就是割草后再长出的那一茬。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “cut once, grow again”: rowen is the grass that returns after mowing.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经古法语和中古英语传来，最终源自拉丁语 tertia hora，意为“第三时辰”。这里的时辰从黎明开始计算，因此传统上对应上午九时左右。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Old French and Middle English from Latin tertia hora, meaning “the third hour.” Because the hours were counted from dawn, this traditionally corresponded to about nine in the morning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 terce 是不可再分析的历史词形，不应拆成 ter- + -ce。tierce 是相关异体拼写；terces 是需要表示多次日课时可用的复数形式，没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, terce is an unanalyzed historical form, not ter- + -ce. Tierce is a related variant spelling; terces is the plural when separate observances are counted, and there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: the third hour（第三时辰）强调传统计时位置，也可指该时辰的祈祷；midmorning prayer（上午中段祈祷）是便于理解的功能性说法；canonical office（日课）是上位词，涵盖多个规定时辰的祈祷。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The third hour emphasizes the traditional time designation and can also name its prayers. Midmorning prayer is a transparent functional description. Canonical office is the broader category covering prayer services at several appointed hours.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“第三”：黎明后第三时辰，约上午九时祈祷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to “third”: the third hour after dawn, traditionally about 9 a.m.

senses.english_definition: An axolotl is a salamander native to Mexico that normally lives in water throughout its life and keeps its feathery external gills as an adult.

etymology_story.zh: 英语名称来自纳瓦特尔语 āxōlōtl，通常被解释为“水怪”。名称中的 ā- 与“水”有关，后半部分也与纳瓦特尔文化中的 Xolotl 之名存在联系。
etymology_story.en: The English name comes from Nahuatl āxōlōtl, traditionally interpreted as “water monster.” The element ā- concerns water, while the second part is also connected with the name Xolotl in Nahuatl culture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 axolotl 是完整借入的动物名称，不按英语词缀硬拆；其纳瓦特尔语历史构成不等于英语中的现代构词。常用复数为 axolotls，也可见不变复数 axolotl；没有常用的直接派生词，axolotl tank（美西螈饲养缸）属于名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, axolotl is a borrowed animal name without productive English affixes; its historical Nahuatl components are not modern English word formation. The usual plural is axolotls, with unchanged axolotl also occurring; there are no common direct derivatives, and axolotl tank is a noun combination.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Mexican axolotl（墨西哥美西螈）是更明确的同物名称；Mexican walking fish（墨西哥行走鱼）是俗称，但它实际上是两栖动物；salamander（蝾螈类动物）是上位词，不专指美西螈。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mexican axolotl is a more explicit name for the same animal. Mexican walking fish is an informal name, although the animal is an amphibian. Salamander is the broader category and does not specifically identify an axolotl.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “水中的小怪兽”：把名称与终生水栖、头旁长着羽毛状外鳃的形象连接起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a “little water monster” with feathery gills beside its head.

etymology_story.zh: Benzedrine 是20世纪创制的商品名，其形式借用了与苯有关的 benz-，并受到 ephedrine（麻黄碱）名称的影响。它最初用于苯丙胺吸入器，后来也用于硫酸苯丙胺片剂。
etymology_story.en: Benzedrine was coined as a twentieth-century trade name using benz-, associated with benzene, and a form influenced by ephedrine. It was first used for amphetamine inhalers and later also for amphetamine sulfate tablets.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代用法中应将 Benzedrine 作为完整商品名记忆；历史命名可概括为 benz- 加仿 ephedrine 的名称结尾，不能把 -edrine 当作具有固定意义的普通英语后缀。没有常用的直接派生词；Benzedrine tablet（苯丙胺片剂）是名词组合，amphetamine（苯丙胺）是通用药名而非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern usage, Benzedrine is best treated as a complete trade name. Its historical formation combines benz- with an ending modeled on ephedrine; -edrine is not an ordinary English suffix with a fixed meaning. There are no common direct derivatives; Benzedrine tablet is a noun combination, and amphetamine is the generic drug name rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: amphetamine（苯丙胺、安非他明）是通用药名，不限于该品牌；amphetamine sulfate（硫酸苯丙胺）专指其硫酸盐形式，与历史片剂的关系更直接；stimulant（兴奋剂）是更宽泛的类别词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Amphetamine is the generic drug name and is not restricted to this brand. Amphetamine sulfate specifically identifies the sulfate salt associated with the historical tablets. Stimulant is a much broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把它与“旧广告上的苯丙胺药品”相连；benz- 提醒名称中的苯相关化学背景。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture an old amphetamine advertisement; benz- recalls the name’s benzene-related chemical background.

etymology_story.zh: brail 经中古英语借自盎格鲁法语 braiel，原指带子或系紧衣物的绳带。其“用带索收拢”的含义进入航海用语，后来也用于某些渔网和相关操作。
etymology_story.en: Brail entered Middle English from Anglo-French braiel, a strap or cord used to fasten clothing. Its association with gathering things by cords developed into nautical uses and later fishing uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：brail 是不可再按常用英语词根、词缀拆分的借入词；名词直接转用为动词。常用屈折形式：brails（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、brailed（过去式及过去分词）、brailing（现在分词及动名词）；无常见的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: brail is a borrowed base with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Inflected forms are brails, brailed, and brailing; there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 就收帆动作而言，furl 指把帆卷起或收好；reef 指缩小帆面以减弱风力作用；gather in 泛指收拢。brail 特别说明使用收帆索这一操作方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the sailing action, furl means to roll or gather a sail for stowage; reef means to reduce its exposed area; gather in is a general expression for drawing something together. Brail specifically identifies the use of brail ropes.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a cord gathering a loose sail into a bundle: the cord is a brail, and using it is to brail.

etymology_story.zh: burd 延续了中古英语中表示少女或女子的相关词形，后来主要保留在苏格兰文学和传统民谣中。其更早来源并不确定，与古英语 brȳd“新娘”的联系是一种解释，不能视为定论。
etymology_story.en: Burd continues Middle English forms meaning a maiden or woman and survives chiefly in Scots literature and traditional ballads. Its earlier origin is uncertain; a connection with Old English brȳd, meaning bride, has been proposed but is not established.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：burd 是整体记忆的历史单纯词，没有可分析的现代英语前后缀，也不应认作外来借词。复数为 burds；无常见的现代派生词，不能仅凭可能的历史联系把 bride 列为其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: burd is a historical simple word with no productive English affixes and should not be treated as a foreign borrowing. Its plural is burds; it has no common modern derivatives, and bride is not a derivative of burd.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: maiden 指少女或未婚年轻女子，带文学色彩；damsel 更有古代故事或骑士文学气息；lass 是较亲切的地方用语。burd 的古老民谣和苏格兰文学色彩更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Maiden is literary and often suggests an unmarried young woman; damsel evokes old tales or chivalric literature; lass is a familiar regional word for a girl or young woman. Burd has a particularly strong association with old ballads and Scots literature.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 burd 放进古老民谣：窗边等候的少女。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Place burd in an old ballad: a young woman waiting at a window.

senses.english_definition: Chichi is decoration or stylish behaviour that seems artificial or unnecessarily elaborate.

etymology_story.zh: chichi 借自法语 chichi，法语中可指无谓的讲究、做作或繁琐的排场。英语将其用于矫饰的风格和装饰，也用作形容词描述刻意追求时髦的人或事物。
etymology_story.en: Chichi was borrowed from French chichi, referring to fuss, affectation, or unnecessary elaboration. English uses it for affected style and decoration and as an adjective for things that seem deliberately fashionable.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chichi 是整体借入词，也写作 chi-chi；重复音节不是两个有独立意义的英语词根。它可直接作名词和形容词；名词通常不可数，无常见的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: chichi, also written chi-chi, is a borrowed word whose repeated syllables are not separate meaningful English roots. It functions directly as both noun and adjective; the noun is usually uncountable, and there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pretentious 强调刻意显得高级或重要；fussy 强调细节繁多、过于讲究；ornate 强调装饰繁复，本身不一定含贬义。chichi 常把追逐时髦与做作、花哨结合起来，带轻微嘲讽。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pretentious stresses an attempt to appear impressive; fussy stresses excessive attention to details; ornate describes elaborate decoration without necessarily criticizing it. Chichi combines fashionable display with affectation, often with mild mockery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一家连小细节都刻意摆出时髦姿态的店：讲究过头，就是 chichi。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a shop where every tiny detail tries to look fashionable: style pushed into affectation is chichi.

etymology_story.zh: Clotho 经拉丁语来自希腊语 Klōthō，意为“纺线者”，与 klōthein“纺线”相关。名字直接体现了她纺出生命之线的神话职责。
etymology_story.en: Clotho comes through Latin from Greek Klōthō, meaning the spinner and related to klōthein, to spin. Her name directly expresses her mythological role of spinning the thread of life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Clotho 是完整的神话人物专名，不能按现代英语词根和词缀拆分，也不是 cloth 加 -o。通常保持单数并大写；所有格为 Clotho's，无常用的现代英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: Clotho is a complete mythological proper name, not a combination of modern English roots and affixes, and not cloth plus -o. It is normally singular and capitalized; its possessive is Clotho's, and it has no common modern English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格的普通词近义词。the Spinner“纺线者”是描述其职责的称号；the Fates“命运三女神”和 the Moirai“摩伊赖”指她所属的整个女神群体，不能单独替代 Clotho。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There are no exact ordinary-word synonyms. The Spinner is a descriptive title for her role; the Fates and the Moirai name the whole group to which she belongs and cannot individually replace Clotho.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字意为“纺线者”：看见 Clotho，就想到生命之线开始被纺出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Her name means the spinner: picture Clotho spinning the beginning of a human life.

etymology_story.en: The word came through Italian donzello and Old Provençal donzel, ultimately from a diminutive of Latin dominus, meaning 'master' or 'lord.' The designation for a young nobleman came to describe an unknighted gentleman or attendant. [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/donzel)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作能产拆分的借入名词：donzel；复数为 donzels。没有常用的现代英语派生词；damsel（少女）是历史同源词，不是由 donzel 加词缀构成的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, donzel is an unanalyzed borrowed noun; its plural is donzels. It has no common productive English derivatives; damsel is a historical relative, rather than a derivative formed by adding an English affix to donzel.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: squire（骑士侍从）更明确指随侍骑士、接受相关训练的人；page（少年侍从）侧重年幼及服务职责；young nobleman（年轻贵族）只说明年龄与身份，不一定承担侍从工作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Squire more specifically suggests service to a knight and preparation for knighthood; page emphasizes a young attendant's duties; young nobleman identifies age and social rank without necessarily implying service.

etymology_story.en: English adopted New Latin guaiacum, a name derived through Spanish guayacán from Taíno in the Caribbean. The tree's name also came to denote its wood and resin. [American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=guaiacum)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 guaiacum 作为完整借词处理，不把词尾 -um 当作能产的英语后缀；指单株树木时复数可用 guaiacums，指木材或树脂时通常不可数。相关形式包括 guaiac（愈创木材、愈创木脂），以及采用相关构词成分 guaiac- 的化学名称 guaiacol（愈创木酚）；Guaiacum 是首字母大写的植物属名。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat guaiacum as a whole borrowed word, rather than analyzing -um as a productive English suffix. Individual trees can form the plural guaiacums, while the wood and resin senses are normally uncountable. Related forms include guaiac, referring to the wood or resin, and the chemical name guaiacol, using the related combining element guaiac-; capitalized Guaiacum is the botanical genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lignum vitae（铁梨木、愈创木）常用于相关树木，尤其强调其坚硬木材；guaiac（愈创木材、愈创木脂）通常指木材或树脂；guaiacum resin（愈创木脂）明确限定为树脂，避免与树木及木材混淆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lignum vitae commonly names the relevant trees and especially their hard timber; guaiac usually denotes the wood or resin; guaiacum resin explicitly identifies the resin rather than the tree or timber.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个树名带出三样：树本身 → 硬木材 → 树脂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One tree name, three connected referents: the tree, its hard wood, and its resin.

senses.english_definition: A hawkshaw is a detective, especially when you refer to one in an old-fashioned or humorous way.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自汤姆·泰勒于1863年创作的戏剧《假释犯》中侦探 Hawkshaw 的名字。人物名后来在美国俚语中泛化为“侦探”，属于专名转为普通名词。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the detective Hawkshaw in Tom Taylor's 1863 play The Ticket-of-Leave Man. The character's name became an American slang term for a detective. [Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/hawkshaw)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词方式为专名普通名词化：Hawkshaw（人物名）→ hawkshaw（侦探）；复数为 hawkshaws。现代“侦探”义不通过 hawk + shaw 的组合来解释，也没有常用的能产派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is conversion of a proper name into a common noun: Hawkshaw, the character, became hawkshaw, a detective; the plural is hawkshaws. The detective meaning is not compositionally derived from hawk + shaw, and there is no common productive derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: detective（侦探、刑警）是中性通用称呼；sleuth（侦探、调查者）偏文学或诙谐，也可指业余调查者；gumshoe（侦探）同属美国俚语，常让人联想到老派私人侦探。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Detective is the neutral general term; sleuth is often literary or playful and can include an amateur investigator; gumshoe is also American slang and often evokes an old-fashioned private detective.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记人物 Hawkshaw，再记“像他一样查案的人”：侦探名 → 侦探。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the character first: a detective named Hawkshaw gave his name to other detectives.

etymology_story.zh: helve 经中古英语传承自古英语 h(i)elfe，原本就指工具的柄，是英语固有词。后来由名词转用为动词，表示“给工具装上柄”。
etymology_story.en: Helve is inherited through Middle English from Old English h(i)elfe, which already meant a tool handle. The noun also became a verb meaning to equip a tool with a handle. [Collins English Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/helve)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代基本词干为 helve，名词可直接转作动词；名词复数及动词第三人称单数均为 helves，过去式和过去分词为 helved，现在分词为 helving。派生形式包括 helver（装柄者）和 unhelved（未装柄的）；axe helve（斧柄）是复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is helve, with direct noun-to-verb conversion. Helves is both the noun plural and the verb's third-person singular; helved is the past tense and past participle, and helving is the present participle. Derivatives include helver, a person who fits handles, and unhelved, lacking a handle; axe helve is a compound expression.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handle（柄、把手）适用范围最广；haft（工具或武器的柄）与 helve 最接近，也常用于刀等器具；shaft（长柄、杆）强调细长的杆状结构，不一定专指握持部分。动词义可用 fit a handle to（给……装柄）准确释义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handle has the broadest application; haft is close to helve but also commonly applies to knives and other weapons; shaft emphasizes a long, narrow structural part that need not be solely a handgrip. For the verb, fit a handle to is a precise paraphrase.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 握住的是 helve；把柄装上去就是 to helve。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The part you grip is the helve; fitting that part to the tool is to helve it.

etymology_story.zh: 羊群义经中古英语 hirsill 追溯至古诺尔斯语 hirzla、hirðsla，原义为“保管、看护”，与 hirða（照管羊）相关。“看护”发展为“统一照管的羊群”，名词又转为表示分群管理的动词。
etymology_story.en: The flock sense goes through Middle English hirsill to Old Norse hirzla or hirðsla, meaning safekeeping or custody, related to hirða, 'to tend sheep.' The idea of keeping sheep developed into the flock under someone's care, and the noun also supplied a verb for arranging sheep into separate flocks. [Dictionaries of the Scots Language](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/hirsel_n1_v1)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词干为 hirsel，无需拆成英语前后缀；名词直接转作动词。复数及第三人称单数为 hirsels；过去式和过去分词为 hirseled 或 hirselled，现在分词及动名词为 hirseling 或 hirselling；动名词可指“羊群分类管理”。hirsle 是拼写变体，不是另一个派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is hirsel, without productive English prefix–suffix segmentation, and the noun converts directly into a verb. Hirsels serves as the plural and third-person singular; past forms are hirseled or hirselled, and participial forms are hirseling or hirselling. The verbal noun can denote the practice of dividing sheep into managed flocks. Hirsle is a spelling variant, rather than a separate derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flock（羊群、鸟群）是标准英语中最自然的对应词；herd（兽群；放牧、赶拢牲畜）范围更广，动词不一定表示分类；sort（分类）强调按标准分组，最贴近 hirsel 的动词义，但不限于羊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flock is the most natural standard-English equivalent of the noun; herd covers a wider range of livestock, and its verb need not imply classification; sort emphasizes division by criteria and closely matches the verb sense, but is not restricted to sheep.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“照管羊”记住“所管的一群羊”；作动词就是把羊分成便于照管的群。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with tending sheep: a hirsel is a flock under care, and to hirsel sheep is to divide them into manageable flocks.

etymology_story.zh: 该词采用植物学拉丁语属名 Manihot，最终源于南美洲图皮语中木薯的名称。英语 manioc 也源于这一组原住民名称；植物分类学将相关名称用于整个木薯属。
etymology_story.en: The word adopts the botanical Latin genus name Manihot, ultimately derived from a Tupi name for cassava in South America. English manioc comes from the same group of Indigenous names, while botanical classification extended the name to the genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中按完整借词处理：manihot，不拆成英语词根与词缀。普通名词复数为 manihots；属名 Manihot 首字母大写，通常用斜体。没有常用的英语派生词族；manioc 和 cassava 是相关名称，并非由 manihot 加词缀派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, manihot is an intact borrowing with no productive English root-and-affix division. Its common-noun plural is manihots; the genus name Manihot is capitalized and normally italicized. There is no established common English derivative family; manioc and cassava are related names, not affixed derivatives of manihot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cassava（木薯）是这种作物最常用的英语名称；manioc（木薯）是同一作物的另一名称；tapioca（木薯淀粉及其制品）主要指加工产品。manihot 更偏植物学用语，还可泛指木薯属的其他植物，不能总与这三个词互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cassava is the usual English name for the crop; manioc is another name for the same crop; tapioca primarily denotes its processed starch or products made from it. Manihot is more botanical and can include other members of the genus, so these terms are not always interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Manihot 记成木薯的“植物学家族名”：木薯是这个属的一员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of Manihot as cassava’s botanical family label: cassava is one member of the genus.

etymology_story.zh: 货币名词 merk 是 mark 的苏格兰语形式，承接日耳曼语中与重量及货币计量有关的旧称。现代俚语动词另见 murk、merc 等拼写，其确切来源存在不确定性，不宜与旧货币名称强行联系。
etymology_story.en: The monetary noun merk is a Scots form of mark, continuing an older Germanic term associated with weight and monetary measurement. The modern slang verb also appears in spellings such as murk and merc; its precise origin is uncertain and should not be forced into a connection with the currency term.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式为 merk，无可用于解释其意义的英语词缀。名词复数为 merks；规则动词形式为 merks、merked、merking。货币名词与俚语动词应分别记忆；mark 是货币义的相关形式，murk、merc 是俚语动词的相关拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: Merk has no English affix that explains its meaning. The noun plural is merks; the regular verb forms are merks, merked, and merking. Learn the monetary noun and slang verb separately: mark is related to the currency sense, while murk and merc are associated spellings of the slang verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 货币义的 mark（马克）是相关名称，但不同地区的具体币值不能混同。动词义的 kill（杀死）语体中性，merk 是俚语；trounce（大败）对应其比赛中的引申义，并不表示真正杀人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the monetary sense, mark is a related name, but its value varies by historical currency. For the verb, kill is neutral in register, whereas merk is slang; trounce matches the figurative competition sense without implying an actual killing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分两格记：旧苏格兰账本里的 merk 是钱；现代俚语里的 merk 是“干掉”，也可引申为“打爆对手”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use two separate pictures: a merk in an old Scottish ledger is money; to merk someone in slang is to take them out, literally or competitively.

senses.meaning_en: A fern of the royal-fern group, especially a member of the genus Osmunda.

etymology_story.zh: 这个蕨类名称经中古英语和古法语 osmonde 传入，与中世纪拉丁语 osmunda 有关。更早的来源并不确定；将它与人名 Osmund 联系起来只是传统解释之一。
etymology_story.en: The fern name passed through Middle English and Old French osmonde and is associated with medieval Latin osmunda. Its earlier origin is uncertain; a connection with the personal name Osmund is one traditional explanation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 osmund 是不可进一步分析的借入植物名称，复数为 osmunds。相关植物学形式包括属名 Osmunda、科名 Osmundaceae，以及表示“紫萁科的”的形容词 osmundaceous；这些形式属于植物学命名体系，不应把 os- 或 -mund 当作现代英语词缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, osmund is an unanalyzable borrowed plant name, with the plural osmunds. Related botanical forms include the genus Osmunda, the family Osmundaceae, and the adjective osmundaceous, meaning belonging to that family. These belong to botanical nomenclature; os- and -mund are not modern English affixes here.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: osmunda（紫萁属蕨）是密切相关的植物名称；royal fern（欧洲紫萁）通常指特定种 Osmunda regalis；fern（蕨类植物）范围更广。osmund 是较少见的类群名称，不能把所有蕨类都叫作 osmund。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Osmunda is a closely related name for these ferns; royal fern usually identifies the particular species Osmunda regalis; fern is the much broader category. Osmund is an uncommon group name and does not apply to ferns generally.

etymology_story.zh: 该词采用植物学拉丁语属名 Panicum，沿用拉丁语 pānicum“黍、粟类谷物”的名称。植物分类学将这个旧作物名称用于一个禾草属；它与表示“恐慌”的英语 panic 没有词源关系。
etymology_story.en: The word adopts the botanical Latin genus name Panicum, continuing Latin pānicum, a name for millet. Botanical classification applied the old crop name to a genus of grasses; it is etymologically unrelated to English panic meaning sudden fear.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语按完整拉丁语借词 panicum 处理，不能拆成 panic 加英语后缀 -um。普通名词复数为 panicums；属名 Panicum 首字母大写，通常用斜体。没有常用的英语派生词族；panic grass 是相关的禾草名称，其中 panic 是旧植物名称。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats panicum as an intact Latin borrowing, not as panic plus an English suffix -um. The common-noun plural is panicums; the genus name Panicum is capitalized and normally italicized. There is no common productive derivative family; panic grass is a related grass name using the older botanical word panic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: panic grass（黍属或相关禾草）是接近的普通名称，其范围可能随分类用法变化；millet（黍、粟类小粒谷物）是跨越多个属的作物统称；grass（禾草）范围最广。panicum 主要表达植物分类归属，不能与 millet 完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Panic grass is a close common name whose scope can vary with classification; millet is a crop category covering small-grained cereals from several genera; grass is the broadest term. Panicum primarily indicates botanical membership and is not equivalent to millet.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Panicum 与“结谷穗的黍属禾草”相连；这里的名称讲谷物，不讲恐慌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link Panicum with millet-bearing grasses: its historical name points to grain, not fear.

etymology_story.zh: Barret 是旧帽名 barrette 的相关形式，经法语与意大利语 berretta 相联系。这个帽名家族通常追溯至晚期拉丁语 birrettum；英语后来保留了若干形近而用途不同的帽饰名称。
etymology_story.en: Barret is a historical form related to the cap name barrette, connected through French with Italian berretta. This family of hat names is generally traced to Late Latin birrettum; English retained several similar forms for different kinds of headwear.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 barret 是完整的历史借词，不宜拆为 bar + -ret；复数为 barrets，没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词。barrette、beret 和 biretta 是历史上相关的词形或词汇，并非由现代英语 barret 按规则添加词缀形成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, barret is an intact historical borrowing, not bar plus -ret. Its plural is barrets, and it has no common derived verb, adjective, or adverb. Barrette, beret, and biretta are historically related forms or words, not regular modern affixations of barret.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cap（帽子、小帽）是宽泛上位词；beret（贝雷帽）通常指柔软、圆而平的无檐帽；biretta（四角帽）通常指基督教教士佩戴的有棱角帽。barret 是历史用词，具体帽形需结合时代与语境判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cap is the broad general term; beret usually means a soft, round, flat brimless hat; biretta usually denotes the angular cap worn by Christian clergy. Barret is historical, and its precise shape depends on the period and context.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Use familiar beret to picture a soft cap in an old portrait: barret is an older member of the same naming family.

etymology_story.zh: 该词可追溯至中古英语中与 col“煤”有关的形式，最终与古英语 col“煤”同源。“煤或烟灰”的黑色自然引出了“用煤灰弄黑、弄脏”的动词义。
etymology_story.en: The word goes back to Middle English forms associated with col, meaning 'coal,' ultimately related to Old English col. The blackness of coal dust and soot naturally led to the verb meaning 'to blacken or dirty.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 colly 视为不可自由拆分的旧词，不把词尾 -y 硬解为现代能产后缀。动词变化为 collies、collied、collying；名词通常不可数。coal（煤）、collier（煤矿工人；运煤船）和 colliery（煤矿）属于历史相关词，并非都由现代 colly 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat colly as an old, unanalyzed base rather than forcing a productive suffix analysis onto its final -y. Verb forms are collies, collied, and collying; the noun is normally uncountable. Coal, collier, and colliery are historically related words, not all direct modern derivatives of colly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blacken（使变黑）只强调颜色变化；soil（弄脏）泛指污染或沾污；soot（烟灰；用烟灰弄脏）最接近 colly 的具体物质含义。colly 带明显古语或地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blacken emphasizes a change to black; soil means to make dirty more generally; soot names the black deposit and can also mean to cover something with it. Colly specifically evokes soot or coal dust and has a distinctly archaic or regional character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住历史联系 coal“煤”：煤灰是 colly，沾上煤灰而变黑也叫 colly。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical link with coal: colly is the black dust, and to colly something is to make it black with that dust.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语传入，源头通常追溯至古北法语或盎格鲁法语中与 gambe“腿”有关的形式。后腿关节的弯曲形状把动物解剖义、屠宰悬挂器具义和折坡屋顶义联系起来。
etymology_story.en: The word entered through Middle English and is generally traced to northern Old French or Anglo-French forms related to gambe, meaning 'leg.' The bent shape of a hind-leg joint connects its anatomical, butchery, and roof senses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gambrel 是整体词干，没有可供现代英语自由组合的词根加词缀拆分。复数为 gambrels；常见复合词有 gambrel roof（复折式屋顶）和 gambrel-roofed（有复折式屋顶的）。gambreled、gambrelled 可表示“有复折式屋顶的”，但使用较少。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: gambrel is a single base with no productive root-and-affix breakdown in English. Its plural is gambrels; compounds include gambrel roof and gambrel-roofed. The less frequent forms gambreled and gambrelled can describe a building with this roof shape.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hock（飞节）是动物关节义的通常用词；spreader（撑杆）强调撑开功能，范围比屠宰用 gambrel 更广；mansard（曼萨尔式屋顶）通常四周都有折坡，而 gambrel 通常只有两个相对的坡面方向。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hock is the usual word for the animal joint; spreader is a broader functional term for a device that holds things apart; a mansard usually has double slopes on all four sides, whereas a gambrel usually has them on two opposing sides.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住一个“弯折轮廓”：后腿关节、撑腿横杆、折坡屋顶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a bent outline: a hind-leg joint, a leg-spreading bar, and a roof with a change of slope.

etymology_story.zh: grunion 通常被认为来自西班牙语 gruñón，意为“爱咕哝的；发出咕噜声者”，与 gruñir“咕哝、低声吼叫”有关。这个名称后来在英语中固定用于北美太平洋沿岸这类会上岸产卵的小鱼。
etymology_story.en: Grunion is generally traced to Spanish gruñón, meaning 'grumbling' or 'a grunter,' related to gruñir, 'to grunt.' In English, the name became established for these small Pacific coastal fish that spawn on beaches.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：grunion 是整体借词，不应拆成英语词根加 -ion 后缀。复数通常仍为 grunion，也可见 grunions；常见组合有 California grunion（加州银汉鱼）、Gulf grunion（海湾银汉鱼）和 grunion run（银汉鱼集群上岸产卵）。没有常用的派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: grunion is a borrowed whole word, not an English root followed by the suffix -ion. The plural is usually grunion, though grunions also occurs. Established combinations include California grunion, Gulf grunion, and grunion run; there are no common derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: silverside（银汉鱼类）是较宽泛的类群名称；smelt（胡瓜鱼类）和 sardine（沙丁鱼）可帮助联想小型银色鱼的外观，但不是 grunion 的准确同义词。grunion 的突出识别点是在沙滩上产卵。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Silverside is a broader group term; smelt and sardine suggest a similar small, silvery appearance but are not exact synonyms. The distinctive feature of grunion is their habit of spawning on sandy beaches.

etymology_story.zh: 该词通常被追溯至意第绪语 gendzl“小鹅”，后来进入美国流浪汉俚语，用来贬称年轻男性伴侣。由于其拼写和发音容易让人联想到 gun“枪”，它后来又发展出“枪手、持枪歹徒”的解释；不能把 gun 当成其可靠的历史词根。

Its resemblance to gun later encouraged the interpretation 'gunman' or 'armed criminal'; gun is not its established historical root.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gunsel 是整体俚语词，不能按 gun + -sel 分析，-sel 也不是这里的英语能产后缀。复数为 gunsels；没有稳定、常用的派生动词、形容词或副词。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gunman directly emphasizes carrying or using a gun; hoodlum means a thug who need not be armed; hitman specifically means someone hired to kill. etymology_story.zh: hirple 可追溯至中古苏格兰语 hirpil、hirple 等形式，较早就有“跛行”的意思；其更早来源并不确定。它保留在苏格兰及英国北部的地域用语中，不能据现代拼写杜撰一个确定的词根故事。
etymology_story.en: Hirple goes back to Middle Scots forms such as hirpil and hirple, already meaning 'to limp'; its earlier origin is uncertain. It survives in Scottish and northern English regional usage, so its spelling should not be used to invent a definite root story.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hirple 是整体词干，名词和动词同形。动词变化为 hirples、hirpled、hirpling；hirple + -ing → hirpling，添加 -ing 时去掉末尾不发音的 e。可规则构成 hirpler（跛行者），但并非常用词；hirpling 用作分词时表示“正在跛行的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hirple is a single base used as both a noun and a verb. Verb forms are hirples, hirpled, and hirpling; hirple + -ing becomes hirpling by dropping the final silent e. Hirpler, 'someone who limps,' is a possible regular derivative but is uncommon; hirpling also functions as a participle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: limp（跛行）是最直接、最通用的对应词；hobble（蹒跚、艰难行走）更强调行动受限和费力；shuffle（拖着脚走）强调脚不太离地，并不一定由腿脚受伤引起。hirple 的主要特色是地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Limp is the closest general equivalent; hobble emphasizes restricted, difficult movement; shuffle emphasizes dragging the feet and does not necessarily imply injury. Hirple is distinguished chiefly by its regional character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把整词绑定“一步高、一步低”的画面：动作是 hirple，步态也是 a hirple。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the whole word to an uneven step: you hirple when you limp, and the resulting gait is a hirple.

etymology_story.zh: Jehu 源自希伯来语人名 Yēhū，通常解释为“他是雅威”。《圣经》描写耶户驾车猛烈，这一形象后来使英语 jehu 获得“鲁莽的驾车人”，以及较宽泛的“马车夫”等旧时含义。
etymology_story.en: Jehu comes from the Hebrew personal name Yēhū, usually interpreted as “He is Yahweh.” The biblical description of Jehu's furious driving later gave English jehu the dated meanings of a reckless driver and, more broadly, a coachman.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可进一步分析的人名使用，不拆分为英语词根和词缀。专名为 Jehu，所有格为 Jehu's；转为普通名词时可写 jehu，复数为 jehus，没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Jehu is an unanalyzable personal name rather than a combination of English roots and affixes. Its possessive is Jehu's; the transferred common noun can be written jehu, with the plural jehus, and has no established everyday family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 专名 Jehu 没有真正的近义词。普通名词义可与 reckless driver（鲁莽的驾驶者）、coachman（马车夫）、charioteer（战车御者）比较：前者突出驾驶危险，coachman 指职业，charioteer 特指驾驶战车的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The personal name Jehu has no true synonym. For the common noun, reckless driver emphasizes dangerous driving, coachman identifies an occupation, and charioteer specifically denotes someone who drives a chariot.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 耶户王驾车猛烈：人名 Jehu → 飞驰的驾车人 jehu。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture King Jehu driving furiously: the name Jehu becomes jehu, a reckless driver.

senses.meaning_en: an immensely long period of cosmic time in Hinduism or Buddhism
senses.english_definition: A kalpa is an extremely long period of time used in Hindu or Buddhist accounts of the universe.

etymology_story.zh: kalpa 直接借自梵语 kalpa，该词与“安排、规定、秩序”等观念有关，并用于指宇宙时间的大周期。英语保留了这一宗教术语；它在印度教与佛教中的具体时长和分类并不完全相同。
etymology_story.en: Kalpa was borrowed from Sanskrit kalpa, a word associated with arrangement, prescription, and order that also denotes a great period of cosmic time. English preserves this religious term, whose precise duration and classifications differ between Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：kalpa 为整体借入的单一词干，没有可独立分析的英语前缀或后缀；复数为 kalpas。kalpa + cycle 可组成 kalpa cycle（劫周期）等名词短语，但这不属于派生构词；没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: kalpa is a single borrowed stem with no independently meaningful English prefix or suffix; its plural is kalpas. Combinations such as kalpa cycle are noun phrases rather than derived words, and there is no established everyday English family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aeon/eon（极漫长的时期）侧重时间之久；cosmic cycle（宇宙周期）突出宇宙的周期性变化；age（时代、时期）最为宽泛。它们可以辅助解释 kalpa，但不能完整替代其宗教技术含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aeon/eon emphasizes immense duration, cosmic cycle emphasizes recurring cosmic change, and age is a broad term for a period of time. These expressions help explain kalpa but do not fully replace its technical religious meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine one tick of a cosmic clock: a kalpa lasts almost beyond imagination.

etymology_story.zh: macchia 借自意大利语 macchia，该词既可指“斑点”，也可指“灌丛”，通常追溯到拉丁语 macula（斑点）。英语借用了它的植被含义，用来描述地中海地区的浓密常绿灌丛。
etymology_story.en: Macchia comes from Italian macchia, meaning both a spot and a thicket, generally traced to Latin macula, “spot.” English borrowed its vegetation sense for the dense evergreen scrub characteristic of the Mediterranean region.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：macchia 是整体借入的名词，不能按英语字母组合硬拆词根词缀；表示植被时通常作为不可数名词使用。macchia vegetation（地中海灌丛植被）是名词修饰名词的短语；没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: macchia is a borrowed noun that should not be divided into supposed English roots or affixes; in its vegetation sense it is normally uncountable. Macchia vegetation is a noun-modifying-noun phrase, and the word has no established everyday English family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: maquis（地中海常绿灌丛）是最接近的对应词；scrub（灌丛）泛指低矮木本植被；garrigue（地中海矮灌丛）通常指更低矮、更稀疏的植被，不能在严格生态描述中随意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Maquis is the closest equivalent; scrub is a general term for low woody vegetation; garrigue usually denotes lower, more open Mediterranean vegetation and is not interchangeable with macchia in precise ecological descriptions.

etymology_story.zh: orache 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语的植物名称演变而来，其词源可通过拉丁语相关形式追溯到希腊语 atraphaxys。它一直保留着植物名称的核心含义，英语中也常拼作 orach。
etymology_story.en: Orache developed through Middle English and Anglo-French plant names, with a history traceable through Latin forms to Greek atraphaxys. It has retained its basic botanical meaning and is also commonly spelled orach.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：orache 是不可进一步分析的单一词干，没有现代英语词根词缀组合；异体拼写为 orach，规则复数为 oraches。garden orache（庭园滨藜）与 red orache（红叶滨藜）是修饰性短语，没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: orache is an unanalyzable stem rather than a combination of modern English roots and affixes; orach is a spelling variant, and oraches is the regular plural. Garden orache and red orache are modified noun phrases, and there is no established everyday family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: orach 是同一个词的异体拼写；saltbush（盐灌木）与部分滨藜属植物的名称重合，但常指灌木状种类；mountain spinach（山菠菜）可用作庭园滨藜的俗名，不能涵盖全部滨藜属植物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Orach is an alternative spelling of the same word; saltbush overlaps with names for some Atriplex plants but often refers to shrubby species; mountain spinach can name garden orache but does not cover the whole genus.

senses.meaning_en: a migratory grassland songbird that breeds in North America and winters in South America
senses.english_definition: A bobolink is a small American songbird whose breeding male has black-and-white plumage and a pale patch on the back of its head.
senses.collocation_en: a male bobolink; a flock of bobolinks
senses.collocation_zh: 一只雄性稻鹀；一群稻鹀
senses.sentence_en: A male bobolink sang above the meadow before dropping into the grass.
senses.sentence_zh: 一只雄性稻鹀在草甸上空鸣唱，随后落入草丛。

etymology_story.zh: bobolink 是英语中的拟声鸟名，与较早的名称 Bob o' Lincoln 有关，模仿这种鸟富于变化的鸣声。它并非外来借词，名称主要来自声音联想。
etymology_story.en: Bobolink is an English imitative bird name related to the earlier name Bob o' Lincoln, echoing the bird's varied song. It is a sound-based English formation rather than a foreign borrowing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bobolink 作为整体拟声词干使用，不应拆成 bob + link 来解释词义；复数为 bobolinks。bobolink song（稻鹀的鸣声）等属于名词短语，没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bobolink functions as a single imitative stem and should not be explained as the semantic combination bob + link; its plural is bobolinks. Expressions such as bobolink song are noun phrases, and there is no established everyday family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reedbird（苇鸟）与 ricebird（稻鸟）都是稻鹀的传统别名，后者尤其关联其迁徙时在稻田觅食的习性；两个名称也可能指其他鸟，因此精确表述时 bobolink 更明确。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reedbird and ricebird are traditional alternative names for the bobolink, with ricebird especially associated with its feeding in rice fields during migration. Both names can also refer to other birds, so bobolink is more precise.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 bob-o-link 念成一串鸟鸣：叫声就是名字。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Say bob-o-link as a little burst of birdsong: the sound supplies the name.

senses.meaning_zh: 焦虑；烦躁；心烦意乱（美式非正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: Anxiety, agitation, or emotional distress, especially in informal American usage.
senses.english_definition: Agita is the worry or nervous discomfort that a difficult or annoying situation causes you.
senses.collocation_en: give someone agita; cause agita
senses.collocation_zh: 让某人焦虑烦躁；引起烦恼
senses.sentence_en: All these last-minute changes are giving me agita.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些临时变动让我焦躁不安。

senses.meaning_zh: 胃灼热；消化不良（美式非正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: Heartburn or indigestion, especially in informal American usage.
senses.english_definition: Agita is an uncomfortable burning or upset feeling in your stomach or chest after eating.
senses.collocation_en: get agita; give someone agita
senses.collocation_zh: 出现胃灼热或消化不良；使某人胃部不适
senses.sentence_en: That rich sauce always gives me agita.
senses.sentence_zh: 那种油腻的酱汁总让我胃里不舒服。

etymology_story.zh: 通常认为，该词经意大利裔美国人的口语进入英语，与意大利南部方言中表示胃酸不适的词形有关，并可追溯至意大利语 acido（酸的）。其意义从胃灼热、消化不良扩展为焦虑和烦躁。
etymology_story.en: The word is generally traced through Italian-American speech to a southern Italian dialect form associated with Italian acido, meaning 'acid.' Its meaning extended from heartburn or indigestion to anxiety and agitation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：agita，作为完整借词使用，无可供现代英语规则分析的词根与词缀；通常为不可数名词。没有常用的直接派生词；agitate（使焦虑、搅动）和 agitation（焦虑、骚动）虽在形式和部分意义上相近，但不应列为它的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: agita is a whole borrowed word with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; it is normally uncountable. It has no common direct derivatives; agitate and agitation resemble it in form and partly in meaning but should not be presented as its derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anxiety（焦虑）是中性的通用词；agitation（焦躁不安）更突出激动、坐立不安的状态；heartburn（胃灼热）对应身体义，而 agita 可借这种身体不适形容心理上的烦躁。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anxiety is the neutral general term for worry; agitation emphasizes an excited or restless state; heartburn corresponds to the physical sense, while agita can use that bodily discomfort to describe emotional distress.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 胃里泛酸，心里发烦：从胃部不适联想到心理焦躁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An acid stomach, an uneasy mind: connect digestive discomfort with emotional distress.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经古典语言传统传入英语，源于希腊语 dareikos，指古波斯金币。这个名称传统上被解释为与波斯王大流士一世有关，但其更早的词源并未完全确定。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through the classical-language tradition from Greek dareikos, the name of a Persian gold coin. The name has traditionally been associated with Darius I, although its ultimate origin is not entirely certain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：daric，作为完整的历史货币名称使用，不能可靠地拆为现代英语词根与后缀；复数为 darics（多枚大流克金币）。没有常用的直接派生词；Darius（大流士）属于传统词源解释中的关联专名。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: daric is a complete historical coin name, without a reliable modern English root-and-suffix division; its plural is darics. It has no common direct derivatives; Darius is a proper name associated with its traditional etymological explanation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gold coin（金 币）是上位概念，不限定时代或地区；stater（斯塔特，古代货币单位或硬币）是相关钱币术语，但不专指波斯大流克金币。daric 明确限定一种古波斯金币。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gold coin is a broader term without a particular historical or geographical restriction; stater is a related ancient monetary term but does not specifically identify a Persian daric. Daric names a particular ancient Persian gold coin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 大流士时代的波斯金币，币面常见王者弓箭手。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a Persian gold coin from the age of Darius, stamped with a royal archer.

etymology_story.zh: didy 是英语 diaper（尿布）的儿语变体，并非外来借词。它通过儿语式的语音改造形成，保留了“尿布”的基本意义。
etymology_story.en: Didy is a baby-talk alteration of English diaper, rather than a borrowing from another language. Its child-directed reshaping preserves the basic meaning 'diaper.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：diaper（尿布）→ didy（儿语改形），不宜机械拆成独立词根加后缀；复数为 didies（多块尿布）。另一拼写为 didie；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: diaper → didy through baby-talk alteration, rather than a transparent root-plus-suffix construction; the plural is didies. Didie is an alternative spelling, and there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diaper（尿布）是美式英语中的普通名称；nappy（尿布）是英式英语中的普通名称；didy 指同一种用品，但带有儿语或照料婴儿时的亲昵色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diaper is the ordinary American term; nappy is the ordinary British term. Didy refers to the same item but has the affectionate tone of baby talk or speech used while caring for a baby.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 diaper 说成宝宝式短词：didy，还是那块尿布。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of diaper reshaped into a little baby-talk word: didy.

senses.meaning_zh: 轮辋；尤指传统木制辐条轮的轮辋或其弧形组成段
senses.meaning_en: The rim of a traditional spoked wheel, or a curved section forming that rim.
senses.english_definition: A felloe is the outer rim of a spoked wheel, or one of the curved pieces that make up that rim.
senses.collocation_en: a wooden felloe; a felloe segment
senses.collocation_zh: 木制轮辋或轮辋段；一段弧形轮辋
senses.sentence_en: The wheelwright replaced a cracked felloe in the wagon wheel.
senses.sentence_zh: 修轮匠更换了马车轮上一段开裂的轮辋。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语传承自古英语 felg 或 felge，长期指车轮的外圈。它与德语 Felge（轮辋）同源，是英语继承的日耳曼词，而非近代外来借词。
etymology_story.en: The word passed through Middle English from Old English felg or felge and has long referred to the outer rim of a wheel. It is cognate with German Felge, meaning 'wheel rim,' and is an inherited Germanic word rather than a recent borrowing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：felloe，是不可再作常规词缀分析的单纯词；复数为 felloes（多个轮辋或轮辋段）。异体拼写为 felly，其复数为 fellies；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: felloe is a simple word without a productive root-and-affix division; its plural is felloes. The alternative spelling is felly, with the plural fellies; there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rim（边缘、轮辋）用途最广，也可指容器等物体的边缘；wheel rim（轮辋）明确限定车轮，却不限于传统木轮；felloe 是较专门的词，常指辐条木轮的轮辋或组成轮辋的一段。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rim is broad and can describe the edge of a container or other object; wheel rim specifies a wheel but is not restricted to traditional wooden construction. Felloe is more specialized and often denotes the rim of a wooden spoked wheel or one of its sections.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从轮毂沿辐条向外看：最外圈的弧形木段就是 felloe。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow a spoke outward from the hub: the curved wooden section at the edge is the felloe.

etymology.text: 英语中古时期已经使用 gyve 这个词。可以把它和古老故事里束缚脚踝的金属镣铐一起记。

senses.meaning_zh: 脚镣；镣铐（常用复数，文学或古旧用语）
senses.meaning_en: A fetter or shackle, especially for the legs; usually plural and literary or archaic.
senses.english_definition: Gyves are metal restraints fastened around a prisoner's legs or arms to prevent free movement.
senses.collocation_en: iron gyves; in gyves
senses.collocation_zh: 铁镣铐；戴着镣铐
senses.sentence_en: The prisoner dragged his iron gyves across the stone floor.
senses.sentence_zh: 囚犯拖着铁镣铐走过石地板。

senses.meaning_zh: 给……戴上镣铐；束缚（及物，文学或古旧用语）
senses.meaning_en: To put shackles on someone or to restrain someone; transitive, literary or archaic.
senses.english_definition: If someone gyves a person, they fasten restraints around that person's limbs or otherwise restrict their freedom.
senses.collocation_en: gyve a prisoner; gyved ankles
senses.collocation_zh: 给囚犯戴上镣铐；被镣铐锁住的脚踝
senses.sentence_en: The captive stood with his ankles gyved.
senses.sentence_zh: 俘虏站在那里，脚踝上锁着镣铐。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语中已有 give、gyve 等形式，指束缚肢体的镣铐，其更早来源并不确定。后来名词转用为动词，表示戴上镣铐，也可引申为限制自由。
etymology_story.en: The word appears in Middle English in forms such as give and gyve for a restraint on the limbs, although its earlier origin is uncertain. The noun later developed a verbal use meaning to put someone in shackles and, figuratively, to restrict freedom.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gyve，是无透明词缀结构的单纯词；名词转用为动词，无须添加后缀。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 gyves；过去式和过去分词为 gyved；现在分词为 gyving；没有其他常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: gyve is a simple word without transparent affixes; the verb is formed from the noun by conversion without an added suffix. Gyves is the noun plural and third-person singular verb form; gyved is the past tense and past participle; gyving is the present participle. There are no other common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fetter（脚镣；束缚）与 gyve 最接近，也常用于比喻；shackle（镣铐；给……戴镣铐）使用更广，语体较中性；manacle（手铐；给……戴手铐）尤其强调手或手腕的束缚。gyve 带有明显的文学或古旧色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fetter is closest to gyve and is also common figuratively; shackle has broader use and a more neutral register; manacle especially suggests restraints on the hands or wrists. Gyve has a distinctly literary or archaic tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一副镣铐是 gyves；把人锁上，就是 gyve。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The restraints are gyves; fastening them on someone is to gyve them.
